translations.text: Here begins the vernacular translation of the Psalter by Notker the Third. A psalm of David. Blessed is the man
who has not walked in the counsel of the ungodly. That man is blessed who did not go into the counsel of the wicked,
as Adam did when he followed his wife's counsel against God. And has not stood in the way of sinners.
Nor did he stand on the sinful way, as Adam did. Adam came onto it; he came onto the broad way that goes to hell,
and he stood on it, because he gave in to his desire. By giving in, he stood. And has not sat in the chair of pestilence.
Nor did he sit on the seat of sickness. I mean that he did not want to rule, because that sickness strikes nearly all of them,
as it did to Adam when he wanted to become God. In Latin, "pestis" means "laying low the cattle." When a pestis spreads, it is a pestilentia,
that is, a plague that has spread far and wide. But his will is in the law of the Lord, and in his law he will meditate day and night. Rather, that man is blessed
whose will is in God's law and who thinks on it day and night. And he will be like a tree that is planted beside the running waters.
And he thrives as well as the tree that is planted beside the running water,
which will give its fruit in its season. It gives its fruit at the right time. The running water is the grace of the Holy Spirit,
the grace of the Holy Spirit. Whoever it waters is a fruit-bearing tree of good works. And its leaf will not
fall off. Nor does its leaf fall. That is to say, his word does not become changeable either.
And all things whatsoever he does will prosper. And everything the tree bears and brings forth thrives, both fruits and leaves,
by which I mean deeds and words. Not so the ungodly, not so. But the wicked do not thrive so well. They do not thrive like that.
But they are like the dust that the wind drives from the face of the earth. Rather, they scatter like the dust of the earth that the wind blows away.
They are blown away from God's kingdom. Therefore the ungodly do not rise again in the judgment. Therefore the wicked do not rise to the judgment.
Even if they do rise, they do not then wait for judgment, because judgment has already been passed on them. FOR THEY ARE ALREADY JUDGED.
Nor sinners in the counsel of the righteous. Nor do sinners then sit in the counsel of the righteous. The first do not rise
in order to be judged, and the second do not rise in order to judge. The first are the worst; the second are not the best,
because both of them are sinful. But those who are the best judge the middling ones. For the Lord knows the way of the righteous.
Because God knows the way of the righteous. He deigns to know them and their works. And the path of the ungodly will perish.
And the path of the wicked will be lost. Because they themselves will be lost, their path will be lost too, and their path is their works.
A PSALM OF DAVID. WHY HAVE THE NATIONS RAGED? Why did the Hebrew nations gnash their teeth against Christ?
And the peoples have meditated vain things, that is, in vain? And why did his own people plot in vain to destroy him?
There it is clear that salvation is God's. You, God, give it. And your blessing is upon your people. And your blessing is over your people.
A SONG OF DAVID. WHEN I CALLED, THE GOD OF MY RIGHTEOUSNESS HEARD ME. The Church speaks.
God, from whom my righteousness comes, heard me when I cried to him. In tribulation you have enlarged me.
To the same one she says: You enlarged me in torments. For in persecution the crowns of the martyrs were multiplied.
Have mercy on me and hear my prayer. Have mercy on me and hear my prayer. Do as you did before:
hear me still. Sons of men, how long will you be heavy of heart? Children of men, how long will you remain in heaviness,
that is, in an unbelieving heart? Before the coming of Christ you were unbelieving. Do you still want to be so?
Why do you love vanity and seek falsehood? Why do you love idols, and why do you seek false gods? DIAPSALMA.
What is that? It is a silence, and a pause in the singing of the psalm, and a change of meaning. Just as sympsalma means the joining of voices in
singing, so diapsalma means the separation of voices. And know that the Lord has made his holy one wonderful.
Know that God has made Christ wonderful, for he brought him back to life from death
and set him at his right hand in heaven. To him you shall pray. The Lord will hear me when I cry to him.
The Lord hears me when I cry to him. The Church says this about herself, as if she were saying to her children:
The Lord will hear you when you cry to him. Cry to him with good works. Be angry and do not sin.
Be angry with yourselves over your sins, and avoid them. Repent of them, so that you do not commit them any more.
Or another way: Be angry, but do not avenge yourselves and your anger. If this [anger] happens,
avoid that [revenge]. What you say in your hearts — supply: say. What you say, say it from the heart,
so that you are not like those of whom it is written: THIS PEOPLE HONORS ME WITH THEIR LIPS,
BUT THEIR HEART IS FAR FROM ME. And be pierced with remorse in your beds. And in your hearts you will be stung with remorse.
Do not let your anger go any further. Let it be put out there, before it shows itself in your deeds.
Offer the sacrifice of righteousness and hope in the Lord. Bring God the offering of righteousness, that is, live rightly,
and hope that he will give you here the gift of the Holy Spirit, and hereafter eternal life. Many say: Who shows us good things?
Many do not know about these things, and they say: Who knows that? Who can tell us anything about eternal life?
Who shows us the good? The light of your countenance is marked upon us, Lord. You, Lord, have shown it to us.
The light of your face is marked upon us. You have made us in your image and likeness.
Which is that? None other than the future Jerusalem. I will worship toward your holy temple in fear of you. Toward your holy house
I pray from here toward there, in fear of you. When I come there, there I will be without fear, because there
is perfect love, which casts out fear. Lord, lead me in your justice because of my enemies. Lead me, Lord, in your justice because of my enemies,
who are hurrying to turn me away from there. Lead me in your justice, not in that of men, to whom it even seems just to repay evil for evil.
Direct my way in your sight. Direct my way in your sight. Direct the heart; that is in your sight,
not in the sight of men. For there is no truth in their mouth. There is no truth in their mouth. In the mouth of those men,
my enemies, it is not. Their heart is vain. Their heart is vain. How then can truth be in their mouth?
Their throat is an open grave. Their throat is an open grave. If the grave were closed, it would not stink. Nor would their throat,
if they kept silent. With their tongues they acted deceitfully. With their tongues they go about deceitfully, because they say one thing
and want another. That is deceit. Judge them, O God. Judge them, God. That is a prophecy, not a curse.
Let them fall from their thoughts. Let them fall away from their thoughts; that is, let them fail in their hope.
According to the multitude of their impieties, cast them out. According to their great wickedness, drive them out. Take from them the inheritance
that holy Church awaits. For they have provoked you, Lord. Because they angered you, Lord, therefore make them disinherited.
And let all who hope in you rejoice. And let all rejoice who trust in you.
They will exult forever, and you will dwell in them. They will rejoice forever, and you dwell in them. They are forever glad of this,
that they are your house. And all who love your name will glory in you. And in you all will glory
who love your name. In you they have the inheritance. For you bless the just man.
For you give blessing to the just man. He has the inheritance from blessing, not from his own justice. Lord, you have crowned us as with the shield of your good will.
As with a shield of good will you have crowned us, Lord. Your good will is our protection and our honor.
PSALM FOR THE OCTAVE. After the seven days of the week comes the eighth. That is the day of judgment,
which comes after these seven ages of the world. Fearing that day, and the judgment,
"Lord, do not rebuke me in your fury," says the prophet. Lord, in your hot anger do not accuse me then.
Nor chastise me in your wrath. Nor rebuke me in your wrath on the day of judgment,
because those whom God rebukes then will not be saved. Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak.
Have mercy on me, for I am unable to fulfill your law. Heal me, Lord, for my bones are troubled.
Heal me, for my bones are troubled. That is: my strength has failed me.
And my soul is troubled exceedingly. And my soul is in great trouble. It became sick from sins in paradise.
And you, O Lord, how long? And how long will you now delay your help, Lord? Turn, O Lord, and deliver my soul.
Turn yourself here to me, Lord, and free my soul from temptation and from punishment. Save me for your mercy's sake.
Keep me for the sake of your grace, because I have deserved it. For there is no one in death who remembers you. For no one in death thinks
of you. In which death? Only when the soul is blinded by sins.
The blindness makes it forget God. But who will confess to you in hell? But who in hell confesses to you?
Whom does his confession help there? I have toiled in my groaning. I toiled with sighs
when I came to repent of my sins. Every night I will wash my bed. THE BED OF THE SOUL IS THE BODY. If that is not enough,
then I wet my bed every night, that is, AS OFTEN AS I STUMBLE. WHOEVER WALKS IN THE NIGHT STUMBLES.
What I have made unclean, I make clean. With my tears I will water my couch. With my tears I wet my bed.
With them I pour over it; with them I wash it. My eye is troubled because of anger. My eye is dimmed
before your anger. Because I fear your anger, I have wept so much that it is dimmed.
I have grown old among all my enemies. I may well weep that I have grown old among all my enemies,
who every day eagerly lead me away from your justice. Depart from me, all you who work iniquity. Separate yourselves from me, all you evildoers.
Stop leading me astray. For the Lord has heard the voice of my weeping. For God has heard my weeping.
The Lord has heard my supplication. He has heard my plea. The Lord has received my prayer. He has received my prayer.
I have not wept so much in vain. Let all my enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled.
Let all my enemies be ashamed together with me and be sorry for their sins, so that God may hear them too. Let them be turned back and be ashamed
very quickly. Let them turn to penitence and be ashamed at once, very swiftly, before his anger comes.
FOR THE WORDS OF CHUSI, SON OF JEMINI. When Absalom was against his father, the father secretly ordered his friend Chusi to go
along with his son, on these terms: that he should let him know whatever dangerous counsel he heard there.
In that likeness David sang this psalm about the Son, whom his Father secretly sent into the midst of the Jews
to turn danger away from humankind. THE VOICE OF THE PROPHET. O LORD MY GOD, IN YOU I have hoped;
save me from all who persecute me, and deliver me. In you, Lord, I have always hoped. Keep me, that is:
save me from my enemies, and free me. Free me from Absalom, or, spiritually, from the devil.
Lest at any time he seize my soul like a lion, while there is none to redeem it nor any to save it. Lest he snatch away my soul like a lion,
when there is no one who frees me or keeps me; that is to say, if you do not help me. If you do not help,
then he will prevail [over] me. O Lord my God, if I have done this, if there is iniquity in my hands, if I have repaid those who repaid me with evils,
may I deservedly fall empty before my enemies. Lord my God, if I did this, if this injustice is in my hands,
that I repaid Saul and Absalom in kind, who did me harm in return for kindness, then I fall justly.
That is to say: then I shall justly be felled by my enemies, emptied of goodness.
Let the enemy pursue my soul and seize it. Then let the devil hunt my soul and catch it. And let him tread my life into the ground.
And let him trample my life into the earth; that is to say, let him defile me with earthly sins. And let him bring my glory down into the dust.
And let him bring my glory to dust. Let him make my conscience, which pleases God, please only men.
Arise, O Lord, in your wrath. Stand up, Lord, with wrath. Let your wrath be against the devil.
And be exalted in the borders of your enemies. And become high, become glorious, in the territories of your enemies.
Take their lands. Take from the devil those whom he has occupied. And arise, O Lord my God, in the precept which you have commanded.
And raise yourself up in your command. You commanded humility. Come with it, and fulfil your command yourself.
And the assembly of the peoples will surround you. And if you do that, then the multitude of the peoples will surround you, both of believers and of persecutors.
And for its sake return on high. For the sake of that multitude, return to heaven, so that you may send the Holy Spirit to the believers
and be out of sight to the unbelievers. The Lord judges the peoples. After that ascension the Lord will come to judge the living and the dead.
Judge me, O Lord, according to my righteousness, and according to my innocence that is upon me. Then judge me according to my righteousness
and my innocence. For I am innocent toward Saul and Absalom, and I have dealt rightly with them.
Let the wickedness of sinners be brought to an end, and you will direct the just, O God who searches the hearts and reins. The wickedness of the sinners will be brought to an end, as it says:
LET THE FILTHY BE FILTHY STILL. And you direct the righteous, O God who searches hearts and reins. In that place you direct
him where you search him. You alone search him there; you alone direct him there.
You direct him there when worldly ambition is not in the heart, nor the delight of the flesh in the reins.
My help is just, from the Lord, who saves the upright of heart. My help from God is just; that is to say,
he rightly helps me, since I was righteous, he who preserves the righteous in their hearts. God is a just judge, strong and long-suffering.
Will he be angry every day? God is the just judge, for he rewards everyone according to his works.
Strong-minded, because he endures much; long-suffering, because he does not hasten to take vengeance. Is he angry every day?
What would he then be saving up for the Last Judgment? Unless you are converted, he will brandish his sword. If you do not turn yourselves,
he will brandish his sword, that is, he will show his wrath. When? On the day of judgment. He has bent his bow and made it ready.
He has fully strung his bow, because he has forced the hardness of the Old Testament with the sinew of the New Testament
and made it pliant [?]. And on it he has prepared the vessels of death. And on it he has made the vessels of death,
for wrongly understood Scripture makes heretics; these are the vessels of death. He has made his arrows for those who burn.
He made his arrows burning. Those for whom he made them, at them he shot them. To those who desired the truth he sent the apostles.
These are his arrows. Behold, he has been in labor with injustice, and has conceived sorrow, and has brought forth iniquity. See what the synagogue of the Jews did.
It began to give birth to injustice when it first attacked Christ. And it had already conceived sorrow in its heart then, because
he said: 'I have God as Father, but you are from below, and you want to do the will of your father the devil.' After that it gave birth to the injustice,
when it said: 'Crucify, crucify him!' He opened a pit and dug it out, and fell into the ditch that he had made. It opened the pit
into which it wanted to make Christ fall, and it dug it, and into that same pit it fell. By lying in wait for him [?],
it slew itself. His sorrow (that is, of the synagogue or of the sinful soul) will be turned back upon his head,
and his iniquity will come down upon his own crown. Its sorrow turns back upon its head, and its injustice crashes down upon its crown.
The soul is the head; reason is its crown. When the soul acts irrationally and serves lust,
then injustice strikes it and blinds it. In this way it comes upon it, and upon its crown.
I will praise the Lord according to his justice, and I will sing psalms to the name of the Lord most high. I, however, will praise God according to his justice,
for he is the one who renders to each according to his works; and I will sing psalms to the name of the Highest.
To the end, for the winepresses. Christ is the end; this psalm is directed to him, concerning the winepresses. What are these? None other than the churches,
in which the good hasten to separate themselves in their minds from the wicked, just as wine and dregs are separated in the winepresses.
O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name in all the earth! Lord, our master, says the Church, how great you are!
How wonderful your name is in all the world! How they all marvel at you! For your magnificence is raised above
the heavens. They may well do so, because your mighty working is raised above the heavens, as is shown by the fact that you are seated there
at the right hand of the Father. Out of the mouth of infants and sucklings you have perfected praise. Out of the mouth of children and of those still nursing you have made praise.
That is: those who were weak in the faith, them you have brought to fulfilment, to your perfect praise.
Because of your enemies. To the shame of your enemies, who could not come so far by their own wisdom.
Who are they? None other than the Jews and heretics. As was evident then, when the Jews silenced the praise of the children,
and Christ reminded them of this scripture. That you may destroy the enemy and the defender. That with it you destroy the enemy
and the defender. Jews and heretics strive to speak in defence of God, though they are his enemies.
For I shall see the heavens, the works of your fingers. For I see the heavens, the work of your fingers.
I understand the Scriptures which you directed, in which you are found, as if in heaven. The moon and the stars which you founded.
I see in them the moon and the stars, which you firmly set. That is: I also see myself in them,
and my children. I recognize you as the bridegroom, and myself as the bride, and the sons of the bridegroom. What is man, that you are mindful of him? What is man,
that you are mindful of him? How can one of Adam's kind earn your favour? Or the son of man, that you visit him?
Or the son of man, that you visit him? As you did then, when you sent Christ here. You made him, that is, the man Christ,
a little less than the angels. You made him somewhat less than your angels, because he could die, though he was without sin. With glory and honour
you crowned him, and set him over the works of your hands. With glory and with honour you crowned him, and set him over the works of your hands.
Over all things that are in heaven and on earth. You have put all things under his feet. All things that are there
you cast under his feet. Even the angels. Sheep and oxen. Sheep and cattle: the innocent and the preachers.
All of them, and also the beasts of the field. In addition, all the beasts of the field. Who are they?
None other than those who go by the broad way and live in pleasure. The birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, which pass along the paths of the sea.
Birds and sea fish, which travel through all the ways of the sea. These are the proud and the curious,
for the evil and the good who are in the winepress all lie under his feet. O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name in all the earth.
FOR THE HIDDEN THINGS OF THE SON. The judgments of Christ: these are the hidden things of the Son. He now does hidden things; this psalm is written about them.
At the end of the world he does manifest things. When here in the world he blinds some to damnation, and scourges others for correction
or for exercise, that comes from his hidden judgment. GOD THE JUDGE BROUGHT FIVE KINDS OF SICKNESS UPON THE WORLD:
THAT OF JOB, OF MIRIAM, OF LAZARUS, OF PAUL; THE FIFTH IS HEROD'S. GUILTLESS JOB LIES IN FILTH. DESERVED LEPROSY BITES MIRIAM.
LAZARUS'S IS FOR THE PRAISE OF THE LORD; PAUL'S IS A GOAD FOR SAFEKEEPING. THE FIFTH KIND IS THE CRUEL DEATH OF ANTIOCHUS OR HEROD.
I WILL CONFESS TO YOU, O LORD, WITH MY WHOLE HEART. I confess to you, Lord, says the prophet, with all
...my heart. I separate myself from those who in all worldly events do not recognize your providence.
And they think that all things happen at random and by chance, that is, haphazardly and accidentally.
I will recount all your wonders. I will tell all your wonders. Enough people tell the open ones, those that are evident,
such as that you raised Lazarus from the death of the body. But I would rather tell how you secretly called Paul back from the death of the soul.
I will be glad and rejoice in you. In you I will be glad and leap for joy, not in worldly good fortune. And I will sing psalms to your name, O Most High.
And I will sing psalms to your name, you Most High. When my enemy is turned back, they will be weakened
and will perish before your face. In turning my enemy back, that is, when you turn my enemy back,
then all his followers [satellites] will be weakened, and they will not come before you. Such people do not come before you, as Saul did not,
nor his followers. For you have upheld my judgment and my cause. For you made the trial be mine [? min uuésen]. And the lawsuit
be mine [?]. Because I was in the right, I therefore contended. You sit on the throne, you who judge equity.
You, the righteous one, sit on the throne. You sit at the right hand of the Father. You rebuked the nations, and the wicked one perished. From there you sent the Holy Spirit
and rebuked the nations, as it is said of him: 'When he comes, he will convict the world.' And then the wicked one was lost.
Afterwards he was no longer wicked, because he then became good. You have blotted out their name forever and for ever and ever.
Then you blotted out the name of the wicked forever and ever. The swords of the enemy have failed to the
end, and you have destroyed the cities. The devil's swords dwindled away to the end, and you destroyed his cities. What are those cities
but unbelief and wickedness? Their memory has perished with a noise. Then the memory of the wicked passed away with the noise of contradiction [contradictionis].
They became good and quiet. And the Lord remains forever. So why did the nations rage against the Lord? He indeed exists forever.
He has prepared his throne for judgment. He set up his throne even then, while men here were holding trial over him.
What can be more hidden? Are these not the hidden things of the Son? And he himself will judge the world in equity.
And he who brings this about so secretly, that same one will pass judgment on the world in equity. In that equity
he withholds his reward from no one more than from another. He will judge the peoples in justice.
He will judge the peoples according to right, so that he does not make the guilty innocent, nor the innocent guilty,
as people do who do not see hearts. There each person's conscience will accuse him or defend him.
And the Lord has become a refuge for the poor. And the Lord is a refuge for the poor, those who are gladly poor here
so that they may be rich hereafter. A helper at the right times, in tribulation. A helper [?] in need and in hardship.
And let all who know your name hope in you. And let all who know your name hope in you. Your name is "est" ("is"), that is, being.
Whoever recognizes "est", that is, being, recognizes you and hopes in you, and changeable things are worthless to him.
For you do not forsake those who seek you, Lord. Rightly so, because you, Lord, do not forsake those who seek you. Sing psalms to the Lord who dwells
in Zion. Sing psalms to him who dwells in Zion. Where there is watching (speculatio), there he dwells. Where is that?
Nowhere but where his saints are, who wish to come from speculatio to visio, that is, from watching to beholding.
He rewards them for the watching, that is, for their hope, with the beholding. Proclaim his wonders among the nations.
Let the preachers proclaim his wonders to the nations; then you sing psalms well. For in requiring their blood he has remembered.
So do not fear death, because he mindfully demands a reckoning for the slaying of his martyrs. He has not forgotten the prayer of the poor.
He does not forget the prayer of the poor, as some suppose because he does not act hastily. Have mercy on me, Lord;
see my humiliation at the hands of my enemies. Have mercy on me, Lord; look on the humility my enemies have brought on me.
They have humbled me, in the same measure as they are proud. The prophet says this in the person of the martyrs. You who lift me up from the gates of death,
so that I may proclaim all your praises in the gates of the daughter of Zion. You who lift me up high from the gates of death, which all seducers are,
have mercy on me, so that I may proclaim your praise in the gates of the Church, which are all those who lead to God,
and so that they may praise you together with me. I will rejoice in your salvation. Following this voice of the poor man, the prophet speaks to God:
I rejoice in your Savior. In Christ I find comfort for my hardships. The nations are stuck fast in the destruction that they made.
The nations put your martyrs to death; in that death they themselves are stuck. The martyrs readily suffered the death of the body; the persecutors lie in the death of the soul.
In this snare which they hid, their own foot is caught. In this snare that they hid, their foot was caught. They wanted to deceive others,
and they themselves are deceived. The Lord shall be known as one who executes judgments; the sinner is caught in the works of his own hands. There God is recognized
as one who executes such judgments that the sinner is caught in the work of his own hands.
He set the snare; in it he is caught. Let sinners be turned into hell. DIAPSALMA. Let sinners be turned into hell.
Let them plunge into the terrible lusts that lead to hell. All the nations that forget God.
Let all peoples who do not acknowledge God fare the same way. Since they want to be without God, let God cast them into a reprobate mind.
For the poor shall not be forgotten to the end. For the poor shall not be forgotten so completely
as people now suppose that God has forgotten them, while they are being oppressed by sinners like this.
The patience of the poor shall not perish forever. The patience of the poor shall never be lost forever.
His mouth is full of cursing, and of bitterness, and of deceit. His mouth is full of evil speaking, because he is a blasphemer,
and of bitterness, because he commands cruel things against the servants of God. Under his tongue are toil and sorrow. Under his tongue lie sorrow and toil.
With his tongue he shows good, when he says that he is God; beneath it he hides the evil, which is toil and sorrow.
He sits in ambush with the rich in secret places. With those whom he has made rich he sits secretly, lying in wait. That he may slay the innocent.
That he may slay the harmless. He slays the harmless when he makes him harmful. His eyes look upon the poor.
His eyes keep watch on the poor man. He lies in wait for the one who is poor in spirit. He lies in wait in secret, like a lion in his den.
He lies in wait as secretly as the lion in his lair. He is both strong and cunning at deceiving.
He lies in wait to seize the poor; to seize the poor while he draws him. He lies in wait to snatch away the poor man; he hastens to snatch him from God,
when he draws him to himself and bids him turn God's honour to him. In his snare he will humble him.
In his snare he brings him low, for with his signs he makes him put his trust in him. He shall bow down and fall when he has lorded it over the poor.
When he has done all that, and has ruled over the poor so far, after that he sinks and falls.
For he said in his heart: God has forgotten; he will turn away his face so as not to see to the end. He shall then come to learn [?] what he thought: God has
forgotten the good; he turns away from them, so that he will no longer look upon them. Arise, O Lord God, let your hand be exalted;
do not forget the poor. Then do not do, Lord, as he thought, but rise up and show your power;
do not forget the poor, as his words claimed. Why has the wicked man provoked God? For he said in his heart: He will not require it.
Why, alas, did the wicked one anger God? Why did he think of him: He will not call me to account for what I do?
You see it, for you consider toil and sorrow. You, God, see what he thought, because you also see the toil and sorrow
that he hid under his tongue. That you may deliver him into your hands. That is why you look upon it: that you may thrust him into your hand,
that is, into your judgement, and that he may not profit from having acted so. For the poor man is left to you.
The poor man is kept for you; his comfort is in you alone. He needs nothing more; in you he is rich.
You will be a helper to the orphan. You help the orphan, whose mother, this world, is dead to him.
Break the arm of the sinner and of the malicious. Against this, crush the arm of the sinful and of the ill-willed.
That is, destroy the power of the one of whom it is said above: HE SHALL HAVE DOMINION OVER ALL HIS ENEMIES.
His sin shall be sought and shall not be found. That too will happen thus: his sin will soon be searched for hard,
and not found, because he himself is lost along with his sins. The Lord shall reign for ever, and for ages of ages.
But our Lord reigns forever and ever. "You nations shall perish from his land." You unrighteous peoples will be destroyed
from his kingdom, where the land of the living is. "The Lord has heard the desire of the poor." The Lord heard the desire of the poor.
They longed for the day of the Lord when they were in distress. He gives it to them after the destruction of Antichrist. "Your ear has heard the preparation of their heart."
Your ear has heard the readiness of their heart. It is ready for you when you come.
For what purpose do you come? "To judge for the orphan and the humble." To judge for the orphan and the humble.
Not only for the orphan, but for the humble orphan. "That man may no longer presume to magnify himself upon the earth."
That no one from now on may presume to exalt himself upon the earth, as Antichrist did; for then there will be an end of all injustice.
UNTO THE END, A PSALM OF DAVID. This psalm of David looks to the end, that is, Christ, because in Christ he rebukes the heretics.
He now speaks to them in the person of the faithful. "IN THE LORD I TRUST. HOW DO YOU SAY TO MY SOUL: MOVE OVER TO THE MOUNTAIN LIKE A SPARROW?"
I trust in God, who is my mountain, in whom I have refuge. How do you heretics say to me:
"Fly up here onto the mountain like a bird"? All little birds are called "passeres" (sparrows), and some of them live in the mountains.
Therefore the heretics speak as if to one of those that is a mountain bird. Christ is the mountain.
They imagine that he is with them; for that reason they lure the catholics there, and for that reason they are answered by them in this way:
"For behold, sinners have bent the bow; they have prepared their arrows in the quiver, to shoot in the dark at the upright of heart."
Why do you say to me, "MOVE OVER TO THE MOUNTAIN"? And "you should do this because sinners have drawn their bow
and have their arrows all ready in their quiver, to shoot secretly with them at those who are righteous in their hearts"?
Why do you threaten me? Since I trust in God, who can lead me astray? "For what you have made perfect they have destroyed."
This voice looks to the Lord. Thus they threaten the Lord, for they have destroyed what you made. They have
corrupted your scriptures with false interpretations. They themselves are guilty of what they accuse others of. They shoot harmful words
with the bow of scripture, so that they lead astray the upright of heart. "But what has the righteous one done?" What has the righteous one done to you?
What guilt does Christ have, whom you revile? "The Lord is in his holy temple; the Lord, his seat is in heaven." He himself is in his house;
his throne is in heaven. The faithful soul is the temple of God; it is heaven. When you revile it,
you revile him. "His eyes look upon the poor; his eyelids question the sons of men." His eyes look upon the poor man;
his eyelids question the children of men. That is to say, he always has his eyes open upon his own.
Even when he acts as if he were asleep, he tests people to see how they honor him in his own.
The Lord examines the just and the wicked. The Lord tests both, the good and the evil. But he who loves iniquity
hates his own soul. But he who loves injustice hates his own soul, and harms himself, not another.
He will rain snares upon sinners. He rains snares upon the sinful. He rains upon them that which torments them.
Just as he sends the rain of his preachers to the blessed for life, so he sends it to the unblessed for death.
As Paul says: TO SOME WE ARE THE ODOR OF LIFE UNTO LIFE, TO OTHERS THE ODOR OF DEATH UNTO DEATH.
Fire and brimstone and the spirit of storms are the portion of their cup. Fire and sulphur and stormy wind: that is the portion of their measure.
For first their desire burns them; when they have fulfilled it, then it turns into an evil stench,
which separates them from the good. After that they are blown away to destruction. That portion is measured out to them.
That is, they receive their portion by measure. Calix (cup) is named from calidus liquor (hot liquid), and here it stands for measure. For the Lord is just and has loved justice.
For God, being just, loves the justice of men. His face has seen equity. Where he knows equity, there he looks. Toward the end, which is Christ,
TO THE END, FOR THE EIGHTH: this psalm looks there, as was also written above concerning others.
Why is it written? What does he pray for? That through the eternal day, which is called the eighth,
this hateful darkness of the world, of which everyone may grow weary, may be destroyed. SAVE ME, O LORD.
FOR THE HOLY ONE HAS FAILED. Keep me safe, Lord, in that world, for here the holy one has passed away. Why, then, is that?
For truths are diminished among the sons of men. For truths have dwindled away among men. How can those be holy
among whom there is little truth? They have spoken vain things, each to his neighbor. They all speak vanity to one another.
Deceitful lips in the heart, and with a heart they have spoken. Deceitful and crafty lips speak with a double heart,
as the Jews did toward Christ. They had one thing in their mind and another in their mouth. May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips.
May God destroy such lips. The tongue that speaks great things. And likewise the boastful tongue. Who have said: We will magnify our tongue.
Such was the tongue of those same Jews, who said: We will make our tongue great; we will make it fearsome.
Our lips are our own. For whose sake should we hold back? We have our lips from ourselves.
Who is our lord? Who is our lord, that we should thank him for them? Because of the misery of the needy and the groaning of the poor
now I will arise, says the Lord. This is the person of the Father. Because of the misery of the poor, says God the Father, and because of the
sighing of the wretched, I arise. That is, for their comfort I show myself in the Son. I will set [?] upon my salvation.
I set their comfort in my Savior. 'Mine', because I give him and I send him forth.
"I will act confidently in him." In him I will work boldly. As it says in the Gospel: "For he was teaching them
as one having authority, not as their scribes." "The words of the Lord are pure words." Pure speeches are the Lord's speeches.
He fulfills as he promises, and sends his Son. "Silver tried by fire, of the earth." Like refined silver of the earth,
in which there is no dross; so pure are they. "Purified sevenfold." Refined seven times.
For the grace of the Holy Spirit is sevenfold, and because he is unlike those "whose truths are diminished." "You, O Lord, will preserve us
and keep us from this generation forever." You, Lord, keep us from now on into eternity: here poor, and there rich.
"The wicked walk round about." The wicked go around in circles, because they never direct their course there, to the rest of the eighth day.
They want temporal things, not eternal ones. "According to your height you have multiplied the sons of men." You have multiplied righteous people
according to your height. You are in heaven. You have made the sons of Abraham many, as the stars of heaven.
TO THE END, A PSALM OF DAVID. He who is the end of the law is invited hither into the world by the prophet.
"HOW LONG, O LORD, WILL YOU FORGET ME TO THE END?" How long, Lord, will you forget, that is,
will you not let me see the end? Why are you not born, Christ? "How long will you turn your face away from me?"
How long will you turn your countenance away from me, and not toward me? I watch for you; you
do not come. "How long shall I take counsel in my soul, sorrow in my heart by day?" How long shall I deliberate,
how long shall I go about sorrowful by day, that is, in this life, because you do not come
or take me away from here? "How long shall my enemy be exalted over me?" How long will my enemy be exalted over me?
That is: how long shall it pain me that unbelief reigns, or that carnal desire also oppresses me?
"Look upon me and hear me, O Lord my God." Look hither, Lord: that answers to "HOW LONG DO YOU TURN YOUR FACE AWAY FROM ME?"
And hear me: that answers to "HOW LONG WILL YOU FORGET ME TO THE END?" "Enlighten my eyes, lest I ever sleep in death."
Enlighten my eyes (I mean the eyes of the heart), lest I fall asleep in death. The enemy loves that sleep
which leads to death; it lies in carnal delight. "Lest my enemy say: I have prevailed against him."
Lest the devil say mockingly: I have become his master. "Those who trouble me will rejoice if I am moved."
The demons who torment me would leap for joy if I were moved from my place and if I fell into sin.
"But I will hope in your mercy." But I have hope in you, that you will hold me fast.
"My heart has rejoiced in my salvation." I rejoice in your Saviour, in Christ your Son. "I will sing to the Lord."
I sing to God, moving the body according to reason, for that is the spiritual song of the soul. Who has given good things to me.
He who has given me spiritual good things. And I will sing psalms to the name of the Lord most high. And to the name of the Most High I will sing psalms.
To the end, for David himself. He whom we shall see when we reach perfection is that 'end' (finis). To him David sings, rebuking the Jews.
The fool has said in his heart: There is no God. The unwise one thought that God does not exist. So too the Jewish people thought
that Christ is not God. They are corrupt and have become abominable in their desires. By loving this world
they were perverted in their minds and made loathsome. Because of that they became so blind that they did not know
whether God existed. There is none who does good, there is not even one. There is none who does well. None, except one.
Who is that? The man-God Christ. On him rest the good deeds of all people. The Lord looked down from heaven upon the children of men.
The Lord looked out from afar, down from heaven, upon the children of men. He looked upon the Jews; to them he sent his Son.
To see if there is anyone who understands or seeks God. So that he might see whether anyone had understanding or sought God.
They have all turned aside together. Then they all turned aside. If any did not turn aside, they were as good as none compared with the others.
They have become useless. They became useless. But to whom? To themselves. There is none who does good,
there is not even one. That was said above. Their throat is an open grave. Their throat stinks like an open grave,
because they speak the things by which they corrupt others. With their tongues they acted deceitfully. With their speech they dissembled.
The venom of asps is under their lips. The venom of asps is under their lips, because they will not listen to the precepts of the law,
just as asps will not listen to the charmer's spell. The asp presses one ear to the ground
and thrusts its tail into the other. Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness. Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.
That is the venom of asps. Their feet are swift to shed blood. They are quick to commit murder, since they
even kill the Son of God. Destruction and misery are in their ways. Crushing and misfortune are in their ways.
Wherever they strive, they strive with toil. And the way of peace they have not known. And yet they do not recognize the way of peace, Christ,
who is the one who takes away the toils! As he himself said: Come to me, all you who labor, and I will refresh you.
There is no fear of God before their eyes. The fear of God is not before their eyes. Although they know him,
they do not fear him. Shall not all who work iniquity come to know? When the judgment comes, will they not then recognize their wickedness,
all who now work it? Who devour my people as they eat bread. Who devour my people like bread,
who hasten to glut themselves to their own perdition. They have not called upon the Lord. They did not call upon God.
Nor do those who are against him truly do so. There they trembled with fear where there was no fear. They feared
what was not to be feared. They feared losing the earthly kingdom, and so they lost the heavenly one. That is why they said:
IF WE LET HIM ALONE LIKE THIS, EVERYONE WILL BELIEVE IN HIM, AND THE ROMANS WILL COME AND TAKE AWAY OUR PLACE AND OUR NATION.
All who are afraid of losing temporal things cannot, for that reason, come to eternal things. For God is in the righteous generation.
For God is in the righteous generation, not in those who love this world. You have confounded the counsel of the poor man.
You confound the counsel of the poor man. That is, you reject the counsel of the Son of God, who chose to come as a poor man for this reason:
so that he might make you rich. Because you did not see the pomp of the world in him, he seemed contemptible to you. For the Lord is his hope.
For God alone is his comfort. That is, because he taught you to put your comfort in God alone.
Who will give the salvation of Israel out of Zion? Since you have rejected him, who then will grant from
Zion that Israel may be saved? Is it not he whom Isaiah promised when he said: THERE SHALL COME OUT OF ZION
ONE WHO SHALL TURN AWAY UNGODLINESS FROM JACOB? When the Lord turns back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice and Israel shall be glad.
When the Lord, at the end of the world, turns back the exile of his people, then Jacob and Israel will rejoice.
When they reach fulfilment, where they are meant to reach fulfilment, there they will rejoice.
A PSALM OF DAVID HIMSELF. 'David' means 'strong of hand'. That is CHRIST; he is the strong-handed one. This psalm is sung to him,
because he is asked a question here, and he gives an answer here. LORD, WHO SHALL DWELL IN YOUR TABERNACLE?
Lord, who dwells in your tent? The Church is your tent. What soldier is fit to be in it?
Or who shall rest on your holy mountain? Or who rests after the warfare in heaven, your holy mountain?
He who enters without stain and works righteousness. Now CHRIST answers: He who goes in there without stain
and works righteousness. That is, he who after his baptism avoids evil and does good
in my Church. He who speaks the truth in his heart. He who speaks truly in his heart, as does the one
who does not lie in his thought. He who has not practised deceit with his tongue. He who practises no deceit when he speaks. Nor has done evil to his neighbour.
And he refrains from doing evil to anyone. And has not taken up a reproach against his neighbours. And he did not too hastily believe evil of others.
The wicked one is brought to nothing in his sight. And the devil was brought to nothing before him. I mean
that the devil could do nothing against him in any temptation, because he did not yield to him at all. But he glorifies those who fear the Lord.
And he honours those who fear God, for God's sake. He who swears to his neighbour and does not deceive him. He who swears an oath to another man and does not deceive him.
because he does not swear to him with those words in order to deceive him. Who has not given his money at usury.
He who has not given his treasure out to earn interest. And has not taken bribes against the innocent. And he has not taken payment against innocent people.
I mean that he has harmed no one for the sake of a bribe. He who does these things shall not be moved for ever.
He who does this rests on his holy mountain, and he will never again be driven out from there.
THE INSCRIPTION OF THE TITLE, TO DAVID HIMSELF. That is, an inscription is made on the cross for Christ himself. He for whom the title was made
speaks here to the Father about his Passion. Preserve me, O Lord, for I have hoped in you. Keep me, Lord, says Christ to the Father,
for I hope in you. Right after that he speaks to us. I said to the Lord: You are my God, for you have no need of my goods.
I said to the Lord what you also should say to him: You are my God, for you are not in need of my good.
You do not become blessed through my goodness. To the saints who are in his land, he has made all my wills wonderful in them.
For the saints who are in his land, that is, those whose hope is in the land of the living, he has made wonderful
all my wills in them. What is this will of mine in them? Only that I have made them eternal instead of mortal
and heavenly instead of earthly. He has taught them to regard this as a wonder. Their infirmities were multiplied.
Their sicknesses were many before this, before they became heavenly and eternal. Afterward they made haste.
After that they hurried to be healed. I will not gather together their assemblies out of blood. Since this is so,
from now on I do not bid them come together to bring me any offering of young animals,
but I want them to offer me my own body and blood. Nor will I remember their names with my lips.
Nor do I remember their old names, so as to call them sons of wrath or sons of the devil. Instead I call them my brothers
and sons of God. The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup. The Lord God the Father is a portion of my inheritance,
that is, of my Church, which possesses him together with me. And he is a portion of my cup.
He is with me in the Passion, from which I come, as if from a cup I have drunk, to the joy of the resurrection.
You are the one who will restore my inheritance to me. You restore the inheritance to me. Not that I lost it, but rather it is those in whom I am,
whom I want to redeem when they are lost. The lines have fallen to me in excellent places. The measuring-cords have fallen to me in splendid portions.
A splendid portion of the inheritance falls to me in you, since you are the portion of my inheritance. For my inheritance is excellent to me.
A splendid inheritance has truly become mine. The righteous are my inheritance and my co-heirs. THE RIGHTEOUS SHALL SHINE LIKE THE SUN IN MY KINGDOM.
I will bless the Lord, who has given me understanding. I give praise to God, who gave me the understanding to recognize such an inheritance.
and to love. Moreover, even until night my reins have rebuked me. Furthermore, my loins rebuked me
until the night. That is: my lower part, by which I am man, taught me to know the darkness of death,
which is not found in the understanding of the inheritance. I foresaw the Lord always in my sight. But while I was in the flesh,
I foresaw that I was to return to God when my journey was completed. For he is at my right hand, so that I may not be moved.
For he is at my right hand; that is, he is my help in this, so that I may be complete with him. Therefore my heart was delighted,
and my tongue rejoiced. Therefore my heart has delight and my tongue rejoices. My words are joyful.
Moreover, my flesh also shall rest in hope. Moreover, my flesh that can suffer rests in the hope of the resurrection.
I fall asleep to life, not to destruction. For you will not leave my soul in hell. For you raise me up
and do not leave me in hell. Nor will you let your holy one see corruption. Nor do you let me, your holy one, suffer corruption.
My body does not decay or rot as that of others does. You have made known to me the ways of life. To me, in my own, you made known
the ways of life. These are the ways of humility, for they fell in Adam through pride. You will fill me with joy with your countenance.
Me, in my own, you will fill with joy with your countenance. When they are allowed to look upon you,
then they have full joy. That is the blessedness and the reward of the saints. Delights are in your right hand to the end.
At your right hand, that is, in your glory, there is delight forever, and no weariness.
A PRAYER OF DAVID HIMSELF. What does that mean? This prayer is to be ascribed to David himself, to Christ himself,
so that we understand him to be praying in it, and his Church together with him. HEAR, O LORD, MY JUSTICE.
Hear, Lord, my right. Since almsgiving prays, as it says: HIDE ALMS IN THE BOSOM OF THE POOR,
AND IT PRAYS FOR YOU, so justice also prays, because almsgiving is justice. Attend to my supplication. Look upon my entreaty.
Receive my prayer with your ears. Not from deceitful lips. Not spoken
with faithless lips, that is, what does not come from the heart. Let my judgment come forth from your countenance.
Let my judgment come from your countenance. As clear as it is to you, since it does not deceive you,
so may it be to me. Let my eyes see equity. May my eyes recognize what is right, so that I do not mistake
or find wrong in place of right. You have proved my heart and visited it by night. You tested my heart
and visited it in the night. You visited it in hardships, to test my patience.
You have tried me by fire, and no iniquity was found in me. You tested me in the fire, and you found no wrong in me.
That is: you tested me closely in the Passion, out of which I came pure to the Resurrection. That my mouth may not speak.
You tested me so closely, and I was found so pure, that I do not speak it so.
You know it. You know what I suffered while I kept silent. The works of men. I suffered the works of men, what they wanted to do to me.
That I endured. Because of the words of your lips I have kept hard ways. Because of the words of your lips,
since you promised it of me through the prophets, I went hard ways. Hard ways of death and of the Passion
I went. Perfect my steps in your paths, so that my footprints are not moved. Make my goings perfect in your ways,
so that my tracks, that is, my feet, do not turn aside from them. Keep me fully in your commandments,
so that my apostles too may stand firm in them. I have cried out, for you have heard me, O God. After all this I cried boldly to you,
because you heard me on account of such merit. Incline your ear to me and hear my words. Bend your ear to me,
because my human nature cannot reach up to you; and so hear me. Make your mercies wonderful. Make your graces a wonder before
the Jews. Give health to the sick through my hand. You who save those who hope in you from those who resist your right hand.
You who preserve in eternal life those who trust in you, from those who stand against your right hand,
that is, your Son. Keep me as the apple of the eye. Guard me as the pupil of the eye. It alone recognizes in the body
what light and darkness are; so I alone recognize among men which are the righteous and which the sinners, and how I am to judge.
Under the shadow of your wings protect me from the face of the wicked who have afflicted me. Shield me under the shadow of your wings,
as a bird does its young. May your love and your mercy defend me against the wicked who torment me.
My enemies have surrounded my soul. My enemies, the Jews, beset me on every side. They have shut up their fat. And they shut in their fat.
That is: they filled themselves to the full with their wickedness by killing me. Their mouth has spoken pride. Their mouth spoke with arrogance:
'Hail, King of the Jews,' and other such things. Casting me out, they have now surrounded me. And having first cast out me and also my teaching,
they now surrounded me, that is, until I hung on the cross. They have set their eyes to turn down to the earth.
And they resolved to fix their eyes on the earth, as those do who are planning evil,
who then do not [?]. They took me as a lion ready for prey. They received me from Pilate when he said:
'Take him yourselves and crucify him,' like the lurking lion that goes out hunting. And like a lion's whelp dwelling in hidden places.
And like its young, which lies hidden and lies in wait. Arise, O Lord, get ahead of them and overthrow them. Arise, Lord,
get ahead of them with vengeance and trip them up. Deliver my soul from the wicked. Free me from the wicked by raising me up. Sword
…your [sword] from the enemies of your hand. Let your sword free me from the hands of the enemies, the sword with which you strike the devil.
Lord, divide them from the few, from the earth. Separate them, Lord, from the few elect; separate them from the land of the living. In their life.
That is, divide them: here in this life scatter them; command Titus and Vespasian to scatter them across all the world.
Their belly is filled with your hidden things, and they are sated with swine's flesh. Their belly was filled with your mysteries,
which they learned from the books of the prophets. Turning away from there, they then filled themselves with uncleanness.
That food was dearer to them. And they left their remains to their little ones. And they left to their children what they had left over. What is that?
Nothing but the curse and the wish: HIS BLOOD BE ON US AND ON OUR CHILDREN. But I shall appear in your sight with righteousness.
But I come before you with righteousness, because I did not wish to be revealed to unclean and dark hearts. I shall be satisfied when your glory is made manifest.
I have enough in those to whom I appeared, who were not defiled with swine's flesh, when your glory is revealed.
UNTO THE END, FOR THE SERVANT OF THE LORD, DAVID. THE WORDS OF THIS SONG ON THE DAY ON WHICH THE LORD DELIVERED HIM FROM THE HAND OF ALL HIS ENEMIES
AND FROM THE HAND OF SAUL, AND HE SAID. David gives thanks to the one who freed him, in the person of Christ and of the Church.
After that he tells the mystery of his incarnation. I WILL LOVE YOU, LORD, MY STRENGTH. Lord, my strength,
I love you. The Lord is my firm support, and my refuge, and my deliverer. The Lord is the one who makes me firm,
and in whom I have refuge, and who frees me. My God, my helper, and I will hope in him. He is my God,
and the one who helps me, and in him I hope. My protector, and the horn of my salvation, and my redeemer. He is my protector,
and the horn of my salvation (as their horns are a protection to animals), and my redeemer. Praising, I will call upon the Lord,
and I shall be safe from my enemies. With praise I cry out to him, and by doing so I am saved. The groans of death surrounded me.
The sighs of death have surrounded me. These are the stings of the flesh, or the multitude of the unbelievers.
And the torrents of iniquity troubled me. And the swift rivers of injustice have troubled me. That is to say,
those who rush swiftly in their injustice, they bring me grief. The sorrows of hell surrounded me. The pains of hell encompassed me.
These are the pagans, who are destined for hell, or envy, which leads to hell. Of this John says:
THERE IS A SIN UNTO DEATH; I DO NOT SAY THAT ANYONE SHOULD PRAY FOR IT. The snares of death came upon me beforehand. The snares of death caught me beforehand.
Original sin lay upon me before I was born. And in my distress I called upon the Lord, and I cried out to my God.
And in my distress I begged the Lord for help, and I cried out to my God. And he heard from his holy temple
my voice. And he heard my voice from my heart, his holy house.
And my cry in his sight entered into his ears. And my cry, which is in his sight and not in the sight of men,
went into his ear. I prayed for his coming; in that prayer he heard me. The earth was moved and trembled.
Through his coming it happened that the earth, that is, sinners, was shaken and trembled.
And the foundations of the mountains were troubled and were moved, because he was angry with them. And the confidence of the proud was confounded
and shaken, because he was angry at it, and he wanted their confidence to be in him,
not in worldly things. Smoke went up in his anger. In his anger the smoke of penitence rose up,
which brings forth tears. Fearing the wrath of God, they wept. And fire will blaze up from his face.
And fire burns from his countenance. Love (caritas) kindles those who know him.
Coals were kindled by him. Extinguished embers were kindled by him. Those who were dead in good works,
he brought them to life. He bowed the heavens and came down. He bowed the heavens and came down here,
because he made heavenly things known to earthly beings. And darkness was under his feet. And darkness was under his feet.
The devil was trodden down by him, as it says: "You will walk upon the asp and the basilisk, and you will trample the lion and the dragon."
And he ascended above the cherubim. And he climbed above the fullness of knowledge, that is, he showed himself to be incomprehensible. And he flew.
And he flew from earth to heaven. And he flew upon the wings of the winds. And he flew above the wings of the winds,
because even holy souls whose virtue has climbed high do not reach him, since he is incomprehensible to all creatures.
And he made darkness his hiding place. And he placed hidden hope in the hearts of believers, where he lies hidden. Or: God came hidden in man.
His tabernacle is round about him. His tent is around him, because where his own are, there he is in the midst of them.
Dark water in the clouds of the air. There is dark water in the clouds of the sky; that is the obscurity in the prophets
or in the teachings of the preachers. Before the brightness in his sight the clouds passed by. These same clouds went from Judea to the Gentiles,
shining in his eyes, though they are dark to us. Hail and coals of fire. Hail and glowing coals went within them,
because they rebuked the Gentiles and kindled them to the love of the faith. And the Lord thundered from heaven. And then the Lord thundered from heaven.
They are his heaven, because he sits in them; through them he made the gospel known to the Gentiles. And the Most High gave forth his voice.
And the Most High spoke out through them, because they told the secrets of God. He sent his arrows and scattered them. He sent preachers and scattered them.
He scattered those to whom he sent them in such a way that to some they were an odor of life unto life, and to others an odor of death unto death.
He multiplied lightnings and threw them into confusion. He performed many signs and terrified them. And the springs of water appeared.
Then the springs of the waters appeared. That is: then the truth of the preachers became known.
And the foundations of the world were revealed. And the prophets were revealed, upon whom this world, through believing,
was built for God. At your rebuke, O Lord. All this happened through your rebuke, Lord,
as when it says: "The kingdom of heaven will draw near." At the blast of the spirit of your wrath.
And through the wrathful rebuke of your spirit, as when it says: "Unless you do penance, you will all likewise perish."
He sent from on high and took me. Up to this point the prophecy of the Lord's incarnation shines out. Now the Church speaks about herself.
He sent his Son from heaven and took me, and wanted me to be his bride. And he drew me out of many waters.
Out of many waters he took me to himself. Out of many who were baptized he gathered me. He rescued me from my strongest
enemies. He freed me from very strong enemies, because I grew through the very persecution with which they meant to destroy me.
And from those who hated me, for they had grown strong against me. And he freed me from those who hate me,
because they were stronger than I was and I could not defend myself against them. They came upon me first on the day of my affliction.
They struck at me first, in the times of persecution, so that they could destroy me before I had fully grown.
And the Lord became my protector. And God became my shelter, because men were lying in wait for me [?]. And he brought me out into a broad place.
And he brought me into the breadth of charity and faith. He saved me. He kept me safe.
Why does she say of herself "saluum" (masculine) and not "saluam" (feminine)? Only because she is looking to the people from which she came into being.
Because he wanted me. For he wanted me before I wanted him. And the Lord will reward me according to my righteousness,
and he will reward me according to the purity of my works. And he will reward me according to my righteousness
and according to the purity of my works, even though he wanted me before I wanted him. For I have kept the ways of the Lord
and have not acted wickedly against my God. For I kept God's ways, and I did no evil by drawing away from him.
Once he had drawn me to himself, I never drew back again. For all his judgments are before my eyes,
and I have not pushed his righteous decrees away from me. For I look on all his judgments, on the good and on the wicked,
and I have not driven his laws away from me, as people do when they grow tired of righteousness.
And I will be spotless with him, and I will keep myself from my iniquity. And from now on I will remain [?] unstained with him,
and keep myself from all wrongdoing. And the Lord will reward me according to my righteousness
and according to the innocence of my hands in the sight of his eyes. And for this he will reward me according to my righteousness.
and according to the sinlessness of my hands, which is before him, not before men. He rewards me not only for the breadth of faith
that works through love, but also for perseverance. WITH THE HOLY YOU WILL BE HOLY. With the holy one you are holy,
because you make him holy. And with the innocent man you will be innocent. And with the harmless man you are harmless, because you harm no one;
each person's own wrongdoing overtakes him. And with the chosen you will be chosen. And with the chosen one you will be chosen.
He chooses you whom you have chosen. And with the perverse you will be perverse. And with the perverse one you will be accused of perversity,
that is, of injustice, because sinners say: THE WAY OF THE LORD IS NOT FAIR. For you will save the humble people.
For you save the humble people. It displeases the perverse that you save those who humbly confess their sins.
And you will humble the eyes of the proud. And you humble the eyes of the proud, who are pleased with their own righteousness
and do not know God's righteousness. As it says: NOT KNOWING THE RIGHTEOUSNESS OF GOD, THEY SEEK TO ESTABLISH THEIR OWN. For you light my lamp, O Lord.
For you kindle my lamp, Lord. We have no light from ourselves.
My God, light up my darkness. We are dark because of sins, but you light up the darkness. For in you I shall be rescued from temptation.
For in you, not in myself, I am delivered from the devil's temptation. And in my God I shall pass over the wall.
And in my God, not in myself, I step over the wall of sins,
which bars heaven to us, just as the turning sword bars paradise to sinners. My God, his way is undefiled.
He who is my God, his way is undefiled; he does not walk the way of sinners. The words of the Lord are tested by fire.
His words are tested in fire. There is no dross in them. As he said before: THE WORDS OF THE LORD
ARE PURE WORDS. He is the protector of all who hope in him. He is the shield of all who trust in him, not in themselves.
For who is God besides the Lord? Or who is God besides our God? For he is God. Who is God except him? Or who is God
except our God? THE GODS OF THE PAGANS are DEMONS. God who girds me with strength. It is God who girds me
with virtue, so that my works and my goings may never be led astray by unrestrained desires.
And he has made my way spotless. And he made my way unspotted. Who has made my feet like those of harts.
Who has made my feet swift as a hart's, to leap over the devil's snares.
And he set me upon high places. And he set me on the height. In heaven he set my hope.
Who trains my hands for battle. Who teaches my hands in war, to overcome my spiritual enemies.
And you have made my arms like a bow of bronze. And you made my arms as strong as a bronze bow.
...to carry out all good works without growing weary. And you have given me the protection of your salvation.
And you gave me the shield of your salvation, which came to me from you. And your right hand has taken me up. And your grace received me.
And your discipline has corrected me unto the end. And your discipline directed me to the end, to which I am to go.
It directed me toward you. And your discipline itself will teach me. And it will also teach me to arrive there fully.
You have enlarged my steps under me. You made my steps wide under me. You made my limbs follow the breadth of the mind.
That breadth is charity. And my footsteps have not been weakened. And therefore my feet are not worn out. I will pursue my enemies and over-
take them, and I will not turn back until they fail. I will break them, and they will not be able to stand; they will fall under my feet. I hunt my enemies
and catch them, and I do not turn back until they are laid low. I break them, and they cannot stand.
They fall under my feet. Taken all together, this means: I fight down carnal pleasures and get the upper hand over them.
And that is the voice of the faithful. But the voice of Christ, which also sounds in it, is understood thus: Those who are against me,
them I hunt and catch, and I break them so that they follow me, and I subdue them with my punishments, my laws. Blessed are those
to whom this happens. And you have girded me with strength for battle. And with the virtue of temperance you girded me to resist.
Or it is said in the person of Christ: WITH THE FORTITUDE OF PATIENCE you made me endure the persecution of the sinful.
You have tripped up under me those who rose up against me. Those who wished to attack me you threw down so that they lay beneath me. And you have made my enemies turn their backs to me.
And you made my enemies be a back to me, that is, behind my back, because they follow me, as PAUL does,
and many others of the Jews. And you have destroyed those who hate me. But those who persisted in their wickedness and hated me,
them you destroyed. They cried out, and there was no one to save them. They cried out in distress; then there was no one to save them.
Who should have, when God would not? To the Lord, and he did not hear them. They cried out to God; he did not hear them.
And I will grind them like dust before the face of the wind. And I grind them to powder like the dust that is carried before the wind.
Like the mud of the streets I will wipe them out. Like the mud on the street I destroy them. Those who walk the broad way of fornication's lusts, they
are the mud of the street that God destroys. You will deliver me from the contradictions of the people.
You deliver me from the gainsaying of the people, who said: IF WE LET HIM GO ALIVE,
THE WORLD WILL GO AFTER HIM. You will set me as head of the nations. You set me as head of the gentiles, as head of the Church.
A people whom I did not know has served me. The people of the gentiles, before whose eyes I did not come in bodily form, as I did with the Jews,
that people served me. At the hearing of the ear it obeyed me. Only by hearing with their ears did they obey me, without seeing with their eyes.
"Strange children have lied to me." Strange children, changelings, the Jews, broke their faith with me. "Strange children have grown old."
Strange children have grown old, whom I wished to renew with new grace. They cling to the Old Testament; they do not care for the New.
"And they have limped." So they limp, because they walk on one foot, that of the Old Testament. "From their paths."
That has happened to them because of their own ways, because of their own inventions, such as those about unwashed hands and about cups.
"The Lord lives, and blessed be my God, and let the God of my salvation be exalted." But for me the Lord, my Father, lives,
and blessed be my God, and so let the God of my salvation be exalted. Let him be exalted in me.
"God, who gives me vengeance and subdues peoples under me." You are God; you avenge me and put the peoples of the gentiles under me.
"My deliverer from my angry enemies." My redeemer from angry enemies, who were shouting, "Crucify, crucify him!"
"From those rising up against me you will exalt me." From those who came at me in the Passion you exalt me in the Resurrection. "From the unjust man you will rescue me." From the un-
-just man who persecutes me you set me free. "Therefore I will confess to you among the peoples, Lord, and I will sing a psalm to you among the nations."
Therefore, Lord, I confess to you among the Christian peoples, and I sing you a psalm among the gentiles. That is: I will bring it about that they confess to you
and sing you a psalm. "Magnifying the salvations of his king." God makes great the salvation of his king, his Son,
which he gives to the gentiles. "And showing mercy to his anointed, David." And God shows grace to his consecrated one, David.
"And to his seed forever." And to his child, the Saviour, the Lord, forever into eternity.
UNTO THE END, A PSALM OF DAVID. This psalm is directed to Christ himself, because it proclaims his first coming. "The heavens declare the glory of God."
The heavens tell of God's glory. The prophets and apostles, in whom God dwells, proclaim the kingdom of God to all people.
"And the works of his hands proclaim the firmament." And his handiworks proclaim firmness. These same heavens are his handiworks.
They proclaim to us: "For his mercy has been confirmed upon us." "Day pours forth the word to day."
Day belches out its word to the day: Christ gives his teaching to the apostles. "And night shows knowledge to night." And night tells night
what it knows: Judas betrays Christ to the Jews. "There are no speeches or words in which (that is, through which) their voices are not heard."
There is no tongue or language where their preaching goes unheard. "Their sound has gone out into all the earth,
and their words to the ends of the world." Their sound went out into all lands, and their words came to the end of the world.
"In the sun he has set his tabernacle." Out in the sun he set up his tent. That is, he showed himself
in the world and made his Church visible. "And he, like a bridegroom coming out of his bridal chamber."
And he himself came out like a bridegroom out of his bride's chamber: out of his mother's womb.
and acts accordingly. And when he receives good things from his judgments, then those very judgments are his reward.
In that reward he rests. "Who understands sins?" But who knows the misdeeds, or who recognizes them all?
Who can guard against them, because they are hidden and because there are so many, even though he loves your judgments? "From my hidden
sins cleanse me, Lord." Cleanse me, Lord, of the hidden ones. Sins are hidden; cleanse me of them. They are hidden,
and they cause hiddenness, for they blind a person so that he does not see other things, nor does he see them.
As is shown in these words: "FATHER, FORGIVE THEM, FOR THEY KNOW NOT WHAT THEY DO." "And from those of others spare your servant." And spare your servant
from the guilt of others. Take my hidden sins from me, and do not let the sins of others come upon me, so that, on top of my own sins,
I am not led astray by others. "If they have not ruled over me, then I shall be spotless." If hidden sins and the sins of others do not rule me,
then I am unstained. "And I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin." And so I shall be cleansed of the greatest guilt. That is pride.
From it come all sins. It cast the angel out of heaven and made him a devil instead of an angel. It made man mortal instead of immortal.
"And the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart shall be such as to please in your sight always." And from this my words shall become such,
and my thoughts, that they please your eyes. The proud soul wants to please the eyes of men;
the humble soul wants to please God. "Lord, my helper and my redeemer." You are my helper in good things and my redeemer from evil.
UNTO THE END. A PSALM OF DAVID. The end is CHRIST. The prophet speaks to him, and together with him to his Church, wishing for the things to come
which he foresaw. "MAY THE LORD HEAR YOU IN THE DAY OF TRIBULATION." May God hear you, CHRIST, in the day of your distress,
when you said: "FATHER, GLORIFY YOUR SON." "May the name of the God of Jacob protect you." He who protected Jacob from his brother
Esau, may his name protect you; that is, may he protect your Church from its persecutors. "May he send you help from the holy place."
May he send you comfort for it from the Holy Spirit. "And from Zion may he defend you." And from the height of his deity,
which watches over all things, may he protect you in your Church. "May he be mindful of all your sacrifice." May he make us mindful of all the injuries
which you suffered for our sake. "And may your burnt offering be made fat." And your crucifixion, where you were offered wholly to God,
may he turn it into the joy of the resurrection. "May he grant you according to your heart." May he grant you, according to your will,
to redeem us, not as the Jews wished, that your name be destroyed. "And may he confirm all your counsel."
And may he make firm all that you have resolved to do: TO LAY DOWN YOUR LIFE FOR YOUR FRIENDS, TO TAKE THE CHURCH AS YOUR BRIDE.
"We will rejoice in your salvation." When this is done, we will rejoice in your salvation, in that you healed us by your death.
"And in the name of our God we shall be magnified." And in the name of our God we shall be magnified. "May the Lord fulfil all your petitions."
May God fulfil all your prayers. Such as this one is: "Father, those whom you have given me, keep them in your name." And again:
"I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from evil." Now I have known that the Lord has saved his anointed (Christ).
Now I recognize that God makes his anointed one rise from the dead. Through prophecy I know that it is to come.
He will hear him from his holy heaven. He will hear him in his prayer, not only as he cries out from the earth, but also from heaven,
where he sits at the right hand of the Father, interceding for us. In mighty powers is the salvation of his right hand. The salvation of his right hand
comes in powers. Those powers exist when corruption is gone, and mortality, and the capacity to suffer. But the salvation that belongs to the left hand,
that comes and brings pride to those who love it. As he now immediately says of them: "Some in chariots and some in horses,
but we shall be magnified in the name of the Lord our God." These, that is, worldly people, now exult upon their chariots and upon their horses.
But we shall then be magnified in the name of the Lord our God, because we put our trust in him,
not in ourselves. "They are bound and have fallen, but we have risen and are set upright." They were bound with worldly desires,
and therefore they plunged into the pit of death; but we have risen from sins and are raised upright. "Lord, save the king,
and hear us on the day when we call upon you." Lord, keep the king: make Christ rise from the dead, and hear us when we cry to you.
UNTO THE END, A PSALM OF DAVID. The title is well known: this psalm is sung of Christ. LORD, IN YOUR STRENGTH THE KING SHALL REJOICE.
Lord Father, in your strength the king rejoices, your son. He says: "ALL THINGS OF THE FATHER ARE MINE,
AND ALL MINE ARE THE FATHER'S." "And in your salvation he shall exult greatly." And he rejoices greatly in your salvation,
which you send to mankind through him. "The desire of his soul you have granted him." You gave him what he longed for. What that was,
he himself told, when he said: "WITH DESIRE I HAVE DESIRED TO EAT THIS PASSOVER WITH YOU." "And you have not defrauded him of the will of his lips." And you have not taken from him
the will of his lips. For what he said has come to pass according to his will: "MY PEACE I GIVE TO YOU,
PEACE I LEAVE WITH YOU." "For you have gone before him with blessings of sweetness." For you went before him with the blessing of sweetness.
You gave him to drink of your Godhead; therefore he could not drink the bitterness of the sins
which all after Adam drank. "You have set on his head a crown of precious stone." You set a crown on his head,
made of precious stone. His disciples encircled him at the beginning of his preaching.
They were the precious stones. "He asked life of you, and you gave it to him." He asked for resurrection with the words that he spoke to you:
"FATHER, GLORIFY YOUR SON." That you gave him. "Length of days for ever and for ever and ever."
In his Church you gave him length of these days, so that it lasts as long as the world stands, and after that, forever.
Great is his glory in your salvation. Great is his glory in your Savior, Christ. Glory and great beauty you will lay upon him.
On him himself you bestow still more glory and more adornment, when you set him at your right hand.
For you will make him a blessing for ever and ever; you will gladden him with joy in your countenance.
For you make him into an everlasting blessing. The blessing is this: that you gladden him with joy in his faithful,
with your countenance. For the king hopes in the Lord. For he, being king, trusts in God and submits himself to him
according to his humanity. Through the mercy of the Most High he will not be moved. Through the grace of the Highest he stands unshaken.
In him in whom he trusts he has steadfastness. His grace is not withdrawn from him [?]. Let your hand be found by all your en-
emies. Let your power, Christ, be shown at the judgment to all your enemies, who did not recognize you in your humility.
Let your right hand find all who hate you. And then let your might come upon all who hate you. You will make them like a fiery oven in the time of your countenance.
Just as the oven lies in the fire when bread is baked in it, so you will lay them in the fire in the time of your manifestation.
The Lord in his wrath will throw them into confusion, and fire will devour them. God will then afflict them in his anger,
and thereupon the eternal fire will swallow them up. You will destroy their fruit from the earth. You take their fruit away from the earth.
You do not let them bear fruit in the land of the living. And their seed from the children of men. And you separate their offspring from the children of men,
from the blessed, who are to possess the eternal inheritance. For they turned evils against you.
