This happens to them because they turned onto you the harms that they themselves expected if they believed in you.
They expected death from the Romans; that they turned against you. They devised plans that they could not carry out.
They thought of things they could not bring about: that they would kill you in place of them all, yet they themselves were killed after all.
For you will make them turn their backs. For you will drive them back and turn yourself away from them. Among your remnants you will prepare their face.
Among your remnants you keep their face. Among the outcasts you hold back their shamelessness for your passion.
Only then will their disgrace bring them before you. Be exalted, O Lord, in your strength. Be exalted, Lord, in your strength,
since they so mocked your weakness. We will sing and make music of your mighty deeds. So we will proclaim your mighty deeds, singing and making music.
For the morning reception, a psalm of David. Here the prophet sings of the Lord's passion, concerning the reception of the dawn, that is, concerning the resurrection,
which the passion leads toward, and in which he took on our nature a second time, now made incorruptible. GOD, MY GOD,
LOOK UPON ME. WHY HAVE YOU FORSAKEN ME? So Christ cries out on the cross to his Father: God, my God,
look upon me. Why did you forsake me? As if he were saying: If you had wanted to stand before me to protect me, I would not suffer such things.
This lament is according to the man [i.e., spoken in his human nature]. What is this, except that he says in Hebrew: Eli, Eli, lama
sabachthani. Far from my salvation are the words of my sins. Far from my salvation be the sinful words.
In the words of those who are mine there are sins, not in my own. In them I am sinful. My God, I will cry out by day, and you will not hear.
My God, I cry to you by day; this you do not hear. However much I am the day, you do not hear me concerning the cup of death.
You do not release me; I do not drink it. And by night, and not unto folly. Nor do you hear me by night in those who are mine,
that is, in their troubles; and that is for their salvation, not for folly. Paul asks you foolishly about the thorn of the flesh;
him you do not hear, for the sake of his salvation. But you dwell in the holy one, the praise of Israel. But you dwell in your holy Son, the praise of Israel,
even though you do not hear his prayer. In you our fathers hoped; they hoped, and you delivered them. Our forefathers hoped in you,
and you delivered them, as you did the children of Israel out of Egypt, and Daniel out of the lions' den, and
the three youths out of the fiery furnace. To you they cried and were saved; in you they hoped and were not confounded. They cried to you,
and by that they were saved; in you they hoped, and therefore they were not put to shame. But I am a worm and not a man.
On the one hand I am a worm, because I am mortal and was born without intercourse; and on the other hand I am not a man, but the Word of God the Father
which was in the beginning. A reproach of men and an outcast of the people. I have become a reproach to men and the castoff of the people.
All who saw me scorned me; they spoke with their lips and shook the head. When they saw me hanging on the cross, they all scorned me.
With their lips they spoke; they shook their heads: HE SAVED OTHERS; HIMSELF HE CANNOT SAVE.
IF HE IS THE SON OF GOD, LET HIM COME DOWN FROM THE CROSS. He hoped in the Lord; let him rescue him. He trusted in God;
let him come and deliver him. Let him save him, since he wants him. Let him save him, for he wants him. These are the words of the Gospel:
He trusted in the Lord; let him deliver him now, if he wants him. For you are the one who drew me out of the womb. Thus they did to me,
because you drew me out of a woman's womb, that is, because I have now become man. My hope from my mother's breasts.
From then on, from my mother's breasts, you were my hope; but before the ages you are my Father.
Upon you I was cast from the womb. Hoping in you I was cast forth, from the time I came out of the womb. I had my comfort for this in you.
From my mother's womb you are my God. From Mary's womb you are my God; from yourself you are my Father. Do not depart from me, for trouble is
near, and there is none to help. Do not forsake me now, for distress comes upon me, and no one else helps me.
Many calves surrounded me; fat bulls besieged me. Many calves have surrounded me; fat bulls have hemmed me in.
The multitude of the people are the many calves; the chief men are the fat bulls. They opened their mouth against me like a ravening and roaring lion. They gaped at me.
like the lion when it seizes its prey and roars out of greed. Their roaring was: "Crucify, crucify him!"
Their gaping was against him when Pilate said: "Take him yourselves and crucify him." I am poured out like water,
and all my bones are scattered. I am poured out like water, and all my bones are scattered. I have sent out my apostles,
who are my strong ones; with them I wash the world clean of its uncleanness. My heart has become like wax melting in the midst of my belly.
My heart has become like melting wax in my belly. My wisdom, which was hidden before, has become gentle in the Church
and to the weak. My strength is dried up like a potsherd. My strength has hardened like an earthen pot. The pot is hardened by the fire;
by the distress of my passion my name has become firm. And my tongue cleaves to my jaws. And my tongue clings to my throat.
My preachers hold fast to me with their teaching, so that they receive wisdom from me.
And you have brought me down into the dust of death. And you have brought me to the dust of death, as my enemies think. They want to know
whether you will let me rot after death. For many dogs have surrounded me. For many dogs surrounded me.
They are called dogs because they hate what is new. They hate the New Testament and the new commandments, just as dogs hate new and unknown people.
The council of the wicked has besieged me. The assembly of the evil-minded besieged me. They dug my hands and my feet. They dug, that is,
they pierced my hands and my feet. They numbered all my bones. They counted all my bones,
so hard was I stretched out. But they themselves considered and looked upon me. They themselves stood and watched and examined me:
the flesh with their eyes, not the Word with their hearts. They recognized me as a man, not as God. They parted my garments among them.
They divided my garments into pieces among themselves. And upon my vesture they cast lots. For my tunic, which I wore next to my body,
which was woven from the top downward, they cast lots to decide who should have it whole.
The garments of Christ are his sacraments, that is, holy mysteries, such as baptism, the solemn celebration of the Mass, and the monks' rule of life.
These could be divided among heretics. But there was one garment, which signifies charity, that no one divided,
for charity is undivided. It is what makes one out of many. Except for those who were heretics, and who are today Richard [and] Poppo,
each of whom says that he is indeed Saint Benedict, and has therefore changed the rule, and has made the Lord's one tunic into two frocks, and so on.
For it is no wonder now that the devil promised himself he would be like God, since his members also have similar ideas. Whoever has it [charity] is saved.
But you, O Lord, do not remove your help far from me. But do not put your help far from me. Make me rise again on the third day. Look to my defense. Look
to my protection. See how you protect me. Deliver my soul from the sword. Free me from the weapon.
from the soldier's lance. And my only one from the hand of the dog. And [deliver] my Church from the power of the dog, of whom [it was said] above,
from the power of him who always rages against her. Save me from the lion's mouth. Keep me, and take me from the devil's mouth.
And my lowliness from the horns of the unicorns. And release my humility from the horns of the unicorns,
that is, of the proud, who seize for themselves a separate lordship and reject fellowship with others.
I will declare your name to my brothers. I promise to make your name known to my brothers, that is, to your faithful ones
who live in love. In the midst of the Church I will praise you. Before all the Church I praise you.
You who fear the Lord, praise him. You who fear God, praise him, not yourselves. All the seed of Jacob, glorify him.
All Jacob's descendants, that is, all the faithful, glorify him. Let all the seed of Israel fear him.
Let everyone who wishes to see God fear him. For he has not spurned or despised the prayer of the poor. For he never rejected
or despised the prayer of the poor man who does not exalt himself through worldly wealth. Nor has he turned his face away from me. Nor did he turn away his countenance
from me, his Son. When I cried to him, he heard me. He always heard me when I cried to him.
I asked him to give life to many through my death. With you is my praise. With you, Father, is my praise;
you are my praise. In the great Church I will pay my vows before those who fear him. In my wide Church,
which is throughout the whole world, I will fulfil my promises, that is, I will give out the sacraments of my body
and blood before those who fear him. The poor shall eat and be satisfied. The poor, who do not love the world, eat
and are satisfied by it, because in it they enjoy heavenly food, which gives them eternal fullness. And those who seek the Lord shall praise him.
And those who long for God praise him. These are the poor. Their hearts shall live for ever and ever. Their hearts live forever
because they have that food. All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord. God had slipped away from the Gentiles;
he had passed out of their memory. But then they remember him again and turn to him from all the ends of the earth.
And all the families of the nations shall worship in his sight. And they worship before him, that is, they worship him from the depths of their hearts, in all the places
where the Gentiles dwell. For the kingdom is the Lord's, and he shall rule over the nations. For the kingdom is his; he rules over them all.
All the rich of the earth have eaten and worshipped. All the worldly rich also ate his sacraments, but not until they were satisfied,
because they have a different hunger; and yet they still worship him. All who go down into the earth shall fall down in his sight.
All who turn their minds toward the earth shall fall before him. He alone sees how they fall. And my soul shall live for him.
But my soul lives for him, because it wants him alone. And my seed shall serve him. And my people, whom I redeemed,
serves him. A generation to come shall be announced to the Lord. The generation to come, the generation of the New Testament, will be made known to him.
His angels will announce it to him. And the heavens shall announce his justice. And the evangelists announce his justice.
To whom? To the people that shall be born, whom the Lord made. To the people that is yet to come into being, whom God created, whom he, through baptism,
commanded to become Christian.
A PSALM OF DAVID. THE LORD RULES ME AND I SHALL LACK NOTHING. The Lord himself rules me, says the Church of Christ,
and I lack nothing. In a place of pasture, there he has set me. In the place where there is pasture he has set me.
He has given me spiritual food in the law and the prophets. Beside the water of refreshment he has brought me up. He has reared me beside the water of refreshment.
That is baptism, by which the soul is refreshed. He has converted my soul. He has turned my soul from evil to good.
He has led me along the paths of justice for his name's sake. He led me along the paths of righteousness for the sake of his name,
not for the sake of my merits. For even if I walk in the midst of the shadow of death. Even if I walk here in the midst of the shadow of death,
that is, among heretics and schismatics, who are images of death. I will fear no evils, for you are with me. Even then I do not fear harm,
that they might corrupt me, for you are with me, for you are in my heart. Your rod and your staff, they have comforted me.
Your rod and your staff, that is, your scourging and your chastisement, they have comforted me,
not grieved me, for I have been made better by them. You have prepared a table in my sight against those who trouble me. After the chastisements
you prepare a table for me, so that I might be fed with stronger food than milk, against those who torment me.
You brought me from imperfection to perfection; you gave me that strength against them. You have anointed my head with oil.
You anointed my mind with spiritual joy. And your cup that inebriates, how glorious it is!
And how very glorious your drink is, which intoxicates people and makes them forget their former desires.
The cup is the grace of the Holy Spirit. And your mercy shall follow me all the days of my life.
And your grace follows me all the days of my life; it watches over me as long as I live. That I may dwell in the house of the Lord for length of days.
So that afterwards I may dwell in the heavenly Jerusalem, in length of days, which in the plural number signifies one eternal day.
A PSALM OF DAVID, FOR THE FIRST DAY OF THE WEEK. What does "first day of the week" mean? Nothing other than the first weekday, which is called the Lord's day and the day of the resurrection.
This psalm looks toward that day. THE EARTH IS THE LORD'S, AND ITS FULLNESS. The earth is the Lord's, and its fullness.
The world and all who dwell in it. His is the globe of the earth and all who dwell on it. The whole world will be made subject to him,
and his Church spreads out over everything. He himself founded it upon the seas. He established it upon the waters of the seas.
these worldly storms do not throw her down. "And upon the rivers he prepared it." That is why he built it upon the rivers.
Where do the rivers flow, if not into the sea? And where do the greedy set their minds, if not on the world?
And his Church overcomes them, because she desires nothing else but immortality. "Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord?"
Who has climbed up onto God's mountain? Who has raised himself even into the height of God's righteousness?
"Or who shall stand in his holy place?" Or who stands firm there in his holy place? "The innocent in hands and clean of heart."
That is the one who is sinless in his works and pure in his thoughts. "Who has not received his soul in vain."
He who does not value his soul in vanity but in eternity. He who knows it to be immortal, not transient, and desires that it
become rich in the unchanging good. "Nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour." Nor has he sworn in bad faith to his neighbour,
but as truthfully as he wishes to gain the true good. "He shall receive blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God his Saviour."
Such a one receives blessing from God and mercy from his Saviour. "This is the generation of them that seek God,
of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob." That is the generation of those who seek God, of those who seek God's face,
who is the God of Jacob, to whom he gave the precedence of the elder, although he was the later in birth.
"Lift up your gates, O princes." Take away your gates, you lords of the land. You who are mighty in the world, take away your vices,
which lead you to death. "And be lifted up, you everlasting gates." And lift yourselves up, you everlasting gates: baptism
and the renunciation of the world. "And the King of glory shall come in." And when this is done, the King of glory goes in to you.
"Who is this King of glory?" Now the prophet asks: Who is this glorious king? And he answers it:
"The Lord, strong and mighty." The Lord, the strong one and the mighty one, whom you thought weak, O Jew, when you saw him on the cross.
"The Lord mighty in battle." The Lord, mighty in battle. As was shown when he only said: "Whom do you seek?"
and at that word his enemies at once fell down. "Lift up the gates of your prince." Take away, you people of the devil, the gates of your prince,
which he set up against God so that they would not let him in; take them away. "And be lifted up, you everlasting gates."
And be raised up, you gates of eternal righteousness that lead to God. "And the King of glory shall come in."
And then the King of glory goes in there to you. "Who is this King of glory?" Who is this
glorious king, at whom even you may marvel, prince of the world? "The Lord of hosts, he is the King of glory." The Lord of powers
is the King of glory. His powers make him glorious. All might gives way before him.
UNTO THE END, A PSALM FOR DAVID HIMSELF. The voice of each one of the faithful. UNTO YOU, O LORD, HAVE I LIFTED UP MY SOUL.
To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul, from earthly desires to spiritual ones. Deus meus in te confido non erubescam (My God, in you I trust; let me not be put to shame).
My God, in you I trust, and I am not put to shame. For when I trusted in myself, I came to shame,
and because of the guilt of wanting to become God, even a little worm can kill me. Therefore I must trust in you,
and not be put to shame. Neque irrideant me inimici mei (Nor let my enemies mock me). Nor let my enemies mock me.
Etenim universi qui sustinent te non confundentur (For all who wait for you shall not be confounded). All who wait for you will not be put to shame.
Confundantur iniqui facientes vana (Let the wicked who do vain things be confounded). May the wicked, who do useless things, be put to shame. Vias tuas domine demonstra mihi (Show me your ways, Lord)
et semitas tuas doce me (and teach me your paths). Show me your ways, the straight ones, and teach me to walk your narrow paths,
not the broad way that leads to hell. Dirige me in veritate tua et doce me (Direct me in your truth and teach me). Direct me in your truth and teach me,
for of myself I know nothing but mendacium (falsehood). Quoniam tu es deus salvator meus, et te sustinui tota die (For you are God my saviour, and I have waited for you all the day). For you are God,
my saviour, and I wait for you through all the time of this world, until you lead me, who was driven out of paradise, back again.
Reminiscere miserationum tuarum domine (Remember your compassions, Lord). Remember your compassions, for people think that they have been forgotten. Et misericordiarum tu-
-arum quae a saeculo sunt (And your mercies, which are from of old). And remember your mercies, which have always existed since the beginning of the world, and which you have always shown.
Delicta iuventutis meae et ignorantiae meae ne memineris (The sins of my youth and of my ignorance do not remember). Do not keep in mind the misdeeds of my youth and of my ignorance.
Secundum misericordiam tuam memento mei tu (According to your mercy remember me). Remember me according to your grace, which befits you, not according to the wrath that I have deserved.
Propter bonitatem tuam domine (For the sake of your goodness, Lord). For the sake of your goodness, Lord, for I have no good merits. Dulcis et rectus dominus (Sweet and upright is the Lord).
Sweet and just is our Lord. Sweet, because he goes before people with grace; but just,

because he destroys those who do not thank him for it. Propter hoc legem statuit delinquentibus in via (Therefore he has set a law for those who go astray on the way). Because he is dulcis (sweet) and rectus (upright),
for this reason he established the law, so that it might direct them onto the way. Diriget mites in iudicio (He will direct the meek in judgment). He directs the meek in his judgment.
There he gives them such order that they will no longer be thrown into confusion. Docebit mansuetos vias suas (He will teach the gentle his ways).
He teaches the tame, those who are also willing to bear him, his ways. Universae viae domini misericordia et veritas (All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth).
All his ways, which he teaches them, are grace and truth. Of these there are two.
In the one he came to you; in the other he is still to come. Just as grace then made him placabilem (placable) for forgiving,
that is, gracious, so truth will yet make him incorruptum for judging, that is, unbribed. Requirentibus testamentum eius (To those who seek his covenant)
et testimonia eius (and his testimonies). He teaches his ways and opens them to those who seek his covenant and his testimonies.
This is what the mites (meek) and mansueti (gentle) do, who search the New Testament and the words of the prophets. In Rome it was the custom that the for- [?]
…they had everything that they bequeathed to their descendants written on tablets, and because their witnesses were written on them,
for that reason the document was called a testament. By the same comparison, the law that God bequeathed to the people of old is called the Old Testament,
and the one that he bequeathed to us is called the New Testament. "For your name's sake, O Lord, you will pardon my sin, for it is great."
For the sake of your name, because you are called Saviour, you forgive my sins, Lord. There are many of them.
They grow every day, so there are many of them. "Who is the man that fears the Lord?" Who among men is it that fears God?
"He has set a law for him in the way that he has chosen." For him he has set a law on the way, that is, on the path of holiness
that he chose out of fear of him. "His soul shall dwell among good things." His soul dwells in joy.
"And his seed," that is, his work, "shall inherit the land." And his work inherits the risen body, free from corruption.
"The Lord is a firm support to those who fear him." The Lord is a source of strength to those who fear him. The fear of men produces faintheartedness,
which is called diffidence (diffidentia). But the fear of God strengthens the mind. "And his covenant, so that it may be made known to them." And he makes sure
that his law, which he bequeathed to them, is revealed to them. "My eyes are always toward the Lord, for he will pluck my feet out of the snare."
My eyes always look to God, for he frees my feet from the snare. The one I look to
is the one who frees me. "Look upon me and have mercy on me, for I am alone and poor." Look upon me, that is, upon your Christian people, and have mercy on me,
for I am your only one, because I keep the right faith among many heresies, and your poor one, because I have no worldly finery.
"The troubles of my heart have multiplied." The torments of my heart are many, because wickedness abounds and love grows cold.
"Rescue me from my distresses." Since I suffer these hardships, free me from them. "See my humility and my toil."
Look upon my humility and see how little I boast. And look upon my toil, which weighs on me as I put up with others,
the undisciplined people who are with me. "And forgive all my sins." And, made favourable by this sacrifice, forgive me all my sins.
"Look upon my enemies, for they have multiplied." Look upon my enemies and do not let them be lost, for there are many of them,
and the more of them there are, the less comfort I can have. "And they have hated me with an unjust hatred." And see that they have hated me unjustly,
for I loved them, and therefore hear me. "Guard my soul and rescue me." Protect my soul, so that it does not become like them,
and free me from their entanglement, which is called perplexity (perplexitas). I am caught in it too, because I go about among them.
"Let me not be put to shame, for I have called upon you." Do not let me be put to shame, for I prayed to you for help and trusted in you,
not in myself. "The innocent and the upright have clung to me." The sinless and upright cling to me, unlike the wicked,
who also go about among me. Rather, the hearts of the innocent and upright are with me. "For I have waited for you." For I did not go away [?].
to the wicked. And I waited for you until your winnowing (ventilatio) should come, which winnows the chaff away.
Libera deus israhel ex omnibus tribulationibus suis. (Deliver, O God, Israel out of all his troubles.) God, free the people whom you will let see you in the future (in futuro)
from all the troubles which they suffer, not only outwardly but also inwardly.
IPSI DAVID. (For David himself.) That is, this psalm suits every perfect Christian.

IUDICA ME DOMINE. (Judge me, O Lord.) Separate me, Lord, from the wicked. Quoniam ego in innocentia mea ambulavi, et in domino sperans non infirmabor. (For I have walked in my innocence, and hoping in the Lord I shall not grow weak.)
For I lived among them without sin, and trusting in you I do not become sick at heart because of their wickedness. Whoever trusts in you
does not lose heart when he sees scandals, nor does he give up his own goodness because of their wickedness.
Proba me domine, et tempta me. (Prove me, O Lord, and try me.) Examine me and test me, not in a way that brings danger but in a way that shows grace,
and in such a way that you make me better and cleanse me of my sins. It is because of dangerous testing that we say:
NE NOS INDUCAS IN TEMPTATIONEM. (Lead us not into temptation.) This testing is the opposite of that kind, the kind that makes a man righteous, as it did Abraham
when he was tempted and proved. Ure renes meos et cor meum. (Burn my reins and my heart.) Burn my loins and my heart. That is,
burn my desires and my thoughts, so that they are not unrighteous. Burn them with the fire of the Holy Spirit (spiritus sancti).
Quoniam misericordia tua ante oculos meos est. (For your mercy is before my eyes.) Therefore do as I ask you, because your grace is before my eyes,
and I am not unmindful of it, nor ungrateful (ingratus). Et complacui in veritate tua. (And I have been pleasing in your truth.) And so I am pleasing to you in your truth,
and I do not care how I may displease men, among whom there is no truth, as long as I please you. Non sedi in concilio vanitatis. (I have not sat in the council of vanity.)
I please you in this: that I did not sit in the crowd of vanity, like those who sit in the theatre (in theatro), or those who give wicked counsel.

Et cum gerentibus iniqua non introibo. (And I will not go in with those who do wicked things.) Nor do I go in with those who act unjustly. I will not readily attach myself to them. Odivi congregationem malignorum. (I have hated the assembly of the wicked.)
I have always hated the crowd of the evil-minded; therefore I separated myself from them. Et cum
impiis non sedebo. (And with the ungodly I will not sit.) And so I do not sit with the godless, such as heretics (heretici) are, since I did not even sit with the vain (vanis).
Lavabo inter innocentes manus meas. (I will wash my hands among the innocent.) I wash my hands with the sinless. That is, I hasten to have pure works,
such as the innocent (innocentes) have. Et circumdabo altare tuum domine. (And I will go round your altar, O Lord.) And when that is done, I encompass your altar.
My heart, which is your altar, on which I offer you good will and pure prayer, is what I then encompass,
and I guard it so that it keeps all its purity. Ut audiam vocem laudis tuae. (That I may hear the voice of your praise.) That I may hear,
I mean, that I may perceive and understand the voice of your praise. What is this voice? Only that my heart confesses
that it has its goodness from you and its wickedness from itself. Et enarrem universa mirabilia tua. (And that I may tell of all your wonders.)
And I tell all your wonders to your praise, not to mine. "Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house." I have always loved, Lord,
the adornment of your house. The Church is God's house. In it there are good and bad people, but the good
are its adornment. "And the place where your glory dwells." And I loved the place where your glory dwells.
Whoever glorifies you through his goodness, and not himself, is "the place where God's glory dwells." "Do not destroy my soul with the ungodly,
nor my life with men of blood." Since it is so that I did not cling to the wicked,
and I sought your glory and not mine, do not now destroy me with the wicked and with murderers.
"In whose hands are iniquities." In whose hands is injustice. How is it in their hands? "Their right hand is filled with gifts."
Their right hand is full of bribes. They do wrong for gold and silver and for praise. For this reason he calls them "men of
blood." "But I have walked in my innocence; redeem me and have mercy on me. My foot has stood on level ground." But I hastened to be without sin;
therefore redeem me and have mercy on me. My foot stood firm in righteousness. "In the assemblies I will bless you, Lord."
Throughout all Christendom I praise you, not only with the tongue but more with deeds.
A PSALM OF DAVID BEFORE HE WAS ANOINTED. David sang this before he was consecrated. "THE LORD IS MY LIGHT
AND MY SALVATION; WHOM SHALL I FEAR?" The Lord is the one who enlightens me to the knowledge of himself, and he is my salvation.
Whom do I fear, who could take either of these from me? "The Lord is the protector of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?" He is the one who protects me.
Of whom should I fear harm? "While the wicked draw near against me to eat my flesh." He protects me when the harmful want to attack me
to devour me. Those who want to vent their fury on me, he does not let them vent it. "My enemies who afflict me,
they themselves have been weakened and have fallen." My enemies who cause me distress are sick and have fallen. "Though armies encamp against me,
my heart shall not fear." Even if whole armies are set against me, my heart does not fear them. "Though war rise up against me,
in this I will hope." Even if war rises against me, I still trust in him. In those very dangers
he protects me. "One thing I have asked of the Lord; this I will seek." I asked only one thing of God;
that is what I seek. There are others who ask for many things; I ask for one. What is that? "That I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life."
That I may dwell in his house all the days of my life. Where all days are one day,
there I long for blessedness. Where there is day without night, where there is life without death, where there is joy without sorrow,
there I long to come and to remain there from then on. "That I may behold the delight of the Lord." That I may see him himself
and may enjoy him, and may have that delight without ever growing weary of it; that is why I long to go there. "That I may be protected from his holy temple."
And I have protection from his holy house. The reason I have his protection is that I am his house.
For he hid me in his tabernacle in the day of evils. For while I was here he hid me in his Church in perilous days,
from temptations and persecutors. Since he protected me here, he will do so all the more there. He protected me in the hidden place of his tabernacle.
He protected me in the hidden place of his tent. That is Christ: he dwells hidden in the hearts of believers.
In him we have protection. He exalted me upon a rock. He raised me up on the rock. That too is he, as it says:
"But the rock was Christ." And now he has lifted up my head above my enemies. And now he has set my head, Christ himself, on high
above all my enemies. That is why they can persecute me: I have not yet come there,
where my head has come. But when I have followed the head there, I will have no more worry
that anyone might harm me there. I went round and offered in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation (cubiculationis), that is, of rejoicing.
I have gone round, that is, I have learned that his Church, which is his tent, is everywhere.
In that tent I offer him the sacrifice of joy. I am glad that I know it is everywhere. I will sing and say a psalm to the Lord.
When I also come there, where he has come, and see his loveliness, then I will be secure, then I will sing
the song of gladness. Hear, O Lord, my voice with which I have cried to you. Hear, Lord, the voice
with which I cried to you for the one thing that I desire. Have mercy on me and hear me. Have mercy on me
and hear me. You know well what it is that my heart desires. My heart has said to you:
I have sought your face; your face, O Lord, I will seek. My heart said to you: I want your face;
your face, Lord, is what I want. Everything I want is there. Hear me in this;
grant me this. Do not turn your face away from me; do not turn aside in anger from your servant. Do not turn your face away from me;
do not turn it away in anger from your servant. That is: do not show me such anger that you turn it away from me.
Or it means: in judgment do not turn it away from me. Turn it away from my sins, not from me. Be my helper.
Be my helper. Even though I have free will, I can never do good without your help.
Do not forsake me, and do not despise me, O God my saviour. Do not forsake me, do not despise me, God my saviour.
For my father and my mother have forsaken me. For my father and my mother, who raised me,
or Adam and Eve, have forsaken me. But the Lord has taken me up. What does that matter? God has taken me to himself.
Set a law for me, O Lord, in your way, and guide me on the right path because of my enemies. Since that is so, now set a law for me in your way.
that there be no further mention of it. Blessed be the Lord, for he has heard the voice of my supplication. Praised be God
that he has heard my prayer, and he does it all according to my request. The Lord is my helper and my protector.
He is my helper in the distress of the passion, and my protector in the immortality of the resurrection.
And in him my heart hoped, and I was helped. And in him I trusted, and from that I have been helped. And it has flourished again,
my flesh, that is, my flesh has risen. And from that my flesh has risen. And of my own will I will confess to him.
And as it pleases me, so I confess to him. I make a willing confession to him in those in whom I am, who are my faithful.
The Lord is the strength of his people. The Lord, my Father, is the strength of his people, which comes to believe in him after my resurrection.
And he is the protector of the salvation of his anointed. And he is the protector of the saved ones of his consecrated one. They are the saved ones
whose salvation is Christ. Save your people, O Lord, and bless your inheritance. Preserve, Lord, your people,
and bless your inheritance, of which you said to me: ASK OF ME, AND I WILL GIVE YOU THE NATIONS AS YOUR INHERITANCE.
And rule them and exalt them forever. Rule them here, and lift them from here into eternal life.
A PSALM OF DAVID, OF THE COMPLETION OF THE TABERNACLE. This is the song of the completed dwelling, that is, of the Church,
in which one must fight here against the devil. The voice of the prophet to the faithful in the Church. BRING TO THE LORD, O SONS OF GOD,
BRING TO THE LORD THE SONS OF RAMS. Children of God, bring to the Lord; bring him the children of the rams, that is, of the apostles.
You are their children; bring yourselves to him. They are the leaders of the flock, that is, they guide the people;
for that reason they are called rams. Bring to the Lord glory and honor. Bring him glory and honor by doing good works.
Bring to the Lord glory for his name. Bring glory to his name. Spread his name everywhere. Worship the Lord in his holy court.
Pray in his palace; that is, your hearts. The voice of the Lord is upon the waters. His voice resounds over
the waters, that is, over the people to whom he proclaims his law. The God of majesty has thundered. The God of mighty powers thundered.
The mighty Christ commands terribly, out of the cloud of his body, that we do penance. The Lord is upon many waters.
He sits upon many waters. Many are his seats, for he dwells in them when he converts them by preaching.
The voice of the Lord is in power. His voice is in strength, for it is capable of much and makes mighty those who listen to it.
The voice of the Lord is in magnificence. His voice is in great working; it turns them to great works.
The voice of the Lord breaking the cedars. His voice is the voice of the one who breaks the cedars, that is, the proud. And the Lord will break the cedars of Lebanon.
On Mount Lebanon grow the tallest cedars; these he breaks. They are those who have climbed highest in the world.
Those he humbles. "And he shall break them in pieces like a calf of Lebanon." And he humbles them after the pattern of himself. He was a sacrifice to the Father;
they become sacrifices to him. He was the calf of Lebanon, because he was a chosen calf, such as are those
that are pastured on Lebanon. "And the beloved like the son of the unicorns." And the Father's beloved becomes man and dies
like one of the Jews. "The voice of the Lord dividing the flame of fire." His voice is the voice of the one who divides the fire,
that is, the raging ones, who were very hot against him; for half of them he took to himself, and half he cast away.
"The voice of the Lord shaking the wilderness." His voice is the voice of the one who shakes the desert. That is, the hearts that were without God
it makes them be startled. "And the Lord shall shake the desert of Kadesh." And he shakes the wilderness of Kadesh. Just as in Kadesh he
made water flow out of the rock, so he makes the scriptures that came from him flow into the desert of the Gentiles.
He himself is the rock, as it says: "But the rock was Christ." "The voice of the Lord preparing the harts," that is, those swift to understand.
His voice is the voice of the one who prepares for himself the harts that are to enjoy the pasture. "And he will reveal the thickets" [written 'conden sa'], that is, the woods.
To the harts he opens up the woods: he lets them into the secrets of the scriptures. "And in his temple all shall speak his glory."
And in his church they all tell his glory, each according to his measure. "The Lord dwells in the flood."
The Lord has his seat in the flood. The Lord was in the ark together with his own when it rested on the flood;
so he is still seated together with his own in the church, which drifts in the midst of the waves of the world,
so that he may now preserve it, as he then preserved the ark, by which the church was signified.
"And the Lord shall sit as king forever." And after that he sits reigning forever. "The Lord will give strength to his people."
The Lord gives his people firmness to endure the waves and the storms of this world,
for he has promised them no peace here. "The Lord will bless his people in peace." After the end of this world
he gives his blessing to his people in peace; that peace they have in him himself. This psalm is adorned with various playful references
which are called allusions, such as the one to the rams, and the one to the harts, and to the unicorns, and to the calf of Lebanon. Allusions are
those that playfully touch on a thing and attribute to it what suits its deed or its nature
or its name. As in Virgil, where he said: "And Achates struck out fire." Fittingly
he said that the one who bore the stone's name struck the stone. Such allusions are in the Life of Saint Gall, which is composed in verse,
where the offices are set down. Note the seven voices of the Holy Spirit in the psalm.
A PSALM OF A CANTICLE FOR THE DEDICATION OF THE HOUSE OF DAVID. This is a song of joy for the consecration of David's house.
Our David is Christ. His house is his body. That house was built in the incarnation and renewed in the resurrection.
This renewal is called dedication. Therefore dedication means that one begins to use a new house.
I will exalt you, Lord, for you have upheld me, and you have not made my enemies rejoice over me. I glorify you, Lord, says the Son to the Father.
I make you famous in all the world, because you have received me and set me at your right hand, and you did not let my enemies have their joy over me,
since I died of my own will; instead you made me rise from hell and from death against their will.
Lord my God, I cried to you, and you healed me. Lord my God, I cried to you when I prayed on the mount before death,
and for that reason you healed me in the resurrection, that is, at the dedication. Lord, you have drawn my soul out of hell.
You led my soul out of hell when I led other souls out of there. You have saved me from those who go down into the pit.
You saved me from those who sink themselves into the lake, that is, from the sinners who persecuted me,
who sank themselves into the depth of sins. Sing to the Lord, you his saints. Sing and give thanks to the Lord, you his saints,
for you have risen together with him, and you shall go after him to where he has gone. And give praise to the memory
of his holiness. And acknowledge the grace of his holy remembrance: that he did not forget you, even though you had forgotten him.
For wrath is in his indignation. For anger is in his wrath. Death came to you once from his wrath, when the first sin took place.
And life is in his will. And eternal life came to you only from his will, without your merits.
Weeping shall linger until evening. In the evening weeping lingers. After midday, when the light of wisdom faded, then it began,
and it lasted from then on. And joy in the morning. But at dawn joy comes. It comes in the resurrection on the last day.
At the same time of day at which Christ's resurrection took place, the last resurrection will take place. The second was signified by the first.
But I said in my abundance: I shall never be moved. When I was in paradise in my abundance,
and had God, and lacked nothing, then I said: From now on I shall not be changed; from now on I shall not become mortal.
I thought true what the serpent says: 'You shall not die the death.' Lord, in your will you have given strength to my beauty.
Lord, now I know that I had no good from myself, and that you, of your own free will, strengthened my beauty.
And this shows it: You turned your face away from me, and I became troubled. That is, you turned away from me,
and at once I was afflicted, and from immortal I became mortal. To you, Lord, I will cry, and to my God I will make my plea.
Because this has happened to me, I cry to you, so that now you may hear me in my humility and receive me,
whom you then cast away for my pride. Or it is better understood of Christ, as follows: I said in my abundance, which [was] in the fullness of the Godhead
...is. I shall never be moved, but I am steadfast. You, Father, willingly gave strength to my beauty,
so that I would be precious above the sons of men. You turned your face away from me, and it was not [?] to me before the passion.
Therefore I became sorrowful even to death. That is why I cry out to God with this prayer: What profit is there in my blood
while I go down into corruption? What use, then, is the shedding of my blood, if I am to come to decay like other men?
How shall I give others the comfort of rising again, if I myself do not rise at once and show them this,
as I promised? Shall the dust praise you, or declare your truth? Does the dust praise you,
or proclaim your truth? If I am turned into dust, where then are those whom I send out
to preach the gospel to every creature? The Lord heard and had mercy on me, and the Lord became my helper. The Lord heard that prayer
and helped me. Hear of that help. You have turned my mourning into joy for me. You turned my weeping into gladness.
You turned my death into the joy of the resurrection. You have cut my sackcloth, that is, my mortality,
and surrounded me with gladness. You tore apart my haircloth and clothed me with joy. You took mortal flesh from me
and gave me immortal flesh. So that my glory may sing to you. So that my divine glory may now sing to you,
not my human lowliness. And I shall not be pierced. And so that I may never again be pierced, as I was on the cross,
and so that my own people may not be pierced by the awareness of their sins, for my passion is to them the forgiveness of sins.
O Lord my God, I will praise you forever. Lord God, I praise you always. In the world to come I will praise you
forever in my members.
FOR DAVID HIMSELF, AN ECSTASY. To David himself this is now sung in ecstasy of mind, that is, in the going-out of the mind.
This going-out of the mind comes either from revelation or from fear. Here in this psalm 'ecstasy' may be understood in both senses,
for in it the whole Christ speaks, that is, head and members, showing fear in his members. IN YOU, O LORD, HAVE I HOPED.
LET ME NEVER BE PUT TO SHAME. In you, Lord, I put my hope; let me not be put to shame forever, as those will be who are to hear:
GO INTO THE ETERNAL FIRE. In your righteousness deliver me. In your righteousness set me free, not in mine. Incline your ear to me.
Bend your ear to me. Come down here to us human beings. Make haste to rescue me. Quickly set me free.
Separate me soon from sinners, before the end of the world comes. Or else make me rise again quickly.
Be to me a protecting God and a house of refuge, to save me. Be my shelter, and a house where I may have refuge,
so that you may keep me in the house of an immortal body. For you are my strength and my refuge. For you are my strength.
…to suffer persecution. And you are my refuge, because, departing from the world, I return to you. And for your name's sake you will be my leader.
And you guide me for the sake of your name, so that I may make it known far and wide. And you will nourish me. And you raise me up,
until, gathering my saints one by one, I grow into the great body of the Church. You will lead me out of this snare which they have hidden for me.
You bring me out of the snares which they secretly laid for me. For you are my protector. Into your hands I will com-
-mend my spirit. Because you are my protection, to you I commit my soul, until I soon and quickly take it back to myself again.
You have redeemed me, O Lord God of truth. When that comes to pass, then you will have redeemed me, God of truth.
Then you will have done as you promised, that you would redeem my people with my blood.
You have hated those who regard vanities to no purpose. Those who pursue vanity in vain, you hate them. Vanity is opposed to truth,
and because you are the God of truth, therefore you hate it. Those who seek riches and honour, they seek vanity.
But I have hoped in the Lord. But I put my hope in God, who is not vanity but truth. I will exult and rejoice in your mercy,
for you have looked upon my humility; you have saved my soul from its distresses. I will leap for joy and rejoice in your grace,
because you took notice of my humility and freed me from distress, that is, from the assault of sin.
Every person must overcome that distress through humility. Of it Paul said: Wretched man that I am!
Who will deliver me from the body of this death? And you have not shut me up in the hands of the enemy. Nor did you shut me up in the devil's hands,
in which those are shut up who do not defend themselves against the distress of desire and sin. You have set my feet in a spacious place.
You made me stand in a wide place; you made righteousness easy for me, which before was difficult for me. Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am afflicted.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am in distress. How can someone be in a spacious place who is in tribulation?
Only in that Christ speaks in the person of the members, some of whom are in peace, some in distress, and some feel for the others, as
it says: If one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. Of certain members he now says: Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am afflicted.
And what follows after that: My eye is troubled with wrath. My eye has become troubled in anger.
Where does that anger come from, if not from the sins of others? Who is there who has resolved to do well
and is not grieved that others who are of the same profession do evil? And my soul and my belly.
And my soul has become troubled, and my belly. My anger struggles within my heart,
since I may not yet avenge the wrong, and rebuke makes worse those whom it ought to improve. For my life has failed in sorrow,
and my years in groanings. For my life has wasted away in grief, and my years in sighing.
Of this suffering it says elsewhere: "The zeal of your house has eaten me up." And again: "Weariness has taken hold of me
because of the sinners who forsake your law." And also: "I saw the senseless and I wasted away." My strength is weakened in poverty.
My strength has become weak in poverty, because I have nothing good of myself. What I have comes from your riches.
And my bones are troubled. And my bones are troubled. That means the strong ones in the church, whom persecution did not terrify:
they are troubled in mind by the wrongdoing of their brothers. I have become a reproach above all my enemies.
I have become a reproach even more than all my enemies. The sons of the church live worse in my sacraments
than the pagans do, who never came to them. And exceedingly to my neighbours, (that is,) I have become a reproach. And to those near
to me I have become greatly a reproach. Those who would gladly believe in me, and are therefore near,
are turned away by the evil life of false Christians. And a fear to my acquaintances. And I have become a fear to my acquaintances. For their acquaintances
are afraid that they are all like that. Those who saw me fled outside, away from me. Those who learned my scriptures
renounced me and fled from me out of the church. Being out there, they invented many heresies against her.
I am given over to forgetfulness like one dead from the heart. To them I have become forgotten like a dead man, out of the heart; that is, like one entirely thrust out
and even cast out of the heart. I have become like a lost vessel. Like a lost vessel that has been broken and thrown away
out of neglect, so worthless have I become to my enemies. For I have heard the reproach of many dwelling round about.
For I have heard the scolding of many who sit around me, who all say: "Look how Christians behave!"
They do not say: "Look how bad Christians behave." They sit around the church because they do not want to go into it.
They sit round about because they love the wheel of time, not the stability of eternity. While they came together,
they took counsel against me to take my soul. When they gathered, they plotted against me in that assembly. What was their plan?
To take my soul; that is, to make me worse and to draw [?] me away out of the church,
as if I could be better saved with them. But I have hoped in you, O Lord. But I put my hope in you, Lord.
I trusted in you more than in them. I said: You are my God; my lots are in your hands, that is, my inheritance. "My
God you are," I said, "my lot is in your hands." Since inheritance was formerly divided by lot,
here "lot" should be understood as "inheritance." Deliver me from the hand of my enemies and from those who persecute me. Free me from the hands of my enemies
and from persecutors. Make your face shine upon your servant, that is, make me see that you deign to look upon me.
Show your face over your servant. Let me become aware that you watch over me.
Therefore you heard the voice of my prayer when I cried to you. Because of that humility, you heard me when I called out to you.
Love the Lord, all his saints. Love God, all his saints. Love him, you who do not love the world. For the Lord will require truth.
For the Lord loves truth. In his own people he loves what he himself is. And he will repay those who act with abundant pride.
And he repays those who act with full arrogance. Who are they? Only those who will not give up their sins,
and go along with them to the end. This is said of all sins, for it says: "Pride is the beginning of all sin."
Act manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, all you who hope in the Lord. Conduct yourselves manfully and have bold hearts, all you who hope in God.
Do not grow impatient for the time when God will avenge you on the sinners. Be patient for a while; he will do it when the time comes.
A PSALM OF UNDERSTANDING, OF DAVID. Here we are reminded to understand what we must do penance for.
For a man does not do penance until he recognizes how he has behaved. Few are those who are able to recognize it.
That is why it says: "WHO UNDERSTANDS SINS?" BLESSED ARE THEY WHOSE INIQUITIES ARE FORGIVEN, AND WHOSE SINS ARE COVERED.
Blessed are those whose wrongdoings are forgiven and whose sins are covered. This is the voice of a penitent.
He longs to become like those he speaks of in this way. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. Bles-
-sed is the man whom God does not blame for his sins, because he has forgiven them. Nor is there guile in his spirit.
Nor is there deceit in his mind, such as thinking that he is good by his own power, or, if he is sinful,
failing to acknowledge it. Because I kept silent, my bones grew old while I cried out all day long. Because I kept silent, that is,
because I would not confess my sins, but instead spent the whole day excusing myself of them,
therefore my bones grew old, that is, my strength grew weak. If I had been willing to confess,
it would have been renewed. For day and night your hand was heavy upon me. For because of that guilt
your hand, laid upon me, weighed on me day and night. I was turned to misery, that is, I was made wretched,
while the thorn is driven in. I became wretched as the thorn pierced me. When you brought me into distress,
I began to acknowledge my guilt, and my conscience pricked me. I made my offense known to you,
and I did not hide my injustices. Then I made my misdeed known to you, and no longer hid my wrongdoing from you.
I said: I will confess my injustices against myself to the Lord; and you forgave the impiety of my sin. I only said in my heart,
"I will confess my wrongdoing to God," and at once you forgave me the wickedness of my sins. Before the words came out,
you had already rewarded my intention with forgiveness. For this impiety every holy one will pray to you at the proper time.
For this wickedness every holy one will pray to you in the fitting time. That is, then, when "the fullness of time" comes,
and God sends his Son, "made of a woman, made under the law." "Yet in the flood of many waters they shall not come near to him." But in the wave of ma-
ny waters, swimming, they do not come near to him. There is one water that pours over them and sanctifies them "in the fitting time";
that is the coming teaching from the Holy Spirit. The many teachings and many sects of heretics or of philosophers do not bring them to God,
but they separate them from him. "You are my refuge from the distress that has surrounded me." You are the one with whom I have refuge from the distress
that has seized me. That is mortality and the corruption over which Paul also lamented,
when he said: "Even we ourselves, having the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan within ourselves,
waiting for the adoption, the redemption of our body." "My exultation, deliver me from those who surround me." You, God, my joy,
release me from the distresses that have surrounded me. How is he in joy who asks to be released?
Only in that his hope gladdens him, as it says: "For we are saved by hope," even though human misery troubles him.
Therefore the response now comes: "I will give you understanding and instruct you in this way in which you shall walk." I give you understanding
that will urge you to penitence, and I teach you what you should do on this way on which you walk.
What is the way, if not this present life? "I will fix my eyes upon you." I fix my eyes over you.
I let the light of my understanding [shine] down upon you from above, untiringly. "Do not become like the horse and the mule, which have no understanding."
This is spoken to sinners. Do not be like the horse and the mule, which are without understanding.
Their own lord or a stranger rides the horse and leads the mule, for they do not know whom they ought to serve. Like them is
the one who serves the devil instead of God and is subject to him. "With bit and bridle bind fast their jaws,
who do not come near to you." With bit and bridle constrain the jaws of those who do not turn toward you. The horselike should have a bridle,
but the balking and stubbornly standing ones should have a camus [a curved bit or muzzle]. Camus is named from crookedness, for camur in Greek
means "curved" in Latin. Those need it who kick against God and do not want to have him as their assessor [companion and guide].
"Many are the scourges of the sinner." Not only a camus but scourges too the untamed one must have, so that he may be subdued.
"But mercy shall surround those who hope in the Lord." But those who trust in God, his grace surrounds.
He guards them on all sides so that no harm can befall them. "Be glad in the Lord and rejoice, you righteous."
Be glad in God, you righteous, and leap for joy in him, not in yourselves. "And glory, all you who are upright of heart."
And glory in him, all you who are upright in heart. Those are upright in their heart who want nothing other than what he wants.
A psalm of David himself. Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous. Rejoice in God, you righteous.
Let your joy be in him, not in this world. Praise befits the upright. Praise befits the upright.
These are the ones who have directed their will according to God's will. Those who will otherwise than God wills,
they are crooked and unworthy of praise. Give praise to the Lord on the cithara. Confess to God on the cithara,
which signifies the active life, because it has its sound-box below. Sing to him on the psaltery of ten strings. On the ten-stringed
psaltery sing to him; this signifies the contemplative life, because it has its sound-box above. In these two lies all religion.
And by this let us know that the ten strings signify the ten words of the Law. They are divided so that three look to the love of God
and seven to the love of neighbor. Sing to him a new song. Sing to him a new song of joy, such as the one the angels sang at his incarnation:
Glory to God in the highest. Sing well to him with jubilation. Sing well to him, jubilating. That is to say:
know that it cannot be shown in words how joyful you ought to be. For that is what jubilating is:
when one shows joy with melodies, without words. For the word of the Lord is right. You should do this because his word is right.
In what way, if not that it makes things right? By his word people are made righteous.
And all his works are done in faithfulness. And all his works are in faithfulness. His faithfulness shines in this,
that he [?] us when he tests our faith. As Paul says: God is faithful, who does not let you be tempted
beyond what you are able to bear. He loves mercy and judgment. He loves mercy and judgment,
that is, grace and judgment. Here he shows grace; for hereafter he reserves judgment.
The earth is full of the mercy of the Lord. The earth is full of his grace, because the Gospel, faith and baptism have come into all the earth.
By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm. But what about the heavens? They were made firm by his word.
That is true of the heavens themselves; it is also true of the apostles, who are therefore called heavens, because by
their teaching the earth was rained upon and made fruitful. That the earth is full of his grace comes from this:
his heavens were made firm and emboldened by God's word, that is, by Christ, the Son of God.
He made them heavens. And all their power is by the spirit of his mouth. And their strength comes from his Spirit.
By receiving him they became heavens. Gathering the waters of the sea as in a bottle. Gathering the waters of the sea
as in a leather bag. That is to say, shutting up evil will in the bellies of wicked people,
evil will that they would gladly show if they could. That is what happened when Christian rulers came and malice began to hide itself.
Laying up the depths in storehouses. He holds the depths of the waters in his treasuries. That is the multitude of the wicked,
whom he nevertheless secretly keeps in reserve for himself, so that he may make his own people better through their persecution. Or else it is to be understood in another way.
He gathers Christians in his Church, which he calls a "wineskin", and he hides deep meanings in his Scriptures.
Let all the earth fear the Lord. For this reason let every earth fear God, that is, every sinful person,
because he does not lack those who avenge him, since he has put the bitter water as if in a wineskin.
And let all who inhabit the earth be moved by him. Let all who dwell on the earth be stirred by him.
If they are stirred by him to harm anyone, may they also be calmed by him.
Why "by him"? For he spoke and they were made; he commanded and they were created. Because all things were made when he spoke,
and were created when he commanded. The Lord scatters the counsels of the nations. God scatters the counsel of the peoples, which they
often took against Christians, saying: LET US TAKE THEM FROM THE EARTH AND BLOT OUT THEIR NAME. But he rejects the thoughts of the peoples
and rejects the counsels of princes. He condemns the thoughts of the people when they are evil, and the counsels of the princes.
But the counsel of the Lord abides forever, the thoughts of his heart for ever and ever. But his counsel endures forever,
his thoughts for eternity. Which thoughts? That he preserves those who are faithful to him. Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord,
the people whom he has chosen as his inheritance. Blessed is the nation whose God is our Lord; blessed is the people that he chose as an inheritance for himself.
Not he is blessed who seeks riches, honors, power and pleasure for the sake of blessedness; but he is blessed
who has blessedness itself, that is, God. The Lord looked forth from heaven. The Lord looked from afar, down here from heaven,
for "prospicere" means to look at something placed far off. That happened when he sent his Son here. He saw all the sons of men.
He saw all the children of men. Those who are predestined by him to the inheritance, those he saw, because he took heed of them
and showed them grace. From his prepared dwelling he looked upon all who inhabit the earth. From his dwelling, which he prepared,
he looked upon all who dwell on the earth. Through angels and apostles and preachers he saw them and visited them. These are his dwelling
and his heavens. He who fashioned their hearts one by one. He who created their hearts individually, because he gave to each one something particular
that another needs. Just as among the limbs, too, each one always has its own particular gift,
and they all need one another. He who understands all their works. He who perceives all that they do. He sees what people do not see.
People see the giving hand; they do not know whether it gives for the sake of righteousness or for the sake of reputation.
But God knows that. A king is not saved by great strength, and a giant will not be saved by the greatness of his might.
The king is not saved by his great strength, nor the giant by the abundance of his might.
A preeminent man is 'rex' (king), because he rules his own body. But one who fights virtuously against all devils is 'gigas' (giant).
The cause of both of them rests with God, not with themselves. 'A horse is a deceptive thing for safety; and in the abundance of its strength it shall not be saved.'
The horse is false for a man's safety; nor is he saved by its being strong enough. 'Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him.'
Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him. He saves them, not the horse, nor their own strength.
'Hoping in his mercy.' Trusting in his grace, not in themselves. 'That he may deliver their souls from death.'
For this reason his eyes are upon them: that he may deliver their soul from death in the other world. 'And may feed them in famine.'
And that he may nourish them in hunger here in the world. These are those 'who hunger for righteousness.' To them he gives spiritual nourishment.
'Our soul waits for the Lord.' Our soul waits for him, for when he will come with his reward, which he promised us.
'For he is our helper and protector.' We should wait for him, because he is our helper and our protector.
'For in him our heart shall rejoice, and in his holy name we shall hope.' For in him our heart rejoices, not in the world,
and in his holy name we hope; therefore we wait for him. 'Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us,
as we have hoped in you.' Your grace, Lord, come upon us, as we have always hoped in you.
A PSALM OF DAVID, WHEN HE CHANGED HIS COUNTENANCE BEFORE ABIMELECH, AND HE DISMISSED HIM, AND HE WENT AWAY.
David sang this psalm when he changed his countenance before Abimelech, whom the books call Achish,
as if he were mad; and he let him go in that state, and he departed from there.
Our David, Christ, changed his countenance before Abimelech, that is, before the Jewish people,
when he was priest, and yet did not teach the sacrificing of victims as Aaron did, but bread and wine, as Melchizedek did.
Of the holy bread and of the holy wine he said: 'He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood
has eternal life.' Because of this he seemed mad to some, who therefore left him
and would not be with him. He also left them and went from them to others; he went from the Jews to the Gentiles.
But why is the name changed from Achish to Abimelech? Only because Abimelech by his name signifies the Jews,
not Achish. Abimelech means 'kingdom of my father', namely David. That was the Jews; they were the kingdom of their father David.
But Achish is interpreted 'How is it?' That points precisely at those who wondered at this,
how they should eat his flesh and drink his blood. 'I WILL BLESS THE LORD AT ALL TIMES.'
I praise God at all times. Whether good or bad befalls me, I thank him. "My soul shall be praised in the Lord."
My soul shall be praised in God. It is through him that I am praiseworthy and glorious, not through myself. "Let
the meek hear and be glad." Let the meek hear this and rejoice. They hear that they ought to be like this,
and they should be glad of it, because those who are not meek are not glad of it. "Magnify the Lord with me." Magnify God together with me.
Do not leave me to do it alone; be with me in it. "And let us exalt his name together," that is, "with one another,"
or "as one." And let us exalt his name together. Let us be undivided in such a saving work.
"I sought the Lord, and he heard me." I sought God, and that is why he heard me. I longed for him himself,
not for gold and riches; that is why he heard me. "And he delivered me from all my troubles." And because of that
he set me free from all my troubles. "Come to him and be enlightened." Go to him with penance, and when you have done so,
you will be enlightened, that is, you will come to understand the truth. "And your faces shall not be ashamed."
And then your faces will not be ashamed. They are rightly ashamed that you did not go to him;
now go to him again, and do not be ashamed. "This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him, and delivered him from all his troubles."
This poor man, I mean the one who recognized that he was without God and so drew near to him,
cried out, and God heard him and set him free from all his distress. He did this by taking him away
from this world, for it could not happen here. "The angel of the Lord shall encamp round about those who fear him."
The Son of God, who is called the Angel of Great Counsel, does this all around those who fear him. What is it that he does to them,
to those who fear him? He surrounds them with his hidden grace. He leaves none of them out, for he encircles them with it.
"Taste and see that the Lord is sweet." Taste, and see for yourselves that our Lord is sweet.
Taste his sweetness in his body and in his blood: not how sweet he is to the mouth, but how sweet he is to the soul,
which receives from it eternal life, as he promised. Some who heard the promise said: "How can this man give us
his flesh to eat?" These were signified by Achish, whose name means in Latin "How is it?" To them it is now said: taste,
and test what you do not know. If they do not do this, he changes his countenance before them
and abandons them. "Blessed is the man who hopes in him." Blessed is the one who hopes in him. Unblessed is the one who hopes in others.
"Fear the Lord, all his saints, for those who fear him lack nothing." Fear God, all his saints,
for those who fear him lack nothing. Nothing is lacking to them, because they have the one who makes them all rich.
The rich have been in want and have gone hungry. The rich became needy and hungry, because it never seems enough to them,
what they have. But those who seek the Lord shall not lack any good thing. Those who seek God lack no good thing.
What good do they lack, who have God, who gives all good? Come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.
Come, children, and listen to me here. I teach you the fear of God, without which no one can be saved,
and which makes you free, not slaves. Who is the man who wants life and loves to see good days?
Who is it, then, who desires life, and also desires to see good days and good times? Keep your tongue from evil,
and do not let your lips speak deceit. If you desire them, then do not let your tongue turn to evil; restrain it,
and let your lips not speak deceitfully. Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it. Avoid harm,
and do good; seek peace and go after it. Seek it in the other world: there it is, and there is life
and good days; here you need not think of it. The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous. The Lord's eyes are over the righteous. He watches over them
and keeps his eyes fixed on them. And his ears are open to their prayers. And his ears are turned to their entreaty. Their prayer succeeds,
because he is present to them. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil, to destroy their memory from the earth. But on the other hand,
his face is set against the evildoers, so that he may wipe out their memory and remove it from the land of the living.
The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them, and he delivered them from all their tribulations. The righteous cried out to him, and he heard them,
and freed them from all their tribulations. He did this by taking them away from here; here it could not have happened.
The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart, and he will save the humble in spirit. The Lord is near to those who have a crushed heart,
and he saves those who are lowly in their mind. Whoever wants him to raise him up to himself, let him humble his heart.
Many are the tribulations of the righteous, and the Lord will deliver them from all of these. The righteous have many tribulations; God frees them from all of them.
Because they have compassion for their brothers, in addition to the temptations and sufferings that they themselves endure, their tribulations are many.
But they need not grieve over them, because he takes them all away from them. The Lord keeps all their bones; not one of them shall be broken.
The Lord guards all their bones; not one of them will be broken. Their patience and their meekness and their other
virtues are so strengthened by him that none of them will be taken from them. But according to the letter, their bones can be broken,
as happened to the thief on the cross, who was then justified by Christ. The death of sinners is the worst. The death of sinners is the worst of deaths,
because they go into eternal hell. And those who hate the righteous will sin. And those who hate the righteous do wrong.
No one was as righteous as Christ; those who hated him sinned most grievously of all.
in whom they did not recognize the redemption of the world. May he cleanse them and draw them to me. "But my soul shall exult in the Lord"
"and shall delight in his salvation." But my soul rejoices in God, and has delight in its Savior.
There is all that I ask for, because in him I have all that I need. "All my bones shall say: Lord, who is like you?"
All my bones say: Who, Lord, is like you? Those who are strong in my body say it to me, because they know
that neither the sun nor the stars are it, nor angels, nor archangels, nor any creature. "Rescuing the needy from the hand of those stronger than he."
Snatching the helpless out of the hands of those stronger than he. "The needy and the poor from those who plunder him."
The needy and the wretched from those who seize him. In this it is clear that no one is like you,
because you do what no one else can do. You set free the wretched man who has no virtue
from the hands of the devils. "Unjust witnesses rising up asked me things I did not know." Unjust witnesses stood up during my Passion
and asked me about things I did not know. I did not know blasphemy; I did not know sin. I did not know them
because I could not commit them. Of these they accused me; about these they questioned me. "They repaid me evil for good,"
"barrenness to my soul." They gave me evil for good, and barrenness to my soul.
In this they showed me their barrenness: they repaid my good with evil. For this reason I cursed that same
barrenness in the tree. "But I, when they troubled me, clothed myself in sackcloth." But I covered myself with haircloth
when they pressed upon me so hard and were so hostile to me. I hid myself in mortality; that is why they did not recognize me.
"I humbled my soul with fasting." I humbled my soul with fasting. I fasted a mournful fast,
because I went without you and found barrenness in you, not fruit. The fast brought me low, and that weighed on me.
"And my prayer shall be turned back into my bosom." And my prayer is turned back into my bosom. The one I pray to, I have within myself.
I AM IN THE FATHER, AND THE FATHER IN ME. Therefore I do not send my prayer away from me; I turn it inward, toward myself.
"As a neighbor, as our brother, so I was pleased," that is, as with a neighbor, as with our brother, so I was pleased, that is, I rejoiced. As with one who is near to us
and who is our brother, so I was mindful of them. I loved them as neighbors; they persecuted me as enemies. "As one mourning and saddened,"
"so I was humbled." Like a man weeping and sorrowful, so I was brought low, because in them I did not find the faithfulness
that I was looking for. "And they rejoiced against me and gathered together." And they rejoiced against me; because I grieved,
they laughed, and watched me [?], and gathered together for their sport. "Scourges were gathered upon me, and they did not know."
Then scourges were gathered upon me, and they did not know me. Or else: they did not know this.
how they would have to pay for it. They were scattered and not pricked with remorse. They were scattered, not stung with remorse.
That they saw the sun darkened, and the earthquake, and many terrors: that scattered them more than it made them repent.
They tempted me. They tested me; they said: "If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross and we will believe you." They mocked
me with mockery. They scorned me by snorting through the nose. Sanna is a sound of the nose that belongs to derision; from it is derived subsanno, subsannas,
and from that subsannatio, which means scorn. They gnashed their teeth at me. They ground their teeth at me.
Therefore let it not seem a great thing to us to suffer for Christ's sake, since Christ suffered for our sake. Lord, when will you look?
When will you take notice of it, Lord? Christ says this according to the habit of human weakness, as if he longed for it:
for the time when his Father would avenge him. Restore my soul from their malice. Bring my soul back from their wickedness.
Give it back to life, slain by them. Raise it up. My only one from the lions. Bring my only one back from the lions.
My church, or my soul, born singly: free it from their savage power.
I will confess to you in the great church; among a weighty people I will praise you. In the wide church I confess to you;
among a weighty people I praise you. In the church there are many who confess God and yet do not praise him.
In it there are grain and chaff together. The chaff goes away from there; the grain is kept back.
The grain are those whom the wind of temptation does not move. Through them God is praised; through the others he is reviled among the gentiles,
because they say: "Look what the Christians do!" Let not those who wrongly oppose me exult over me. Now do not let it go so;
do not let those who are against me unjustly mock me. Do not let the sons of the church become chaff,
a mockery to pagans and heretics. Who hate me without cause and wink with their eyes. Those who hate me though I am guiltless, and wink with their eyes,
because they are deceitful and hypocrites. For they spoke peaceably to me, and besides, in anger, they plotted deceitfully.
As is plain where they greeted me in a friendly way, when they said: "Master, is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar or not?"
and yet they were deceitfully plotting toward their anger, that is, they showed their wrath together with their deceit.
After this there follows at once: And they opened their mouth wide against me. And they opened their mouth wide over me.
Not deceitfully, but boldly crying out: "Crucify, crucify him!" They said: "Well done, well done," that is, good, good,
"our eyes have seen it." And at the cross they rejoiced over me, saying: "Well, well,
now it has come before our eyes. Now what we wanted has come about: that we see you on the cross." You have seen, Lord;
do not keep silent, that is, from judgment. You have seen it, Father; now do not keep silent about it, do not let it go unjudged.
Do not depart from me. Do not forsake me, since you have bidden me to be so humble.
Arise, Lord, and attend to my judgment. Stand up, Lord, and look upon my unjust condemnation, the condemnation that I suffer.
See what they have found against me. See how unlike it is to the judgments of others, who suffer it for their guilt.
My God and my Lord, into my cause. My God and my Lord, look upon my intention. See how I mean it,
why I suffer it. For everything depends on this: not what one suffers, but why. As it says:
Blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness' sake. See that I suffer it for the salvation of the human race.
Judge me according to my righteousness, Lord my God. Judge me according to my right, Lord my God,
since they judged me unjustly. And let not my enemies triumph over me. And let not my enemies hold me in derision.
Bring it about that they cannot boast of how they have destroyed me. Make me rise again, and turn the world to follow after
me. Nor let them say in their hearts: Well done, well done, to our soul. Nor let them say: Well, well for our soul! Well for us
for what we have done! Do not grant them that joy. Nor let them say: We have swallowed him up. Nor let them say:
We have swallowed him up; he is laid in our bodies, because he has become one of us.
Rather bring it about that they become mine, than that any of mine should follow after them. Let them blush and be ashamed together
who rejoice at my misfortunes. Let them be ashamed and reverent together, those to whom my suffering is pleasing, and thereby let them be made better.
Let those who speak evil against me be clothed with shame and reverence. Let shame and reverence be the garment of those who speak evil of me.
Let them put on haircloth, in which they may atone for their audacity and their impudence: the audacity with shame, the impudence with reverence.
Let them exult and rejoice who desire my righteousness. Let them leap and rejoice who desire my right,
