who wish to hold to me. And let them say always: The Lord be magnified, those who desire the peace of his servant. And those who desire the peace of his servant —
I mean of Christ, his Son — let them always say: May the Lord be magnified;
not as the Jews said: Well done, well done, to our soul. And my tongue shall meditate on your righteousness, on your praise all the day.
And my tongue meditates on your righteousness; it teaches them all the New Testament, and all the day they meditate on your praise.

To the end, for the servant of the Lord. Who is named here the servant of the Lord? None but he who, taking the form of a servant, became obedient unto death; of whom Isaiah says: My servant, I will uphold him.
The unjust one said that he would sin within himself. The unjust one, says the prophet, resolved with himself
that he would do wrong. He hides it from other people. Why is that? There is no fear of God before his eyes.
For the fear of God, which ought to weigh more with him, is not before his eyes. For he has acted deceitfully in his sight.
"That he might find his iniquity and hate it." For he acted deceitfully in this before himself, as if he would find his wrongdoing and hate it.
He did not want to find it or hate it. If he had wanted to look for it, he would have found it. So the deceit lies in the looking.
If others point it out to him, he still will not admit it. Instead he says:
"Everyone does that. I alone do not." So hear this: "The words of his mouth are iniquity
and deceit; he would not understand, so that he might do well." The words of his mouth are wrong and deceitful. He would not take it to heart
that he should do well. It was the will he lacked: he could have done it if he had wanted to. "He has devised iniquity on his bed."
In his inner chamber he devised the wrong. He devised it in his heart, as the earlier verse says: "within himself."
"He has set himself on every way that is not good." He set himself on every way that is not good. He never failed to be on the wrong way.
"But he did not hate evil." But he did not hate evil, and so he was never without it.
"Lord, your mercy is in heaven." Lord, your mercy is in heaven, and it is above every other mercy,
and you give it only to your saints. The other mercies, the ones on earth, you give to the wicked and the good alike.
These are honors, riches, bodily health, and things like that. Or else by "heaven" he means the saints, in whom God's
mercy shines most. "And your truth reaches to the clouds." And your truth reaches to the clouds.
The clouds are the apostles; through them you make the truth known. "Your justice is like the mountains, Lord." Your justice, Lord, is like the mountains.
The apostles are your justice, because they fulfill it, and they are like mountains. The sun shines first on the mountains,
and from them it comes down to the plain. In the same way God's justice came first to the apostles, and from there it was spread over all. "Your judgments are a great abyss."
Your judgments are a great abyss, that is, without bottom, because no one can fathom them or search them out.
Why you draw one person and harden another, who can know? "Men and beasts you will save, Lord,
as you have multiplied your mercy, O God." Lord, you save men and beasts, since you have multiplied your mercy.
Its abundance shows in this: it reaches so far that it extends to both people and animals. But this salvation is temporal,
and it is shared by all. Those who love it are called only "men," just as Adam was only a man and not a son of man.
"But the children of men will hope under the cover of your wings." But the children of men, who are called "sons of men" after the Son of Man,
take comfort in the cover of your wings. They do not seek earthly happiness, but the mercy that is in heaven.
"They will be drunk with the abundance of your house." They will be drunk with the abundance of your house. They become so full of spiritual joy
that they lose worldliness and gain godliness. His house, holy Church, has this abundance.
...that drunkenness comes to their children. And you will give them drink from the torrent of your delight. And with the torrent of your
delight you will give them drink. The torrent is the wisdom of God, which comes from heaven,
in which they taste every delight. It comes with force, like a torrent, and it is 'reaching mightily from end to end.'
For with you is the fountain of life. For with you is the source of life. It flows from the place where the source is,
and it gives drink to whoever thirsts for it. And in your light we shall see light. And in your light
we see light. In your Son Christ we see you, the Father, for he is the light of light, and light from light.
Extend your mercy to those who know you, and your justice to those who are upright of heart. Put forth your grace, that is, show it,
and give it out to those who know you, and give out your justice to those who are upright in their hearts. Those who want something other than what God wants
are crooked in their hearts, not upright. If he wills you to be healthy, his will pleases you in that;
but if he wills you to be sick and that displeases you, then you are not upright in your heart.
Let not the foot of pride come to me. Let the foot of pride not come to me, for I cannot stand on it.
Pride is like something one-footed, for it always falls at once and cannot stand for long.
And let not the hand of the sinner move me. And let the sinner's hand not move me. Let the deeds of the evildoer not lead me astray,
as happens to the one to whom the foot of pride comes. There those who work iniquity have fallen. There those who do wrong fell.
On that foot they could not stand. On it Adam fell. On it the evil angel fell. They were cast out, and could not stand.
They were thrust out; they could not stand. The one was thrust out of heaven, the other out of paradise.
FOR DAVID HIMSELF.
DO NOT EMULATE EVILDOERS, NOR envy those who work iniquity. Do not take your example from the evil-willed,
nor take as your example those who live wrongly. For like grass they will quickly wither, and like green herbs they will soon fall away.
For they will wither as quickly as hay, and as swiftly as herbs they will fall away.
Hope in the Lord and do good. Trust in God and do well. Believe in him, and show it by your works.
Dwell in the land, and you will be fed with its riches. Dwell in the land, and then you will be fed with his riches.
That is, in his Church; then he will feed you in heaven with the sight of himself. Delight in the Lord, and he will give you the requests of your heart.
Take delight in God, and he will give you what your heart desires. Let him be your delight, and if you delight in him,
he will give you himself. Reveal your way to the Lord. Open your way to him. Whatever you suffer, confess it to him.
So Paul says: "The flesh lusts against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh." He gives you relief from it.
"And hope in him, and he himself will do it." And hope in him, and he will do what you wish. "And he will bring forth your righteousness like light."
And he brings forth your righteousness; that is, he makes it as plain to see as light. Your righteousness is your faith,
which is now hidden. It stays hidden "until the Lord comes, who will also bring to light the hidden things of darkness
and will make known the counsels of hearts, and then each one will have praise from God." "Then the righteous will shine like the sun." "And your judgment like the noonday."
And he makes your judging as plain to see as midday. Judge rightly that you should be a follower of Christ. That will be made
manifest to you, more glorious than midday is. For it says: "When Christ, your life, appears,
then you too will appear with him in glory." "Be subject to the Lord and pray to him." Be subject to God
and pray to him. "Do not envy the one who prospers in his way, the man who does injustice." Take no example from the one
who has succeeded on his journey, I mean the person who goes the wrong way. Let him go the broad way;
you go the narrow one. The broad way brings him into narrow straits; the narrow way brings you into open space. "Cease from anger, and forsake fury."
Let go of your anger, and give up your hot temper. Do not be angry that an evil man prospers
while you are despised. "Do not be envious, so that you act wickedly." Do not become like him, so that you act with ill will as he does.
"For those who act wickedly will be destroyed." For those who do evil willingly will be cast out.
They will be cast out of the city of God. "Nequitia" (wickedness) means deliberate malice,
which does not let them in there right away. "But those who wait for the Lord will inherit the earth." But those who wait for God
and give up hope in worldly good fortune will possess the land of the living. "And yet a little while, and the sinner will be no more, and you will seek his place
and will not find it." And before long the sinner is no longer here. Then you look for where he is, and you do not find him. Where he made his home
and where he wanted to be, there you will find him missing. "But the meek will possess the land." But the gentle, who bear with others,
will possess the land; they will possess the heavenly Jerusalem. "And they will delight in the abundance of peace."
And there they will joyfully enjoy peace, because it is eternal for them. "The sinner will watch the righteous man and gnash his teeth at him." The sin-
ner watches the righteous man, that is, he lies in wait for the righteous man and gnashes his teeth at him. When he sees that the righteous man is unlike himself,
he hates him, and then he begrudges him his life. "But the Lord will laugh at him, for he sees that his day is coming."
But God mocks him for having so forgotten his own day, because God knows in advance that his day is coming,
on which God will repay him for his wickedness. "The sinners have drawn the sword; they have bent their bow, to bring down the poor and needy."
BECAUSE HIS LIFE IS UNLIKE OURS. But the Lord will not leave him in his hands. But God does not leave him in his hands.
For he gives him no power over his soul. Though he may harm the body, the soul is saved
when the body rises again. Nor will he condemn him when he is judged. Nor does he condemn [?] him when judgment is passed on him!
by the wicked. By God he is not condemned. Wait for the Lord and keep his ways. Wait for my Lord
and keep his ways. Do not grow weary of waiting for his comfort, but recognize that here is the time of labor!
The time of sowing! The time of cold! The time of tears! Hereafter comes the time of consolation. And he will exalt you, so that you take the land as an inheritance. And
if you wait for him, then he will exalt you so that you receive as an inheritance the land of the living.
When the sinners perish, you will see it. When the sinners are lost, then you will see it. When you are at the right hand,
then you will see them at the left, where they are lost. I saw the wicked man highly exalted and lifted up like the cedars of Lebanon.
I saw an evil man exalted and raised up like cedar trees on Mount Lebanon. What then? And I passed by,
and behold, he was not. And I moved on past him [?], in that I cast away carnal thought, and at once he had vanished.
When I rose above earthly thought, I did not see him. And I sought him, and his place was not found.
And I sought him, and I could not come to where I might find him. Before, I knew his place, as long as I was without understanding;
when I came to my senses, I could not find it. Keep innocence and look upon uprightness. Guard and keep your sinlessness, and look toward righteousness.
Do not look at these present things, for in them is crookedness; look at the things to come: there is straightness.
Why should you look there? Because there are remnants for the peaceable man. Because for the peacemaking man there are remnants. That is,
his life will be left to him as a remnant, with eternal reward. But the unjust will perish together. But the unjust will be lost together.
The remnants of the wicked will perish. The remnants of the evil pass away. That is because they have no life after death.
But the salvation of the righteous is from the Lord. The salvation of the righteous is from God. Therefore no one can take it from them.
And he is their protector in the time of tribulation. And he is their shield when they are in distress. And the Lord will help them.
And God helps them. And he will set them free. And he sets them free. And he will rescue them from the sinners. And he frees them from the
sinners. And he will save them, because they hoped in him. And he preserves them, because they put their hope in him.
FOR DAVID HIMSELF, IN REMEMBRANCE OF THE SABBATH. Thus David lamented, remembering the rest. He longed for the rest
that is in the other world. He yearned for it; he was weary of this life. From this comes this lament.
O LORD, DO NOT REBUKE ME IN YOUR FURY, NOR CHASTEN ME IN YOUR WRATH. Lord, do not reproach me in your hot anger.
nor rebuke me in your wrath. When the day of judgment comes, then do not destroy me.
For your arrows are fixed in me. So have mercy on me, because your arrows now stick in me. Your chastisements are upon me.
And you have made your hand firm upon me. And now you have fastened your hand on me. I am now under your constraint.
There is no health in my flesh. My body is not whole. What is wrong with it? Corruption lies upon it, and mortality.
Where does that come from? From the face of your wrath. From the presence of your anger, which Adam earned in paradise.
because what came to him as punishment has now become nature in us. There is no peace in my bones. In my very bones
there is no rest. Where did the unrest come from? From the face of my sins. From the presence of my sins.
They provoked your anger, which has made me unhealthy. Or it means: FROM THE FACE OF YOUR WRATH,
that is, from the remembrance of your anger, which is still to come on the day of judgment; and from the face of my sins,
that is, from the remembrance of my sins, of which I am conscious. For my iniquities have gone over my head. And this is because
my wrongs have climbed over my head. Reason is the head; wrongdoing overcame it in paradise. As a heavy burden
they have weighed heavily upon me. They are as heavy on me as a heavy load. They press me down.
Therefore I have no rest. Rightly I think of the sabbath, where this will be made good for me.
For there will happen what has been promised to us: THIS CORRUPTIBLE SHALL PUT ON INCORRUPTION, AND THIS MORTAL
SHALL PUT ON IMMORTALITY. My scars have rotted and grown worse because of my foolishness. My wound-scars became foul
and grew worse from the presence of my folly. A wound that had healed festered and became worse
than it was before. That is: I renewed sins that had been forgiven, and became worse than before.
Pain upon pain came to me from my folly. It brought on me everything that I suffer.
I have become wretched and troubled even to the end. I have become wretched and sorrowful until the end of my life.
There will be no relief for me before the sabbath. All day long I went about sorrowful. All my life I went unhappy,
however boldly I could go [?]. Why? For my soul is filled with illusions. Because my soul is filled with deception. What is that deception,
except that it wants one thing, and then something else comes into its mind? In this way delusion deceived mankind before Christ came,
so that people thought wood and stones were God. In this way they always went astray over some bodily or bodiless figure
that appeared to them as God, whom they were seeking. The same thing happens to us when we want to think about God while we pray:
our thoughts drift off to other things, and all sorts of thoughts hardly let us pray. From all this we will be healed on the sabbath.
"And there is no health in my flesh." And in my flesh there is no health. Health of the flesh will come when [the] ... is taken away from the soul
illusion. Both of them came from original sin. "I am bowed down and humbled exceedingly."
I am bent and brought very low. Whoever thinks of the glory of the sabbath recognizes his own lowliness here.
He may well be displeasing to himself, when he compares himself with that glory which makes him like the angels of God.
"I roared from the groaning of my heart." I roared because of the sighing of my heart. That is how very heavily it weighs on a man
when something has happened to him, so that his sighing is like a roar. As we read of Esau: "He roared with a great cry."
The speaker says that the cry of his heart is just like the cry of the body.
Man hears that cry; God hears this one. The one who longs to go there sighs like this. It is the memory of the sabbath that causes the sighing.
"And all my desire is before you." And all that I long for is before you. I long for the sabbath; you know that, not man.
"And my groaning is not hidden from you." And my sighing is not hidden from you. Because it comes from the heart, it is open only to you.
"My heart is troubled within me." My heart is troubled within me, that is, it is frightened and sorrowful. Why is that?
"My strength has left me." My strength has abandoned me. Fright comes from the weakness of the heart,
and sorrow too. "And the light of my eyes is not with me." And the light of my eyes is not with me. Man had the light of his eyes
as long as he had God. When God abandoned him, the light went out for him, and he began to live in darkness.
Up to this point is the lament over inward sorrow. After this follows the lament over outward sorrow.
"My friends and my neighbours drew near against me." My friends and those who were close to me drew near a-
gainst me. In this way the Jews drew near to Christ, in order to crucify him; or the friends of Job, in order to revile him.
Some said that this whole psalm was written in his person, I mean Job's. "And they stood"
And they stood against me. "And those who were near me stood far off." And those who were near me stood far away.
Near in their feet, near in their lips, far away in their hearts. As it says: "This people honours me with their lips,
but their heart is far from me." "And those who sought my soul used violence." And those who sought my soul used force against me.
They sought it for an evil purpose, because they did not want to be my body, in which they would have had it. They sought it out of hatred,
and to kill its body. "And those who sought evil for me spoke vanity." And those who sought to do me harm
spoke vanity. "And they planned deceits all day long." And they plotted deceit all day long. They planned to give false testimony against me.
"But I, like a deaf man, did not hear." But I did not hear it, that is, I did not answer it, as if I were deaf.
And like a mute man not opening his mouth. So I kept silent, like a speechless mute. And I became like a man who does not hear.
So I became like a man who does not hear. And having no rebukes in his mouth. So I was like one who has no rebukes in his mouth.
I often rebuked before; in the Passion I kept silent. I wished to be judged in humility, so that I might come again in power to judge.
For in you, Lord, I have hoped. I did that because I hoped in you, Lord, who can turn my sorrow into joy.
You will hear me, O Lord my God. You hear me, you in whom I hoped, Lord my God. You perceive my
defence, even if no one else will listen to it. For I said: lest at any time my enemies exult over me.
For I said this to you: may my enemies never mock me. Those who cling to me, may they not act so wickedly
that they become a laughingstock to them. And when my feet were moved, they spoke great things against me. So when my feet wavered,
that is, when they slipped, they spoke great things about me. They accused me of great evil
when my limbs that are still on earth sinned, and they reminded them of their guilt, they who ought to have helped them [?]. For I am ready for the scourges.
And so I do not become a mockery, because I am ready to suffer chastisements. Those that I am not guilty of and so need not suffer,
those I gladly suffer for the guilty. And my sorrow is ever before me. So my pain is always before me.
Which pain? For I will declare my iniquity, and I will be concerned for my sin. That I show my wrongdoing
and am anxious about my sin. What pains me and is before my eyes is what I have done, not what I suffer.
But my enemies live, that is, act freely, and are made strong over me. But my enemies live as they please,
and things go well for them, and they are made strong over me. Adversities befall me; prosperity befalls them. And those who hate me unjustly are multiplied.
And there are many who hate me unjustly, who wrongly repay me, though I am well-disposed toward them.
Those who repay evil for good slandered me, because I pursued justice. Those who repay good with evil
spoke against me behind my back, because I eagerly sought justice. I sought their salvation; for that they defamed me.
Do not forsake me, O Lord my God; do not depart from me. Do not forsake me, Lord my God, and do not depart from me. Our Head says this in
our stead. Attend to my help, O Lord, God of my salvation. Turn to my help, Lord of my salvation. He does it for his own praise.
UNTO THE END, FOR IDITHUN, A SONG OF DAVID. This is David's song of joy for the one who leaps over. Whoever steps over earthly delights
and has leapt over them, and has only heavenly things in his mind, David rejoices over him unto the end. For him he sings thus.
He directs this song to Christ, who is the end. I SAID. I said in my heart and resolved thus: I will guard my ways,
so that I do not sin with my tongue. I will guard my ways so that I do not sin with my tongue. He who is Idithun
who has many detractors and many slanderers, against whom he must show patience by keeping silent. He speaks here.
I set a guard on my mouth when the sinner stood against me. When the sinner was against me, I guarded my mouth.
When I knew that he was lying in wait for my words, I kept silent. I became mute and was humbled, and kept silent even from good things. I became mute
and humbled myself, and therefore I kept silent even from what was good. Fearing that I might speak evil,
I avoided speaking well. And my sorrow was renewed. And from that my pain was renewed. It grieved me because of their wickedness;
after that it grieved me that I had not shown goodness by speaking. My heart grew hot within me, and in my meditation a fire will flare up.
After the pain my heart grew warm within me, and fire burned in my thinking. It became so hot for me
that I was set on fire. These were desires for those who have gone hence; they set me on fire. I spoke with my tongue: make known to me,
O Lord, my end. Then I spoke with my tongue: make known to me, Lord, my end. Let me know
how I should bring my life to its end, and to what perfection I should fasten myself; and make me know God,
who is the end. And the number of my days, which is. And make known to me the number of my days, which only "is", without "was".
It has neither past nor future, and therefore it is without "was" and without "will be". That I may know what I lack.
Make the number known to me, so that I may know what I lack here. So that I may be humble, because what I have
is so little compared with what I lack, and so that this may seem nothing to me when I think of that.
Behold, you have made my days old. Behold, you have made my days old here. Give me those old days
that cannot pass away. And my substance is as nothing before you. And before you my being is as nothing.
As long as I am here, it is nothing compared with what it will be in the future. Yet all things are vanity, that is, changeableness,
every man living. Even if a man leaps beyond the world, he is, as long as he lives, wholly changeableness.
Transience, passing away and worthlessness are all that he is. Although man walks in the image of God, yet he is troubled in vain.
However much man walks in the image of God, he is still troubled in his mind in vain.
It is a great thing that he bears God's image within him; but because of the first transgression of Adam he is confused in his mind,
worrying in vain about many things. Why in vain? He stores up treasure and does not know for whom he will gather it. Because
he stores up treasure and does not know for whom he gathers the treasure. What can be as vain as striving to keep
what cannot last long, and saving it, and yet not knowing for whom? And now what is my expectation?
And what is it now that I wait for? Is it not the Lord? Is that not my Lord? That you give yourself to me.
for that I wait. And my substance is before you. Therefore my being is before you. That I am Jeduthun pleases you; that is in your sight.
If I have substance of gold and silver, even men can see that. From all my iniquities deliver me. Release me from all my unrighteousness.
What need does Jeduthun have of this prayer? Only that he teaches us to be humble, even though we have become aware of grace in ourselves.
You have made me a reproach to the foolish. You have made me a reproach to the foolish man. You wanted me to be among them,
and to tell the truth to those who love vanity more, and to whom I am nothing but a mockery. I was mute and did not open my mouth, because you did it.
Among such people I became mute, and I did not open my mouth, because you did it. You gave me the patience
to be able to keep silent so profitably. Remove your strokes from me, for I have fainted from the strength of your hand in rebukes.
Take your chastisements away from me, for I am weary from the rebukes of your mighty hand. Spare me after so many scourgings
that have made me powerless. For iniquity you have corrected man. Because of unrighteousness you chastise man.
You hold his guilt against him. And you made his soul waste away like a spider. And you made him waste away and wither
like the spider. You made him so worn down by hardships and so lean, as the spider is in its limbs.
In this way you punished him for his unrighteousness. Nevertheless every man is troubled in vain.
Every man is nonetheless troubled in mind over vain things. For all this he does not give up idle worries,
sometimes about clothing, sometimes about food. What he worries about depends on God, not on himself;
therefore his worries are idle. Hear my prayer, O Lord, and my supplication; with your ears perceive my tears.
Hear my prayer and my supplication, Lord; with your ears perceive my tears. Perceive what they ask for,
why I shed them. Do not be silent, for I am a stranger with you, and a pilgrim, as all my fathers were.
Do not be silent: do not fail to say, "Your sins are forgiven you," or "I am your salvation." For I am a newcomer with you, and an exile,
as all my forefathers were. They all came from Babylon to Jerusalem and were pilgrims here. As Paul says:
"As long as we are in the body, we are pilgrims away from the Lord." Forgive me, that I may be refreshed. Forgive me my sins; unburden me of them,
that I may be cooled from my worries and find rest in my conscience. Before I go away and shall be no more.
Before I go hence and am here no longer. Or it means: before I go hence in such a way that I no longer exist.
For whoever is not with God does not exist. His existence is of no use to him; therefore he does not exist. Here praise the Lord, for the psalm is good.
UNTO THE END, A PSALM OF DAVID. WAITING I WAITED FOR THE LORD. The Church says: Waiting I waited for my Lord. We wait with waiting
for what we greatly long for; that is the reason for this doubling. And he attended to me. And he looked toward me. That is, he took notice of me.
for he sees many to whom he pays no heed. That is why it does not say "attendit me", but "attendit mihi".
And he heard my prayers. And he heard my petitions. Where did that show itself? And he brought me out of the pit
of misery and out of the mire of clay. And he led me out of the pit of wretchedness
and out of the filth of the clay. He took me out of sins. That is where it showed itself. And he set my feet upon a rock
and directed my steps. And he set my feet on the rock, which is Christ, and on him he directed my steps.
Whoever walks on him does not go astray. And he put a new song into my mouth, a hymn to our God. And he gave into my mouth
a new song, a song of praise to our God. If I used to sing to idols, says the holy Church, now I sing instead to Christ.
Many shall see and shall fear. Many will then see this and fear for themselves. They see me praising God;
from this they begin to fear for themselves. And they shall hope in the Lord. And so they learn from me that they too should put their hope in the Lord.
Blessed is the man whose hope is the name of the Lord. Blessed is he whose comfort is the name of my Lord. Blessed is he who wants him himself
and nothing else. And has not looked to vanities and false follies. And who did not look at vanity
and at false madness. Who has no curiosity about how the charioteer in the circus performs on his chariot,
and how smoothly he turns four horses together, and how obedient they are to him at every turn,
however he pleases. That is vain, because it does not make blessed those who delight in watching it.
It is false madness. What else can madness be but false? It always deceives the one it dwells with.
Many are the wonders you have done, O Lord my God. Many are your wonders that you have done, Lord, and they are more worth pondering
than what the mime and the charioteer do in the circus or in the theatre. If the chariot moves over the ground there, a chariot carried Elijah into heaven. If
the actor walks along a rope there, Peter walked on the waves. And in your thoughts there is none who is like you. And there is none like you in your thoughts.
No arts make men ride to heaven or walk over the sea. I have declared and I have spoken;
they are multiplied beyond number. I proclaimed it beforehand, says Christ, by the mouth of the prophets, and told it myself when I came:
that the multitude of the wicked exceeds the number of the righteous. As it stands in the Gospel: For many are called, but few are chosen.
Sacrifice and offering you did not desire, but a body you have prepared for me. What was formerly consecrated and offered,
that you have rejected, and you have given me myself a body. The foreshadowing is gone;
the truth has come. A lamb from the flock used to be offered; the Lamb of God is now offered. Burnt offering
and offering for sin you did not demand. Even the burnt offering for sin you do not require, as you once did before.
[that] you now want a contrite and humbled heart. Then I said: Behold, I come. Then I said: Lo, I come.
When I commanded that an unblemished lamb be offered, then I meant myself. Then I promised what I have now done:
that I myself would come and become the sacrificial victim. At the head of the book it is written of me that I should do your will.
In the first scroll it is written of me that I do your will, as it says: His will is in the law of the Lord.
My God, I willed it. My God, I willed what was promised there, and I have shown that will.
And your law in the midst of my heart. And I willed your law in the midst of my heart, as it also says there:
He will meditate on his law day and night. I have proclaimed your righteousness in the great church. I proclaimed your righteousness in the catholic Church.
In that I did your will. Behold, I will not restrain my lips; Lord, you know it. Behold,
I do not close my lips so as not to speak your righteousness. You know that in my heart,
where no human knows it. Here Christ teaches us that his righteousness should be in our mind, not only in our mouth.
I have not hidden your righteousness in my heart. I did not hide your righteousness in my heart. When it was time for it,
I did not conceal it. But in the Passion it was not the time for it, so I kept silent. I have spoken of your truth and your salvation.
I declared your truth and your Saviour. I revealed to them that I am Christ. I have not hidden your mercy and your truth from the great assembly.
I did not hide your grace or your truth before the great multitude. By grace I mean this: whoever renounces his sins,
you forgive them to him. And by truth I mean this: to whoever walks in righteousness [?], you give the crown.
But you, Lord, do not put your mercies far from me; your mercy and your truth have always upheld me. But do not put far from me
your grace. Do not withdraw your grace from my imperfect members, which still limp in righteousness,
for your grace and your truth have always received me. Love comes from grace, fear from truth.
These received me and lead me. For evils without number have surrounded me. That is why there is need, I mean,
that you not put your mercies far from me: because countless evils have surrounded me in those members. Listen to what they are.
My iniquities have seized me. My iniquities have caught me. There are so many of them that they cannot be numbered.
And I was not able to see. And because of how many they were, I was not able to see the true light,
which is God himself. They are multiplied beyond the hairs of my head. They are more
than the hairs of my head. Such a multitude can easily choke a person who does not guard against them. Whoever does not commit grave sins
but does not fear many small ones is buried by sand, even though no great mass crushes him.
And my heart has forsaken me. And my heart has forsaken me. That is: it is unable to know itself.
Just as Peter did not know his own heart when he said: "I am ready to die with you." What wonder is it if God forsakes the heart
that forsakes itself? Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me. Since that is so, may it now please you, Lord,
to deliver me. O Lord, look to helping me. Lord, look to my help; that is, be ready to help me.
Let them be confounded and put to shame together who seek my soul to take it away. Let them be ashamed together because of my miracles,
and let them be afraid because of my resurrection, those who seek my soul to kill it.
Let them be turned backward and blush who think evil against me. Let them be turned around behind me, so that they follow after me,
and let them be ashamed who wish me evil. Let them straightaway bear their confusion who say to me, "Well done, well done." Let them straightaway bear their shame,
those who say to me "Well done, well done," and do it mockingly, or speak it to me as praise,
as if it came from me and not from God. Let them exult and rejoice who seek you, O Lord. Let them leap for joy and rejoice,
those who seek you, Lord, and say "Well done" to you, because it is you who give it. And let them say always: The Lord be magnified,
those who love your salvation. And let those who love your Savior say always: May the Lord be magnified,
for he gives to man everything good that he has. But I am needy and poor; the Lord takes care of me. But I, to whom they say
"Well done, well done": I am needy and poor! God takes care of me; in him I am rich.
Be my helper and my protector, O Lord; do not delay. Be my helper and protector, Lord my God; do not delay.
Unto the end, for David himself. Blessed is he who understands concerning the needy and the poor. Blessed, says the prophet, is he
who has understanding concerning the needy and the poor. That person understands Christ who understands why he became needy and poor:
so that he might make us rich. He said of himself in the preceding psalm: But I am a beggar and poor,
and the Lord takes care of me. How does it appear that he is blessed? In the evil day the Lord will deliver him. On the day of judgment God will deliver him.
What helps him is this: he did not take offence at him, nor misunderstand him, and he knew him inwardly as God, even though he saw him outwardly as a man.
May the Lord preserve him and give him life. May God keep him safe in all the perils of the world and make him alive, for all others are dead
except those who live in him. And may he make him blessed on earth. And may he make him blessed in the homeland of the saints.
And may he not deliver him into the hands of his enemies. And may he not give him into the power of his enemies, neither here nor in eternity.
May the Lord bring him help upon the bed of his sorrow. May God bring him help upon the bed of his pain.
His weakness is called the bed of sorrow. I mean someone who cannot get up because of weakness.
if he cannot bridle the flesh, then may God help him. You have turned all his bed in his sickness.
You have turned all his bed into his sickness. Where he wanted to rest, you gave him unrest.
If he hurried to gain house and household, wife and property and other possessions, you made him hold all of it with bitterness.
Why? So that he would love nothing else but eternal life. On the bed of pain you help him; on the bed of rest you are against him.
That is how you train your own. I said: Lord, have mercy on me. Therefore I said: Lord, have mercy on me.
Heal my soul, for I have sinned against you. Heal my soul, for I have sinned against you.
If you did not spare Christ, your Son, though he was guiltless, I, however, am guilty.
You rightly scourge me so that you may heal me, because when I was whole in paradise, I did not listen to you.
My enemies spoke evil to me. My enemies, says Christ, spoke ill of me. What did they say? When will he die
and his name perish? When will he die, and when will his name be destroyed? They said: This is the heir.
Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours. And they came in to see. And they came in to me
to spy on me. Judas spied on me myself; my other members are spied on by many.
Their heart spoke vanity. Their heart spoke what was worthless. They intended to lie against me. They gathered iniquity to themselves.
They gathered iniquity to themselves. They thought they were harming me; they harmed themselves. They went outside and spoke to the same end,
that is, with one counsel. Those who had gone in there went out and spoke with one voice.
With one voice they plotted my death. And all my enemies whispered against me. All my enemies went about whispering against me.
Against me they plotted evil for me. Against me they thought evil for me. They devised death for me; that became life for others.
They set an unjust word against me. They set an unjust word against me. That is: He is guilty of death. Shall he who sleeps
not rise again? Do you think that he who now sleeps will not rise afterward? You think you have
killed him, but he is sleeping. Death is sleep to him, because he lets himself into it for a while
and then soon throws it off again. The man of my peace, in whom I hoped, who ate my bread, has greatly increased his tripping-up of me.
Judas, my protégé (that is, the one who kissed me), in whom I trusted, that is, in whom my followers trusted,
who ate with me, tripped me up far and wide. Far and wide because he drew the Jews into it.
If you would rather say: he magnified his tripping-up of me by being against me, that is still the same thing.
But you, Lord, have mercy on me. But you have mercy on me, Lord. This is spoken in the form of a servant, and in the form of the needy and the poor.
And raise me up. And raise me up. And I will repay them. And then I will repay them. I will bid the Romans come and destroy them.
By this I knew that you favored me: that my enemy will not rejoice over me. By this I recognize that you favored me,
for my enemy does not rejoice over me. They can still see the whole world turned to me.
So they do not rejoice that my name has been wiped out, as they wished. But you have upheld me because of my innocence.
Because of my innocence you received me. You knew me to be gentle and meek; that pleased you in me.
And you have strengthened me forever. And you strengthened me forever, though you weakened me for a time.
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel. Praised be the Lord God of Israel, that is, of the younger son, whom the elder serves. As is now plain to see.
For the Jews, who came to the faith earlier, have that written down which we point to for the pagans
when we want to bring them to the faith. It is they who hold the writings with which we instruct the pagans in the things they doubt in us.
Their scriptures serve us for that, and they are, as it were, our chamberlains, because
it says: "The elder son shall serve the younger." From age to age. From this world on into that world,
may he be praised. So be it, so be it. So may it happen, so may it happen, that we may praise him here and in eternity.
Understanding, for the sons of Korah. This psalm is understood as being about the sons of Calvary. What is Calvary? Nothing other than the place of the beheaded, so named from bald bones,
that is, from bare, gleaming bones. Condemned men were put to death there; Christ too was crucified there.
Therefore the sons of Korah are those who have received the sign of the Cross. As the hart longs for the springs of water,
so my soul longs for you, O God. As the hart makes for the spring of the waters, so my soul longs for you, God.
The hart swallows the serpent and then hurries to the water. This signifies that once our vices have been driven out and slain,
we can become thirsty for the spiritual refreshment that comes from Christ, who is the fount of refreshment.
My soul has thirsted for the living God; when shall I come and appear before the face of God? My soul is thirsty, that is,
it longs for the living God. It yearns for the day when I come and appear before God's sight.
My tears have been my bread day and night. While I waited for this, my tears were my bread day and night.
Those I ate, and that was the food I gave my soul, when I could not drink from the fount. While it is said to me every day: Where is your God?
I ate tears every day, while every day it is said to me: Where is your God? The one who
worships the sun or the moon points to his god, and taunts me: where is mine? For no one can see him.
These things I pondered, and I poured out my soul above myself. On this I reflected, and I poured out my soul, out beyond myself.
That is to say: I directed my thought above the sight of myself. Inwardly I see myself.
Understanding, which is given to the sons of Korah, shows me my invisible soul, and far above it my invisible God.
For it is changeable; he is unchangeable. If it could not reach above itself, how then would it reach him
who is so high above it? "For I shall go into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God." So I learned to seek him.
For I came into the place of the wonderful tabernacles, wonderful here on earth, until one arrives fully
up to the house of God. Outside the Church one need not seek him.
The Church is wonderful in all God's faithful, wonderful for many virtues. In it one must go on until one fully arrives there,
where God's house is, where wondering ceases, because the fountain of understanding is there, and all questions are untied there.
"With the voice of exultation and confession, the sound of one feasting." Within it, in the voice of joy and confession, I hear the sound of one feasting.
My soul feasts on these two voices: that I praise God, and that I know myself, until I come there.
They sound so sweet to me that their sound is a feast to me. "Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me?"
Why are you sad, and why do you make me joyless, my soul? As if you did not know how to answer those
who say to you, "Where is your God?" As if you were not in the wonderful tabernacle, at those feasts of exultation and confession.
Why do these people who wander in error in this world trouble you? Why do they grieve you so? "Hope in God."
Hold fast to God, put your hope in him; he will take you out of there. "For I will confess to him."
He will do so, because I confess to him. What do I confess? "The salvation of my countenance, my God." The salvation of my face is my God.
This I confess to him: he heals my face, which is sad now, and makes it glad when I see him.
"My soul is troubled within myself." Turned toward myself, my soul is saddened; turned toward God, it is comforted. He is steadfast;
I am unsteadfast. My unsteadfastness weighs on me; his steadfastness gives me courage. It gives me hope of coming there
where I shall become steadfast. "Therefore I will remember you from the land of the Jordan and of Hermon, from the little mountain." Therefore I remember you from the land of the Jordan
and from Hermon, the little mountain. In Latin, Jordan means "their descent" and Hermon means "anathema". The Jordan signifies baptism;
anathema signifies abomination. In both of them humility is understood. Humility teaches a person to lower himself, which is called "to descend",
and to loathe himself, which is called "to anathematize". So it means: being humble and making myself small,
I remember you. "Deep calls to deep." Abyss calls on abyss. The Old Testament foreshadows the New Testament.
"In the voice of your cataracts." In the voice of your waterfalls, that is to say:
at the teaching of your preachers. They teach how one testament looks toward the other.
Or it means: one wise man makes another wise by the voice of your teaching, not his own.
You grant that his teaching is of use to another. "All your heights and your waves have passed over me." All your surging billows and your
waves have passed over me. That is: the threats of your judgments are not hidden from me,
which you will raise up at the end of the world; nor have the hardships of the present world passed me by.
"In the day the Lord commanded his mercy, and in the night he declared it." By day the Lord commanded his grace, and by night he showed it.
Whoever learned his law in peace, him he delivered in trouble. Let us learn his law while it is well with us; then he will help us in need.
"With me is prayer to the God of my life." With me is prayer to the God of my life. I have at home what he seeks:
that is my prayer, not my sacrifice. How is that done? "I will say to God: You are my upholder; why have you forgotten me?"
This is how it is done. I say to God: You are the one who receives me; why do you forget me? I am in such distress here
as if you had forgotten me. "Why have you driven me away?" Why did you push me back when I, in ecstasy of mind, tasted
the heavenly sweetness? Why did you not let me stay in its fullness, so that I would not grow cold like this? "Why do I go about sad
while the enemy afflicts me, while my bones are broken?" Why do I go about sorrowful, because the enemy breaks me like this
with many stumbling blocks, by which even my bones are broken? Why do you let the devil
make even the strong in the Church give way through temptations? "Those who trouble me have reproached me, while they say to me day by day:
Where is your God?" Those who trouble me have reproached me with this, that they say daily:
Where is your God? They heap this reproach on me over your martyrs. Because my soul is troubled by this,
I say again: "Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me?" Why are you unhappy
and sorrowful, my soul? "Hope in God, for I will confess to him, the salvation of my countenance, my God."
Trust in God, for in confessing to him I say: You are my salvation, my God.
A PSALM OF DAVID. This is the voice of one who always
laments that he is here among the wicked, because he would gladly be gone to where only the good are.
"JUDGE ME, O GOD, AND DISTINGUISH MY CAUSE FROM A NATION that is not holy." Judge me, God,
and separate my cause from the unholy people. Though we are here together, do not let us be alike.
"From the unjust and deceitful man deliver me." From the unjust and crafty man deliver me. "For you, God, are my strength."
"Why have you driven me away? Why do I go about sad while the enemy afflicts me?" Since you, God, are my strength, against that sadness,
why did you push me away from that strength? And why am I sad when the devil troubles me with temptations?
Evil love and evil fear attack me. I struggle against them. In that struggle I am sad.
Why is that, since you are my strength? You are my strength; why is the weakness of sadness upon me?
Is it not that I wrongly resent the punishment of original sin, from which all temptation has come,
when the justice of God, which leaves no wrong unpunished, ought rather to make me glad? Therefore I should say:
"IT IS GOOD FOR ME THAT YOU HAVE HUMBLED ME, SO THAT I MAY LEARN YOUR JUSTIFICATIONS." Temptation oppresses me; in it I learn how just you are.
"Send forth your light and your truth." Send forth, and cause Christ, your light, to be born,
and your truth. "They have led me and brought me to your holy mountain and into your tabernacle."
They led me and brought me up onto your holy mountain and into your tent. The light and the truth, which are Christ,
brought me into the Church, which is the mountain and the tabernacle. She is the mountain which, from
a little stone, grew so large that it filled the whole earth, according to Daniel's prophecy. She is a tent,
because she belongs to those who fight and those who are travelling. The house to which they are travelling is in heaven. Of it is written:
"BLESSED ARE THEY WHO DWELL IN YOUR HOUSE; FOR EVER AND EVER THEY WILL PRAISE YOU." "And I will go in to the altar of God."
And coming from that tabernacle, I go in there to God's altar, where I myself become a burnt offering.
That is the invisible altar in heaven, which this one here on earth signifies: the very throne of God, which no one there approaches
except one who approaches this one here worthily. "To God, who gladdens my youth." I go in to God, who there gladdens my youth,
that is, my newness. He gladdens my newness there, because here he has made my oldness sad.
In that newness I endure; I no longer grow old, I no longer age. "I will praise you on the cithara, O God, my God."
I praise you on the cithara, God, my God. That is: in hardships I praise you, in hardships I sing to you.
The cithara has its sound box below, just as the psaltery has it above. From the lower part, where the body is and where mortality is,
hardships come to us. When we praise God while we suffer them, we sing on the cithara. That song is sweet,
because patience makes it pleasing to God. "Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me?" Since it pleases God,
why then are you sad, my soul? And why do you trouble me? Why do you let any grief come upon you?
Since the image of God is in you (I mean reason and intellect, which are also called the mind), why then do you not push away from yourself
then what is unfitting for them? Hope in God, for I will confess to him. Hope in God, for to him
I confess thus. The salvation of my countenance is my God. Salvation is of my countenance, my God.
UNTO THE END, FOR THE SONS OF KORAH, FOR UNDERSTANDING. Korah, which means baldness or skull, signifies the sons of the cross,
for in Calvary, that is, in the place of baldness, Christ was crucified. To them this psalm is given for understanding of the matter
that God often closes his ear when he is asked for temporal things, so that one will ask him for eternal things.
O GOD, WE HAVE HEARD WITH OUR EARS; OUR FATHERS HAVE DECLARED TO US the work that you wrought in their days and in the days of old.
We have heard, Lord, with our ears what our forefathers told us. Our forefathers told us of your work
that you wrought in their days and in old times. We have heard how you delivered them,
though you do not deliver us now. Your hand destroyed the nations, and you planted them. Your hand, they said, destroyed other peoples,
and in their place you planted them. You afflicted the peoples and drove them out. For their sake you afflicted other peoples, the Amorites,
the Hivites, and the Girgashites, and drove them out so that you made room for them. For not by their own sword will they possess the land,
and their own arm will not save them. They do not possess their land by their own prowess, nor did their own strength save them.
But your right hand and your arm. Rather your right hand, that is, your power, and your arm, that is, your Son.
And the light of your countenance. And the revealing of your countenance, in that you showed yourself to be present in those works.
Because you were pleased with them. For you were pleased with them. You yourself are my king and my God. You are still the same, my king
and my God. You who command salvation for Jacob. You who proclaim to Israel his salvation. However
you do not shine forth face to face, nor have you shown your hidden substance, which you are to show at the resurrection,
you nevertheless made known through angels what they should do. In you we will toss our enemies with the horn. Is your help then now to be gone?
May it not be so. In you was their victory; in you we too drove our enemies with the horn.
With your strength we will hunt them. And in your name we will despise those who rise up against us. And in your name we despise
those who venture against us. For I will not hope in my bow. I do not trust in my bow
any more than our forefathers did. And my sword will not save me. Nor will my sword preserve me any more
than it saved them. For you have saved us from those who afflict us. You have saved us from our persecutors.
I say it in the past tense because it is as certain as if it had already happened. And you have put to shame those who hate us.
And those who hate us, you have put them to shame. At the resurrection they will be put to shame; that is certain now.
In God we shall be praised all the day. In God we shall be praised every day. Where there is day without night, there we shall be praised.
For you have rescued us from those who afflict us. And in your name they shall give praise forever. And in your name we shall give praise forever.
In that world the praise of the saints is eternal, and they can never grow weary of it, for it is their blessedness. But now you have cast us off and put us to shame.
Although that is to come for us in eternity, you have nevertheless now thrust us away, your martyrs,
and put us to shame, because we who are called Christians are made hateful by the pagans. And you will not go out, O God, with our forces.
And you do not go out with us, God, among our forces, as you did before. You leave us powerless
when we rise up to march against our enemies, though you made our forefathers strong in battle.
You have turned us back before our enemies, that is, in front of our enemies. You have turned us away, turned our backs
before our enemies. You have scorned us while they looked on. And those who hated us plundered for themselves.
And those who hate us have carried us off for themselves. You have given us like sheep for food, and scattered us among the nations.
You have given us to them to be devoured like lambs for slaughter, and you have scattered us among the heathen.
Because this is the voice of the martyrs, this lament is to be understood of those who fell away during martyrdom
and turned back to paganism. You sold your people without price. You gave away your people without receiving others in exchange for them.
You gave your martyrs up to slaughter. What did you receive in return for them? And there was no multitude in their exchanges.
And there was no great payment in the bargain. Of those who were given away there were many;
of those received in return there were none. You have made us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a mockery to those who are around us.
You have made us a reproach to our neighbours, and an object of scorn and mockery to those placed around us.
You have made us a byword among the nations, a shaking of the head among the peoples. For the heathen you have made us a likeness of your passion,
and a [?head-]wagging for the people, as you were for the Jews. All the day my shame is before me. All day long my shame was before me.
Other people feel ashamed now and then; our shame went on and on. And the confusion of my face has covered me. And the shame of my face
covered me. Because of the voice of the one who reproaches and reviles, before the face of the enemy and the persecutor. Where did it come from?
From the voice of the one who reproaches and speaks against me, and from the sight of the enemy
and of the persecutor, who is always present against me. All these things have come upon us. All this has come upon us
For understanding, for the sons of Korah. So that they may know how God led our forefathers out of Egypt,
and how he will lead us in the resurrection out of this Egypt of this world, so that in the meantime we must suffer every hardship here.
and [that] we are to be tested to see whether we are willing to serve God gratis, that is, without payment. Freely he gave us life,
freely he redeemed us, freely we ought to serve him. I mean that we should desire no reward here,
but in the future. Therefore it says after this: "Nor have we forgotten you." Nor did we forget you because of that.
No tribulation made us forget you, because you willed it to happen to us. "For understanding, for the sons of Korah": for us sons of Korah,
for us sons of the cross. "And we have not acted wickedly in your covenant." Nor did we do wrong in what you appointed for us,
that is, in your law. "And our heart has not turned back." Nor did our heart give way backward, as the hearts of those do
who come to despair because of hardships. "And you have turned our paths aside from your way." And you turned our paths away from your way.
That is, you taught us how far our way, which we wanted to go, is from yours,
which you want us to go. Ours leads to death; yours leads to life. "For you have humbled us in the place of affliction."
For you have humbled us in this wretched place, in this toilsome
world. "And the shadow of death has covered us." And the image of death has covered us. What is that? Nothing but mortality, which is common to all.
But what is death itself? Nothing but eternal damnation with the devil. "If we have forgotten the name of our God, and if we have spread out our hands to a strange god,
will not God search this out?" If we had forgotten the name of our God, and if we had spread out our hands to a strange god,
would God not ask about it? Why does he ask about what he already knows? Only so that he may let us know it,
and so that we, by recognizing ourselves, may be made better. "For he knows the secrets of the heart." He knows the secrets of the heart.
Therefore he has no need to ask. Yet he asks when he tests us, and through the testing he makes us recognize who we are.
So he did with Peter, who did not know himself before the temptation, when he said: "With you I am ready to die,"
but who began to know himself in the temptation, when he wept over his denial. "For your sake we are put to death all day long."
You know the secrets of our hearts: that we are put to death for your sake all day long, that is, at all times,
not for vainglory, nor for our crimes. If there were none who would readily die out of boastfulness,
not out of love, then Paul would not have said: "If I give my body to be burned, but have not love,
it profits me nothing." "We are counted as sheep for the slaughter." And [you know] that we are reckoned as sheep for sacrifice.
Sheep do not defend themselves; we do not defend ourselves. "Arise, why do you sleep, O Lord?" Stand up, Lord, why do you sleep?
This is an abuse of a word, that is, a misuse of a word, which in Greek is called catachresis. How can God sleep?
Rather, his martyrs cry out to Christ that he make his resurrection known to the gentiles, for he sleeps to those who know him as dead.
and they do not believe that he has risen. They rightly long for this, because when it happens, persecution comes to an end. "Arise, and do not cast us off to the end."
Stand up, and do not push us away to the end. Do not reject us at the resurrection. "Why do you turn away your face?"
Why do you turn your face away from us, as if you no longer wanted to care for us?
"Do you forget our poverty and our tribulation?" And why do you forget our poverty and our distress,
as if you yourself had not become poor and suffered torment for us? "For our soul is humbled in the dust,
and our belly has cleaved to the earth." Remember us, for our soul is humbled in the dust as it prays to you,
and our belly lies low and clings to the earth. Or else "belly" stands for the carnal people, who fell away from the faith during persecution
and went over to cling to the pagans, and holy Church laments them here now. She has a mouth in the saints and a belly in the carnal.
That is why someone said: "I took the book, and the book itself was sweet in my mouth and bitter in my belly,"
because God's commandments are sweet to the spiritual and bitter to the carnal. "Arise, Lord, help us, and redeem us for your name's sake."
Stand up, Lord, that is, make your resurrection known to the gentiles, so that even those who now cling to the earth
may be raised up from the earth. Help us and set us free for your name's sake, not because of our merits [?].
To the end, for those who shall be changed, for the sons of Korah, for understanding, a song for the beloved.
This song looks to Christ, for the changed sons of Korah, for understanding concerning
the beloved. The sons of the cross have been changed from unbelievers into believers. For them this song is for understanding concerning Christ, the beloved of the Father,
about whom those who crucified him had no understanding. For it says: "For if they had known,
they would never have crucified the Lord of glory." "My heart has poured forth a good word." The Father speaks about the Son.
My heart has poured forth a good word; that is, I have a good Son who has come forth from my own self.
He is his Word, because he makes him known to people, just as he is also his Wisdom, because he makes them wise.
"I speak my works to the king." I tell my works to the king. This repeats the meaning of the preceding verse, because "to speak"
means to bring forth a word. And because all of God's works are in the Son, for God to beget him is to speak his works to the king.
The telling is nothing other than the begetting. "My tongue," that is, my word, "is the pen of a scribe," that is, the writing of a scribe.
My word is as lasting as the writing of the scribe. A human word passes away; God's word is co-eternal with him. "Of one who writes swiftly."
It is like the writing of someone who writes swiftly. What can be as swift as a single word? There is one Word
that the Father has spoken. It is swift because it is not spoken in separate syllables.
yet it is spoken so eternally that in the speaking there is neither beginning nor end. "Beautiful in form above the sons of men."
When the Word becomes flesh, then it is man, then it is the bridegroom. What kind of bridegroom? "Beautiful above the sons of men." That means:
beautiful before all men, for no other was innocent except him, and no other had the
beauty of our redemption. "Grace is poured out on your lips." Grace is spread on your lips, for the word of grace is on your lips.
That is, for example: "Whoever believes shall be saved." And again: "Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood
has eternal life." "Therefore God has blessed you forever." Now the prophet speaks to Christ.
Therefore God blessed you forever. Others he blessed for a time: those who were under the Law,
who received the Promised Land. To you he gives the kingdom of heaven because of grace. He does this in those who are under grace.
"Gird your sword upon your thigh, O most mighty one." Gird your sword about your thigh, very mightily. Here in the flesh, arm yourself
with the sword of your teaching, which mightily separates the son from the father and the daughter from the mother.
"With your comeliness and your beauty." Do this with your human form and with your divine beauty.
God and man, do it. "Attend, proceed prosperously, and reign." Look upon us, and come here prosperously from heaven,
and reign here in your Church. "Because of truth and meekness and justice." Because of truth
and gentleness and justice. Let truth teach us in the holy Gospel, let gentleness shine forth in the Passion, let justice be shown in the Judgment.
"And your right hand shall lead you wonderfully." And your right hand, that is, your power, leads you wonderfully.
For you live wonderfully, and you rise again wonderfully. "Your arrows are sharp, O most mighty one."
Your arrows are sharp and very mighty. Your words are very powerful; they pierce through hearts
because they are sharp, and they turn hearts to righteousness because they are mighty. "The peoples shall fall under you, into the heart of the en-
emies of the king." The peoples fall under you. Where does the fall happen? In the heart of the king's enemies. You are the king.
They submit themselves to you, and become humble in the place where they were proud. "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever."
Your throne, O God, and your kingdom last forever. The throne of the Jewish kingdom lasted for a time; the throne of your kingdom lasts without end.
"The rod of direction is the rod of your kingdom." The rod of straightening is the rod of your kingdom. Let those be made straight who were crooked before
and twisted, because they wanted to reign without him and do their own will, and to force God's will to follow theirs.
"You have loved justice and hated iniquity." You loved what is right and hated what is wrong. This shows that your rod is
a rod of direction. It cannot be bent, because it is made of iron. It guides some and crushes others: it guides the spiritual and crushes the carnal.
Therefore God, your God, has anointed you. Therefore God anointed you, your God. The Father consecrated you and anointed you,
because you loved right and hated wrong. What is the ointment? It is spiritual and invisible, which by something bodily and visible
is signified. With the oil of gladness above your fellows. With the oil of joy he anointed you; that is innocence,
which remembers nothing of anything that might weigh on it, so that it would need to repent. Above your fellows (or: partners). That is to say,
further than other saints, because from you, the anointed one, others are called anointed. Myrrh and gutta and cassia from your garments.
From your garment come the scents of myrrh, and of gutta, which is called ammoniac, and of cassia, which is called fistula.
That is to say: from the faithful and from the whole Church comes the report of virtues, which is as sweet as the scent of precious
herbs. Out of the ivory houses. It comes out of ivory houses, that is,
from holy virgins, who are signified by ivory, because the elephant is a chaste animal
and, beyond one mate, takes no other. From which, that is, among which, the daughters of kings have delighted you in your honor.
Among those houses the daughters of kings, who were born to your honor, delighted you. Those who delighted you
were the daughters of the apostles, chosen for your honor, not for theirs, because they are called Christians, not Petrians or Paulians.
Or the daughters of kings are the many churches, which are all called Christ's, not Peter's or Paul's. The queen stood at your right hand.
The queen herself, your Church, which is made up of many churches, stood at your right hand.
There her children hear: 'Come, you blessed of my Father.' She who stands at the left is not the queen;
she hears: 'Go into the eternal fire.' In gilded clothing. In a gilded garment, that is, with the adornment of wisdom.
Surrounded with variety. Wrapped around with many colors, of either virtues or languages,
because she exists in various languages and she has various virtues. Hear, daughter, and see. 'Hear, daughter, and see,' says the prophet.
Mother of many children, daughter of the prophets and apostles, [hear] what the gospel of Christ commands you, and after that you will see the glory of God.
Faith in the gospel cleanses your heart, so that you can see him whom only the pure in heart shall see. And incline your ear.
And humbly incline your ear; take careful note of this counsel. And forget your people and your father's house.
And put out of mind your people, the people of Babylon, from whom you were born, and your father's house, the devil's, who is king there,
who bore you unsightly, with the stains of your sins; and you are reborn in Christ to the beauty of innocence.
For the king has desired your beauty. For the king, your bridegroom, desires your beauty. He is beautiful through himself;
you become beautiful through him. He wants you to be without spot and without wrinkle. He makes you so.
It is strong. "A helper in the tribulations which have found us exceedingly." A helper in troubles, of which many have come upon us.
Among all troubles there is no trouble greater than the consciousness of sins. Therefore it is from this above all that one must flee to God. So did those who had slain Christ
and, when admonished by Peter, were pierced with compunction and asked him, "What shall we do?" To them it should be said:
"A helper in the tribulations which have found us exceedingly." And when they were baptized and were secure about their sins,
then they could say what follows here: "Therefore we will not fear when the earth is troubled." Therefore we do not fear
when the earth is troubled. That is the Jewish people, because it is surrounded by the gentiles, as the earth is surrounded by the sea.
Trouble was coming upon that earth, but they did not need to fear it, because God was their refuge. "And the mountains shall be carried into the heart of the sea."
"And we do not fear," they can say, "when the mountains are carried into the heart of the sea." That is: when the apostles leave Judea
and give the hearts of the gentiles their teaching, which the Jews rejected, then we have nothing to fear, because we follow those mountains.
This is to be understood of that very mountain which is on the top of the mountains, which was cast from the earth into the sea
according to his own promise. He said: "If you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you shall say to this mountain, 'Be taken up
and cast into the sea,' and it shall be done." He is the mountain that they carried from Judea to the gentiles by their faithful preaching.
"Its waters (that is, the sea's) roared and were troubled." Those same mountains resounded in preaching, and its waters were troubled,
because the gentiles raged when they heard the new teaching. "The mountains were troubled in his strength." And the mountains were troubled
in his strength. Whose strength? Only God's, who is power. Which mountains? Other mountains, which are called mountains of the world, not
mountains of God, because the powerful of this world resented that their laws were to be destroyed by God's laws.
Yet for all that, it was not left at that [?]. But how did it go? "The rush of the river gladdens the city of God."
The rushing of the river gladdened God's city. The flood of the Holy Spirit made it mighty.
The apostles drank so much of it that springs of living water flowed from their bellies, enough to satisfy all their hearers.
Then the earth was watered; then barren hearts were made fruitful. For this the city of God rightly rejoiced.
"The Most High has sanctified his tabernacle." By doing this, the Highest made his dwelling holy. "God is in the midst of it; it shall not be moved."
God is in the midst of the city. Even if the mountains of the world rage, he is never moved from there. He is in the middle there in such a way
that he helps all alike. "God will help it with his countenance." God helps it with his face.
Through his works he makes it aware that he is there, because God's manifest working is his countenance.
"The nations were troubled." Because of this the peoples were troubled, that is, they came into anguish and fear. "The kingdoms were bowed down."
And the kingdoms humbled themselves, because they came and worshipped him. The Most High uttered his voice, and the earth was moved.
The Most High gave his voice, and by it the earth was moved. Sinners heard it
and trembled at it. To them he gave it as a gift; his apostles brought them that glorious gift.
The Lord of hosts is with us. The God of virtues, the God of powers, who is power itself, he is with us.
If he is with us, who then can be against us? Our receiver is the God of Jacob. The God of Israel is the one who receives us.
He receives us into that dwelling, out of which we shall never again be thrust. Come and see the works
of God, which he has set as wonders upon the earth. Come and see his works, which he has set as signs upon the earth.
What are they? Or how does he do them? Taking away wars to the ends of the earth. Taking away wars
to the end of the earth. That happened at his coming, when the gate of Janus was closed by Augustus. Or, spiritually:
that none of his faithful puts his trust in his own weapons, but in God's protection. He will crush the bow and break the weapons
and burn the shield with fire. He will crush the bow, and he will break the weapons, and he will burn the shield in the fire.
He takes all defence and all protection away from you, so that you flee to him and say:
MY HELPER AND MY RECEIVER IS THE GOD OF JACOB. Then he gives you the weapons of the Gospel: of truth, of self-restraint, of salvation, of hope,
of faith, of love. You will then have these from him, because he has burned your own weapons with the fire of the Holy Spirit.
Be still and see that I am God. Be still! For what purpose? Be still and see that I am God,
not you. I created you; I protect you. Stop fighting; let me fight.
I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted on the earth. I will be exalted among the peoples and on the earth. I will show that I am God
among the Gentiles, who are called the sea, and among the Jews, who are called the earth. Blindness has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in;
at the end of the ages the Jews will come, and so all Israel will be saved. The Lord of hosts is with us; our receiver is the God of Jacob.
The God of powers is with us, because he became man on earth. The God of the younger son has taken on our body.
UNTO THE END, A PSALM FOR THE SONS OF KORAH. For the sons of the bald one, that is, of CHRIST. He is called bald because of Calvary (the place of the skull), where he was crucified. Those who
mocked his baldness and said, "CRUCIFY, CRUCIFY HIM," were long ago foreshadowed by the mockery of the children
who said to Elisha, "GO UP, BALDHEAD, GO UP, BALDHEAD." The bears devoured those; the demons swallowed these.
ALL YOU NATIONS, CLAP YOUR HANDS. Clap your hands, all peoples. Be glad that you are redeemed on the cross. What the Jews mocked,
you rejoice in. Clap with your hands, that is, show your joy in good works. Shout to God with the voice of exultation.
Shout for joy to God with a joyful voice. Show your joy with your hands and with your tongues. For the Lord most high is terrible.
For the high God is terrible. Now that he has gone up to heaven he is terrible, even though on earth he was an object of scorn to the Jews.
A great king over all the earth. A great king, that is, mighty over all the earth. Mighty over the Jews and over the gentiles.
He has subjected peoples to us, and nations under our feet. He has made peoples subject to us, and nations under our feet.
This is the voice of the faithful concerning the unbelievers, because the Christians rule and the pagans are subject to them; or else it means that they are far beneath them in their merits.
He has chosen us as his inheritance. He chose us Christians as his inheritance. The beauty of Jacob, which he loved. He chose the likeness of Jacob,
which he loved. He chose his beauty. In what was he beautiful? Only in this: that spiritual things were worth more to him
than carnal things, and so he bought his brother's birthright with lentils. That is why it was said: THE ELDER SHALL SERVE THE YOUNGER.
For the impious must be subject to the pious, and the proud to the humble. God has gone up with jubilation, and the Lord with the sound of the trumpet.
God went up to heaven with jubilation and with the sound of horns. The apostles shouted for joy.
The angels sounded the clearest of horns, which said: THIS JESUS, WHO IS TAKEN UP FROM YOU INTO HEAVEN,
SHALL COME IN THE SAME WAY AS YOU HAVE SEEN HIM GOING INTO HEAVEN. Sing praises to our God, sing praises. Now sing, sons of Korah,
sing to our God, for he is not only a man but also God. Sing praises to our king, sing praises. Sing to our king,
sing to him. For God is the king of all the earth. For God is king of all the earth. Before, he was king of the Jews,
as long as only they knew him. Now all the gentiles know him, and he is king of all. Sing praises wisely. Sing wisely.
Those people did not sing wisely who had understanding and yet sang to idols that have none. But now we sing wisely if we acknowledge the God
whom we do not see as all the mightier, because it could happen that we would reject him if we were able to see him,
as the Jews did. The Lord has reigned over the nations. The Lord has reigned over the nations since his ascension,
and before that over a single nation. God sits upon his holy throne. At the right hand of the Father he sits on his holy throne,
above the cherubim and seraphim. You too, O Christian, make yourself into his throne. Have a pure heart;
that is where he sits. The princes of the peoples are gathered together with the God of Abraham. The princes of the peoples are gathered together with Abraham's God.
The princes of all the gentiles come to believe in Christ, who is Abraham's God, just as the centurion did, who came from the gentiles
and of whom the Saviour said: I HAVE NOT FOUND SUCH GREAT FAITH IN ISRAEL. For the strong gods of the earth are greatly exalted.
This is because the Jews, who were once gods but are now strong earth, are greatly exalted,
that is, they are very proud. What are men but earth? They are the ones who look for strength in themselves and not in God.
who are called the mighty of the earth. This is the sense: because the pride of the Jews has been rejected by the God of Abraham,
therefore princes are gathered from among the Gentiles, so that they may receive Abraham's faith in place of the Jews.
A PSALM OF A SONG FOR THE SONS OF KORAH, ON THE SECOND DAY OF THE WEEK. Here again it is sung for the sons of Korah, concerning Monday.
On that day the firmament was created, which signifies those in holy Church who are firm and strong against all temptations.
Of these it is now sung for the sons of Korah: GREAT IS THE LORD AND GREATLY TO BE PRAISED. Mighty is the Lord and highly worthy of praise.
In the city of our God. Where is he worthy of praise? In our God's city, that is, in holy Church.
It cannot be anywhere else. Many are unbelieving and malicious; they are not the city of God. On his holy mountain.
On his holy mountain. In that city and on that mountain he is worthy of praise. Let us climb the mountain,
as the prophet urges us. He says: COME, LET US GO UP TO THE MOUNTAIN OF THE LORD. How should one climb up there?
We must believe in him, and in him strive upward to the height of the virtues. Spreading the rejoicings of the whole earth.
Spreading the joy of the whole earth! The great Lord has spread the faith of holy Church through all the world. Mount Zion,
the sides of the north, the city of the great king. Zion, which is in Jerusalem, and the north side, that is, the Jews in sin and the Gentiles in the north,
are the city of the mighty king. The Church is made up of these two. That is the widespread joy of all
