the world. God will be known in her houses when he receives her. When God receives her, he will be recognized in her houses.
By receiving her he causes her to know him. For behold, the kings are gathered together. For kings are gathered together,
who were called the sides of the north above. Where? They came together into one: to one king, to one cornerstone,
which joins two walls together. Seeing this, they marvelled. Seeing his signs, they marvelled.
They were troubled, they were moved, trembling seized them. They were troubled and shaken, and fear came upon them.
Why? Only because they recognized their sins and were terrified at them. There were pains as of a woman in labour.
There their pains were like those of a woman giving birth. Their pain was penitence, which they brought forth. With a violent wind
breaking the ships of Tarshish. That same trembling was in a swift wind, that is, by its own strength it broke the ships of Carthage.
The greatness of the fear broke the pride of the Gentiles. Why is the pride of the Gentiles signified by the ships of the Carthaginians?
Only because, among all the Gentiles, they prided themselves most on seafaring. As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts,
in the city of our God. As we heard it foretold by the prophets, so have we seen it fulfilled by the apostles,
in the city of the mighty Lord, in our God's city. God has founded it forever. God laid its foundation for eternity.
And the meditation of my heart [shall speak] prudence. So the thinking of my heart speaks wisdom. From the heart came my words,
with which I make you wise. I do not act like those who say one thing and want another. I will incline my ear to a parable.
I incline my ear to my saying. I myself do what I teach. But the Pharisees teach
what they do not carry out in deed. I will open my proposition on the psaltery. Through the body I open my secret. I myself come in the body (in corpore)
and teach you a hard understanding. Why shall I fear in the evil day? Why should I be afraid on the evil day,
when the day of death comes? Shall the iniquity of my heel surround me? Will the injustice of my heel then surround me,
that is, of my end, as it does others? Those who trust in their own strength and glory in the multitude of their riches?
As it does those who trust in their own strength and pride themselves on their great
riches? A brother does not redeem; shall a man redeem? Whoever says "Father" to God says "brother" to Christ. The one whom Christ did not redeem,
can a man redeem him, as those suppose who rely on their own strength? He shall not give to God his propitiation. Whoever supposes this
does not give God anything with which to win His favour. And the price of the redemption of his soul. Nor the price of his soul's ransom.
He does not give alms; he does not make himself friends of the mammon of iniquity. And he shall labour forever, and shall still live unto the end.
And because of this he is always in torment, and lives on forever without end. Just as the rich man, buried in hell, lives without end in torment.
He shall not see destruction when he sees the wise dying. Such a person does not recognize destruction when he sees wise men die,
and he says: "They are lost. What good has their wisdom done them?" If he recognized destruction,
he would know that he himself was lost, not they. The unwise and the foolish shall perish together. Those who are wise are not lost;
the unwise and the fool are lost together. The one who is so unwise that he does not know himself, and the one so foolish
that he does not care for his salvation: each of them is lost. And they shall leave their riches to strangers.
And they leave their riches to strangers. But what if they have children? Those too are strangers to them,
because they are of no use to them. Just as those who took possession of the rich man's wealth were strangers to him when he was in hell.
And their graves are their houses forever. And their graves, so they think, are their houses forever.
Their tents in generation and generation. And their tents from generation to generation. That is why they make marble tombs,
as if these were to be their dwellings forever. If the rich man had been housed there, he would not be burning in hell. They have called their
names in their lands, that is, in their graves. There at their graves they called on them by name.
Their descendants visited their graves and, holding feasts there, called on them there, according to heathen custom.
What did that profit the dead? And man, when he was in honour, did not understand. And man did not know that he was in honour.
That the image of God adorned him, he did not recognise. Because of this, it happened to him like this. How?
He is compared to the senseless beasts, and is made like them. He was compared to the senseless cattle, and he became like them.
That is how far he fell. This way of theirs is a stumbling block to themselves. This is their way, a stumbling for themselves,
that is, an offence. If anyone else thinks them blessed, it also becomes a stumbling block to him. And afterwards they will bless with their mouth.
And after that they thank God with their mouth. After all their going astray they become hypocrites, because they have temporal goods,
they do not praise God from the heart, though they do it with words. Like sheep laid in hell. They are like sheep,
and not merely sheep, but like sheep driven down into hell. Death is their shepherd. Death is their shepherd. Christ is life;
the devil is death. Just as Life is the shepherd of the good sheep in heaven, so in hell Death is the shepherd of the mangy sheep.
And the righteous shall rule over them in the morning. And the righteous rule over them at dawn. Here it is night; here the unrighteous rule over the righteous.
When the night passes and day begins to break, then the righteous in turn rule over the unrighteous. And their help shall grow old in hell, away from their glory.
And their help grows old in hell; there they lose their glory. All help, whether of treasure, of friends or of power,
and everything that belongs to glory, they lose there. But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell, when he receives
me. But God redeems my soul from the power of hell when he receives me. Christ says this openly about himself
and about his members. He went to hell; he was also received into heaven with his own. Do not be afraid when a man has become rich
and when the glory of his house has been multiplied, for when he dies he will not take all these things, and his glory will not go down with him. Do not fear
that you are unfortunate when another man has become rich and the glory of his household has been multiplied, for when he dies
he does not take it away with him, and his glory does not go with him either. What did the rich man have in hell except fire?
For his soul will be blessed in his lifetime. Because he is called blessed as long as he lives, he is therefore wretched
when he dies. He will praise you when you do good to him. He thanks you, God, when you do good to him. When you chastise him,
then he reviles you. He shall go in even to the generation of his fathers. He goes off into the old lineage of his forefathers. As wicked as they were,
so is he. Abel and Cain are every man's forefathers. Whichever of the two a man imitates, that one is his forefather. Whoever is such
as is written here, his forefather is Cain. He shall never see light, for ever. He will never see God, who is light.
Why is that? Man, when he was in honour, did not understand; he is compared to the senseless beasts, and is made like them. That is because
he did not recognise his honour, and therefore he was compared to cattle and horses, and became like them.
A psalm of Asaph. Who was Asaph? He was the son of Barachiel, one of the chief singers, of whom one reads in Paralipomenon [Chronicles],
who in those times sang these psalms to God. In that sense this psalm is Asaph's,
because he sang what David taught him. And to understand it more deeply: Asaph means "synagogue." The synagogue of the believers
and of the holy forefathers speaks here. This psalm is theirs. THE GOD OF GODS, THE LORD, HAS SPOKEN. The God of gods,
that is, of the saints, who are called gods by grace, the Lord himself, he spoke. What did he do by speaking?
And he called the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting. He spoke and directed the whole earth to his faith, all who dwell on the earth,
from the rising of the sun to its setting. Out of Zion the beauty of his comeliness. From Zion comes his beautiful image.
Zion is in Jerusalem. From there came the apostles, who proclaimed Christ to us, whom his divinity adorned above all others.
God will come openly. God comes openly. He who came secretly before comes openly the second time. When he came,
he was judged; when he comes again, he will judge. Our God, and he will not keep silent. Our God comes
and does not keep silent, though he keeps silent now, for at the judgment he will say: GO INTO THE ETERNAL FIRE. A fire will burn before him.
Fire burns before him. It burns the chaff. Whoever recognizes himself as chaff, let him fear the fire. And round about him a mighty tempest.
And around him a strong wind. It separates the good from the evil. That wind is made by the winnowing fan that is in his hand,
as it says: WHOSE WINNOWING FAN IS IN HIS HAND, AND HE WILL CLEANSE HIS THRESHING FLOOR AND GATHER THE WHEAT INTO HIS BARN,
BUT THE CHAFF HE WILL BURN WITH UNQUENCHABLE FIRE. He shall call the heaven above, and the earth. He summons the heaven above, and
the earth. That is, he summons the righteous and the unrighteous to his judgment. Why? To separate his people. To separate his people.
From whom? From the wicked. Though the wicked and the good dwell together here, there he will separate them.
Gather his saints to him. The synagogue now speaks to the angels. Gather his saints to him. For then it will happen as CHRIST says in the Gospel:
FOR HE WILL SEND HIS ANGELS, AND ALL NATIONS WILL BE GATHERED BEFORE HIM. Who set his testament in order. Who set his testament in order.
Those who distribute and act as he has commanded in the books. Those who show charity, give alms,
and receive guests. Above sacrifices. Such works are dearer to God than offerings. For he said: I DESIRE MERCY
AND NOT SACRIFICE. And the heavens will declare his justice, for God is judge. And by doing this the heavens proclaim,
that is, the righteous proclaim, his justice, for they know that God himself is the judge, whom nothing deceives.
Hear, my people, and I will speak. Now CHRIST speaks. Hear, my people, and then I will speak. If you will not listen to me,
then you are not my people, and I will keep silent. Israel, and I will testify to you. Hear, Israel, and I will tell you.
I am God, your God. Understand this; I say it to you: I am God, I am your God. If you listen to me, then I am your God.
If you do not listen to me, then I am God, but not your God. To my own good I am God; to your ruin I am not your God.
What reward do you want, other than me myself? In this you have me: that I am your God. Where you have me, there you have every good thing.
I will not reprove you for your sacrifices. I do not rebuke you because of your offerings, for I do not blame you for not bringing me a fat bull, or
the best he-goat. But your burnt offerings are always in my sight. Your burnt offerings are always before me. That is to say:
I want your mind to be set on fire with charity. That is the tribute I demand. In the past it was the custom,
when regions became provinces, that they were ordered to pay tribute. That command was called an indiction. Now we are the Lord's province,
that is, his land under obligation [?], and now we have heard what taxes he wishes to impose on us. Now let us be glad to live under his indiction.
I will not take calves from your house, nor goats from your flocks. I do not want calves from your house
or goats from your herds. As long as I cared about that, in the Old Testament, I was foreshadowing what I want to receive in the New.
For all the beasts of the forests are mine, the cattle on the mountains and the oxen. Therefore I do not want to demand them from you,
for all the wild animals are mine, and the grazing livestock on the mountains, and the oxen standing in the stall at the manger.
I know all the birds of the sky. I know all the birds of the air. If I wanted them,
I know them better than any human does, for I knew the nature they now have before they came to be.
And the beauty of the field is with me. And the beauty of the field is with me; it is known to me entirely. If I were hungry, I would not tell you. If I am hungry,
I do not complain of it to you. For the world and all its fullness are mine. The world is mine, and everything that is in it.
What do you give me? Shall I eat the flesh of bulls, or shall I drink the blood of goats? Do you think that I eat bulls' flesh
or drink goats' blood, however it might come to me as an offering? Offer to God the sacrifice of praise. Offer to God
the offering of praise, because whatever good you have done, you have it from him, and he forgives you whatever evil you
have done. You have that offering within yourself; you do not need to look for it outside. That is what I seek,
what I want to impose on you. And pay your vows to the Most High. And deliver your vows to the Highest.
And call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will rescue you, and you will honor me. And call on me when you are in need, and then I will set you free,
and for that you will praise me. But to the sinner God said: Why do you recite my righteous decrees, and take my covenant in your mouth?
Now Asaph speaks again. To the sinner God said: Why do you talk about my law,
and why do you take my testament, the Old or the New, into your mouth? But you have hated discipline and have thrown my words behind you.
You hated discipline and threw my words behind you. You did not want to keep my teaching before your eyes.
Whom, then, can you teach? "If you saw a thief, you ran with him, and you threw in your lot with adulterers." You went along with the thief
when you caught sight of him, and you had a share with those who lie with other men's wives. That is to say:
you helped those who did evil and stood by them. "Your mouth abounded with malice." Your mouth was full, that is to say,
your heart was full of ill will. You were glad to see things go badly. "And your tongue contrived deceits."
And your tongue spoke the deceit cleverly. You knew well how to flatter the one who did wrong.
"Sitting, you spoke against your brother." Sitting idle, you slandered another man. "And against the son of your mother
you laid a stumbling block." And you made your mother's child stumble: you led astray the sons of mother Church. "These things you did, and I kept silent."
So you did, and I was silent; I bore it from you. "You thought wickedly that I would be like you." Because of my silence you supposed
wrongly that I am like you. "I will rebuke you." I will reproach you when the time comes,
when God comes openly, "and he will not keep silent." "And I will set you before your face." And I will set you opposite your own face.
I will make you know yourself and be displeased with yourself. Because you did not want to know before who you were,
you will find it out in hell. "Understand these things, you who forget God." Take note of this, you who so forget God [?].
"Lest he snatch you away, and there be no one to rescue you." Lest he snatch you away to punishment, and no one help you.
"The sacrifice of praise will honor me." The offering of praise honors me, not one from evil but one from good.
"And there is the way by which I will show him the salvation of God." And there is the path on which I will show him God's Savior, Christ.
Praise, that is, psalmody, leads him to heaven, where Christ is. [?] one sin brought on the other.
A PSALM OF DAVID, WHEN NATHAN THE PROPHET CAME TO HIM, BECAUSE HE HAD GONE IN TO BATHSHEBA.
This psalm was David's lament when Nathan reproached him for his misdeed: that he had slept with Bathsheba,
the wife of his chief warrior Uriah, and had him killed because of her. And so one sin brought on the other.
"Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy." Have mercy on me, God, according to your great mercies.
Such a wound cannot be healed except by your renowned medicine. "And according to the multitude of your compassions
blot out my iniquity." And according to the abundance of your compassion, blot out my iniquity. That was iniquity:
that I did to another what I would not want done to myself. "Wash me yet more from my iniquity." Now wash from me more thoroughly my
wrong done knowingly than you washed away before what I did unknowingly. As much greater as this is, so much more wash me.
"And cleanse me from my offense." And cleanse me of my misdeed. "For I acknowledge my iniquity." For I myself acknowledge my wrongdoing.
Therefore do not take note of it yourself. Because I punish it, therefore do not punish it yourself. "And my offense is ever before me."
And my misdeed is always before me. I keep remembering, always, what I have done.
"Against you alone have I sinned." Against you alone I sinned. You alone are a just judge who repays, because you alone are without sin. Or else it means this:
If another man sins, he sins against God alone; if a king sins, he sins against God and the king [?]. "And I have done evil before you."
And I did evil before you. It grieves me that I dared to do this while you were looking on.
"That you may be justified in your words." Have mercy on me, so that you may be true in your words. Which words?
"Of the fruit of your body I will set upon your throne." "And that you may prevail when you are judged": namely, that you must do nothing unworthy.
And you prevail in upholding your promise when you are judged as to whether you could rightly abandon it [?].
If someone should say that I have forfeited it, then remember your mercy and set it right [?]. "For behold, I was conceived in iniquities,"
"and in sins my mother bore me." Behold, I was conceived in wrongdoing, and my mother bore me in sins.
Have mercy on me, for besides new guilt I have old guilt, with which I was conceived and born.
Which is that? It is the guilt that came from Adam to all people, and baptism was instituted because of it.
Christ alone came here without it. "For behold, you have loved truth." Behold, you loved the truth.
It pleased you that I told the truth in confessing my sins, as it says: "A pure confession frees from death." "The uncertain and hidden things
of your wisdom you have made known to me." You revealed to me the uncertain and hidden things of your wisdom.
You showed me that Christ, your wisdom, was to come here into the world, even though I have now gone so far astray.
"You will sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed." When he comes, you will sprinkle me with hyssop, as lepers are sprinkled, and then I shall be cleansed.
For it is commanded in Leviticus that lepers were to be sprinkled seven times with hyssop dipped in the blood of the sacrifice,
and that they were healed by this. "You will wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow." Then you will wash me, and then I shall be whiter than snow.
For you will give me a soul purer than any body could become. "To my hearing you will give joy and gladness."
You will let me hear joy and gladness when you say: "Come, blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom
that has been prepared for you from the beginning of the world." "And the humbled bones shall rejoice." And then they will rejoice,
the bones that are now humbled in penitence. There is also another kind of hearing that gladdens a person, one that is in the heart. John spoke of it:
"The friend of the bridegroom stands and hears him, and rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom's voice." A hearing of this kind makes the bones humbled.
because he recognizes the glory of the one whose voice he has heard inwardly. The prophets and apostles and all the teachers had this inward hearing.
From this, this sentence can also be understood: Turn away your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.
Turn your gaze away from my sins, and blot out all my sins. Create a clean heart in me, O God. Create
a clean heart in me, so clean that I do not do wrong like this again. And renew a right spirit within my inward parts.
And a right mind, by which I mean reason, which I made crooked by sinning: renew it in my inmost parts,
from which this adultery came. Strengthen me there, where I was just now frail. Do not cast me away from your face.
Do not cast me away from your sight. Cleanse me so that I may see you.
And do not take your holy spirit from me. And do not take your holy spirit from me, that is, the spirit of prophecy,
which I had before, however much I have now forfeited it. Restore to me the joy of your salvation.
Give me back the joy of your Savior, Christ, which I had before these sins, and which I now see has been diminished in me.
And strengthen me with the principal spirit. And strengthen me with the foremost spirit. Who is that, if not God, of whom it is written:
GOD IS SPIRIT. Strengthen me in this way: since you have now forgiven me, let me not become guilty again.
I will teach the wicked your ways. Then I will teach the unrighteous your ways, and tell them how you showed mercy to me, a wicked man,
so that they too do not despair of mercy. And the impious shall be converted to you. And the godless will be turned to you.
Not only to the unrighteous and sinful, but even to the very worst, I will then promise mercy from you,
if they are willing to mend their ways. Deliver me from blood, O God, God of my salvation. Deliver me, God, from the works of flesh and blood,
that is, of corruption, for it is written: FLESH AND BLOOD SHALL NOT POSSESS THE KINGDOM OF GOD, NOR SHALL CORRUPTION POSSESS INCORRUPTION.
Deliver me, God of my salvation, the salvation we do not yet have, because it is still to come.
And my tongue shall exult in your justice. And then my tongue will joyfully tell of your justice,
how you choose to receive the penitent not only out of mercy but also out of justice.
Lord, you will open my lips, and my mouth shall proclaim your praise. Lord, you open my lips,
and my mouth proclaims your praise: that you created me and did not abandon me when I sinned, and received my confession,
and released me from my sins. For if you had wanted sacrifice, I would surely have given it. For if you wanted an offering for my sins,
I would give it to you. I could bring you many young sacrificial animals, if you wanted them. But you will not delight in burnt offerings.
But you do not care for them; you do not want burnt offerings. They foreshadow the saving sacrifice, which will come when its time comes.
then nothing else is needed. A troubled spirit is a sacrifice to God. A crushed spirit is a pleasing offering to God. A contrite and humbled heart, O God, you will not despise.
A crushed and humbled heart you do not despise, O God. Priests bring a saving sacrifice; let every man bring a contrite heart.
Deal kindly, O Lord, with Zion in your good will. Lord, deal lovingly with Zion in your good will.
Show good will to your Church. And let the walls of Jerusalem be built. And through that will let the city walls of Jerusalem be built.
Let the fortifications of our immortality be built, in faith, hope and charity. Then you will accept the sacrifice of righteousness.
Then you will receive the sacrifice of righteousness: the shedding of the blood of Christ. Oblations and whole burnt offerings. And you will receive oblations
and burnt offerings. These are the people who turn to God, and also those
who set themselves on fire with the love of God. Then they will lay calves upon your altar. Then the priests
will lay calves upon your altar that please you. They will not be taken from the herd,
but will be young men brought up in holy Church, holy and innocent, as Lawrence and Vincent were, and others like them.
Unto the end. An understanding of David. When Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, and said: David has come into the house of Abimelech.
This understanding of David looks toward Christ, because his enemy, the Antichrist, is rebuked here,
whom Doeg the Edomite signifies. Out of envy of David, Doeg slew the priests; out of envy of Christ, the Antichrist slays martyrs.
Why do you boast in malice, you who are mighty? Let all say with David: Why do you glory in evil,
you who are mighty? Cannot beasts and worms also do evil? Iniquity all the day.
Why do you glory in iniquity all day long? You always do to another what you would not want done to yourself.
Why does that seem glorious to you? Your tongue has devised injustice. Your tongue planned wrong. Wrong was in your mind and in
your mouth. Like a sharp razor you have worked deceit. You have acted with treachery as a razor does: it takes the hair,
not the body. In the same way, with all your wickedness you have taken from him what is outward. You took his goods;
his soul you could not harm. You have loved malice more than kindness. You loved ill will more than good will.
Iniquity rather than speaking what is just. And to speak wrong rather than right. Darkness was dearer to you than light.
You have loved all words that throw down headlong. You loved all words of overthrow, by which I mean those that send people plunging into death.
In what way? With a deceitful tongue. With cunning words. For you knew that another man did evil,
yet you said that he did well. Therefore God will destroy you in the end. Therefore God destroys you in the end.
If he does not destroy you now, he will destroy you when the end of the world comes. He will pluck you out and remove you from his tabernacle.
He will tear you out and carry you far away from his tabernacle. And your root from the land of the living.
And he will cast your roots out of the land of the living. He will not let you dwell together with the blessed.
The righteous shall see and shall fear. The righteous see here in this world what shall happen to him in the other world.
and they fear for themselves. And they shall laugh at him. And in the other world they laugh at him. And they shall say. And this is what they say.
Behold the man who did not make God his helper. Look, there is the man who did not seek God's help. But he hoped in the multitude of his riches.
But he trusted in his great wealth. And he prevailed in his vanity. And he grew powerful in his vanity
and succeeded by it. But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, have hoped in the mercy of God. But I was not
like him, says David. In God's house I was like the fruitful olive tree, and I hoped in God's grace,
not in treasure, as he did. Because I wanted to take root in God, I am a fruitful tree.
Therefore I bear Christ, who is the oil of his elect. For ever and for ages of ages. How long do I hope in him?
Only now? Both now and forever, world without end. I will confess to you forever, because you have done it.
I acknowledge to you that you did it. You separated me from this Doeg. You chose me
and cast him away. And I will wait for your name, for it is good in the sight of your saints. And I wait for your name
because it is good in the sight of your saints. There, where their joy is fulfilled without end, they come to know your good name.
UNTO THE END, FOR AMALECH, UNDERSTANDING OF DAVID. This understanding belongs to David, for the woman in labor. That is the Church; she is the one in labor.
She lies in childbed; she is in distress; she suffers tribulation here. THE FOOL HAS SAID IN HIS HEART: THERE IS NO GOD.
Who is so foolish as to say that God does not exist, other than the one who does evil and says: God wills it so? He denies
that he is God. For if injustice pleases him, then he is not God. The Jews also said of Christ: HE IS NOT GOD. LET US KILL HIM.
They are corrupted. Those who deny God in this way are corrupted in their minds. And they have become abominable in their pleasures.
And therefore they are loathsome in their desires. Their wills are impure. There is none who does good; there is not even one.
Not one of them does good. The Lord looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there is anyone who understands or seeks God. God
looked down here from heaven upon the children of men, to see whether any of them knows God or desires him.
God does not need to look, for he knows all things; but he makes those in whom he dwells look. They look from heaven,
where their thoughts are. All have turned aside together. There he saw that they had all turned aside. They have become useless.
And they have become useless. There is none who does good; there is not even one. For they are only children of men.
not of God. Therefore there is not among them even one who does good. Do not all who work iniquity know?
Shall not all those who now do it, and do not want to know it, still come to know their wrong? The day is coming
when they will say: WHAT HAS PRIDE PROFITED US, AND THE BOASTING OF RICHES? ALL THOSE THINGS HAVE PASSED AWAY LIKE A SHADOW.
Who devour my people as food of bread. I mean those who devour my people like bread.
Who are as untiring at slaying them as at eating bread. They have not called upon God.
They did not call upon God to give them himself, but to give them honour and treasure here.
What they desired, that they called upon; that is what they wanted to come to them. There they trembled with fear, where there was no fear.
They were afraid for themselves where there was nothing to fear. They were afraid of losing riches, not wisdom,
which would have been worth more to them. For God scatters the bones of those who please men. For God breaks the bones of those
who please men. The Jews wanted to please the Romans; for that reason their bones were broken.
Christ wanted to please the saints and the faithful, who are sons of God, not sons of men; his bones were not broken.
They were confounded, because God despised them. They were put to shame, because God rejected them. And rightly so,
since they did not want to please God, and they said: THERE IS NO GOD. Who will give the salvation of Israel out of Zion?
Who will give Israel a saviour from Zion? Who, except the one of whom they said: THERE IS NO GOD? When the Lord turns back the captivity of Zion,
Jacob shall exult and Israel shall be glad. When God turns back Zion's exile, Jacob will leap for joy and Israel will rejoice.
The younger son, the true Jacob, the true Israel, he rejoices in it. When will that be? At the resurrection, on the last day.
TO THE END, IN HYMNS, UNDERSTANDING, FOR DAVID HIMSELF, WHEN THE ZIPHITES CAME AND SAID TO SAUL: IS NOT DAVID HIDDEN AMONG US?
To David himself there is understanding in hymns, that is, in this present psalm, which looks toward Christ.
He sang it then to Christ, at the time when the Ziphites came and told Saul that David was hidden [? text has 'born'] there among them. Ziph was the name of a town;
from it those who lived there were called Ziphites. 'Ziphites' is interpreted in Latin as florentes, that is, 'blooming'
and 'flourishing'. By them are signified sinners, who flourish here in the world
and are green. But David signifies Christians, who hide themselves here, but will be revealed at the judgment,
when Christ, their glory, comes. Now David prays that God may free him from them.
O GOD, SAVE ME IN YOUR NAME, and judge me in your strength. God, save me from the Ziphites
in your name, and judge in my favour in your strength. For when people curse, they say: MAY GOD JUDGE YOU.
With what boldness is it said here: JUDGE ME? Except that he said before: SAVE ME. As if he said: BY SAV-
-ING, JUDGE ME. O God, hear my prayer. God, hear my prayer, for I do not wait for the flower of the Ziphites. Give ear to the words of my mouth.
Take in with your ears the words of my mouth, for I desire to receive eternal goods. May the prayer come to fulfillment
and not turn away from your ears. For strangers have risen up against me. For strangers have risen up
against me. Why strangers? Are the Ziphites not of the tribe of Judah, as David is? Only in that they are wicked, and therefore strangers.
And the strong have sought my soul. And strong men sought my soul. Saul and his servants plotted against my life.
And they have not set God before their sight. And they did not set God before their eyes. That is to say,
they did not have God before their eyes. For his sake they did not leave off from it. For behold, God helps me. See now, God helps me,
inwardly, in secret, not outwardly. And the Lord is the upholder of my soul. And the Lord is the receiver
of my soul. There is his help. Turn back the evils upon my enemies. Turn evil away from me, onto my enemies.
That is not a curse but a prophecy of the fire to come. In your truth destroy them. In your truth destroy them.
They flourish now in their vanity; let them then perish in your truth. Willingly will I sacrifice to you.
Willingly I make offering to you. Willingly I praise you, not for the sake of anything else, but for your own sake. And I will confess to your name, for it is good.
And I confess to your name, for it is good. It is nothing other than good. You are called Good; that is your name.
For you have delivered me out of every tribulation. For that you released me from all afflictions, that has taught me
that your name is good, and the highest good. And my eye has looked down upon my enemies. And my eye looked down upon my enemies,
the Ziphites. I have looked past their flower by looking upon you, and have learned this: that all flesh is grass, and the glory of man is like the flower of grass.
UNTO THE END, IN HYMNS, UNDERSTANDING, FOR DAVID HIMSELF. Christ is the end. Christ is our perfection. Toward him looks
what is sung in these praises. These same praises are understanding for David, that is, for the Christian people. Why are they understanding for him?
Because here is not a region of rejoicing but of groaning, not of exulting but of lamenting. And if there is any exultation in our hearts,
it is in hope, in hope, not in reality. HEAR, O GOD, MY PRAYER, AND DO NOT DESPISE MY SUPPLICATION.
Hear, God, my plea, and do not disregard my entreaty. Attend to me and hear me. Pay heed to me
and hear me. I am saddened in my exercise. I have become unhappy in my exercising. That is to say, in the suffering
that has come upon me from the wicked, which exercises and chastens me, I am so overcome that I can scarcely bear it.
And I am troubled by the voice of the enemy and by the affliction of the sinner. And I am troubled before the voice of the enemy.
and from the tribulation of the sinner. I wanted to love those who hate me. Now infirmitas mentis (weakness of mind) hinders me,
that is, sickness of mind, and takes from me the clearness of the heart. "For they have turned iniquity upon me."
For my enemies turned their injustice upon me. They were my enemies unjustly, because I was kind to them.
"And in anger they were troublesome to me." And in their anger they were a burden to me. God wants me to be tested by this,
and he puts me to the trial with it. But that I should endure it is beyond my strength. "My heart is troubled within me." By this
thing my heart is troubled, because it weighs on me. "And the fear of death fell upon me." And the fear of death came upon me.
Hatred is death, as love is life. I feared hatred. "Fear and trembling came upon me, and darkness covered me."
Fear and trembling came upon me, and darkness covered me. Love is light, hatred is darkness, as it says:
"He who hates his brother is in darkness." "And I said." And then I said: "Who will give me wings like a dove, and I will fly and be at rest?"
Who will give me feathers like a dove's, so that I may fly and rest? Who will help me flee with love into solitude,
or die, so that enmity never overcomes me? "Behold, I have gone far off in flight, and stayed in the wilderness." Behold,
I have gone far away in flight, and I lived in solitude. I stayed in the secret place of the heart, where only God is with me.
There I sought rest and found sorrows. "I waited for the Lord, who would save me from faintness of spirit and from the storm."
So I waited for the Lord, that he might heal me of faint-heartedness and of the storm.
He slept in my ship while I was faint-hearted, and while I did not think about what he suffered for me.
When I remembered it, and he awoke in me, the waves grew calm. Then it no longer weighed on me that I suffered,
because I knew that he had suffered greater distress. "Cast them down, Lord." Strike them down, Lord. Make them fall,
because they are too high. "And divide their tongues." And divide their tongues, which speak with one voice for evil.
"For I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city." Because I saw injustice and contradiction in the city. That is why I fled into solitude,
because what was in the city displeased me. That is the city where the tongues were divided, which God cast down, though
all sinners still keep hurrying to build it. "Day and night iniquity shall surround it upon its walls."
Iniquity surrounds the city above the walls. Its injustice is higher than its walls. "And toil is in its midst, and injustice."
And in its midst are toil and injustice, that is, oppression and unspeakable judgments. "And usury and deceit have not departed from its streets."
And in its streets there was no lack of usury and deceit. He practises usury wickedly who gives little
and takes much. He practises usury worse who commits manslaughter over a word. "For if my enemy had cursed me."
I would surely have borne it. For if my enemy had spoken evil to me, I would have endured that. And if he who hated me had spoken great things against me,
I would surely have hidden myself from him. And if he who openly hates me had spoken arrogantly about me and had made threats against me,
then I would hide myself from him. I would give way to such people and go into the wilderness. But you, a man of one mind with me,
my guide and my acquaintance. But you, my like-minded one, my guide, my acquaintance, attacked me.
That weighs more heavily on me. You who took sweet food together with me. You ate together with me. We walked in the house of God in agreement.
You and I walked together in unity in the house of God. We confessed one God and prayed to one God,
whom you did not honour in me. Let death come upon them. Let death come upon those who are like this,
as fire took those who strove against Moses. And let them go down alive into hell. And let their leaders go alive to hell,
like Dathan and Abiram, who were the heads of the schism. But in the mystical sense, those go alive to hell
who are lost knowingly. For wickedness is in their dwellings. For malice is in their dwellings.
There, where they are to be only for a while, they show their wickedness. In the midst of them. In their midst. That is, their heart.
There is their malice. But I cried to God, and the Lord will save me. I, the Christian people, cried to God, and he saved me
and took me out from among the hostile. Evening and morning and noon I will tell and proclaim, and he will hear my voice.
In the evening [?], because Christ was then on the cross; in the morning, when Christ rose; at midday, when he was exalted
to the right hand of the Father, I tell and proclaim, and he hears my voice. He will redeem my soul in peace from those who draw near to me.
Though they storm against me, he redeems me in peace from those who draw near to me.
Why do you say "draw near"? For they were with me among many. For they were with me among the many who are chaff,
not with the few who are wheat. God will hear, and he who is before the ages will humble them. God hears me
and humbles them, he who is before the world. They are led by someone, I do not know who, who has come recently [?],
but he who reigned before the world humbles them. For there is no change for them, and they did not fear God. That is because
there is no change in their life, and they did not fear God. He stretched out his hand in repaying. He stretches out his hand to give reward.
At the judgment he repays them. They defiled his testament. They corrupted his testament. How does the scripture say?
IN YOUR SEED SHALL ALL NATIONS BE BLESSED. Whoever is a heretic and schismatic is separated from the body of Christ;
he does not seek the blessing in the seed of Abraham; therefore he does not listen to the testator. They were divided by the wrath of his face, and his heart drew near.
By his wrath they were divided, and then his heart drew near. When the Arians came, then in the Trinity God's [?]
...whose will was fully revealed. Then the right understanding of the Catholics came near.
Their questions were debated. From that point the truth began to shine. "His words are softer than oil, and they are darts."
His words are smoother and softer than oil, and those same words are arrows. God's words, which were hard,
have become soft. In that softness they have not lost their force; rather, the holy preachers have turned them into missiles.
"Cast your care upon God." Do not let the missiles frighten you. Cast your care upon God.
"And he will nourish you." And he will sustain you, and he is your harbor. "He will not let the righteous be tossed about forever."
So he does not let the righteous be tossed by the waves forever. If it happens for a while, that is exercise for him.
But what happens to the others? "But you, O God, will bring them down into the pit of destruction." You, God, cast them into the pit of perdition,
into the pool of the fire of hell. "Bloodthirsty and deceitful men shall not live out half their days." Murderers and deceivers do not live out half their days.
God cuts their days in half; they have no power over them. Though they promise themselves a long life, God is the one who does not give it to them.
"But I will hope in you, O Lord." But I hope in you, Lord, that you will not destroy me along with them.
TO THE END, FOR THE PEOPLE WHO HAVE BEEN MADE FAR FROM THE HOLY ONES. TO DAVID HIMSELF, FOR THE INSCRIPTION OF A TITLE, WHEN THE FOREIGNERS HELD HIM IN GATH.
This psalm is sung to David himself, that is, to Christ, about the people who were separated far from the holy ones
over the inscription of the title. For they said, "DO NOT WRITE 'THE KING OF THE JEWS',
BUT THAT HE SAID, 'I AM THE KING OF THE JEWS.'" By this they denied Christ, and that took their holiness from them. Thus sang
David when the allophyli, that is, the foreigners, held him in Gath, that is, in the winepress. If David is Christ,
how is he held in the winepress? Only in this sense: the Church, which is his body, suffers pressing here in the world.
In that pressing she gives the fruit of patience, just as the grape gives wine in the winepress. And so she should pray like this:
"HAVE MERCY ON ME, O GOD, FOR MAN HAS TRAMPLED ME." God, have mercy on me, because man has trampled me.
If you are a wine-grape, then you give wine when you are trampled. So do not fear the trampling.
"All day long he has fought and afflicted me." All day long he fought and oppressed me. That is the voice of all "WHO WISH TO LIVE GODLY IN CHRIST JESUS,"
because they are never free of war at any time. "My enemies have trampled me all day long, from the height of the day," that is, from worldly pride.
All day long my enemies trampled me because of their pride, which does not last long. "For many who make war on me will be afraid."
This happens because many who now attack me will fear for themselves on the Day of Judgment. Then they will burn [?] for
what they now do for their own pleasure. "But I will hope in you, O Lord." But I hope in you.
Therefore I shall not need to be afraid then. Those who are now insensible (stupidi), that is, those who feel nothing of their own state,
and have lost the sense of pain (sensum doloris), will then become fearful (timidi). In God I will praise my words. In God I will praise my words.
For he gave them to me; he makes them be good. In God I have hoped; I will not fear what flesh may do to me.
In God I have trusted. I do not fear what man may do to me. A grape I was; I was trodden; wine I become. All day long they abhorred my words. All day long
my words were abhorred. But in them God, who gave them to me, was abhorred. All their counsels are against me for evil.
All their counsels are aimed at evil against me. That separates them from the saints. They will dwell, and they will hide.
They dwell in the holy Church, and hide what they are. What do they do? They will watch my heel.
They watch my heel; they lie in wait to see whether I slip, whether I do wrong even in a single word. As my soul has endured.
As I have suffered, as I also knew before, as has often happened to me at their hands. For nothing you will save them.
Even such people you save for nothing, freely; and without any merit of theirs you save many like them.
Such a persecutor was Saul before he became Paul. In wrath you will break the peoples.
In your wrath you soften the peoples. That wrath is fatherly; with it you correct them.
You chastise them, and by that they are saved. O God, I have declared my life to you. To you, God, I made known my life.
I praised you for this, that you made me live. By your grace I live; to you I confess it, as Paul confessed when he said:
I WHO WAS BEFORE A BLASPHEMER AND A PERSECUTOR AND INSOLENT, BUT I OBTAINED MERCY.
You have set my tears in your sight, as in your promise, that is, as you have spoken. You looked upon my tears,
as you promised when you said: CALL UPON ME IN THE DAY OF TROUBLE AND I WILL DELIVER YOU. My enemies will be turned back.
My enemies will be turned backward. It is better for them to go after you than to wait in front of you.
On whatever day I call upon you, behold, I have known that you are my God. On whatever day I call upon you, I know that you are my God.
By this you show that you are my God: because you help me when I ask. You are the God of all, but mine
in particular, and of those to whom you give yourself. In God I will praise the word. In the Lord I will praise the speech. In God I have hoped;
I will not fear what man may do to me. This has been explained before. In me, O God, are vows, which I will render as praises to you.
I have within me the promises of praise which I will render to you in the other world, for such comfort.
What kind of comfort? Because you have rescued my soul from death, my eyes from tears, my feet from falling.
That you will then have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears.
so that your praise may resound over all. They prepared a snare for my feet. They set a snare for my feet.
I walked on earth with rebuke and with promise, as if with two feet. There they lay in wait for me.
And they bowed down my soul. And they made me stoop, for among them I was bowed, not upright.
and their works always looked to the earth. They dug a pit before my face, and they fell into it. They dug pits for me.
and they plunged into them. They were overthrown in them, not I. Whoever wishes to betray another
is himself betrayed. My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready. Now my heart is ready, since you will it so, God.
It is ready to endure their wickedness. I will sing and recite a psalm. Therefore I sing to you, and sing psalms to you thus.
Arise, my glory. Stand up, my glory. Show yourself by rising again and ascending. Arise, psaltery and harp.
Stand up and show yourselves, miracles and sufferings. In the psaltery the strings sound from the upper part.
From there came Christ's miracles. But in the harp they sound from the lower part; from there were Christ's sufferings. Let the psaltery sound,
so the dead rise, and the blind, the lame, the paralysed and the sick are healed. Let the harp sound, that Christ suffers hunger and thirst,
that he sleeps, is seized, is scourged, is mocked, mocked, is crucified, is buried. I will arise at dawn. I arise early.
At daybreak the psaltery and harp arose, that is, the Lord's body. I will confess to you among the peoples, Lord, and I will sing a psalm to you among the nations.
I confess to you among the peoples, Lord, and sing a psalm to you among the nations. That is now fulfilled, for psalms and
the praises of God are in all kingdoms. For your truth is magnified up to the heavens, and your mercy up to the clouds.
For your truth is magnified up to heaven, and your mercy up to the clouds.
This is to be read in reversed order, for truth is pure in the angels, and through mercy it is also shared with the men
who are preachers of the truth. Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and your glory above all the earth. That stands earlier.
UNTO THE END, DESTROY NOT DAVID, FOR AN INSCRIPTION OF A TITLE. That also stands before the previous psalm. IF YOU TRULY SPEAK JUSTICE,
judge what is right, sons of men. Christ says to the Jews: If you children of men speak what is right, then judge it rightly.
Judge it just as you speak it. Many speak what they do not judge that way. They say, if someone asks them,
that good faith is better than treasure, and yet they do not judge it so, for treasure is dearer to them.
If they were in earnest about it, they would show it; then they would not exchange good faith for treasure.
For in your heart you work iniquities on the earth. You work unrighteousness on earth in your heart. All who are on earth
have their hearts full of unrighteousness before it comes to deeds. How does that show?
Your hands fashion iniquity. Your hands contrive injustice. It comes from the heart to the hands.
That is why your hands are in league with injustice. Sinners are estranged from the womb. Sinners went astray from their mother's womb.
From what did they go astray? From the truth, from the kingdom of God, from the blessed life. God knew their wickedness
before they were born. Or else it means that they were removed from the womb of holy Church.
They went astray from the womb. They wandered from the womb, where truth is. How so?
They spoke false things. That is why they lie, and that is why they became heretics. Their wrath is like a serpent's.
Their wrath, the wrath of the Jews, is like a serpent's. Like that of the deaf asp, which stops its ears. Like that of the deaf asp
which stops its ears. It makes itself deaf so that it will not hear the charmer
who wants to lure it out of its hole. It does this by pressing one ear against the ground
and plugging the other one with its tail. Which will not hear the voice of the charmers, nor the spells that are chanted by the wise one.
So it does not hear the voice of the charmers, nor the spells that are sung by the one skilled in the art.
The people who disputed with Stephen in the Acts of the Apostles imitated it: they stopped their ears when they heard the name of Christ.
God will break their teeth in their mouth. God crushes their teeth in their mouth. They wanted to bite him
when they asked him, 'Is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar or not?', whichever answer he gave, 'It is lawful' or 'It is not lawful'.
But he broke their teeth in their mouth when he said, 'Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar's,
and to God the things that are God's.' So they went back to the people who had sent them
with the report that no one could answer him. The Lord will break the molars of the lions. The Lord breaks the lions' jaw-teeth.
They were asps in their cunning and lions in their cruelty. The lion's roar was 'Crucify him, crucify him.' But the crucified one rose again, and the faithful spread over
the whole world, and kings worshipped him. Where was their savagery then? What could they do then? By then the lions' jaw-teeth had been broken.
They will come to nothing, like water running away. They pass away like a sudden flood that soon runs off. He bends his bow until they are weakened.
God bends his bow until they grow weak. He frightens them and makes them stop, as he did to Saul
when he said, 'Why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the goad.' Like melted wax they will be taken away.
But those who do not mend their ways because of these threats, and who here are like wax melted by the fire of desire,
will be taken away from his sight. Their impurity does not let them come before him.
Fire fell upon them. The fire fell upon them. Desires of many kinds came upon them. And they did not see the sun.
And therefore they did not see God, who is the true sun. Before your thorns bring forth the bramble,
as if living, as if in wrath, he swallows them up. He says "your thorns" in place of "their thorns." God swallows them up
before their thorns bring forth the bramble. He destroys them before their wickedness grows strong. The thorns on the bramble are soft at first;
after that they become terribly hard and strong. As if they were living, he swallows them up; but they are dead,
though they seem to themselves to be alive. And as if in wrath, when in fact he is acting for good. When he says "he swallows them up,"
it is as if he said: he takes them away and does not let them live as long as they had intended.
The just man shall rejoice when he sees the vengeance. The righteous man rejoices when he sees in the sinners the punishment of the first sin.
That is evil desire, which comes from the first sin. The just man flees from it; therefore he has a pure conscience
and rejoices. He shall wash his hands in the blood of the sinner. He washes his hands in the sinner's blood. That is to say,
he becomes better because of the sinner's ruin. As the wise Solomon says: "When the fool perishes, the wise man becomes more astute."
And man shall say: If indeed there is fruit for the just man, then indeed there is a God who judges them on earth. And so people say: If the righteous man gains profit,
if he has his reward even here, then God is on earth, judging over them, before the Day of Judgment comes. So this is true:
he gives the righteous spiritual joy here as an advance payment, and eternal life hereafter.
Unto the end. Destroy not. For David, for an inscription of a title, when Saul sent and watched his house in order to kill him.
David sang this psalm when Saul sent men and besieged his house in order to kill him there.
The other part of this title was explained earlier. Saul signifies the Jews, who set a guard on the sepulchre of Christ
so that they might destroy him in his members. For if they could deny the resurrection, his name would be destroyed.
Against them Christ now prays: Deliver me from my enemies, my God. Free me from my enemies, my God.
And from those who rise up against me set me free. And save me from those who attack me. Deliver me from those who work iniquity.
Free me from those who act unjustly. And from men of blood save me. And protect me from murderers.
For behold, they have seized my soul. For they have captured me. They have brought me into the distress of the Passion.
The strong have rushed upon me. Strong ones have set upon me: the devil and his servants. Neither my iniquity nor my sin,
O Lord. There is no injustice and no sin in me. Without iniquity I ran, and I was directed.
Without injustice I ran, and I turned rightly to where I was meant to go. Even though they are strong,
they cannot follow me. Arise to meet me. Stand up toward me; help me so that I may rise again. And see.
And let them see the direction of my course; that is, so that others may see it and follow me,
and recognize me as like you. And you, O Lord God of hosts, God of Israel. And you, Lord, mighty God, God of Israel,
of a single people, as people suppose. Attend to visit all the nations. Hasten to visit all peoples. Bring them all to faith.
Have no mercy on all who work iniquity. Nor do you forgive it to all who work injustice.
Do not let it go unpunished. Either they themselves pay for it, or you make them pay for it. There are also sins
which God does not forgive. These are the sins of those who say: "If God had not willed it, I would not have done it."
They lay their guilt on God, which is intolerable. They shall return at evening,
and they shall suffer hunger like dogs. At evening they will be converted, that is, at the end of the world. For when Elijah and Enoch come,
then the Jews will become believers. Then they will hunger for the faith, like the Gentiles, whom they called dogs
because the Gentiles seemed unclean to them. And they shall go round about the city. And they go around the city.
They travel around the whole world preaching. What Paul and the other apostles did, they will then do. Behold, they shall speak with their mouth,
and a sword is in their lips. Then they will speak with their mouth what is not now in their mind, and there is a sword in their lips,
that is, the word of God. For who has heard? For who heard it? They say this angrily, which is the sword in their lips:
why do others not hear what they themselves would not hear before? As if they themselves had not been converted
at evening. And you, O Lord, shall laugh at them. And you, Lord, mock those who will not hear your word.
You shall bring all the nations to nothing. You count all unbelieving peoples as nothing. Or it means: for you it is easy,
and as nothing, to convert all peoples. I will keep my strength for you. I keep my strength with you,
because apart from you I do not have it; if I go away from you, I lose it.
For you, God, are my protector. For you are the one who takes me up. I was wicked; I lay in sins; from there you took me
and drew me to you. My God, his mercy shall go before me. He is my God, whose grace goes before me.
I did no good unless he first urged me to it. My God, show me among my enemies.
My God, show me your grace among my enemies, so that they too may be made better
and turn from enemies into friends. Do not slay them, lest at any time they forget your law. Do not slay them,
lest they then forget your law. Do not slay the Jews in that way,
so that they forget your law. Let them endure until evening, and then convert them.
"Scatter them in your power." Scatter them in your strength, as far as the Roman empire extends. "And destroy them, O Lord, my protector."
And destroy them, that is, their unrighteousness, my Lord, my protector. "The offences of their mouth, the speech of their lips."
Do not slay them; slay the misdeed of their mouth, slay the word of their lips. Bring them into the bride,
so that they may see him whom they demanded be put to death risen to life. "And let them be caught in their pride."
And let them be caught in their arrogance. How foolishly they thought themselves strong, slaying a man in whom God lived!
"And from cursing and lying they shall be pulled out." And so they will be taken out of cursedness and out of lying. That brings
them to repentance and to baptism. "In the wrath of consummation," that is, of perfection. In the anger of perfection.
In that they will be saved. They will grow angry at themselves [the text is garbled here, but this is the probable reading]; that will make them perfect. "And they will not be," that is, proud.
And then they will not be as proud as they were. They will acknowledge their guilt and say to the apostles:
"WHAT SHALL WE DO, BRETHREN?" Then they will hear: "REPENT, AND LET EACH ONE OF YOU BE BAPTIZED."
"And they shall know that God will rule over Jacob and over the ends of the earth." And then they will know that God rules not only over the Jews
but over all the ends of the earth. And how does it come about? "They shall return at evening, and shall suffer hunger like dogs."
Afterwards, late, after Christ was slain, they will be converted, and will be hungry like dogs. "And they shall go round the city."
And they will preach to the gentiles, who are called the city of the surrounding region. Paul was one of these dogs.
This verse refers to the Passion; the one before it, which is like it, refers to the end of the world. "They shall be scattered to eat."
They will be scattered to eat spiritual food, as it was said to Peter: "KILL AND EAT."
"But if they are not filled, they will murmur." From this it happens that, if they are not filled, they murmur.
As in this: "WHO HAS BELIEVED WHAT WE HEARD?" "But I will sing of your power." But I sing of your strength, Father, in my members
when they come fully into your sight. "And I will rejoice in your mercy in the morning." And in the morning I will rejoice in your grace.
When this night of the world passes and the true sun shines forth, then I will rejoice in them. "For you have become my upholder."
For you are the one who receives me. You receive me and keep me in your kingdom. "And my refuge in the day of my tribulation."
And my refuge on the day of my torment. When I am in need, I flee to you. "My helper, to you I will sing psalms,
for you, God, are my upholder." My helper, to you I sing, for you are the one who receives me. "My God, my mercy."
My God, my grace. How is he my grace? Whatever I am [?], that comes from your grace.
TO THE END, FOR THOSE WHO SHALL BE CHANGED, FOR THE INSCRIPTION OF THE TITLE, TO DAVID HIMSELF, FOR TEACHING, WHEN HE SET FIRE TO MESOPOTAMIA OF SYRIA.
"And Syria Sobal. And he turned Moab, and struck Edom in the Valley of the Salt Pits, twelve thousand." This psalm looks to Christ. It is sung for those
who are to be changed, in keeping with the inscription, so that they turn from King Devil to Christ,
the king of the Jews: to serve David himself, Christ himself, and to give thought to his teaching. So it came about
when the true David burned Mesopotamia of Syria and Syria Sobal. He burned them rightly, as the interpretations of the names show.
Mesopotamia means "exalted calling," Syria "lofty," Sobal "vain oldness." Pride, vanity and oldness were burned by him
who came to send fire on the earth. And he converted Moab, that is, the enemy, and struck Edom, that is, the earthly.
He converted hostile people and earthly people. He struck twelve thousand in the Valley of the Salt Pits.
Those settled toward the twelve winds he made to live in humility and in the savor of wisdom, dead to the world, living to God.
"O God, you have cast us off and destroyed us." In these words Christians thank Christ for changing them.
You, God, have thrust us back, because you did not allow us to go the wrong way.
And you tore us down so that we might be built up better. "You were angry." You were angry at the old error.
"And you have had mercy on us." And you took pity on us, teaching us newness of life. "You have moved the earth."
You shook the earth: you made sinners recognize themselves. "And you have troubled it." And you brought it into fear
and also into sorrow. "Heal its breaches, for it is moved." Heal the crushing of their minds, for they have been moved to penitence.
Comfort them with pardon. "You have shown your people hard things." You showed your people hard and toilsome things
in persecution. "You have made us drink the wine of compunction." You gave us the wine of compunction to drink. What is that wine?
"You have given a sign to those who fear you." You gave a sign to those who fear you, in the distresses of persecution,
"so that they may flee from before the bow." So that they may flee before the bow that shoots at sinners.
The faster someone wants to shoot, the farther back the string of the bow is drawn.
God also delays judgment so that it may be all the sharper. "So that your beloved may be delivered." So that your beloved ones may be delivered.
So that they may be delivered by fleeing the bow, hard things happen to them here.
"Save me with your right hand." Preserve me with your right hand, since I must suffer worldly distress.
"And hear me." And hear me, for prayer for heavenly goods is worthier to you than prayer for earthly ones.
"God has spoken in his holy one." God the Father spoke in his holy Son Christ, saying that it shall go this way.
"I will rejoice." I, his people, am glad of this. "And I will divide Shechem," that is, "shoulders." And I divide the shoulders.
who bear the burden of the Lord, in the varied distribution of the Holy Spirit. The idols were buried by Jacob in Shechem. Therefore
the place signifies the gentiles, who afterwards offered their shoulders to the burden of Christian devotion.
And I will measure out the valley of tabernacles, that is, the people of the Jews. And the valley of the encampments, where Jacob stalled his sheep,
I measure out for myself as a share. I am gathered from Jews and gentiles. Gilead is mine, that is, the heap of witness. The multitude of martyrs is mine.
From them too I am gathered. And Manasseh is mine, that is, forgotten. Forgetfulness of my persecution will yet come to me
when I may dwell in peace. And Ephraim, that is, fruitfulness, is the strength of my head. And the strength of my head is my fruitfulness.
The death of Christ is my multiplication. THE DEAD GRAIN OF WHEAT BRINGS FORTH MUCH FRUIT. Judah is my king. I acknowledge the inscription.
CHRIST is my king. Moab, that is, the gentiles, is the pot of my hope. The people that came from an unlawful union, that is the pot of my hope.
Because it has become a pot, because it has been fired in the fire of persecution, therefore it has shown me the hope of its salvation, not of its consumption.
Into Idumea, that is, the earthly, I will stretch out my shoe. Even to those who lead an earthly life I stretch out my shoe.
I send thither feet shod in the preparation of the gospel of peace. To me the foreigners are subject. Strangers worship me, says CHRIST.
WHO ARE NOT TO REIGN WITH ME. Who will lead me into the city of the surrounding region? That is, among the gentiles, who are spread around the one nation of the Jews.
Who leads my preachers to all the peoples settled all around the Jews? Who but God? Who will lead me even into Idumea?
Who makes me known even to those who do not wish to profit from me? Is it not you, O God, who have cast us off? Do
you not do it, you who thrust us away from the old error? As the psalm said earlier?
And you will not go forth, that is, you will not appear, in our forces. You do not show yourself in our strength as you did in the time of Moses
and Joshua son of Nun, and David, when hostile gentiles could not resist us. Inwardly you teach us,
inwardly you strengthen us. If we wished to fight, the fight would be for the present life, not for the future one.
Give us help from tribulation. Give us all the more help in tribulation, since people think we are without help from you.
And vain is the salvation of man. Give us help, give us salvation; give it to us inwardly. The outward salvation of man
is vain. In God we shall do valiantly, and not by the sword. In God we show the virtue of patience, not of resistance.
And he will bring to nothing those who afflict us. And he brings to nothing those who afflict us. As is now evident: where are they?
UNTO THE END, IN HYMNS, TO DAVID HIMSELF. This psalm looks to Christ, sung in praise of David himself, of CHRIST himself.
HEAR, O GOD, MY SUPPLICATION; attend to my prayer. Hear, O God, my plea; look to my prayer,
take heed of it. Who says this? THE FAITHFUL PEOPLE. From the ends of the earth I have cried to you. I cried out to you.
from the ends of the world, as far as your possession extends. Holy Church is spread through all regions of the world.
From there she cries out; from there hear her. "While my heart was in anguish." When my heart was oppressed by the temptations of the flesh.
"You have lifted me up on the rock." On the rock you lifted me up. You are a high and firm rock; on it you set me, so that
the anguish of temptation and persecution may not overthrow me. "You have led me, because you have become my hope." You are my leader.
You lead me, so that I follow you to the other life, because you are my hope
and I desire to gain nothing else. "A tower of strength in the face of the enemy." You are a strong tower to me against the enemy.
Whoever takes refuge in you, the enemy has no power over him. "I will dwell in your tabernacle forever," that is, until the end of the world.
I, your people, am a dweller in your Church until the end of this world. "I shall be protected under the covering of your wings."
I shall be protected under the cover of your wings against the anguish of temptations. "For you, O God, have heard my prayer."
That is why I shall be protected: because you heard my prayer as often as I said, "HEAR MY SUPPLICATION."
"You have given" (you heard my prayer) "an inheritance to those who fear your name." You have given an inheritance to those who fear you.
The inheritance is in heaven. "Days upon days of the king." In eternity there is one day of the king, CHRIST, in addition to these days
that he lived through here. "You will add to his years until the day of generation," namely this one, "and of generation," namely the future one.
You, Father, add his years to him until the day of this birth and of that one.
He reigns in both. "He will remain forever in the sight of God." He will remain forever before his Father.
Or: the faithful people will remain forever before him. "Who will seek out mercy and truth for him?" Who learns mercy for him,
and truth? Many learn them from books, yet do not show them by doing, only by teaching.
Such people learn them for themselves, not for God. Or it means: Who will demand, there in that world, that mercy be shown,
where no one is in need of it? Or truth, where no one goes astray? "So will I sing a psalm to your name forever and
ever, that I may fulfil my vows from day to day." So may I sing a psalm forever,
so that from this day on I keep my vows until that day.
TO THE END, FOR IDITHUN, A PSALM OF DAVID HIMSELF. This psalm looks toward the end. It is sung for the one who leaps over, to David himself,
to CHRIST himself. Who is the one who leaps over, for whom this psalm is sung? All the worldly people, whom he, looking down on them from above,
would gladly draw up to himself by this song, so that together with him they would despise earthly things.
He is above others, and above him is another. To that one he sings thus: "SHALL NOT MY SOUL BE SUBJECT TO GOD?"
Am I not subject to God? I am your superior; should you not be likewise? For from him is my salvation.
Rightly so, for from him CHRIST, my saviour, has been sent here into the world. For he is my God and my saviour,
my protector. He is truly my God, and the one who keeps me and receives me. I shall not be moved any more. Since he receives me,
I shall no longer be moved to wrongdoing. Since that is so: how long will you set upon a man?
How long, then, will you heap upon anyone so firmly established reproaches and false accusations? Will you kill them all?
How long will you slay all those so firmly established, whom you cannot turn to follow you? As if they were a leaning wall and a battered fence?
Why do you think you can treat them like a leaning wall and a fence pushed down,
which would fall even without a push? That I endure from you pagans. There were others who did not do that. But yet my honour
they planned to cast down. But yet they wanted to obstruct my honour. Heretics and false Christians were against those
who wanted to worship me with sincere faith. I ran in thirst. I ran after them in thirst. I longed for them; they did not long for me.
With their mouth they blessed, and with their heart they cursed. They partake of my body and blood, but they were not of a kindly mind.
But yet my soul shall be subject to God. But yet, says Idithun, my soul shall be subject to God.
Persecution does not take it from me. For from him is my patience. For such patience is granted to me by him.
Without God a human being could not endure that. For he is my God. For he is my God;
therefore he invites me here to himself. And my saviour. And my saviour: therefore he justifies me here.
So he saves me. My protector. My receiver: therefore he will glorify me there in the other world. I shall not depart.
I shall not go out, once I am received into his house. From then on I shall be there. In God is my salvation and my glory.
In God is my salvation and my glory. In him I am not only saved but also glorious.
That I shall attain there, where the righteous shall shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. What is my comfort in the meantime? The God of my help.
That is God, who helps me amid all the troubles of the world. And my hope is in God. And my hope is in him,
until both come to me, salvation and glory. Hope in him, all the assembly of the people. Trust in him, all you multitudes of people.
In him you will not be deceived. Pour out your hearts before him. Pour out your hearts before him, praying,
confessing, weeping. What you pour out in this way, you will not lose. God is our helper. For God is our helper; no other
is so strong. But yet the sons of men are vain. But yet the sons of men are vain. If you put your trust in them,
then you will see that they are false. God, however, is strong. The sons of men are liars on the scales. The children of men are liars.
on the scales. They have deceitful scales, most of all in that they weigh themselves wrongly, judging themselves righteous
when they are not so. "That they themselves may deceive, out of vanity, into the same thing," that is, into one. That is, out of vanity they deceive in one way.
Because they all take their deceiving from vanity, they therefore deceive in one way. "Do not hope in iniquity."
Do not place your hope in injustice. Do not rely on gaining anything by fraud
or by guile. Put your trust in God, passing over together with me. "And do not covet in robbery."
And do not desire to gain anything by plundering, even though you are poor, even though you are in need of it. "If riches abound,"
but if riches have come pouring in to you, "do not set your heart on them." Then do not let your heart rest on them,
and do not think that they make you blessed. "God has spoken once." In Christ the Father spoke once,
and commanded everything that exists to come into being all together. He commanded all at once in eternity that those things should come into being which came one by one in time.
"These two things I have heard." These two things I heard as I passed over: "that power belongs to God, and mercy to you, Lord." For the power is God's,
and mercy belongs to you, Lord. These two you make plain: how mighty and how merciful you are.
"For you will render to each according to his works." For you reward each one according to his works: as the mightier toward the wicked, as the more merciful toward the good.
When David was in the wilderness of Idumea, this psalm was his song. Here in the world is the wilderness of holy Church.
Here she is thirsty. Thirsting, she sings thus: "O God, my God, to you from the light," that is, at daybreak,
"I keep watch." O God, my God, I keep watch for you at dawn. Your dawn wakes me. When day breaks for me from you,
and you make me know the truth, then I become watchful for you, not for worldly desires. "For you my soul"
My soul thirsts for you. It longs only for the sight of you. "How manifoldly for you my flesh," that is, as manifoldly as it labors,
so manifoldly it thirsts. How manifoldly my flesh thirsts for you, because it is also troubled in many ways
about food, drink, clothing, sleep, expense, and countless other things. Because of all these it longs for the resurrection.
"In a desert land, without a way and without water." Here in a land that is desolate, without a road and without water.
What is that? This world. Christ found it desolate. But when he came into it,
then those drew near to him for whom he became the way and to whom he gave the water of the Holy Spirit. "So in the holy place I have appeared before you,"
"that I might see your power and your glory." In that same wilderness I appeared before you with a holy mind, with so holy a purpose,
that I might see from there your power and your glory, and might come to understand how far both of them surpass all else.
"For your mercy is better than lives." For your mercy is better than all lives are.
which they have chosen for themselves in various ways: trading, farming, money-lending, soldiering. Only one life is eternal,
the one that your grace gives. That one is above all others. "My lips shall praise you." For such grace my lips praise you.
"Thus will I bless you in my life." So I praise you in my life, looking upon that same grace
then, from which I have it eternally. "And in your name I will lift up my hands." And in your name I lift up my hands.
Here in Idumea, here in the wilderness, I will keep this daily practice: to lift up my hands in prayer
and to good works. "Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness." So may my soul be filled with marrow and with fatness.
May it be filled with all good things in that world. Or it means: from such prayer,
in which I advance toward you with good works, may the fullness of heavenly wisdom come to me. "And with lips of rejoicing they shall praise your name."
And after that the lips of my joy shall praise your name. When the time of prayer passes,
then comes the time of praise, in that life. Then comes refreshment from the wilderness, then comes refreshment from the thirst, then joy has come.
"If I have remembered you upon my bed, I will meditate on you at dawn, because you have become my helper." If I remembered you while at rest,
then I will also think of you at dawn, because you gave me help. Humility in prosperity makes me mindful at dawn,
that is, at work, because dawn is the time for work. Whoever does not forget God in prosperity
does not forget him in any deed. God also helps him, so that he does not grow weary of it.
"And in the shelter of your wings I will rejoice. Protect me under the shadow of your wings." Shelter me under the shadow of your wings,
so that the kite does not snatch me away. You know that I am without strength. Shelter me from the enemy.
"My soul has cleaved behind you." Behind you my soul clings to you. Not in front of you,
nor beside you, but behind you. What happens to someone who wants to go in front of Christ?
The same as happened to Peter when he tried to turn Christ away from his passion with these words: "Far be it from you, Lord; be merciful
to yourself." And Christ answered him: "Get behind me, Satan, for you do not understand the things that are of God, but the things that are of men."
Because Peter thought his own counsel should go before God's counsel, Christ rebuked him. "Your right hand has upheld me."
Christ, your right hand, received me, to protect me under his wings. "But they have sought my soul in vain."
But they sought my soul in vain, the soul of Christ, my head, not to believe in it but to persecute it.
Who did that? The Jewish enemies. "They shall go into the lower parts of the earth." Far down into the earth they go, that is, into earthly desires.
Worrying about the earth, they said: "Lest perhaps the Romans come and take away our place and our nation." What then?
As it says: "What the wicked man fears shall come upon him." They killed Christ to keep their land. Because they killed Christ,
they lost both their nation and their land. "They shall be handed over to the power of the sword." They will be killed. "They shall be a portion for foxes."
They will be given to the foxes as their share. They will become like foxes, which have holes in the earth. Or else the Roman kings are called foxes,
just as Christ called Herod a fox. Or else foxes and wolves eat their dead bodies. "But the king shall rejoice in God." But Christ, the true king,
whom they thought they had killed, rejoices in God the Father over the redemption of humankind, the redemption of humankind, at His right hand.
