"All who swear by Him shall be praised," that is, those who make vows to Him and keep them. All those who make promises to Him and keep them will be praised.

"For the mouth of those who speak wicked things is stopped." For the mouth of the wicked is stopped, that is, of the Jews and the persecutors. The Lion of the tribe of Judah has won the victory. He has silenced them.
To the end. A psalm of David.
"Hear my prayer, O God, while I am in distress." Hear my prayer, God, when I am oppressed in persecution. This is the voice of the body of Christ.
"Rescue my soul from fear of the enemy." Free my soul from fear of the enemy. May it never happen to me as it happened to those
who denied Christ out of fear and were swallowed up in this way, that is, they became like their enemies,
because they passed over into their enemies' body. "You have protected me from the crowd of those who do wrong." You protected me from the crowd
of the Jews who did wrong. This is the voice of the head. His divine nature protected Him, so that no one took His soul from Him,
but He gave it up willingly Himself and sent it where He wished. "For they have sharpened their tongues like a sword."
For they sharpened their tongues like a sword. They killed Him with those tongues when they said, "Crucify, crucify Him!"
Then it became clear how sharp they were. "They have bent the bow, a bitter thing." They bent bows, that is, they set secret traps for Him,
and hurried to betray Him through His own disciple. That is the terrible thing they did. "So that they may shoot the spotless one in secret."
Why did they bend their bows against Him? So that they could shoot the spotless lamb. Was that not a bitter thing? "They will shoot Him suddenly and will not be afraid."
They shoot Him suddenly, and they are not afraid of doing so. They thought it was sudden. But how could anything be sudden to Him
who knows all things beforehand? "They have fixed an evil word firmly on themselves." Because they did not fear Him, they fixed on themselves, to their own ruin,
that wicked word: "He deserves death. Crucify, crucify Him!" But when Pilate was afraid for Him and declared Him free of guilt with these words,
"I find no reason for death in this man," did they not fix the evil word on themselves once again?
What did they say? "His blood be on us and on our children." "They planned to hide snares."
"They said: Who will see them?" They decided to hide their snares so that no one would notice them.
They said, "Who sees them?" As if He who knows everything did not know them. "They have searched out wicked deeds."
"They failed, searching out searchings," that is, they failed while turning over and seeking out bitter and sharp counsels. They searched out the wrong thoroughly.
Searching and searching, they failed. Standing behind a subtle counsel, they failed, because it could not be
that they should plot it and yet be guiltless. The subtle plan went like this: "Let him be handed over not by us, but by his own disciple.
Let him be killed not by us, but by the judge. Let us do everything, and seem to have done nothing." "Man shall come to a deep heart,
and God shall be exalted." That is: man shall come in a deep heart, and God shall be exalted in the power of his majesty. What does Christ the man do after that?
He comes forward and lets himself be crucified, and his hidden heart conceals the Godhead.
And when the man is slain, then God is exalted; then he reveals himself. "The arrows of children have become their wounds."
Their arrows became children's arrows, which children make out of stalks to shoot with.
They could do no more. "And their tongues have been made weak against them." And their own tongues turned against them.
They lied when they said: "Let him come down from the cross and we will believe him." Why did they not do so
when the soldiers told them that he had risen? Was it not a greater thing to rise from the tomb than to come down from the cross?
Were their tongues not turned against them then, when they said: "We give you money,
and say that his disciples came while you were sleeping and took him away"? Were they not defeated then
in their searchings? Was not everything they had plotted made void then? "All who saw them were troubled," that is, saw that they had failed in searching out their counsels.
Then all the other Jews were troubled when they saw the chief priests and elders failing like this,
and saw miracles being done by Christ's disciples in his name. "And every man feared." And everyone feared him. Whoever did not fear him was not a man;
he should rather be counted among the beasts. Then those who were terrified said to Peter and to the other apostles: "What shall we do, men and brethren?"
Then they heard: "Do penance, and let every one of you be baptized." "And they declared the works of God."
Then they made known God's works: the resurrection and the ascension. "And they understood his deeds." And then they perceived that his works
were divine. "The righteous shall rejoice in the Lord." Now the righteous man rejoices in the risen Lord.
"And he shall hope in him." And he puts his hope in him, not in worldly comfort. "And all the upright of heart shall be praised."
And all who are upright in their hearts will be praised, that is, those who are pleased with God's will.
To the end, a psalm of David, a song of Jeremiah and Ezekiel, from the people of the exile, when they began to go out. These words have the following construction:
To the end, a psalm of David, concerning the people of the exile, through the prophecy of Jeremiah and Ezekiel, when they began to go out. David's psalm looks toward Christ,
who is his song of joy, sung by the exiled people because exile had befallen them.
according to the prophecy of Jeremiah and Ezekiel. When did he sing it? When he saw in the prophetic spirit that they would begin to depart from there.
There we see how Paul said: "NOW THESE THINGS HAPPENED TO THEM IN FIGURE." In our times, those are in captivity
who are in desire [of the world]. But those who begin to go from there to love, David means them; to them he sings this song of joy.
A HYMN BEFITS YOU, O GOD, IN ZION. That is the voice of those going out of captivity. To you, God, a song of praise is fitting in Zion, not in Babylon.
Those who have their hope in Zion sing in Zion; they sing in contemplation. And to you shall the vow be paid in Jerusalem.
And the vow shall be fulfilled to you in Jerusalem. He who here has united himself to God as a living sacrifice
will become it more fully in the heavenly Jerusalem. There he will become a holocaust, that is, wholly burnt.
Everything mortal, everything corruptible will there be consumed in him by the divine fire. Hear my prayer; to you all flesh shall come.
that is, from every kind of flesh. Hear my prayer; to you come people of every kind. From every nation, from every condition come those
who become a holocaust there. The words of the wicked have prevailed over us. The teaching of wicked forefathers overpowered us.
They led us to Jupiter and to Mercury. Through their fault we worshipped wood and stones, the works of our hands.
And you will be merciful to our impieties. And you, the priest, will atone for our evils, when you offer yourself to the Father as the evening sacrifice;
then the error will be forgiven. Blessed is he whom you have chosen and taken up. Blessed is the man whom you chose
and took to yourself. He shall dwell in your courts. He dwells in your courts. It is one man,
one faithful people, whose head is Christ. He chose him, he gave him a dwelling. He bids him be where he himself is.
We shall be filled with the good things of your house. We shall be filled with the good that is in your house. Which good?
WHAT EYE HAS NOT SEEN, NOR EAR HEARD, NOR HAS IT ENTERED INTO THE HEART OF MAN. Or as it says next:
Your temple is holy, wonderful in justice. That your holy house is wonderful in righteousness: with that fullness you fill us.
He will be filled with blessedness who makes himself a holy temple for you, wonderful in justice. Hear us, O God our savior.
Our savior, hear us. The hope of all the ends of the earth and of those far off on the sea. The hope of all the ends of the earth,
the hope of the outermost just as of the innermost; the hope of those who live far away in the sea,
among those turned to the world, who are far from you because they are bad fish, breaking the nets. Preparing the mountains in your strength.
Preparing preachers against them in your strength, not in their own. Girded about with power. Surrounded by your majesty.
Or surrounded by those to whom you gave the power of miracles, to all of whom you are common and in whose midst you stand. You who trouble the depths of the sea.
Through their preaching you trouble the bottom of the sea, that is, you stir up the hearts of unbelievers to persecution. Who shall bear the sound of its waves?
Who can endure the roar of its waves? Only those to whom you give fortitude, as you gave strength to the martyrs.
The nations will be troubled. The heathen will at first be in distress. And those who dwell at the ends of the earth will fear at your signs.
Then afterwards those who dwell at the end of the world fear you, because of your signs, which the apostles perform
in your name. You will delight the goings-out of morning and evening, that is, you make them delightful. You make the goings-out delightful
for your faithful, in the morning and in the evening, in prosperity and in adversity. You teach them to despise prosperity and not to fear adversity.
You have visited the earth and made it drunk; you have multiplied, to enrich it. You visited the earth, that is, mankind,
and drenched it with the preaching of the truth, and made it rich in many ways. Where did the riches come from?
The river of God is filled with waters. The people of God was filled with the Holy Spirit. You have prepared their food, for such is your preparation.
You prepared spiritual food for them, for such is your preparation beforehand: that the food is given freely by you, not because of their merits.
Drench its furrows. Drench the furrows of that same people. Open their hearts with the ploughshare of the word of God,
and then fill them with the Holy Spirit. Multiply its generations. Multiply its offspring, that is, its increase,
so that from some of the faithful other faithful came, and from those in turn others, until the Church spread abroad.
It will rejoice in its drops when it springs up. When it springs up, it rejoices in the drops. As long as it is not yet strengthened in the faith,
certain drops of the sacraments suit it, because it cannot take in the fullness of the truth. You will bless the crown of the year of your goodness.
You bless the victory of the times when you show your goodwill without regard to their merit.
And your fields will be filled with abundance. And your righteous will be filled with the abundance of thirtyfold, sixtyfold and hundredfold fruit.
The borders of the desert will grow fat. Then even the outermost nations, which were a desert until the coming of Christ, will grow fat with virtue.
And the hills will be girded with rejoicing. And those who stretch themselves up toward heaven will be girded with joy.
The rams of the sheep are clothed, namely with rejoicing. Then the leaders of the sheep are glad,
that is, the apostles themselves, because they see their fruit and see that they did not labor in vain. And the valleys will abound with grain. That is:
THE HUMBLE WILL BRING MUCH FRUIT. For they will cry out; they will say a hymn. They cry out. What is the cry? They sing a song of praise to God.
UNTO THE END, A SONG OF A PSALM OF RESURRECTION. This song of joy, the psalm so named, looks toward the end,
the resurrection shared by gentiles and Jews, against the Jews, who promised it to themselves and denied it to the gentiles.
SHOUT FOR JOY TO GOD. Shout for joy to God. Who? All the earth, not Judea alone. The whole catholic Church.
Those who are not catholics and deny the resurrection may howl, but not shout for joy. Sing psalms to his name; give glory to his praise.
Sing to his name, and turn the glory of the song to his praise, not to yourselves.
Say to God: How terrible are your works, O Lord. Say to him: how terrible your works are, Lord.
As you taught us when you said: I came so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.
Who are the ones who do not see? Those who know that they are blind. Who are the ones who see? Those who think that they see.
In the greatness of your power your enemies will lie to you. When you do countless signs, they lie to you.
To show their contempt for you, they lie like this: He does these signs by Beelzebub. Let all the earth worship you and sing psalms to you;
let it sing a psalm to your name, O Most High. Since they would not, let all the earth worship you and sing to you.
Let it sing to your name, O Most High, and let the falling away of Israel become the bringing in of the Gentiles. Come and see the works of the Lord. Come,
you Gentiles; avoid the lying Jews. Come and see God's works. Which works? How terrible he is in his counsels over the sons of men.
How terrible his counsel is over men: how the Jews are blinded and the Gentiles are enlightened.
The Jews are out; the Gentiles are in. He turns the sea into dry land. He turns the sea into dryness. He has made the whole world,
which was once bitter water, dry of that kind of water, and thirsty instead for sweet water.
They will pass through the river on foot. They wade across the river on their feet. Who? Those same thirsty ones. They do not sit on horses;
they are not proud. "On foot" means that they make good progress with humility across the river of this mortality.
Christ drank from this river, as Scripture says: He drank from the brook; therefore he lifted up his head. The river is mortality.
In it we are carried away. But we are also saved in it, if we hurry with humility toward immortality.
And when we get there, what then? There we will rejoice in him. There we will have joy in him. In whom?
In him who rules forever by his power. He rules forever in his strength. From him our strength comes as well;
we have none of our own. His eyes look upon the nations. His eyes look over the Gentiles.
They watch over them, not only over the Jews. He would not have paid so great a price for only a few.
Let those who provoke him not be exalted in themselves. Those who anger God with their sins will not be exalted in themselves.
If they become humble, then they will be exalted in Christ. Bless our God, you nations, and hear the voice of his praise.
Now praise God for this, you Gentiles, and listen to the voice of his praise, and hear it gladly, not the
voice of your own praise. Who is this God? He who has set my soul in life. He set my soul in life,
though it was once in death. And he has not let my feet be moved. And he did not let my feet waver.
He set them firm in life. "For you have tested us, O God; you have tried us by fire as silver is tried by fire." As is plain from this:
For you tested us. You put us in the fire, as one does with silver. There we were purified, not melted away.
"You led us into the snare." You brought us into the snare, where our bodies were caught and our souls were set free.
"You laid troubles on our back; you set men over our heads." You loaded hardships onto our back. Where did they come from?
From this, that you set men over our heads. You let sinners rule over us. "We passed through fire and water."
We have passed through fire and water. We were so tempered in the fire that we could not
perish in the water. Adversity strengthened us; prosperity did not make us soft. "And you brought us out into refreshment."
And by doing this you brought us into the coolness of eternal rest, where it is neither
too hot nor too cold, and where there is no temptation of either kind, of fire or of water. "I will go into your house with burnt offerings."
With burnt offerings I go into your house, where the divine fire burns up the corruption of the flesh and the impurity of the soul.
There I become an offering, as a whole burnt offering. "I will pay you my vows." There I will fulfil my promises to you,
the promises of eternal praise. "Which my lips distinguished." Which my lips always distinguished,
because I always made promises of your praise, not of my own, for I recognized that I am changeable and you are unchangeable, that without you I am nothing,
but that you do not need me. "And my mouth spoke in my tribulation." And in my distress in the world my mouth spoke. What did it say?
"I will offer you burnt offerings full of marrow." I bring you offerings rich in marrow. I love you in my bones. But a person does not do this
who wants to please people more than God. "With the incense of rams." With smoke, that is, prayers. Whose prayers?
Those of the wise men and leaders of God's flocks, that is, the apostles, who pray most of all for the flocks.
"I will offer you oxen with goats." I bring you cattle together with the goats: preachers together with sinners.
The goats would not be acceptable if the fruits of the trees did not help them. To them it is said:
"Make friends for yourselves of the mammon of iniquity, so that when you fail they may receive you into eternal dwellings."
Holy Church has brought such offerings to God, and this is her voice in her tribulation.
"Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell how much he has done for my soul." Come here, all you who fear God,
listen, and I will tell you what God has done for my soul. "I cried to him with my mouth." That means this:
With my mouth I called out to him. From then on he was mine, from the time he began to be the true one to me.
The one was false and foreign whom my pagan parents taught me [?] to wood and stones. "And I exalted under my tongue."
And I exalted him secretly under my tongue, in the privacy of my heart.
That he granted to my soul; that I will boast of to you all. If I have regarded iniquity in my heart, God will not hear.
If I had regarded wrong in my heart and loved it, then God would not hear my prayer. Therefore
God has heard, and has attended to the voice of my supplication. Because I did not do so, therefore God heard me,
and therefore he listened to the voice of my prayer. Blessed be God, who has not taken away my prayer
nor his mercy from me. Praised be the God who did not take my supplication away from me,
nor his grace. When he did not let me grow weary of supplication, then he willed to show me grace.
A PSALM OF DAVID. MAY GOD HAVE MERCY ON US AND BLESS US. May God be gracious to us, and bless us.
The rain of his teaching, the rain of his instruction, may he give us; the blessing of eternal life may he give us.
May he make his face shine upon us. The face of the sun he makes shine upon the good and the wicked.
May he make his own face shine over us, so that we may see it.
Or else it is understood thus: may his image, which he gave us, be lit up in us with the light of wisdom.
And may he have mercy on us. And in that shining may he be gracious to us. To what does that lead us?
That we may know your way upon earth. That we, Lord, here in this earth may know Christ, your way,
who leads to you. Your salvation among all nations. And that we may know your Savior, that same Christ, among all peoples.
Let the peoples confess to you, O God; let all the peoples confess to you. What will happen then? Then the peoples will confess to you, God;
all peoples will confess to you. Let them confess their own iniquity and the grace of God; let them accuse themselves and praise him. Let the nations rejoice and exult.
In that confession let the peoples rejoice and leap for joy. What gladdens them? Because you judge the peoples in equity.
For you judge over the peoples according to right and according to their conscience. And you will direct the nations on earth. And the crookedly walking peo-
-ples you direct on earth to the right way. Let the peoples confess to you, O God; let all the peoples confess to you. The earth has yielded its fruit.
The earth brought forth its fruit. Where did it come from? Only from their confession. After penitence and after confession came good works.
May God, our God, bless us; may God bless us. May the Holy Trinity bless us. Blessing aims at multiplication; therefore it says next:
And let all the ends of the earth fear him. And may all the ends of the earth fear him. Let the multiplication come about from that.
UNTO THE END, FOR DAVID HIMSELF, A PSALM OF A SONG. In a psalm there is resonance; in a song, joy.
Here are both; therefore this song is a psalm of a song. LET GOD ARISE AND LET HIS ENEMIES BE SCATTERED.
God arose, and his enemies were scattered. That has happened: Christ has risen.
The Jews [?], his enemies, are driven apart. Let those who hate him flee from his face. And let those who hate him be put to flight
from before his face. So they are, everywhere that the faithful dwell, in whom the face of God shines.
As smoke vanishes, so let them vanish. As smoke passes away, so let them pass away. They pass away from the land of the living on the day of judgment.
As wax melts before the fire, so let sinners perish before the face of God. As wax melts before the fire,
so let the sinful Jews pass away before the face of God. And let the righteous be glad, and exult in the sight of God, and be delighted in gladness.
And let the righteous be made joyful, and rejoice before God, and be delighted in joy. When?
When they hear: COME, YOU BLESSED OF MY FATHER, RECEIVE THE KINGDOM. Sing to God, sing psalms to his name. But you
faithful, you who are still here in the [?] world, sing to God in purity of heart; sing psalms to him in good works.
Make a way for him who ascends above the setting. Prepare the way for him who climbed over death by rising again. The Lord is his name.
Lord is his name. The Jews did not know that. Had they known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of majesty.
And exult in his sight. And be glad before him, as it says: AS SORROWFUL, YET ALWAYS REJOICING. They shall be troubled. Who?
The sinners of whom it was said before: AS WAX MELTS BEFORE THE FIRE, SO LET SINNERS PERISH. From his face. Whose 'his'?
From the face of God. What God? The father of orphans and judge of widows. Sinners will be thrust away from the face of him
who is the father of orphans and judges widows. God in his holy place. In them is God, in his holy place.
God makes those of one manner, or of one custom, that is, those of one mind, to dwell in a house. God makes them dwell of one mind in his house.
That is, their hearts. Where the Greek has 'tropos', which means both custom and manner. Nor does it have
'who makes to dwell in', but only 'makes to dwell'. Who leads out those in fetters in strength. He who takes those held captive in sins
out of their bonds in his strength. Likewise those who embitter, that is, who provoke, who dwell in tombs. Likewise those
who are still worse, because they provoke God, who are even buried in their sins, the most wicked of all men:
even them he raises from the grave and makes them live in his strength. O God, when you go forth before your people. You do that, God,
when you go forth before your people. When is that? When you make them perceive your works, such
as they are: that you make them dwell of one mind in the house, leading out those in fetters in strength,
likewise those who embitter, who dwell in tombs. When you passed through the desert, the earth was moved. When you went forth and were preached among the gentiles,
then earthly men were moved to repentance. For the heavens dropped down. That came about for this reason:
for the heavens rained on them: the teaching of the apostles had come to them. From where was it sent? From the face of the God of Israel.
From the God of Israel, who sent them out filled with the Holy Spirit. Mount Sinai, at the face of the God of Israel.
The heavens rained; the mountains rained. Those who are the heavens are also the mountains. Among them was Mount Sinai,
by which Paul is understood, who likewise rained from the face of the God of Israel. Setting apart a voluntary rain, O God, for your inheritance.
You were then setting apart a willing rain for your inheritance. Willing because it came freely, as a gift,
with no merits going before it. Set apart, because it did not come to the earlier nations; it was saved for the last ones. And it was weakened.
And the inheritance was weakened, because it recognized that it is nothing by itself, but, as Paul said: By the grace of God I am
what I am. But you have perfected it. You perfected it, as he also said: For strength is made perfect in weakness.
Your animals will dwell in it. Your cattle dwell in it. They dwell in the holy church, which is the inheritance of the Lord.
You have prepared in your sweetness for the needy, O God. Why the needy? Because it was weakened so that it might be perfected. For the needy one you have prepared in your sweetness
a ready will to do good work, not out of fear but out of love. The Lord will give the word to those who preach the gospel with great power. The Lord gives and
shows his preachers what they should say, in the great power of preaching [?], of signs and miracles. To his animals he sends such food.
Which Lord? The King of the powers of the beloved. The King of the powers of his dear one and his beloved, Christ,
which he directs together with him and turns according to his will. Of the beloved: of his beloved
and his chosen one. To what end? And to divide the spoils for the beauty of the house. Also to divide the spoils for the beauty of the house.
The house is the holy church, which he has made beautiful with those he took from the devil: apostles, prophets, teachers,
those who speak in tongues, those who have the gift of healing. If you sleep among the midst of the lots. If you rest among the inheritances of the Old and the New Testament,
in such a way that I [?] you give up hope of the earthly happiness that was promised in the Old, and you patiently wait for
the eternal immortality that is promised in the New. The wings, that is, you will be the wings of the silvered dove, and the hinder parts of her back in the paleness of gold.
Then you will become the feathers of the silvered dove, the holy church, and the hinder part of her back,
where the wings have their root. Wings: because you fly to heaven with the twin commandments of love. Back:
because you bear the yoke of the Lord, in the beauty of the pale gold. The holy church is the silvered dove,
because she is taught by the divine words. She has the greenness of gold on her back, because her strength lies in the power of love and wisdom.
While the heavenly one marks out kings over her, that is, over the dove. When the heavenly King marks out his kings in her,
they will be made white as snow in Selmon, that is, in shadow. Then they are made white in the shadow.
Why are they called kings (reges)? Because they rule (regentes) the desires of the flesh. How does he distinguish them
among themselves? As it says: AND HE GAVE SOME AS APOSTLES, SOME AS PROPHETS, AND SOME AS EVANGELISTS,
AND SOME AS TEACHERS AND PASTORS. How? With snow in the shade, because the grace of the Holy Spirit gives them shade
against the heats of the flesh. Selmon is the name of a certain mountain in Palestine. I do not mean that one. The mountain of God, I call a fertile mountain.
I mean the visible Christ, the highest mountain of God: abundant, fruitful, full of milk
for nourishing little ones with milk. Why do you suspect other fertile mountains? This is the mountain in which it has pleased God to dwell.
Why do you suppose other mountains to be fruitful? Why do you think any one of them is a mountain so pleasing to God as a dwelling place?
For he himself said: THE FATHER WHO DWELLS IN ME, HE DOES THE WORKS. I AM IN THE FATHER AND THE FATHER IS IN ME. For the Lord will dwell
that is, in those fertile mountains, until the end. As God dwells in him, so he dwells in them, according to the words: I IN THEM
AND YOU IN ME. How long? Until he brings them to the end, which is he himself. The chariot of God: they are God's chariots.
Therefore he sits in them, therefore he guides them, until he brings them to the end. Ten thousand times manifold. Ten-thousandfold,
that is, manifold, because there is no counting them. Thousands of those who rejoice. A thousand joyful ones. Why should they not be?
The Lord is among them. The Lord is within them; therefore they rejoice. In Sinai, in the holy place. That is, in the commandment, which is holy.
God is within them and establishes them in his holy commandment. You have ascended on high, you have led captivity captive, you have received gifts among men.
You, CHRIST, ascended to heaven; you made captive the captivity of men; you slew death.
You received various gifts in them. Because they are your body, their gifts are therefore yours. And from these gifts some became
apostles, some prophets, some teachers. Such you made them. What were they before? Not believing that the Lord God dwells among them.
Unbelieving. In what? That God should dwell in them. They did not trust that God would dwell in them
and that they would become chariots of God; you made them believe this. BLESSED BE THE LORD FROM DAY TO DAY. For this let God be praised
from day to day, because he still is, and always will be, leading captivity captive and receiving gifts among men.
The God of our salvation will make our journey prosperous, our God, the God of saving. God of our salvation, our God, God of saving:
he makes our journey go forward. He makes the course of life prosperous. And the Lord's are the ways out of death. And the departure of the Lord's death:
what does it do? It makes our journey prosperous. Or it means: the departure of death also belongs to the Saviour. Since he died innocent,
why then should we not take comfort in it, guilty and sinners as we are? But God will shatter the heads of his enemies,
the hairy crown of those who walk on in their offences. But although he suffered death, he shattered the heads of his enemies.
and the crowns of the hair of those who go on in their misdeeds. As it says: "Raise me up, and I will repay them."
The Lord said: from Bashan, that is, from dryness, I will turn them back; I will turn them back from the depths of the sea. Thus the Lord promised.
From dryness I turn them to greenness. From the depths of the sea, that is, from the perils of the world, I turn them back.
I take them out of the waves of vices. "That your foot may be dipped in blood." So inwardly do you turn them to yourself,
that your foot may be dipped in the blood of martyrdom together with them. They are your members; in them you suffer persecution. "The tongue of your dogs
[?] from the enemies, from him." Those who were formerly your enemies become the tongue of your dogs. They become your preachers.
From where does this come to them? From where, if not from him, the very one who turned them back from Bashan and from the depths of the sea?
"Your goings in were seen, O God." Your goings in, God, were seen here in the world, and also in your own incarnation,
and also when you came on the clouds, of which you said: "Henceforth you shall see the Son of Man coming on the clouds."
They are also your chariot, on which you have ridden through all this world. "The goings of my God, my King,
that is, were seen, who is in the holy place." The goings of my God, of my King, who is in his holy temple. Which are these?
Those who are also clouds and a chariot. "The princes went before, joined to those singing psalms, in the midst of young maidens playing timbrels."
The apostles came first; right after them others who followed them were joined to them, singing God's praise in voice and in deed.
They came and were set in charge in the midst of the new churches, which sing with timbrels, because they lived in the mortification of the flesh,
just as a timbrel is made from dried and stretched leather. "In the churches bless God." The churches are the timbrel-playing maidens.
In them they praise God. "The Lord from the fountains of Israel." Praise the Lord from the springs of Israel. The first fountains,
I mean the apostles, who came from Israel. They were fountains; they were the springs.
From them came rivers. "There is Benjamin, the younger." There among the fountains was Paul, of the tribe of Benjamin,
"the younger," that is, the last of the apostles. "In ecstasy," that is, in a going out of the mind. In being startled,
as he was startled when he heard from heaven: "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" Or it means: in that
departure of the mind, as happened when he was caught up to the third heaven. "The princes of Judah," that is, of confession,
"their leaders. The princes of Zebulun," that is, of strength; "the princes of Naphtali," that is, of breadth. The apostles were princes of confession, of strength, of breadth,
that is, of faith, hope, and charity. "Command, O God, your strength." Commend to us, O God, your strength. Make Christ dear to us, God the Father,
who is your strength. Teach us to love him who died for us. "Confirm, O God, what you have wrought in us."
Make firm, God, the faith that you gave us. "From your temple, which is in Jerusalem, kings shall offer you gifts."
Away from your house, which is in the lower Jerusalem, kings bring you gifts in the upper Jerusalem.
These are the ones who here subdue the desires of the flesh. "Rebuke the wild beasts of the reed." Rebuke the beasts of the reed.
Rebuke the heretics, the enemies of Holy Scripture. "The herd of bulls among the cows of the peoples, so that they may be shut out", that is, so that they may stand out,
those who have been tested like silver. These same heretics then go about like so many bulls among the people's cows. Who are these?
None other than stubborn and misled people, like the cows that follow the bulls; so that those may be raised up
who are praiseworthy in the divine scriptures. As Paul said: "There must also be heresies, so that those who are approved may be made manifest among you."
The wickedness of the heretics makes the goodness and the wisdom of the catholics shine. Therefore it says here:
"Excludantur" means "exprimantur" (let them be pressed out, made to stand out). Just as the makers of silver vessels are also called "exclusores". "Scatter the nations that want wars."
Scatter, Lord, the heretics, who are called "nations" not because of the generations of families but because of
the kinds of sects. Destroy them before they gain a succession. "Let them bring quickly out of Egypt."
Let the nations quickly bring their souls to God out of Egypt, out of the darkness; let all nations hasten to him.
"Let Ethiopia hasten to give its hands to God." Let Ethiopia hasten to hold out its hands to God, hasten to surrender to him, as the defeated do in war.
According to Jerome it reads thus. "Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing psalms to the Lord." For such manifold grace
sing to God, all kingdoms of the earth; sing praises to the Lord. "Sing psalms to God, who ascended above the heaven of heavens toward the east."
Sing praises to God, who went up above all the heavens before his disciples at Jerusalem, which is in the eastern regions; or else "toward the east"
means toward the Father. "Behold, he will give his voice, a voice of power." When he comes from there to judge, then he will make his voice known,
the voice of power, that is, "Come" or "Go". Then he who once wished to be silent will become very loud.
"Give glory to God; his magnificence is over Israel." Glorify God, for then his greatness will come over Israel;
then he will magnify the faithful people. "And his power is in the clouds." And then his power will shine in the clouds,
in the apostles and prophets, who here were clouds and there become judges. "God is wonderful in his saints, the God of Israel."
Then the God of Israel will become wonderful in his saints, the God of the one who sees God. "He himself will give power and strength to his people;
blessed be God." Then he will give his people the power of the resurrection, the strength of incorruption. May God be praised for this.
UNTO THE END, FOR THOSE WHO SHALL BE CHANGED, TO DAVID HIMSELF. This psalm is sung to David himself, to Christ himself.
In it he himself tells us of his passion, by which we were redeemed and changed from mortal life
to eternal life; changed from earthly life to heavenly life, from corruptible life to incorruption. SAVE ME, O GOD.
FOR THE WATERS HAVE COME IN even to my soul. Save me, God, for waters have come to me, even up to my life.
Those are rightly called waters who, like waters, always rush and roar in storm and strife, as the Jews did.
Why does he ask the Father to keep death from him at their hands, since he died willingly? Only by transforming us into himself.
We fear death. [He asks] so that this fear may never make us like our enemies or turn us over to them.
I am stuck fast in the mire of the deep. What does that mean? I STUCK IN THEM. THEY HELD ME. THEY KILLED ME. They are the mire.
Because they are earth: they would have become gold if they had been willing to follow me up to heaven.
Now instead they drag downward. That is why they are the mire of the deep, and I am stuck in it. And there is no substance.
And they are not anything. That means: they are nothing at all. And such sinful mire
is not the substance that I created. I did not create a corrupted nature. I came into the depth of the sea,
and the tempest overwhelmed me. I came into the depth of the sea, and there the storm drowned me.
I came among sinners, and their persecution killed me. I have labored crying out. I wore myself out with calling: WOE TO THE WORLD BECAUSE OF OFFENSES.
WOE TO YOU, SCRIBES AND PHARISEES. My throat has become hoarse. My gums became hoarse from the calling,
because they had no ears to hear. My eyes have failed from hoping in my God. This is said of the body. My disciples' eyes
grew weary of hoping. As one of them said: AND WE HOPED THAT HE WAS THE ONE WHO WOULD REDEEM ISRAEL.
He cured them of that weariness when he rose. They are more numerous than the hairs of my head,
those who hated me without cause. Those who hate me for nothing are more than the hairs of my head. There may well be that many of them,
since even one of the twelve was among them. And all of them hate me gratis, that is, without cause. My enemies who persecute me unjustly have been strengthened.
My enemies who persecute me unjustly were strengthened. Unjustly, because I was without guilt. What I did not seize, I then paid back.
I paid back what I did not seize. I did not sin, and yet I paid the penalty. And I gladly gave up equality with God, which I had not seized,
taking the form of a servant. Adam wanted divinity by robbery, and so he lost happiness. The one who had done this before him taught him that.
What happened to that one too? He usurped what he had not received, and he lost what he had received. God, you know my foolishness.
God, you know my foolishness. You know the cause. You know why I was willing to die then,
when I could easily have escaped it. If they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of majesty. But my foolishness
is wiser than men. You recognize its fruit, even though it seems foolish to them. And my offenses are not hidden from you.
And the offenses of my members are not hidden from you. They show their wounds to you, because you are their healer.
Let those who wait for you, Lord, not be put to shame because of me, Lord of hosts. Let those who wait for you, Lord, not be put to shame because of me,
Lord of powers. Let no one say to them: "Where is he who said to you, BELIEVE IN GOD AND BELIEVE ALSO IN ME?" Let them not be con-
-founded because of me, those who seek you, God of Israel. And do not allow my enemies so much power against me
that those who seek you, God of Israel, are ashamed of me. For it is for your sake that I have endured reproach.
Shamelessness has covered my face. For I suffered reproach because of you, and because of you shamelessness covered my face.
If anyone said to me, "You are a Christian, a worshipper of the crucified one," I felt no shame at that and did not hold back from it.
I have become a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to the sons of my mother. I have become a stranger and a foreigner to my mother's children.
I am a son of the synagogue, and still they say: "BUT AS FOR THIS MAN, WE DO NOT KNOW WHERE HE COMES FROM." Why is that?
For zeal for your house has consumed me. For zeal for your house devoured me. That is the reason: I zealously punished their wrongdoing.
That is why they did not see fit to acknowledge me. If they acknowledged what is right, they would acknowledge me, and then I would be without zeal against them.
And the insults of those who insulted you have fallen on me. And the insults of those who insulted you came upon me. Why is that?
Because no one reviles me without also reviling you: I and you are one. And I covered my soul with fasting,
and that became a reproach to me. I covered my soul with fasting, and that too became a reproach to me.
When I hungered for them and they were bitter to me, I would not take them into my body as they were.
I chose to fast from them. I would not consent to their wickedness, and for that they reproached me. And I made sackcloth my garment,
that is, I set my flesh before them so that they could vent their rage on it, but I hid my divinity from them. I offered them my garment of haircloth,
my mortal body, so that they could commit their crime against it and destroy themselves, and their crime might become atonement for others.
And I became a byword to them, that is, an object of mockery. I became a comparison to them, a mocking comparison: "Just as it happened to that one,"
they said, "so may it happen to him. Just as that one perished, so may this one perish. That one was evil,
and evil came upon him. This one is evil; may nothing better come upon him either." Those who sat in the gate insulted me,
that is, in public. Those who sat at the city gate, where people went in and out, mocked me.
There they held me up to scorn. And those who drank wine made songs about me. They sat drinking wine
and sang about me. Many still do the same: they sing about anyone who keeps them from their wrongdoing. But I [directed] my prayer
that is, I directed it to you, Lord. But I prayed to you for them: FATHER, FORGIVE THEM, FOR THEY DO NOT KNOW WHAT THEY ARE DOING.
A time of good pleasure, O God; that is, the time of your good pleasure has come. A favourable time is still coming, God the Father. When?
In the multitude of your mercy. In the manifoldness of your grace, by which your Son rises from death,
and mankind together with him. Hear me in the truth of your salvation. Hear me in the truth of your salvation.
The salvation that you promised, which you will grant: in that, hear me. Save me from the mud, so that I do not stick fast. Of which he said above:
I AM STUCK FAST IN THE MIRE OF THE DEEP. Free me out of the mire, so that I do not stick fast in it. Of whom do you speak?
Deliver me from those who hate me. I say: free me from those who hate me. They are the mire. And from the depth of the waters.
And from the depth of the waters. These are all the same people. They roar in their storm like rushing waters.
Let not the tempest of water drown me. So says the body of Christ. Let not the storm of the waters drown me. In the flesh it has done
it, as stands above: AND THE TEMPEST HAS DROWNED ME. In the spirit let them not do it. Let me not become one who consents to them; then I will not go into the depth of the mire.
Then they will not swallow me; then I will not go into their body, for I am the body of Christ.
Let everyone take care that his body does not come into their power. But if it should happen, let him pray for the soul,
that they may not gain power over it. Nor let the deep swallow me up. Nor let the deep swallow me up.
Nor let the pit close its mouth over me. Nor let the pit shut its opening over me. Whoever plunges into sin
plunges into the deep and into the pit. But if he nevertheless confesses his sins there,
as it says, OUT OF THE DEPTHS I HAVE CRIED TO YOU, O LORD, then he is not shut in the pit. These words belong to the body of Christ.
HEAR ME, O LORD, FOR your mercy is sweet. Hear me, Lord, for your grace is sweet to me.
I am in such great hardships that your grace must needs be sweet to me. Great hunger makes bread sweet;
great hardships make grace sweet. According to the multitude of your mercies look upon me. According to the multitude of your mercies,
not of my sins, look upon me. Do not turn your face away from your servant. Do not turn your face away from your child,
whom the discipline of tribulation has made little. For I am in tribulation; hear me speedily. Hear me speedily,
for I am in distress. Attend to my soul and redeem it. Pay heed to my soul and free it.
Because of my enemies deliver me. Because of my enemies free me. Free the soul in secret; free the body openly,
so that, having learned of the resurrection of the body, they may turn from enemies into friends. For you know my reproach, and my confusion,
and my shame. You know that my reproach is hostile, such as this one: HE SAVED OTHERS;
HIMSELF HE CANNOT SAVE. And my confusion, which gnaws at the conscience, which is found in my members, not in me myself.
Such as this one: SAUL, SAUL, WHY DO YOU PERSECUTE ME? And my shame, in which there is fear, which comes from weakness.
which is also in the members, as in Peter when he denied Christ thus: "O man, I am not." This verecundia (shame) is also called reverentia.
Now, Father, you know my reproach. But of those who are mine you know both the reproach
and the confusion and the shame. Do not reject them because of that, but help them too, because they are in me.
"In your sight are all who trouble me." You look upon all who afflict me, in myself and in those who are mine.
Therefore set me free. "My heart has expected reproach and misery." My heart awaited those two things, which it knew beforehand.
It knew that my reproach was to come, and the misery of the Jews, for whom, out of pity, I prayed thus: "Father, forgive them,
for they do not know what they do." "And I looked for one who would grieve together with me, and there was none; and for comforters," that is, I looked for them,
or, "I sought, and I found none." And so I waited for someone who would be sad together with me over their misery,
and there was no one. And so I, the physician, had sorrow; for that sorrow I sought comforters and found none.
What use was it then that I had foretold it in the prophets? "And they gave gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink."
And so they threw gall into my food, and gave me vinegar to drink when I was thirsty.
It was bitter to me that I did not find what I sought, and their oldness was vinegar to me. I wanted them themselves; then they were
embittering me. I wanted their faith; then I found oldness. Like them also are those who throw gall into my food,
who partake of my sacraments and yet live contrary to them. They are the embittering ones; those I do not take into myself.
That is the wine mixed with myrrh which I tasted on the cross and would not drink. "Let their table become a snare before them."
Now let their table become a snare to them while they look on. They brought an evil taste to my table; let their table be their snare.
Let them turn their knowledge against their own scripture. "And for recompense and for a stumbling block." And as a reward and as a cause of going astray.
As a reward, because it is just; as a cause of going astray, because they lead themselves astray. "Let their eyes be darkened so that they do not see."
Let their eyes grow blind so that they do not see. Why so? "So that, since they saw to no purpose, it may befall them not to see."
Because they were knowing to no purpose, let them become unknowing. "Let their eyes be darkened so that they do not see."
Let their eyes grow dark so that they do not see, those who, though seeing, would not see. "Bow down their back always."
Bend their back always. Since they would not know the things above, let them think about the things below. "And let the indignation of your wrath seize them."
And let the anger of your wrath catch them. Do not let them escape, since they are guilty.
"Let their habitation be made desolate." Let their dwelling place become a wasteland. As we now see, Jerusalem is desolate as far as they are concerned.
From the place where they killed Christ, from there they have been driven out. "Let their eyes be darkened": that is a hidden judgment. "Let their habitation be made desolate."
That is open vengeance. And let there be none to dwell in their tents, that is, of their number. That is still the same thing
as what came before. For they persecuted him whom you struck. For him whom you struck and ordered to die
for the world, him they struck out of envy. And they added to the pain of my wounds. And they increased the pain of my wounds.
I am mortal because of original sin; on top of that they strike me. Add iniquity to their iniquity.
Lay one of their wrongs on top of the other. Since they strike a righteous man, let them strike the Son of God. Let them become blind,
so that they do not recognize him. So their wounds grow, for they are not worthy for you to heal them.
And let them not enter into your righteousness. And let them not come into your righteousness. Let them not lay hold of righteousness. Let them be blotted out of the book of the living.
Yes, let them be scraped out of the record-books of the living, where they think their names stand because of good merits.
And let them not be written with the righteous. And let them not be written together with the righteous.
This is what they deserve by your justice, because they relied too much on their own righteousness. I am poor and sorrowful.
I am poor and sorrowful. All of you, learn from me to be like this. For it says: BLESSED ARE THE POOR.
BLESSED ARE THOSE WHO MOURN. And the salvation of your countenance, God, has received me. And the salvation of your face, God, received me.
Everyone hopes for those riches. So you will have refreshment for poverty and sorrow. I will praise the name of God with song; I will magnify him with praise.
I praise God's name with song; I magnify him in praise. I have this in place of riches.
And it shall please God more than a young calf bringing forth horns and hoofs. And God wants that sacrifice more gladly
than a young bullock with horns and hoofs, for that bullock signified the spiritual sacrifice.
Let the needy see and rejoice. Let the poor understand this and rejoice: that he wants praise more than a calf. Seek the Lord,
and your soul shall live. You all seek bread so that the body may live; seek God, and your soul will live.
For the Lord has heard the poor. For God heard the poor, whom he would not have heard if they had not been poor.
And he has not despised his fettered ones. And he did not reject his oppressed ones. What are the fetters? Mortality itself
and corruption. From these he unbinds those who now cry out to him from there. Let the heavens and the earth praise him,
the sea and all creeping things in them. Let the heavens and the earth praise him, and everything that creeps in them. Why?
For God will save Zion. For God preserves his Church and makes it incorporated into his Only-begotten.
And the cities of Judah shall be built. And the cities of confession shall be built; these are the churches,
from which the proud are driven out, those who are ashamed to confess. And they shall dwell there and acquire it as an inheritance.
And they shall dwell therein, and they shall win it as an inheritance. Zion is their habitation here;
in heaven it is their inheritance. "And the seed of his servants shall possess it." The imitators of the faith of the apostles and prophets shall possess it.
"And those who love his name shall dwell in it." And those who love his name are the seed of his servants; they dwell therein.
THE VOICE OF THE MARTYRS TO CHRIST. O GOD, COME TO MY AID. O LORD, make haste to help me. God, look to my help. Hasten. To what?
To help me. Let every man say this; let him say it most of all when he is in distress. Let him hold this prayer in common with the martyrs.
For he too does not lack persecution, if he wishes to be good. Daily
offenses torment the soul of the righteous man, even if he suffers no torments of the body. "Let them be confounded and put to shame who seek my soul."
Let them be ashamed and come into fear who seek my soul, not to imitate it but to destroy it.
Let every man intercede for his enemies in this way; let him wish them well in this way. "Let them be turned backward and blush who think evil against me."
Let them be turned away, back behind, and be ashamed, those who wish me evil. Let them walk behind, not in front:
those who wish to lead the Church astray with wicked counsels. Just as Peter wrongly wished to go in front, when Christ turned him back, saying:
GET BEHIND ME, SATAN. "Let them be turned away at once, blushing, who say to me: Well done, well done." Let them turn away at once, ashamed,
those who say to me in flattery, "WELL DONE, WELL DONE." These are the ones who praise a man insincerely,
seeking favor and not truth. They are the most dreadful persecutors. "Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you, and let them say,
those who love your salvation: Let the Lord always be magnified." Let those who seek you rejoice and be made joyful in you,
and let those who love your Savior, Christ, say this. What? "Let the Lord always be magnified."
He is the one we should magnify, but no one should magnify himself. What then should he say about himself?
"But I am needy and poor." I am needy and poor. Why should he be, if his sins have been forgiven him?
Because it says: I SEE ANOTHER LAW IN MY MEMBERS, WARRING AGAINST THE LAW OF MY MIND. That is why he is sick and poor.
"O God, help me." God, help me. Say this often; let it be in your mind and in your mouth; do not grow weary of it. "Be my helper,
O Lord, do not delay." Say this along with it: Be my helper, Lord; do not delay in it. This is the voice of the martyrs; let it be the voice of all.
OF DAVID HIMSELF. OF THE SONS OF JONADAB, AND OF THOSE WHO WERE THE FIRST TO BE LED INTO CAPTIVITY.
What does this psalm, sung of David himself, admonish us about? The sons of Jonadab do this: they kept their father's command
and by that obedience won God's favor. Their father commanded them not to drink wine,
and not to live in houses but outside, in their tents. They kept this just as if God himself had commanded it of them.
because he commanded all children to be obedient to their parents. From this they received a blessing from the Lord.
and it was shown to all the people in them through Jeremiah the prophet, who was his messenger, when they were led into captivity,
that they should be obedient to God in their exile, for he would not release them from it until he redeemed them out of it,
just as the sons of Jonadab obeyed their father in what he chose to command them. Let us now be obedient to God in the same way,
so that he may free us from the captivity that Paul showed us in our members, when he said:
"BUT I SEE ANOTHER LAW IN MY MEMBERS, FIGHTING AGAINST THE LAW OF MY MIND, AND LEADING ME CAPTIVE IN THE LAW OF SIN WHICH IS IN MY MEMBERS."
This captivity is perilous. It can be overcome only with God alone, as he also said about it:
"WHO WILL DELIVER ME FROM THE BODY OF THIS DEATH? THE GRACE OF GOD THROUGH JESUS CHRIST OUR LORD." There is no other remedy for it except
the grace of God, which this psalm teaches us to recognize. IN YOU, O LORD, I HAVE HOPED; LET ME NOT BE CONFOUNDED FOR EVER.
In you, Lord, I have hoped; let me never be put to shame. As I am now, so may I never be. In Adam I am put to shame;
in you may I be free of shame. In your justice deliver me and rescue me. In your justice set me free,
and in your justice take me out of injustice. In yours, not in mine. May I never be one of those
who, "not knowing the justice of God and seeking to establish their own, have not submitted to the justice of God." Incline your ear to me. Bend your ear to me.
You stand upright, O physician; I lie down below and cannot raise myself up. Bend down to me. And save me.
And save me. Be to me a God, a protector. God, be my protector, for I cannot protect myself. And into a fortified place.
And into a strong place, where I cannot be overcome in battle. That you may save me. That you may keep me safe.
For you are my strength and my refuge. For you are my stronghold and my refuge. Whether persecution comes or temptation comes,
I flee to you. Adam should have fled to you; he fled from you. He went away, he perished, but he was found.
My God, deliver me from the hand of the sinner. My God, set me free from the hand of the sinful one. From the hand of the one who transgresses the law, and of the unjust.
Both of the one who transgresses the law and of the unjust one who is without law. Let me be like neither of them:
neither the bad Christians, who have the law, nor the pagans, who are without the law. Let their hand not draw me to them. And if I must also endure them, help me in that as well.
For you are my patience. For you are my patience. O Lord, my hope from my youth. Lord, my hope from my youth
onward. In you I have been strengthened from the womb; from my mother's womb you are my protector. And even earlier, from the time I was conceived [lit. 'born'],
you strengthened me; from my mother's womb onward you protected me. My song is always of you.
My song, which tells of my joy, is always of you. Not only in the time of faith, which is now,
but also in the time of sight, which is still to come, when men become like the angels. I have become as a wonder to many.
I am like a wonder to many. Why? Because I believe what I do not see. They rejoice in visible things: in food,
in drink, in luxury, in fornication, in avarice, in riches, in worldly honours, in the whitewashing of a mud wall.
But my hope is in the invisible things. Their word is: LET US EAT AND DRINK, FOR TOMORROW WE SHALL DIE.
My word is the opposite: RATHER LET US FAST AND PRAY, FOR TOMORROW WE SHALL DIE. But you are a strong helper. But you are a strong helper.
That gives me courage on the narrow way, which you passed along before me. Let my mouth be filled with praise, so that it may sing your glory, and all day long your greatness.
Let my mouth be filled with praise, so that it may sing your glory, and all day long your greatness,
both in prosperity and in adversity. Do not cast me off in the time of old age. Do not cast me away when I grow old. What does that mean?
When my strength fails, do not forsake me. That means: when I become without strength, do not cast me away. Lack of strength
is old age. Let your strength be in me when mine fails. Why do I ask this? Because my enemies have spoken against me,
and those who watched my soul took counsel together, saying: God has forsaken him; pursue him and seize him, for there is no one to rescue
him. For my enemies, lying in wait for me, said: God has forsaken him. And those who watched me for evil and not for good
took counsel together, saying likewise: God has forsaken him. Lie in wait for him and seize him; there is no one to free him.
God, do not be far from me; my God, look to my help. You, God, do not be removed from me. God, look upon me to help me.
Look upon me in my need to help me. Let those who disparage my soul be put to shame and fail. Let those who speak evil of me be put to shame and fall away.
Let them begin to be ashamed of it; let them begin to grow weary of it. Let those who seek evil for me be covered with confusion and shame.
Let those who think evil of me be covered with shame and with bashfulness, as is the way of those who are bashful,
that they turn red under the eyes. But I will always hope in you, and I will add to all your praise.
But I hope in you always, and I increase your praise. The new praise of the redemption of the human race I add to all your other praises.
My mouth has proclaimed your justice, all day long your salvation. My mouth told of your justice, all day long your salvation.
At all times, by day and by night, I taught this: THAT SALVATION IS THE LORD'S AND NOT MAN'S. For I have not known letters.
For I did not acknowledge the written books of Moses as my salvation, as the Jews boast, but the grace of God. As Paul says:
FOR THE LETTER KILLS, BUT THE SPIRIT GIVES LIFE. Other translators said: FOR I HAVE NOT KNOWN TRADERS, that is, those who do not pursue leisure.
These, however, are the Jews, who want to be justified by the works of the law and not by grace. I will enter into the power of the Lord. I go into the power of my Lord and seek
his salvation there, because I do not acknowledge my own. Lord, I will remember your justice alone. That is what I do: I make mention only of your justice, yours alone.
I do not trust in my own [righteousness], as they do. You are my justifier, not I myself. How do I know that?
God, you have taught me from my youth. You, Lord, taught it to me, all the way from my youth until now:
how my righteousness was lost back then, when I believed the deserter more than the emperor;
and how I then became divided against myself, so that the flesh lusts against the spirit, because I would not be subject to the One;
and how afterwards I would not have needed to be redeemed by Christ if I had not then become a captive.
"And until now I will declare your wonders." And from then until now I proclaim your wonders. What is more wonderful than to justify the ungodly?
Is that not to raise the dead? "And even to old age and very old age." And I will always proclaim it, on into old age and decrepitude,
where the end of this life comes. "Lord, do not forsake me until I declare your arm to every generation that is to come."
Lord, do not forsake me; be with me until I make Christ known to all the generations to come,
your arm, with which you redeemed us. "Your power and your righteousness." Until I tell them
not of my own strength, not of my own righteousness, but of your power and your righteousness. Until I say this to everyone:
"You are nothing by yourself. Call upon God. The sins are yours; the merits are God's. Punishment is owed to you, and when the reward comes,
he will crown his own gifts, not your merits." "God, even to the highest things, the great things you have done." I tell them that your power and righteousness reach
up to the highest things, which you did mightily. For angels, archangels, thrones, dominions, principalities,
and powers owe it to you that they exist, owe it to you that they live, owe it to you that they live righteously, owe it to you that they live blessedly.
"God, who is like you?" God, who is like you? Indeed, wretched Adam, you wanted to be like him. How? Through pride,
not through humility. You would have been like him if you had willed what he willed. He willed your obedience,
your subjection; but you offered contempt instead. And how has that turned out for you? So that you are like the senseless beasts.
Now acknowledge your misery and say with penitence: "God, who is like you?" Say this also:
"How many tribulations you have shown me, both many and evil." How many hardships you have shown me because of this, that I wanted to make myself your equal.
How many, how evil! However evil they may seem to me, yet they are discipline and admonition to me,
not abandonment; and I should thank you with these words: "And turning, you gave me life, and brought me back again from the depths of the earth." And yet, having turned toward me,
you gave me life in your resurrection, and led me out a second time from the depth of the earth, because I, having risen in you,
shall also rise in my own self. You rose first in our nature; afterwards we shall rise in the same nature. "You have multiplied your righteousness,
and turning, you comforted me." You multiplied your justice in the rebukes we suffer for our sins.
and, turning back to mercy, you comforted me, for I have hope of the coming resurrection. But I will confess to you
But I praise you and confess your mercies. With vessels of psalm, your truth.
With the vessels of the psalm I confess your truth. On the psaltery I sing to you; what is sung on it
is called a psalm. I will sing psalms to you on the cithara, holy one of Israel. I sing psalms to you on the cithara, holy one of Israel.
Because you gave us the Spirit from above, I therefore sing to you on the psaltery. The psaltery has its belly up at the top, facing down. Because the body also is from the earth,
I therefore sing to you on the cithara, which has its belly lying below. My lips will rejoice when I sing to you
and my soul, which you redeemed. Then my lips will rejoice when I sing to you like this, and so will my soul,
which you redeemed. When is that? Listen further. But my tongue also will meditate on your justice all day long.
And my tongue praises you all day long. That 'all day' is in eternity without end. When those are confounded and put in fear
who seek evil for me. Then it will be, when those who wish me ill come to shame and fear: when Christ comes in judgment.
FOR SOLOMON. This psalm is sung of Christ. He is the true Solomon, which means 'peacemaker'. He gives peace upon peace:
first the peace of reconciliation, after that the peace of immortality. GOD, GIVE YOUR JUDGMENT TO THE KING, and your justice to the king's son.
God, entrust to the king, the king's son, your judgment to carry out and your justice to uphold. For he said:
THE FATHER JUDGES NO ONE, BUT HAS GIVEN ALL JUDGMENT TO THE SON. To judge your people in justice and your poor in
judgment. To judge your people and your poor in justice and in judgment. Those who do not wish to be your poor
are not your people. Why? BECAUSE BLESSED ARE THE POOR IN SPIRIT. Whoever is poor in spirit is not proud in spirit.
Let the mountains receive peace for the people, and the hills justice. The apostles receive peace from Christ, that is, reconciliation, to proclaim it to his people,
and the lesser ones in turn learn justice from them: how they should believe and live. He will judge the poor of the people
and will save the children of the poor. He judges and preserves both the humble and their sons. They are one,
just as the city of Zion and the daughter of Zion are. And he will humble the slanderer. And he brings low the slanderer: the devil,
who held the kingdom of death. He deposes him. A slanderer is one who twists good deeds into evil and accuses the innocent.
As he did: DOES JOB WORSHIP GOD FOR NOTHING? And he will endure with the sun. And he lasts together with the sun.

Christ reigns at the right hand of the Father. The Father is the sun, and the Son is his splendor. Before the moon, generations of generations; that is, going before the moon and the generations of generations.
In his immortality he surpasses all mortal things. In accordance with this it says: CHRIST, RISING FROM THE DEAD, DIES NO MORE.
DEATH SHALL NO LONGER HAVE DOMINION OVER HIM. For the moon signifies mortal things; among them are generations of generations, that is, the successions of mortals.
And he shall come down like rain upon the fleece. And he will come as softly into his mother's womb as the rain onto the fleece.
in Gideon's time, when the fleece was made wet on the dry threshing floor, and then the second time the threshing floor was made wet, the
fleece being dry. For teaching came first to the Jews, and none to the Gentiles; and then later, when teaching came to the Gentiles, the Jews lost it.
And as drops falling upon the earth. And like drops of rain falling onto the earth, that is how silently he comes. In his days justice shall rise up
and abundance of peace, until the moon is taken away. In his days justice comes, and plenty of peace, until mortality passes away. Or it says "extollatur" ("is raised up"),
because the Greek "anthanarethe" means both. Then it says: and until the Church is raised up to reign with Christ.
And he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth. And he will rule from one sea to the other,
from the Mediterranean Sea to the Ocean, and from the Jordan to the end of the world. The Ethiopians shall fall down before him,
and his enemies shall lick the earth. The most distant Ethiopians worship him, and his enemies lick the earth.
These are the ones who love Arius and Sabellius and Donatus and Apollinaris. Those men are earth, and the enemies of Christ love them.
They are called Arians and Sabellians, Donatists and Apollinarists after them. The kings of Tarshish and the islands shall offer gifts; the kings of the Arabians and of Sheba shall bring gifts.
Kings from Tarshish and the islands bring him gifts; kings from Arabia and from Sheba bring gifts to him.
And all kings shall worship him; all nations shall serve him. And all kings worship him; all peoples serve him.
For he has delivered the needy from the mighty, and the poor man who had no helper. For he set free his needy one
and the poor people who were helpless, from the mighty devil, who became mighty through men's sins,
not through himself. He shall spare the needy and the poor. He spares him by forgiving the sin.
And he shall save the souls of the poor. And he keeps their souls safe. He teaches them to live rightly, and that is how he keeps them safe.
He shall redeem their souls from usury and iniquity. He redeems them from usury and from injustice.
The evil usury of the murderer is this: when he slays the body, the man himself is slain by it, in soul and in body.
He redeems them from that. He does the same with injustice, for he brings them to justice. And their name shall be honourable in his sight.
And their name is honourable before him, namely that they are called Christians, even though their enemies mock it. And he shall live,
and he shall be given some of the gold of Arabia. And he lives, not here, for it says: HIS LIFE SHALL BE TAKEN FROM THE EARTH,
but in heaven, as it says: RISING FROM THE DEAD, HE DIES NO MORE. And gold comes to him from Arabia.
If it came to that Solomon, it comes all the more to this one, the true one, to whom the wisdom of faith, that is, the three gifts,
is offered from there. And they shall always worship by him. And they always pray, as they learned from him himself.
THY KINGDOM COME. All day long they shall bless him. At all times they praise him. And there shall be a firmament on the earth on the summits of the mountains.
And he will be the confirmation on earth of all the scriptures that came from the prophets, who are called the summits of the mountains,
because they are the highest authors of the holy scriptures. He came to earth to fulfil them. His fruit shall be exalted above Lebanon.
His fruit will be raised above Lebanon. Above the prophets, who are called mountains, and above Lebanon, that is, above every most excellent
patriarch or prophet, his fruit, that is, love, will be raised. Paul pointed to this when he said:
BUT THE FRUIT OF THE SPIRIT IS LOVE. Of this he also said: YET I SHOW YOU A MORE EXCELLENT WAY,
the highly exalted way. And they shall flourish out of the city like the grass of the earth. And from there his saints will blossom, coming from this city to that one,
like the hay of the earth when it gains reviving flowers out there. May his name be blessed forever.
May his name be praised forever. His name endures before the sun. The sun signifies temporal things. His name outlasts them.
And in him all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed. And in him all the tribes of the earth will be blessed. So it was promised to Abraham:
IN YOUR SEED ALL NATIONS SHALL BE BLESSED. All nations shall magnify him. All peoples magnify him. Blessed be the Lord God, who alone does wonders.
May he be praised who alone does wonders. Whoever does them, in him he does them. And blessed be the name of his glory
forever, and all the earth shall be filled with his majesty. And may his glorious name be praised forever, both before the end of the world
and after the end. And all the earth will be filled with his majesty, from the river to the ends of the world.
So be it, so be it. Now you have commanded it; now let it be so. So let it be.
A PSALM OF ASAPH. THE HYMNS OF DAVID THE SON OF JESSE ARE ENDED. David the son of Jesse composed songs and taught the priests to sing them, as it is written,
so that they would praise God with them. They sang them to God in thanks for the temporal goods that he had given them as a figure of the eternal ones. But because they
did not love the eternal things, and also lost the earthly things because of their sins, and their kingdom fell apart,
for that reason the songs also came to an end. Hence this psalm is of Asaph, that is, of the synagogue, whose voice sounds here.
HOW GOOD IS THE GOD OF ISRAEL. The God of Israel, how good he is! To whom? To those who are upright in heart.
To those who are upright in their hearts, who are pleased by his will. But my feet were almost moved.
But my feet, says Asaph, almost wavered off the right way. My steps had almost slipped.
My steps had almost gone astray. Because I was zealous over the wicked. Because I was angry about the unjust
and envied them. Seeing the peace of sinners. Seeing their peace and their comfortable life, when I knew they were sinners
and yet prosperous in this world. For there is no turning aside of their death. For death does not suddenly bow them down. And firmness in their affliction.
Nor is their punishment lasting. They are not in the toil of men. They are not in toil together with other people who are better.
And they will not be scourged with men. And they are not flogged together with them. Therefore pride held them.
Therefore they are proud. They are covered with their iniquity and their impiety. Because of this they were covered with their injustice
and with their wickedness. They did not want to be moderately evil; they plunged themselves wholly into injustice.
Their iniquity came forth as if from fat. Their injustice came as if out of fat, not out of leanness.
That is, they did it without need, not out of need. For although both displease God,
those who do wrong out of necessity and those who do it without necessity, there is still a great difference between them. The poor man says:
"Because I had nothing, therefore I stole." The rich man robs, and does not want anyone to dare even to mention it to him.
Why do they do that? They have passed into the disposition of the heart. Because they overstepped in the thoughts of their hearts,
so that they consider themselves above others, not alongside others. They have exceeded the bounds of the human race; they do not think themselves equal to other men,
though they are in fact like other people. They have thought and spoken wickedness. Evil they thought, evil they spoke.
They have spoken iniquity on high. They spoke the injustice openly. They did not want to hide it.
They have set their mouth in heaven, and their tongue has passed over the earth. They raised their mouth up high, and their tongue went over the earth.
They did not speak as though they were made of clay and mortal. Therefore my people will return here, and full days will be found in them.
Therefore my people turn back here, says Asaph; they turn back to God and consider these people,
and turn their thoughts on them, as to what will come of it that they are prosperous in the world. When?
When full days will be found in them. When the days are fulfilled in them: the coming of Christ. When he comes,
he teaches them to consider it. He tells them how the rich man clothed in purple was buried in hell. And they said: How does God know?
And the same people, the ones returning, said, before they began to return: How does God know human affairs, since the wicked are so fortunate?
And if there is, that is, and whether there is knowledge in the Most High? Is there really any knowledge in the Highest? How can I trust that?
Behold, these are sinners, and they abound; in the world they have obtained riches. "Behold", that is, now see, truly
they are sinful and yet they have plenty, and they also have worldly riches. Not merely enough,
but even more than enough. And I said, that is, Asaph: Then in vain have I justified my heart and washed my hands among the innocent.
In vain I made my heart righteous, in vain I washed my hands,
that is, in vain I practised good works together with the sinless, since I have no such thing.
I am good and poor; the wicked man is rich. Et fui flagellatus tota die (And I was scourged all the day long). And I suffer scourging without ceasing.
He adorns the unrighteous; me, the righteous, he scourges. Et castigatio mea in matutino (And my chastisement in the morning). And always at once, early.
That is: my punishment came early, not after a long time, or else never. Si dicebam narrabo sic (If I said, I will speak thus).
ecce nationem filiorum tuorum reprobaui (behold, I have rejected the generation of your children). If I thought: "I will tell others this, as I have found it out,
deum non curare humana, iniquos maxime felices esse (that God does not care about human affairs, that the wicked are the happiest)," then I have rejected the generation of your children.
Then I have rejected nationem iustorum (the generation of the righteous), who taught nothing of the kind, but the opposite.
Et suscepi cognoscere (And I undertook to know). And then I turned away from that and undertook to understand this kind of dispensation of God.
Hoc labor est ante me (This is toil before me). But that is hard to do; though it may be easy before God, before my eyes it is toilsome.
Donec intrem in sanctuarium dei (Until I enter into the sanctuary of God). Until I come into God's house, into the hidden understanding of the scripturae (scriptures).
Et intellegam in nouissimis eorum (And I understand their last things). And there I perceive what lies ahead, and I think on their final end,

how it will turn out for them. Verumtamen propter dolos posuisti eis (Nevertheless, because of their deceits you have set [it] for them). But even so, because of their deceiving, you prepare deceit for them.
What they are in the habit of doing befalls them. They hasten to deceive people; they themselves are deceived, in that

they think terrena bona eligenda esse pro aeternis (that earthly goods are to be chosen in place of eternal ones). Deiecisti eos dum alleuarentur (You cast them down while they were being lifted up). You cast them down even while they were being raised up.
Their very exaltation was their downfall. Quomodo facti sunt in desolationem subito! (How suddenly they have come to desolation!) How is it that they are now so suddenly deposed
and turned into a wasteland? Defecerunt (They have failed). They have passed away, as if they had never been. Perierunt propter iniquitatem suam (They have perished because of their iniquity).
Because of their iniquity they are lost. How? Veluti somnium exsurgentis (Like the dream of one who wakes). Like the dream of one getting up, who dreamed
that he had treasure, and when he gets up he has nothing. Domine in ciuitate tua imaginem ipsorum ad nihilum rediges (Lord, in your city you will bring their image to nothing).
Lord, you have destroyed their image in your city, for they do not come to heaven, where they would see you.
