Here they did not show your image; there you do not let their image shine. Quia delectatum est cor meum (For my heart was delighted)
et renes mei mutati sunt (and my reins were changed). Because of them it happened to me that my heart came to desire their happiness
and my loins changed, following them, a luxu ad luxuriam (from excess to lust), from excess to lechery.
Et ego ad nihilum redactus sum (And I was brought to nothing). And so, together with them, I was brought to nothing in my mind and in my understanding.
Et nesciui (And I did not know). And I myself did not know my own folly. Vt iumentum factus sum apud te (I became like a beast before you). I became like the cattle in your sight,
for those who love earthly things are like that before your eyes. Et ego semper tecum (And I am always with you). And yet I am always with you.
I did not go after strange gods; I did not attach myself to demons in order to gain anything through their favour. This is what the synagogue says.
...which did not serve idols. You have held my hand, that is, you have raised up the power of my right hand. You held up the power of my right hand. Earthly desire was
my left hand. For I am always with you. For I was always with you. My right hand was with you.
From that right hand I have the power to become one of the sons of God. And in your will you have led me. And in your will,
by your grace, not by my own merits, you led me and brought me among the sons of God.
And in glory you have received me. And in glory you received me. What is this glory? None other than the glory of the resurrection,
which cannot be put into words. For what is there for me in heaven? And besides you, what have I wanted on earth? Indeed, what is it that is kept for me in heaven?
Who can tell it? You have kept immortal riches for me there. And what, then, did I want to gain from you on earth?
Gold, silver, gems, households? Sinners have those too. My heart and my flesh have failed.
My heart and my flesh have wasted away. The wrongful desires of the heart and of the flesh have passed away.
Now I want spiritual things, not carnal things. God of my heart, and God is my portion forever. The God of my heart is in heaven,
and God is my portion forever. In him I have found my riches. For behold, those who go far from you will perish.
For those who put themselves far from you will be lost. I strayed from the way, but not far. They went far,
they who are covered with iniquity. You have destroyed all who commit fornication away from you. You have destroyed all who forsake you,
for they love something other than you. Even if they love you, if they love you for the sake of something else, that is not chaste love,
because that other thing is dearer to them than you. But for me it is good to cleave to God. But for me it is good to cleave to God.
That alone is what I want. That will come when I see him face to face. To put
my hope in the Lord. And it is good for me in the meantime to hope in him, because I do not yet have it in reality, so that I may have it in hope.
That I may proclaim all his praises in the gates of the daughter of Zion. And it is good for me that in the meantime I proclaim all his praises.
Where? In the gates of the daughter of Zion: here in the holy Church, which is the daughter of the eternal contemplation.
UNDERSTANDING OF ASAPH. This psalm is the understanding of the synagogue. She understands and recognizes what is going to happen to her from now on
because of the punishment for her killing of Christ. She laments this; she weeps over it. Christ himself also weeps over it.
As it says: SEEING THE CITY, HE WEPT. WHY, O GOD, HAVE YOU REJECTED US TO THE END? Why, God, have you cast us off utterly?
Why are those now hateful to you who were once dear to you? Has your fury been kindled against the sheep of your flock?
Why are you angry with your flock of sheep? Is it not because we loved earthly things and did not recognize the shepherd?
Remember your congregation, which you have possessed from the beginning. Remember your congregation, which you possessed from the first.
and your right hand out of the midst of your bosom. How is this to be understood? As God said to Moses:
"Put your hand into your bosom." And when it was put in, it was sound. And he said again: "Draw out your hand."
And when it was drawn out, it was leprous. And he said again: "Put it in." And when it was put in, it became sound again.
So it is with you, Jew. Outside, without God, you are unclean; inside, together with him, you are clean.
How long will you stay unclean without him? Did it not go the same way with Moses' rod?
In his hand it was straight; let go out of his hand, it became crooked; but drawn back again, it became straight once more.
Should you not recognize, Jew, that this is written about you? "But God our king has worked salvation before the ages in the midst of the earth."
But God our king worked salvation before the world, in the midst of the earth, that is, in the midst of the Gentiles. Faith and baptism were destined for them before the ages.
Now they are converted to Christ; why then are you turned away from him? "You made the sea firm by your power."
You, God, made the Red Sea firm by your strength, so that it stood like a wall until Israel had passed through it.
In that you prefigured this baptism of the Gentiles, by which they are now delivered from the devil,
as they were then delivered from Pharaoh. "You crushed the heads of the dragons in the water." By doing so you have crushed the pride of the demons. "You broke the head of the dragon."
You broke the pride of the greatest devil in baptism. "You gave him as food to the peoples of the Ethiopians."
You gave him to black people to devour, from among whom some have now become white. They eat the body of the Lord; how then do they eat the devil?
As Augustine says: "Christ, by whom they are made perfect; the devil, whom they consume." They eat Christ in order to be made perfect;
they devour the devil to his destruction. In this sense Moses once gave the Israelites the head of the calf to drink,
first melted in fire and then ground to powder. For true Israelites must melt the devil, grind him, and destroy him.
What could signify the devil more fittingly than that idol in which he was worshipped? For this reason it was said to Peter,
when he saw the unclean things: "Kill and eat." Or else it is understood this way: "You gave him as food to the peoples of the Ethiopians."
You gave him to the Gentiles for their improvement, because through his persecutions they become martyrs and are made perfect. "You broke open springs and torrents."
You broke them open into many streams, springs and brooks. These are the preachers, whom temptation tests to show whether they are
springs or torrents. "You dried up the rivers of Etham," that is, of the strong one. You have dried up the devil's rivers. These are the heretics, the soothsayers,
and the astrologers. "Yours is the day, and yours is the night." Yours are the spiritual, and yours are the carnal. You can keep them both.
Those who have spiritual understanding are able to understand God when they hear "In the beginning was the Word." Those who have carnal understanding
think of the sound from the mouth, as if that were the word. "You made the sun and the moon." You made the wise and the unwise.
Therefore neither of them is to be despaired of. As Paul said: TO THE WISE AND TO THE UNWISE I AM A DEBTOR. You have perfected all the boundaries of the earth.
You have perfected all the boundaries of the earth. Which is the earth? Which are the boundaries? It stands above:
HE HAS WROUGHT SALVATION IN THE MIDST OF THE EARTH, and that means in the midst of the nations. Its boundaries are the apostles. They tell them how far they should reach,
and where they should turn back. That is: NOT TO BE WISER THAN ONE OUGHT TO BE WISE, BUT TO BE WISE UNTO SOBRIETY. Summer and spring,
you formed them. Summer and spring, these you [?] made. The fervent in spirit are summer; the new in faith are spring.
All of these are to be counselled: let them not glory as if they had not received. You made them. Be mindful of this your creature. You who have made all this,
remember this your creature; remember the Jewish people. Thus Asaph, having understanding, intercedes for the one who is still without understanding.
This Asaph is the one of whom it is said: THE REMNANT SHALL BE SAVED. From this one Peter came, and all the apostles.
This Asaph was formerly without understanding but now has understanding, because he now sees fulfilled everything that was prophesied to him.
The enemy reproached the Lord. A hostile people reproached their Lord. What did they say? THIS MAN IS A SINNER. WE DO NOT KNOW
WHERE HE IS FROM. WE KNOW MOSES; GOD SPOKE TO HIM. THIS MAN IS A SAMARITAN.
And a foolish people has provoked your name [?]. An unwise people angered your name. Did they not also say otherwise:
COME, LET US ABOLISH ALL THE FEAST DAYS OF THE LORD FROM THE LAND. Do not deliver to the beasts the souls that confess to you.
Do not give to the beasts the souls that confess to you. Do not give them to the devil and his angels, but give them forgiveness when they say:
WHAT THEN SHALL WE DO, MEN AND BRETHREN? TELL US. Then let them hear, for their salvation: DO PENANCE,
AND LET EACH ONE OF YOU BE BAPTIZED IN THE NAME OF OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST, AND YOUR SINS WILL BE FORGIVEN YOU.
Do not forget the souls of your poor to the end. Do not be forgetful of the souls of your needy ones to the end;
when they humbly give themselves up to you, then remember them. Look to your testament. Look to your covenant;
remember what you have appointed for us: not the land of Canaan, but the kingdom of heaven. Do not let that inheritance escape us.
For those who are darkened are filled with the earth of the houses of iniquities, that is, of wicked houses. For those are filled with the earth
who are blinded by it. Which earth? That of the unrighteous houses. Those who look toward the earth get the dust in their eyes,
and it blinds them. That means: those who have earthly thoughts are thereby led astray in their minds. Whose, then, are those thoughts
if not those of unrighteous houses? These are unrighteous hearts. Let it not happen so to your testament, your people,
that earthly thoughts so blind their hearts; rather, let the remnant be preserved.
Let not the humble one, put to shame, be turned away, that is, not be driven back. Your people, humble and ashamed of its sins, let it not be-
[?] ... be driven away from you. The needy and the poor shall praise your name. The needy and the poor praise you. You should take care of them.
Arise, O Lord, judge my cause. Lord, stand up. Be my advocate. Judge whether I am in the right.
that I believe what I do not see. Be against those who say to me: "Where is your God?"
just as if you did not exist for that reason, because you are invisible to bodily eyes. Remember your reproaches,
those which come from the foolish man all day long. Remember your reproaches, those that come from the unwise man!
at all times. These are the ones who do not believe in the judgment and the resurrection, and they say: "He will no longer know us."
Do not forget the voices of those who pray to you. Do not forget the words of those who beseech you, for they believe your promises.
Let the pride of those who hate you rise up continually. Let the arrogance of those who hate you also come before you.
UNTO THE END: DO NOT DESTROY. This title is spoken to Christ. Do not destroy what you have promised; give it to us in the end.
Give us eternal life. WE WILL CONFESS TO YOU, O GOD, WE WILL CONFESS to you, and we will call upon your name. We confess to you, God,
we confess to you, and we call upon your name. For confessing comes first, and calling upon comes after it.
So make our temples clean through confession, so that when you are called upon they may be visited by you. I will tell of your wonders.
Emptied of evils through confession and filled with good things through calling upon you, I begin, by telling of them, to pour out the things you have filled me with. When I receive the time,
I will judge righteously. When it is time and the day of judgment comes, then I will judge justly. This means the whole Christ,
head and body, for he does not judge alone, but the saints together with him. The earth has flowed down. The earth flowed down.
People drew themselves downward; they longed for what is lower. In this they all do wrong:
when they are told to long for what is higher, they long for what is lower. And all who dwell in it. And all who dwell on it.
This explains what came before. The earth has flowed down in those who live on it. What are they but earth?
I have strengthened its pillars. That is why I strengthened its pillars. The pillars of the faithful are the apostles, and they also wavered during the Passion,
but they were made firm at the resurrection. After that they taught others not to flow down. I said to the wicked: Do not act wickedly.
I said to the unjust: Do not act unjustly. Did they avoid it because of this? Not at all. That is how they became mortal
and wretched. And to the sinners: Do not lift up your horn. And to the sinners I said: Do not raise your horn.
If you are sinful through greed, do not deny it out of pride. Whoever does not admit it is both wicked
and lifting up his horn. So do not be lifted up; do not speak wickedness against God. Do not be arrogant,
do not speak unjustly against God, as someone does who says to you: "Why does God blame me more than others?"
"Although I am not righteous, others are more unrighteous than I am. It goes well with them; it goes badly with me." Whoever speaks this way accuses God,
and thinks himself more righteous, because God's judgments displease him. For neither from the east nor from the west nor from the desert mountains.
Take heed, for you will not escape the judgment of him who is over all, whether from east to west,
or from west to east, or in any desert mountains, or among people in between. Wherever you are,
there he is. Whatever you say, he hears it. Why is that? For God is the judge.
For God himself is the judge, not a human being. If it were a human being, he would not hear everywhere, as God does.
He humbles this one and exalts that one. He brings low the proud Jewish people; he raises up the humble Gentile people. For a cup is in the hand of the Lord.
For in God's power is the law given to the Jews, which is called the Old Testament. It is the cup. What kind of cup? A cup of pure wine.
A cup of clear wine. Full of mixture. Yet it is full of mixture, full of dregs, as in new wine (must),
where the two are mixed together. For there the New Testament lay hidden in the dregs of the bodily sacraments.
There was circumcision of the flesh, which for us is circumcision of the heart. There was the temple, which for us is the holy Church. There was the land of promise,
which for us is the kingdom of heaven. There were many sacrifices, which signify the one sacrifice that was offered on the cross of Christ.
And he poured from this into that. And so he poured out of that cup of the Old Testament into this cup of the New Testament
the clear wine, that is, the spiritual understanding. But its dregs were not emptied out. But the dregs were not scooped out;
they were left there, for the carnal understanding remains with the Jews. All the sinners of the earth shall drink.
The Jews drink of these dregs together with all sinners, for the carnal understanding pleases them. But I will rejoice forever.
But I rejoice forever: Christ, together with his body. For it says in the title: "To the end, do not destroy." And I will break all the horns of sinners.
I will overthrow the high positions of the proud. And the horns of the righteous shall be exalted. The gifts of Christ are the horns of the righteous; they will be exalted at the end.
A psalm of Asaph. A song to the Assyrians. I. [?] To those who direct.
All those who want to direct their feet into right paths are the ones Asaph greets. God is known in Judea. Only in Judea is God known.
Be in confession, and so you make yourself known to God. Those who said, "We have no king but Caesar," do not confess him.
His name is great in Israel. In Israel his mighty name is known. Those who recognize God in Christ, as the Gentiles do, are Israelites;
they are the ones who see God, and his name is known to them. Those who recognize him only as a man, as the Jews do, are not Israelites.
His noble name, that he is called God, is not known to them. And his place was made in peace, and his dwelling in Zion.
And his place is in peace. It is among those who want what he wants. Among the like-minded there is always peace.
And his dwelling is in contemplation. In eternity, where one sees him face to face, there he dwells in them. There is peace.
There he broke the powers of the bows, and the shield, and the sword, and war. There he has broken strong bows,
and shield, and sword, and war itself, because there is eternal peace. Here there is war against you.
The war is within you. You are struggling with yourself, because you struggled against God. But still,
so that you may win victory over it, follow Paul. What does he say? "Therefore let sin not reign in your mortal body,
so as to obey its desires." If you follow him, you will come from this lack of peace to eternal peace.
You give light wonderfully from the eternal mountains. You shine out wonderfully from the eternal mountains,
whose height never passes away. Through the apostles you have given light to the whole world.
All the foolish of heart were troubled. As some of them were enlightened, so others were troubled. Which ones? All the unwise.
All the men of riches slept their sleep, and found nothing in their hands. The rich slept their sleep,
and when they woke, they had nothing in their hands. Those sleep away their life to whom riches have come here,
and whose delight is in them, and who do not love the other life, nor send anything ahead from here to there
for them to find there. Here they slept; there they will be woken. Here they had,
there nothing. At your rebuke, O God of Jacob, those who mounted horses fell asleep. At your rebuke, God of Jacob,
those who sat on horses fell asleep. The very thing that should have woken them made them fall asleep. Who were they?
Those whom their pride carries along. You are terrible, and who will stand against you then, in your wrath? You are terrible, and who will stand against you then,
when the day of judgment comes? Who will escape your anger then? From heaven you hurled judgment;
the earth was afraid and was still. You shot the judgment from heaven: "Go into the eternal fire." At that the sinner was terrified,
and he stopped, he who before would not stop. There he has put an end to sins. When God rose up in judgment
to save all the meek of the earth. That was when it was: it was in the judgment, when he also rose up
to save all the gentle, of whom he said: "Blessed are the meek." Where he loses the one group,
there he keeps the other. For the thought of man will confess to you, and the remnants of thought will keep a feast day for you.
For the thought of man first confesses to you, and the remnants of the thought hold a feast for you. Confession pleases God first; the remem-
brance of past crimes holds feasts for him. That is why David said: "And my sin is always before me."
Make vows and pay them to the Lord your God. Vow to God, and fulfil your vows. It is better not to vow.
…than to vow and not pay. All who are round about him offer gifts to the terrible one. All who are around him bring gifts to the terrible one.
Christ is common to all, and therefore he is in the middle. Those who love him are around him. Or else: there at the altar,
where his body is consecrated, all who stand around make offerings. And to him who takes away the spirit of princes. And they make offerings to him
who takes away the proud spirit of the princes and gives a humble spirit. Terrible with the kings of the earth.
To the one who is terrible together with the rulers of the earth. "Chastise your body and bring it into subjection" [?]. By doing this you are a king, and he is terrible to you.
To the end, for Idithun. A psalm of Asaph himself. Idithun means "leaping over"; Asaph means "congregation." What does that mean?
It is the congregation that leaps over which speaks here, the congregation that wants to come to the end, where there is nothing more to leap over.
With my voice I cried to the Lord, and my voice reached God, and he attended to me. With my voice I cried to the Lord,
and it reached God, and he paid heed to me. Because it called him himself to me and aimed at nothing else,
he therefore heard it. In the day of my tribulation I sought God. On the day of my trouble I sought God, and not for anything else,
because I am one who leaps over, but only for him himself, so that I may cleave to him securely. What is the day of tribulation? Nothing but all
this life, of which it is written: "The life of man on earth is temptation." If it is temptation, then it is tribulation.
With my hands, that is, with my works. With my hands, that is, with [?] my works. By night. By night. In this world.
Before him, not before men. And I have not been deceived. And in this I am not deceived, because my reward is more certain, and what was promised to me
comes to me. I refused to comfort my soul. I would not comfort my soul. This life is so hateful to me,
I am so weary of it, it is such an exile, that I care nothing for human comfort in it.
I remembered God and was delighted. I remembered God; that was delightful to me, that gave me joy. I chattered.
Out of that joy I spoke playful words; I could not keep silent for gladness. Or it says: "I was exercised." I took my fill of that delight
by thinking further on it. And my spirit failed. And in that thinking I gave out. It reaches higher than my mind.
No one can know its delight. All my enemies anticipated the watches. All my enemies were more watchful,
the powers of the air, at deceiving me than I could be at keeping guard. I was troubled. My mind became troubled because of the danger of my chattering.
And I did not speak. And I fell silent. Or it says: "My eyes anticipated the watches.
I was troubled and did not speak." I woke early in the night, and in silence I grieved over my sins.
We now call these watches nocturns. That is why we hold assemblies before dawn. I thought on the days of old.
In that stillness I thought on the old days that are now gone, in which the human race sinned without growing weary of it. From that came
[?] I [was] troubled. And I had the eternal years in mind. And for comfort I took into my mind the eternal years, of which it is written:
AND YOUR YEARS SHALL NOT FAIL. These thoughts I set against those who grieved me. And I meditated in the night with my heart.
And so I thought at night in my heart. I babbled. My mind played there in the heart, while the words were silent,
because that babbling was less dangerous for me. And I searched my spirit. And I searched my mind; I talked with myself.
And I said. And I thought thus: Will God cast off forever? Will God reject the human race for good?
And will he not add, so that it may yet be pleasing to him? And will he not yet act through his passion so that it becomes pleasing to him?
Or will he cut off his mercy forever from the world and from generation? Or will he take his grace away entirely from the world
and from the generation of men? Or will God forget to have mercy? Or will he forget to show the grace of his incarnation
which he has promised? Or will he hold back his mercy in his anger? Or will anger take his grace away from him? And I said.
And, passing beyond, I thought thus: Now I have begun. Before, it was not; now it is. Passing beyond, I began to understand these things.
This is the change of the right hand of the Most High. I understand well whose change this is, and I am glad of it. Christ is the right hand of the Most High,
who has changed the human race from darkness into light, from slavery into the freedom of the children of God; who has brought me myself out of myself.
I have now stretched myself out toward him; it would be dangerous for me if I relied on myself. I remembered the works of the Lord,
for I will remember your wonders from the beginning, and I will meditate on all your works. This shows that I remembered God's
works: that I remember your wonders from the very beginning, and that I ponder all your works. You made man in your image;
you received the gifts of Abel; you saved us in the ark; you required Isaac as an offering, as a type of Christ.
All of this makes me rejoice. And in your affections I will babble. And I talk joyfully about your loving deeds. Since the babbler is one
who cannot keep silent, it follows that I too cannot keep silent. O God, your way is in the holy. O God, your way is in Christ.
He said: I AM THE WAY. What god is great like our God? Who is a God as mighty as our God? You are the God who alone does wonders.
You are God; you alone do wonders, and by this you show that there is no other. You have made your power known among the peoples.
Christ, who is your power, you have made known to the gentiles. You have redeemed your people with your arm. In him you have redeemed your people.
He is your power; he is your arm. The sons of Israel and of Joseph. You have redeemed both: both the sons of Israel
and the people of the gentiles, which clings to the true Joseph, whom that earlier one signified. The waters saw you, O God; the waters saw you.
The peoples saw you; the peoples saw you. That was because you made your power known among the peoples. And they were afraid.
And they feared you; that was the change of the right hand of the Most High. And the depths were troubled. And the watery depths were troubled.
that is, the consciences of men. What can be deeper? A multitude of the sound of waters. Great was the roar of the waters.
in hymns and canticles and prayers. Where did that come from? The clouds gave forth a voice. The clouds sounded: the apostles preached.
For your arrows passed through. Your words went through the hearts of men. The voice of your thunder in
the wheel. Your terrible works shall resound through the circle of the earth. Your lightnings lit up the world.
Your miracles shone out to the whole world, because they went round about, thundering and flashing. The earth was moved and trembled.
Because of that the earth was moved and trembled: men were terrified by it. Your way is in the sea. Your ways were among the nations.
you came to them then. And your paths are in many waters. Your journeys were among many peoples. And your footsteps shall not be known.
And your journeys were not recognized by the Jews. They still say: "Christ has not yet come." You led your people like sheep
by the hand of Moses and Aaron. Yet you led that same people of yours like sheep out of Egypt by the hands of Moses and Aaron.
Now they have repaid you with poor thanks, in that they alone among all peoples will not acknowledge you.
Understanding of Asaph. What does Asaph proclaim to us? Only that we should hear one thing and understand another. Hear
how the old people was ungrateful for the benefits of God, and understand that we must not be the same.
Attend, my people, to my law. My people, understand my law. Incline your ear to the words of my mouth.
Incline your ear to the words of my mouth. I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter propositions from the beginning.
I will open my mouth in comparisons; I will speak hidden sayings from the beginning of your journey out of Egypt.
Every day we hear parables in the holy Gospel, as when Christ compares himself to a grain of wheat. There we also hear
propositions, such as this one: "What do you think of Christ? Whose son is he?" What did the Jews say then? "David's."
And what did he say in turn? How can Christ be both, both the son of David, as you say, and the lord of David, as David himself said
when he spoke of him like this: "The Lord (that is, the Father) said to my Lord (that is, to his Son Christ): Sit at my right hand"?
In a hidden way the proposition taught them to understand Christ as the son of David in time and as the Son of God in eternity. Parables and propositions are the figures
of which Paul said: "All these things happened to them in figure." How great the things we have heard and known, and our fathers have told us.
This is the voice of a man, the voice of Asaph; before this it was the voice of God. What mighty things we have heard and understood,
which he did in the Old Testament, and now we have recognized them in the New; and our forefathers, Moses and the prophets, told them to us.
They are not hidden from their children in another generation. They are not hidden from their children in another birth.
We are the other birth, the other generation, to which regeneration has now come. Telling the praises of the Lord and his mighty works.
and his wonders which he did. Before this it says: "Our fathers have told us." This belongs with: "Telling the praises of the Lord."
Telling us his praise, his power and the wonders that he did. And he raised up a testimony in Jacob
and set a law in Israel. And he set up a testimony in Jacob. What is that? It is only what follows:
and he set a law in Israel. The law itself was the testimony, which people were to believe, because God devised it
and acknowledged it as his own. Which he commanded our fathers: how many commandments he gave our forefathers. For what purpose? To make
them known to their children. To make them known to their children. Why to them? That another generation may know. So that the other generation might know them,
which they did not know. Which generation is that? The children who will be born. The Gentiles, who are born in the New Testament. And they will rise up.
And they will rise with Christ. And they will tell their children. And they tell them to their children. In what words?
That they may set their hope in God. That their children may set their hope on God, not on their own righteousness, as those others did.
And may not forget the works of God. And that they may not forget God's works, for he, not man, is the doer of good works.
And may seek out his commandments. And that they may strive to fulfil his commandments with his help. That they may not become like their fathers,
a perverse and embittering generation. That they may not become a perverse generation with a bitter taste,
like their forefathers, who died in the desert. A generation that did not set its heart right. Such a generation as did not set its heart right.
And whose spirit was not faithful with God. And did not make itself one in mind with God. The sons of Ephraim, bending the bow and shooting their arrows,
turned back in the day of battle. The sons of Ephraim fled when the battle came, even though they drew their bows and shot with them.
They began to fight; afterwards they went back on it [?]. When temptation came, they worshipped the calf, though before they had said:
"Whatever the Lord our God has spoken to us, we will do and we will hear." They did not keep the covenant of God
and would not walk in his law. That is where this belongs, and by Ephraim understand all of them. They did not keep God's law. "Covenant" means law,
as "testimony" did above as well. In it they would not walk. And they forgot his good deeds and
his wonders which he showed them. And they forgot his kindnesses and his wonders, which he showed them.
In the sight of their fathers he did wonders in the land of Egypt, in the field of Tanis. In the sight of Moses and Aaron he did wonders in Egypt,
where the city of Tanis is, whose genitive in Greek is Taneos. He split the sea and brought them through; he made the waters stand as in a skin bag.
He broke the sea apart, led them through, and made the waters stand as if they were held [?] in a skin. And he led them in a cloud by day
and all night by the light of fire. And by day he led them with a cloud, by night with the glow of the fire.
He split the rock in the wilderness and gave them drink as from a great deep. He broke the rock in the wilderness and gave them drink.
as from a deep flood. And he brought water out of the rock, and brought forth waters like rivers. And he let water out of the stone,
as abundant as a river. And they went on still to sin against him, that is, not to believe him. Yet they went further still
in disbelieving him. Even then they did not grow weary of their unbelief. They provoked the Most High to anger in the waterless place,
that is, in the drought. They provoked God to anger there in the dryness. The land was dry, and their minds were dry.
That provoked God to anger. And they tempted God in their hearts, by asking food for their souls. And then they tempted God in their hearts,
in that they asked food for their souls, not to nourish the soul, but to have it inside them.
And they spoke evil of God. And so they spoke evilly about God: Can God prepare a table in the desert?
Can God give food here in the wilderness? For he struck the rock, and the waters flowed and the streams overflowed; can he also give bread, or prepare
a table for his people? Since he struck the rock and at once abundant water flowed out of it,
can he also give bread and set tables for his people? Therefore the Lord heard, and put off (that is, vengeance).
Therefore the Lord heard it, and postponed his punishment. And a fire was kindled in Jacob, and wrath went up in Israel.
And in keeping with their behaviour, a fire burned in Jacob, and his anger went up in Israel. His anger was the fire.
Because they did not believe in God, nor hope in his salvation. Because they did not believe in God, nor trust in his Saviour.
Whose? Israel's, of course. And he commanded the clouds above, and opened the doors of heaven. And then he commanded the clouds above,
and he opened the doors of heaven. And he rained manna on them to eat, and gave them the bread of heaven. And he rained manna on them to eat,
and gave them heavenly bread. Man ate the bread of angels. Man ate the bread of angels. He ate manna, which signifies Christ;
he is the bread of angels, because they live by him. He gave them food in abundance. He gave them food in abundance.
In historical terms that is how it happened, but it was all a figure of the later things that have taken place in the New Testament.
He moved the south wind from heaven, and by his power brought in the southwest wind. He brought the south wind from heaven,
and the southwest wind (Africus), which is also called Lips, he brought by his power. And he rained flesh upon them like dust.
And with these he threw flesh upon them, as thick as dust. And feathered birds like the sand of the sea.
And birds like the sand of the sea. And they fell in the midst of their camp, around their tents. They fell into the camps and around the
camps. And they ate and were filled exceedingly. And they ate their fill, and were filled beyond measure. And he brought them what they desired.
And so he fulfilled their desire. They were not deprived of what they desired. Nor did he deny them what they craved.
What happened then? Their food was still in their mouths, and the wrath of God came up upon them. While their food was still in their mouths,
then God's wrath came upon them, which he had held back so that he might first show them what he is able to do.
And he slew very many of them. And so he destroyed many of them. Or it says "the fat ones among them", that is, those who were proud among them.
And he hindered the chosen of Israel. And the wrath of God hindered God's chosen ones, such as Moses, Aaron and Phinehas,
so that they could be of no help to them. In all these things they sinned still, and did not believe in his wonders. In all these things
they kept on sinning, and in his wonders, that is, while looking upon his wonders,
they were unbelieving. And their days came to an end in vanity. And in vanity, not in truth, their days passed away.
And their years in haste. And their years quickly. When he slew them, then they sought him, and they turned back.
When he slew them, then they sought him and turned back to him, not out of love but out of fear.
Before daybreak they came to him. Then they came to him early. And they remembered that God is their helper,
and the most high God is their redeemer. And because of that distress they remembered that the most high God is their helper
and their redeemer. And they loved him with their mouth, but their heart was not right with him, and with their tongue they lied to him, nor
were they held faithful in his covenant. And they loved him in their words, but their heart was not right toward him, and with their tongues they lied to him,
nor were they faithful to his law. But he is merciful, and he will be gracious toward their sins, and will not destroy them.
But he is merciful, and he will be appeased concerning their sins, that is, he accepts atonement for their sins
even when they slay the Son of God. And so he does not destroy them, but instead the remnant is to be saved.
And he abounded in turning away his wrath. And it pleased him fully to turn away his wrath.
And he did not kindle all his wrath. Nor did he kindle all his wrath. He did not let his wrath be as great
as they had deserved, neither then nor afterward in his Passion. And he remembered that they are flesh,
a spirit that goes and does not return. And he did this remembering their frailty, that they are flesh. And what more besides?
A spirit that goes away and does not return. It returns at the judgment, but it does not return here to dwell.
How often they embittered him in the desert, provoked him to wrath in the waterless land. Ah, how often they angered him in the wilderness,
how often they provoked him to wrath there in the dry land. And they turned and tempted God. And they were turned to God,
and right after that they tempted him again. And they embittered the Holy One of Israel. And they angered the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember his hand on the day he delivered them from the hand of the oppressor. They did not remember the power that he showed
when he freed them from the power of Pharaoh, who oppressed them. How he set his signs in Egypt and his wonders in the field of Tanis. How he [set] signs
…did in Egypt, and wonders in the fields of Tanis. Taneos means "humble command." Therefore many hold
that Taneos is the name of a city and does not decline. But others say, as stands above: Tanis is the nominative,
Taneos the genitive. "And he turned their rivers into blood, and the flowings of waters," that is, waters bubbling up from the depths, "so that they might not drink."
He turned rivers and springs into blood, so that they could not drink. The Egyptians dug and searched for springs of water,
but instead of water they found blood. "He sent among them the cynomyia," that is, the dog-fly, "and it devoured them; and the frog, and it destroyed them."
He sent dog-flies upon them, which devoured them, and the frog, which [?] them. "And he gave to the blight
(that is, to the rust) their crops, and their labours to the locust." He gave their crops to blight [?] and their labours to the locusts.
"And he killed their vines with hail and their mulberry trees with frost." He destroyed their vineyards with hail and their mulberry trees with hoarfrost.
"And he gave their cattle over to the hail and their possessions to fire." He gave their cattle to the hail, and everything else they owned to the lightning.
Blight, frost and fire do not appear in Exodus; instead there are three others: gnats, sores and darkness. "He sent upon them the wrath of his indignation,
indignation and wrath and tribulation, visitations sent by evil angels." He sent upon them the anger of his wrath: wrath,
and indignation, and troubles, and he sent harm upon them through the devils. These were servants of an evil will, so that they would hate the people of God.
and sickness, so that they became covered in scabs, and death, so that they lost their firstborn.
Visitations (immissiones), which are called "castings-upon," come both from good angels and from evil angels.
Good angels cast fire upon Sodom. Evil angels cast fire from heaven to burn up Job's property, and also what we read here:
sickness and death upon the Egyptians. Whether the evil angels also produced the frogs, the gnats and the blood is an open question.
"He made a way for the path of his wrath; he did not spare their souls from death, and he shut up their cattle in death."
He cleared the way for his anger, since he gave them no protection; he did not spare their lives from death.
He shut up their stall-cattle in death. "And he struck every firstborn in Egypt, the first fruits of their labour in the tents of Ham."
He struck the eldest in every place, and he struck the first fruits of their labour in the dwellings of Ham.
The two halves of the verse say the same thing, because Ham's descendants settled Egypt. "And he took away his people like sheep
and led them through the desert like a flock." After doing this, he took his people away like sheep
and guided them through the wilderness like his flock. "And he led them out in hope." He led them out in the hope of the promised land,
just as he has now also redeemed us from the darkness of unbelief and leads us through spiritual pastures in this world,
as if in the desert, with the hope of the heavenly kingdom. "And they did not fear." They did not fear him, and neither should we.
IF GOD IS FOR US, WHO IS AGAINST US? And the sea covered their enemies. And the sea overwhelmed their enemies. Baptism has done the same to ours.
And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctification. And he brought them onto Zion, his holy mountain; but us he brought into the holy Church. The mountain which ac-
-quired his right hand. The mountain which his right hand won, as Christ won the Church. And he cast out the nations before their face.
And he drove the nations out of their sight. He still does the same to the evil spirits, who are the authors of the errors of the heathen. He keeps casting them out of the hearts of the faithful.
And by lot he divided the land for them with a line of distribution. And he divided the land by casting lots, with a measuring-rope,
as is now done with a measuring-rod. So now it is one and the same Spirit, dividing to each one as he wills. And he made the tribes of Israel dwell in their tents.
And he made Israel dwell in their places. In the heavenly seat from which the evil angels fell, there he settles his people.
But what did their children and their descendants do afterwards? And they tempted [?] and provoked God most high, and did not keep his testimonies.
They did the same: they tempted the heavenly God again and angered him, and they did not keep his testimonies.
And they turned away and did not keep the covenant, just as their fathers did not. And they turned away from him and did not keep their agreement
which they had made with God, just as their forefathers also did not keep it. The forefathers did evil
while travelling on the way; the descendants did no better while sitting at home. They were turned into a crooked bow.
They were turned and changed into a crooked bow, because they aimed at evil, not at good.
And they stirred him to anger on their hills. And [?] they provoked him to anger on their hills,
where they practised idolatry. And with their graven images they provoked him to jealousy. And with their idol-images they provoked him to enm-
-ity. God heard, that is, God took notice. Then God observed all of this. And what then? He utterly despised Israel
and brought them to nothing. Then he utterly rejected them and brought them to nothing. And he rejected the tabernacle of Shiloh,
his tabernacle, where he dwelt among men. And he thrust away from himself the tabernacle that was in Shiloh,
where he had dwelt in people, not in a tent. Nor was the building dear to him once he no longer cared for those
for whose sake it had been made. This happened under Eli the priest. And he delivered their strength into captivity, and their beauty into the hands of the enemy.
And he sent their strength and their beauty into exile and into the hand of the enemies. That was the ark of the Lord,
which the foreigners took from them. And he shut up his people with the sword and despised his inheritance. And he surrounded his people with the sword
and rejected his inheritance. Fire, that is, the wrath of those waging war, devoured their young men, and their maidens were not lamented.
War destroyed the young men; no one mourned the young women who had been taken, as custom required;
each man was more concerned for himself. Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows will not be wept for.
Hophni and Phinehas, the sons of Eli, lay dead in battle. And their widows too, one of whom died at once in childbed,
were not mourned. The common grief did not allow them to be. And the Lord was awakened as one sleeping,
like a mighty man drunk with wine. Then the Lord was awakened as if he were sleeping, like a mighty man
drunk with wine. Who would dare to speak this way of God without his Spirit? He seemed to the Philistines to be asleep
when he allowed them such things, and they said: WHERE IS THEIR GOD? But he awoke and showed them that at once.
And he struck his enemies in the hinder parts. And he rose up and struck them in the hinder parts. Why? Because they loved the hinder things,
which should have seemed to them like dung. Whoever receive the testament of God and yet practise vanity set the ark of God beside the idols,
whose vanity is thrown down, as Dagon was. But the ark of God, that is, the secret of the testament, which is the kingdom of heaven, remains forever.
He gave them everlasting reproach. He gave them eternal disgrace, because nothing so shameful happened to others.
And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim, but he chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loved. And God did not want Joseph or Ephraim;
he did not want the old people, who sought earthly rewards. But he wanted Judah; he wanted the new people, who desire heavenly things,
and Mount Zion, the Church, which looks toward future rewards, the rewards to come. Joseph was of outstanding merit;
Ephraim was preferred by Jacob over his brother Manasseh. What then is to be understood by such renowned names
except the whole Jewish people? Since God speaks to us in parables, be understanding of his words, which say one thing
and signify another. And he built his sanctuary like that of the unicorns, that is, his sanctification, in the land which he founded forever.
And he built his sanctification like the unicorn, in the land that he established forever.
The holy Church is founded upon the rock. In it is his sanctuary, the people of God, which is like the unicorn because of its single hope. And he chose David his servant.
And he chose David his servant over Joseph and over Ephraim. He chose Christ, whom he calls a servant because of
the form of a servant. And he took him from the flocks of sheep; from following the ewes with young he took him, to feed Jacob his servant and Israel his inheritance.
And he took him from the flocks of sheep; from walking after the ewes he received him. For what purpose did he receive him?
To feed Jacob his servant and Israel his inheritance: to pasture the people instead of the sheep. For Christ too has now been taken from the Jews,
and he tends the flocks of the Gentiles. And he fed them in the innocence of his heart. And he tends them in the sinlessness of his heart.
Who is as innocent as Christ? And he led them in the understandings of his hands. And he led them in the understandings of his hands,
that is, of his deeds. Their understanding is his deeds. Therefore they say to him: GIVE ME UNDERSTANDING AND I WILL SEARCH YOUR LAW.
A PSALM OF ASAPH. The congregation of God here laments the desolation of the city of Jerusalem and of the temple of God, which happened under Antiochus.
as the things that happened under Titus and Vespasian are lamented earlier, in the seventy-third psalm. Those who have read the First Book of Maccabees
know it. O GOD, THE NATIONS HAVE COME INTO your INHERITANCE. God, avenge it! The nations have come into your inheritance.
This is spoken in the past tense on behalf of those who were still to suffer it, just as things to come are written about in the same way elsewhere.
THEY GAVE GALL FOR MY FOOD. They have defiled your holy temple. They have defiled your holy house.
They have brought the abomination of idols in there, and they force us to sacrifice the flesh of swine. It can also be under-
stood of those in holy Church who, in a time of persecution, were forced by torture to deny God,
some of whom later made their peace with God through penance. They have made Jerusalem like a shelter for guarding fruit. They made Jerusalem as desolate
as the huts for guarding fruit that people put up in an orchard, which stand empty once the fruit has been gathered in.
They have given the dead bodies of your servants as food to the birds of the sky, and the flesh of your saints to the beasts of the earth. They gave the corpses of your servants
and the flesh of your saints to birds and beasts to tear apart. They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
They poured out their blood around Jerusalem as if it were worth no more than water, and there was no one who would bury them.
They were slain inside and outside, in the city and around the city, and there they lay unburied.
We have become a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a mockery to those who are around us. We have become a disgrace to our neighbours,
a thing to sneer at and a mockery to those who are around us. How long, Lord, will you be angry? To the end? That is: Lord, do not be angry to the end.
How long, Lord, will you be so angry, to the end? Will your jealous anger burn like fire?
How long will your indignation be kindled? Lord, never show your anger and your indignation to the end.
Anger looks to vengeance; jealous anger looks to the demand for chastity. What is this chastity? That the soul should not scorn the law of its Lord
and perish by going whoring away from its God. Pour out your wrath on the nations that have not known you, and on the kingdoms that have not called upon your name.
Pour out your wrath on the peoples who do not acknowledge you, and on the kingdoms that do not call
upon your name. Turn your wrath against those who refuse to have any knowledge of God. For they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling place.
For they devoured Jacob, turning some of them to their side with threats and terrors, and they laid waste his dwelling place,
as it says earlier: LIKE A SHELTER FOR GUARDING FRUIT. Do not remember our former iniquities. Our old wrongdoings
that have come down to us from our parents, do not remember, for even the new ones are too many for us. Let your mercies come quickly to meet us.
May your grace come quickly to meet us with forgiveness, before we are brought to judgment. For we have been brought very low.
That is, in righteousness. For we are utterly without good. Help us, O God our saviour. Help us, God our saviour.
because we are poor and weak. Though we have free will, we still cannot do without your help.
For the glory of your name, Lord, deliver us. Set us free for the glory of your name, so that he who glories, not in himself,
but in the Lord, may glory. And be merciful to our sins for your name's sake. Be gracious to our sins for the sake of your name,
not for our sake, because we have earned nothing other than punishments. Lest they say among the nations: Where is their God?
So that the peoples may never say: Where is their God? and think that there is no God, or, if there is, that he does not help his own.
And let it, namely vengeance, be made known among the nations before our eyes. And among the peoples let the vengeance become known,
so that we may see them either in punishment or in penitence. And that is not a curse but a prophecy. Let the groaning of the fettered
enter into your sight. Let the sighing of the oppressed come before you. Let it move you to pity how great their distress is in their chains.
The very corruptibility of the body is a heavy fetter, under which all good people sigh. Take note of that sighing. According to the greatness of your arm,
take possession of the children of those put to death. According to the greatness of your power, take possession of the children of the slain.
Let their descendants be multiplied according to your strength, so that persecution makes Christians sprout forth, not perish.
Render to our neighbours sevenfold into their bosom. Give sevenfold into their bosom to our neighbours. Give them secretly, in their hearts,
full reward: cast them into a reprobate mind. Their reproach with which they reproached you, Lord. Repay them the reproach they made against you.
All these words were fulfilled on Antiochus. But we your people and the sheep of your flock will give praise to you forever.
But we, your people, whom they meant to destroy, and the sheep of your flock, will give praise to you always, until the end of the world.
From generation to generation we will proclaim your praise. We will proclaim your praise in generation after generation,
for in that other world, where God is seen as he is, no one there proclaims God to another.
UNTO THE END, FOR THOSE WHO SHALL BE CHANGED, A TESTIMONY, TO ASAPH HIMSELF, FOR THE ASSYRIANS. This psalm is directed toward Christ; it is sung for those
who are changed into what is better: a testimony to the truth, given by the synagogue itself, of this matter, that Christ shall come
and that his vineyard, the holy Church, shall be planted. It is also sung for those who set their hearts aright, so that we may not be [?] a generation that did not set its heart aright.
YOU WHO RULE ISRAEL, ATTEND. You who rule Israel, look upon us, show us your grace, rise for us, new sun.
So says he who waits for him, who longs for him, who sets his heart aright. You who lead Joseph like a sheep, who sit upon the cherubim, appear.
You who lead Joseph like a sheep and sit upon the cherubim, show yourself incarnate. You who lead the faithful people
and sit upon the fullness of knowledge, come here to us. Before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh. Show yourself before the Jews,
before Israel, where Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh are. Stir up your power and come, to save us. Awaken your power.
show it, and come, so that you may save us. God of hosts, turn us. God of powers, turn us to you,
for we had been turned away from you. And show your face, and we shall be saved. And show your countenance,
and so we shall be saved. First the face of the man; after that, when the time comes, the face of the Godhead. So we will be saved.
O Lord God of hosts, how long will you be angry at the prayer of your servant? Lord God of powers, when you then come,
how far will you be angry then, as a father and not as a judge, at the prayer of your servant?
We were enemies. But when we are reconciled, how then do you answer us concerning the words
that you teach us: LEAD US NOT INTO TEMPTATION? You will feed us with the bread of tears, and you will give us drink in tears, in measure.
This is how you answer us: you feed us and give us drink with tears, in measure. So you let us be tem-
pted, weeping, in order to instruct us, not to crush us, according to the words of Paul: GOD IS FAITHFUL, WHO DOES NOT LET YOU BE TEMPTED
BEYOND WHAT YOU ARE ABLE TO BEAR. You have made us an object of contradiction to our neighbours. You have set us, says Asaph,
as an object of contradiction to our neighbours. You sent us to the gentiles like lambs among wolves. We preached Christ to them,
but they said: WHO IS THIS PROCLAIMER OF NEW DEMONS? And our enemies mocked us. And our enemies jeered at us
because we said that a dead man had risen. And that turned into such contradiction that we were fed with the bread of tears and given drink in tears,
but still in measure. O Lord God of hosts, turn us, and show your face, and we shall be saved. That stands above. You brought a vine out of Egypt;
you drove out the nations and planted it. You brought a vineyard out of Egypt, for whose sake you drove out the peoples,
and you planted it. You drove out the Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, Amorites and Jebusites, and made room for it.
You made a way before it, and planted its roots, and it filled the land. You made a way in its sight, and planted its roots,
and filled the earth with it. The Jewish people dwelt from the Jordan to the Great Sea,
although some dwelt beyond the Jordan. But the later vineyard, which grew out of that one,
filled the earth. The beginning of the vine went to the sea and to the river. The beginning of the vineyard reached to the sea on one side and to the river on the other.
The end went from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth. And by this the earth was filled with it. Its shadow cov-
ered the mountains, and its shrubs the cedars of God. Its shadow, that is, of the former vineyard, covered the mountains;
I mean the patriarchs and prophets. And its small shrubs, those of middling faith, God made into his cedars, men of the highest merit.
You stretched out its branches to the sea, and its shoots to the river. You stretched the branches of the vineyard to the Great Sea, which lies nearby,
and its shoots to the river Jordan, as one renews old vines by bending them down and burying them in the earth.
Thus they are called propagines (shoots), from 'porro pangendo', that is, from stretching forth. Since you planted it, how did it then come to be so?
Why have you destroyed its wall, so that all who pass along the way harvest it? Why did you then tear away its fortification,
with which it was enclosed? And why, on account of those sins, do all who go along their way now harvest it? That is, those who rule in temporal things.
The boar from the forest has laid it waste, and the solitary wild beast has fed upon it. Why has the boar out of the forest now laid it waste,
Titus, out of the gentiles? And why has the solitary wild boar, which does not go with the herd, devoured it so?
The Roman prince, and every proud man who does not acknowledge anyone else as his equal: he is the 'solitary one'. God of hosts, turn.
God of hosts, turn to mercy, even though it has come to this. Look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vine,
and perfect it, which your right hand planted. Look from heaven, and look upon this vineyard that has come from that former one,
and visit it, and bring to completion that which your right hand, Christ, planted.
Since you have torn apart the synagogue, establish the holy Church. And upon the son of man whom you have strengthened for yourself. And fully
[complete] it upon the son of man whom you have made firm for yourself and laid as the foundation, of whom it is written:
"No one can lay another foundation than that which has been laid, which is Christ Jesus." Burned with fire and dug under,
they shall perish at the rebuke of your countenance. By the rebuke of your face those two shall be destroyed
from which all sins come: desire and fear. The things kindled by fire are desires; the things dug under are fears.
Love kindles both the good and the wicked. You are loving for this reason: that it may go well with you. Evil love does not give you that,
but good love does. So too you are fearful for this reason: that it may not go badly with you. Good fear gives that, not evil fear.
Flee the two that are evil. Keep the two that are good, and keep God gracious to you. Let your hand be upon the man of your right hand,
and upon the son of man whom you have strengthened for yourself. Let your hand be stretched out over the man of your right hand, for the perfecting of the vineyard,
and over the son of Mary, whom you have made firm for yourself to be your only beloved. And after that we shall not depart from you.
You will give us life, and we will call upon your name. In him you bring us to life, and therefore we call upon your name.
We were dead then, when we loved the earth and not God. In him you renew us,
and give us the life of the inner man. Lord God of hosts, turn us, and show your face, and we shall be saved.
To the end, for the winepresses, on the fifth day of the week. A psalm of Asaph. Baptism [?], that is what 'the fifth day of the week' means [?]. It is a song, that is, a psalm sung to Asaph himself,
that is, to the very congregation of the Lord that looks toward Christ. Why was it sung? Because of the winepresses, by which the oil is secretly drained off into the oil-vessel [?],
and the dregs are poured out into the street. What are these winepresses? They are the afflictions of the holy Church, by which all those
those who are baptized, good and bad, are tested and are separated, so that the good may be kept like oil
and the bad thrown out like the dregs of the oil. "The fifth day of the week" points us to the baptized, because on that day living creatures were created from the waters.
REJOICE IN GOD OUR HELPER. Rejoice, to the honor of God your helper, all you who are called his Asaph,
because this psalm is sung to you. Shout for joy to the God of Jacob. Sing out wordless songs of joy to him where words fail you,
so that you may still show your joy that way. If some serve the belly and others serve vanity,
you, though, be mindful and glad of heart toward God your helper. Take up a psalm and give the timbrel. Receive what is spiritual; give what is carnal.
The psalm is spiritual. The timbrel, which is made of leather, is carnal. Be generous with carnal things, so that God may give you spiritual things.
For Paul also says: IF WE HAVE SOWN SPIRITUAL THINGS FOR YOU, IS IT A GREAT THING IF WE REAP YOUR CARNAL THINGS?
The pleasant psaltery with the harp. The one is pleasant together with the other: the psaltery together with the harp.
The psaltery has its sound box at the top, and from there the strings run down, like heavenly preaching. But the harp has its sound box at the bottom,
because bodily works must answer to the preaching of the word of God. This and the earlier verse are one: there it is psalm and timbrel,
here it is psaltery and harp. The psaltery is now called in German [?] 'rotta',
from the sound of the voice, which grammarians call a 'made' word (onomatopoeia), like 'tintinnabulum' (little bell) and 'clocca' (bell). Sing with the trumpet at the beginning of the month.
Blow the horn when the moon is new. That means: preach the new life more confidently and more clearly. As another prophet says:
CRY OUT AND LIFT UP YOUR VOICE LIKE A TRUMPET. On the notable day of your solemn feast. Blow on your famous feast day.
The Jews still practise this in a carnal way. They begin on the first day of the month of September, which is the notable day of solemn feast
among them, and they blow for seven days, not knowing that it was commanded to them for this reason:
because the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit was to be preached to those who were to be baptized throughout the whole world. For it is a commandment in Israel
and a judgment of the God of Jacob. That is why they sing with the trumpet at the beginning of the month: because the law was given through Moses in Israel,
and judgment is given to the God of the Christians, the new people, who are signified by Jacob. He said: THE FATHER JUDGES NO ONE,
BUT HAS GIVEN ALL JUDGMENT TO THE SON. And again: I CAME INTO THIS WORLD FOR JUDGMENT, SO THAT THOSE WHO DO NOT SEE MAY SEE
AND THOSE WHO SEE MAY BECOME BLIND. In this way the mystery of the winepress makes some blind and some seeing. He set it as a testimony in Joseph
when he went out of the land of Egypt. In Joseph, who also signified the gentiles, he bore witness to it when he went out of Egypt and
baptized them in the Red Sea, freeing them in this way from the Egyptians, just as the later people is now freed from sins in baptism.
There not one of the Egyptians was left alive, and in our baptism not one of our sins is left. Joseph means 'increase'.

That is [the voice/testimony] of the Christians, because many are the children of the desolate woman, more than of her who has a husband. He heard a language which he had not known. He heard the language
when he came out of Egypt, which he did not know. What is that? When a person comes out of the vices at baptism,
then he hears mysteries which he did not know before; then he hears where he ought to have his heart. He turned his back away from the burdens.
God turned his back away from the burden. He unloaded him. His hands served in the basket.
He had need of it, because his hands served at baskets. A cophinus is a basket which is used for servile work,
when one has to clean out, spread dung, carry earth. So they all serve before baptism, as it were with a basket,
because whoever commits sin is the slave of sin. There they become free. Blessed is he who keeps that freedom afterward.
In tribulation you called upon me, and I delivered you. In distress you called upon me, when you made bricks and carried the basket.
Then I heard you. Before your baptism, while your conscience oppressed you, I took heed of you. And I heard you in the hidden place of the storm.
And I heard you in the secrecy of the storm. Of which storm? Not of the sea, but of the heart. Where you were in anguish, there I heard you.
I proved you at the waters of contradiction. I tested you at the waters of gainsaying. Waters are peoples, as
in the Apocalypse it was answered to him who saw many waters and asked what they were:
they are peoples. There is no lack, day by day, of gainsaying peoples for the baptized, by whom God tests them.
The martyrs felt these waters. To Christ himself it was foretold that he would be a sign that would be spoken against.
Nor is there yet any good person whom these waters do not meet. But according to the history, the waters of contradiction were
where the children of Israel strove with Moses and Aaron. Up to this point the interpretation was about the oil of the winepress;
after the interposed diapsalma, it comes to the dregs of the oil. Hear, my people, and I will speak and testify to you.
Hear, my people, I speak to you and testify to you. Israel, if you hear me, there shall not be in you, that is, in your heart,
a new god. If you listen to me, Israel, then there is no new god with you; then you know the true one,
the eternal one, not one devised in the meantime in the fantasy of the heart, as pagans and heretics do. He who always was, before time,
cannot be like any of the things that came into being in time, nor can any of them be God, because they are God's works.
Nor shall you worship a foreign god. Nor will you worship any foreign god if you do not take him into your heart.
For whatever creature you take into your heart, thinking it to be God, it deceives you.
For I am. I am. But what is not, how can you worship that? I am the Lord your God. I, your Lord,
I, your God, I am. Why? Because I am who I am. Because I am; I alone am truly [God] to you. Who brought you out of the land of Egypt. I
…who showed you that, and led you out of Egypt, out of darkness. Let all listen to this: God is addressing us and them.
He has led us all out of Egypt. We have all passed through the Red Sea. We have been dipped in the baptism consecrated in the blood of Christ.
And there our enemies, who pursued us, were left behind. Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it. Open your mouth.
I will fill it for you. Open it to me, praying and confessing. For with me is the fountain of life, not with a new god.
And my people did not hear my voice. And after all those kindnesses, my people did not hear my voice.
And Israel did not heed me. And Israel did not think of me. And I let them go according to the desires of their heart; that is, I gave them over to themselves.
They will walk in their own wills. And then I let them do according to their desires. And that is what they do.
They live according to their desires. But nothing worse could ever happen to them than that he lets them go astray
who ought to guide them. Therefore they show dregs instead of oil. If my people had heard me, if Israel had walked in my ways,
I would perhaps have humbled their enemies for nothing, and laid my hand upon those who afflict them. But if my people Israel had listened to me
and shown by it that he walked in my ways, then it could have happened that I would have brought their enemies low
and laid my hand on those who torment them. But now they are their own enemies; what then can they complain of?
The enemies of the Lord have lied to him. The Lord's enemies lied to him. How? By renouncing evils and returning to them, and by saying, 'I go to the vineyard,' and not going. And their time will be
forever, that is, the fire. And their time lasts forever. Eternal fire is made ready for them.
Many read this truth who say: 'That is not spoken of me, but of the impious.'
'However much I am a sinner, an adulterer, a defrauder, a robber, a perjurer, I nevertheless have Christ as my foundation. God is merciful; I am a Christian.'
'I am baptized; I am purged through fire, and because of the foundation I do not perish.' You are a Christian; that is good. What else are you as well? A robber,
an adulterer, and other such things. What did Paul say about these? Those who do such things shall not possess the kingdom of God.
But about light sins he said: Those who build upon the foundation wood, hay, stubble
do not perish but are saved, yet so as through fire. If you wish to be perfect, then build upon the foundation
gold, silver, precious stones, and you will be saved without fire. Hold yourself to that, and do not put your trust in false things.
But which enemies are these? Pagans or Christians? Christians. And he fed them with the fat of wheat. And these are the ones
whom he fed with the fat of the grain-food. 'Fat' (adeps) is said of the fatness of meats; from there it is transferred here
to the sacraments of the Lord's body, with which he fed many who are against him, as Judas was, to whom he gave the morsel at the supper,
of whom one may boldly say: The enemy of the Lord lied to him, and his time will be forever.
And from the rock he satisfied them with honey. And with honey he sated them, honey that came from Christ. Christ is the rock. He gave them an understanding of sweetness
in parables and mysteries, until they were full, together with the fat of the wheat. And they say this, giving the solution to many deep matters [?].
NOTHING BETTER, NOTHING SWEETER CAN BE UNDERSTOOD OR SPOKEN. AND YET THE ENEMIES OF THE LORD LIED TO HIM.
A PSALM FOR ASAPH HIMSELF. This psalm is sung for Asaph himself, that is, for the synagogue itself, and to it he promises the coming of the Lord.
GOD STOOD IN THE SYNAGOGUE OF THE GODS. Christ came here and stood here, visible, in the midst of the assembly of the gods,
that is, of the Israelites, of whom he says further on: I SAID, YOU ARE GODS, AND ALL OF YOU SONS OF THE MOST HIGH.
And in the midst he judges between the gods. Standing there in the midst, he separates them, making out of the same lump some vessels for honor
and others for dishonor. How long will you judge unjustly and accept the persons of sinners? How long, you Israelites, will you keep doing this,
judging wrong to be right and showing favor to the persons of sinners? Those who were disobedient to the law
killed the prophets and now want to kill Christ. How long will you follow them and be like them in appearance?
You are the people of God, and you are such a great multitude that the princes must fear you. How can you be guiltless
if you let them do such evil? For your sake Christ has become needy and an orphan. Judge for the needy and the orphan.
Therefore secure justice for him, as is right: stand up to protect him. No one dares to kill him unless you are willing. Justify the humble and the poor. The princes,
proud and grown rich in themselves, do not think him righteous. But you should regard Christ, who has become lower for your sake, as the only righteous one.
Rescue the poor man. Take the poor man away from there. And free the needy from the hand of the sinner. And set the wretched man free
from the hands of the sinner, so that you too do not become sinful by consenting, and do not follow them in this:
that you demand Barabbas for life and Christ for death. They did not know and did not understand; they walk in darkness.
They did not know these things and did not perceive them. For if they had known, they would never have crucified the Lord of majesty.
They walk in darkness because they are blinded, and not they alone, but you along with them. All the foundations of the earth will be shaken.
Therefore all the foundations of the earth will be shaken. For there were earthquakes then, when these blind men crucified Christ.
Or it means that those founded on earthly happiness were moved to wonder at the signs and to repentance for their sins
when these men were blinded. As Paul said: BLINDNESS HAS COME UPON PART OF ISRAEL, UNTIL THE FULLNESS OF THE GENTILES SHOULD COME IN.
I said, You are gods, and all of you sons of the Most High. But you shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes. How so, you Jews?
I said, You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High. That is what I wanted you to be, beings who do not die. But you die,
as men who were once gods must do, and you are not exalted as sons of the Most High. Instead you fall through pride of heart.
Like one of the princes, that is, the devil. That is rebuke and reproach. Arise, O God, judge the earth. Stand up, God, from death, and judge
over the earthly ones who sat in judgment over you; judge them, the earth-dwellers, on the last day.
For you shall inherit among all nations. For you possess all nations through faith and love.
A canticle of a psalm of Asaph. The loudest song is Asaph's. This speaks to the congregation of the people of God about the second coming of the Lord. O GOD, WHO SHALL BE LIKE YOU?
When you come, Christ, to judge, who will then be like you? In your first coming you were like human beings, and you were even like robbers,
for you appeared in the form of a servant. But when you come in glory, who can then be found like you? Do not keep silent, and do not hold back, O God.
Since you kept silent when you came hidden, now that you come openly, do not keep silent and do not hold back your judgment.
For behold, your enemies have made an uproar, and those who hate you have lifted up their head. For your enemies were very loud,
and they raised up their head, the Antichrist, whom the Lord Jesus will slay with the breath of his mouth. Against your people they have devised a malicious plan,
and they have plotted against your saints. They devised an evil plan against your people and plotted against your saints.
They said: thus they spoke: Come, and let us destroy them from among the nations. Come, let us gather together; let us wipe them out from among the peoples,
so that they may no longer exist among the peoples. And let the name of Israel be remembered no more. And let the name of Israel no longer be mentioned.
For they have plotted together with one mind. For they plotted together in agreement. Against you they have made a covenant. They made a pact against you.
Testamentum means both things: the kind that has no force until the testators are dead, and also every pact and agreement is called a
testamentum, as when Jacob and Laban made a testamentum that they were to keep while they were still alive. The tents of the Edomites and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagarenes,
Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, the foreigners together with the inhabitants of Tyre. These made the pact. Their names show that they are God's enemies.
Edomites: earthly, or bloody. Ishmaelites: obedient to themselves, that is, not to God but to themselves. Moab: from the father,
because his mother conceived him by her own father in an unlawful way. Hagarenes: proselytes, that is, newcomers, who have the mind of strangers, not of fellow citizens,
who show their true selves once they find a chance to do harm. Gebal: empty valley, that is, falsely humble. Ammon: a troubled people, or a people of sorrow.
Amalek: a licking people, as it is said: HIS ENEMIES SHALL LICK THE DUST. Foreigners: born elsewhere, and for that reason enemies. Tyre:
distress, or tribulation. For Assyria too came with them. The devil himself came along with them. They came to help the children of Lot,

that is, of the one who turns aside. The devil is the one who turns aside from God, and his angels are the children of the one who turns aside. These people came to help them. Whatever they want to do,
they and their father the devil, the children of unbelief help them with it. Do to them as you did to Midian and Sisera, and to Jabin at the brook Kishon.
Deal with them as you dealt with Midian, whose name in Latin means 'turning aside judgment', and with Sisera, whose name means 'exclusion of joy'.
and Jabin, whose name means "wise" — not for good but for evil. They were defeated at the brook Kishon,
which in Latin means "their hardness." They perished at Endor. They were lost in the "fountain of generation," because they did not seek the fountain of regeneration,
in which they could have been saved. They became like the dung of the earth. They became like the dung of the earth, they who could not
bring forth anything but earthly birth. Make their princes like Oreb and Zeb and Zebah and Zalmunna. Set their princes — how?
As you once set Oreb, whose name means "dryness," and Zeb, whose name means "wolf," and Zebah, whose name means "victim" —
whose victim? The wolf's, of course — and Zalmunna, whose name means "shadow of commotion." All their princes, who said: Let us take possession of the sanctuary of God as an inheritance.
In this way all their princes will be destroyed, who said to one another: Let us take possession of God's temple.
What is the temple but the people of God? They are always eager to turn that people to their own will. That is "empty sound,"
which is why it says earlier: YOUR ENEMIES HAVE MADE A NOISE. My God, make them like a wheel. My God, make them unsteady in their counsel,
like a wheel. Or else: a wheel rises at the back and falls at the front. In the same way the Lord's enemies rise here among the lowest goods;
further on, among the best, they fall; there they fail. And like stubble before the face of the wind.
And like the stalk before the wind. Give them light hearts, so that they cannot stand firm before temptation. Like the fire that burns up the forest
and like the flame that burns up the mountains, so you will pursue them with your storm, and in your anger you will trouble them. But when? At the judgment.
On the last day you will pursue them with your storm, and in your anger you will trouble them, coming as terribly
as the fire that burns the forest and the flame that burns the mountains. In this verse, "you will pursue" and "you will trouble" mean the same thing,
and so do "with storm" and "in anger," and "fire" and "flame." But understand "forest" as the barren, and "mountains" as the proud.
Fill their faces with shame, and they will seek your name, O Lord. Fill their faces with disgrace, and then they will seek
your name, Lord. Fight them with adversities, and then they will begin to flee to you. Those who do not do this —
