what will happen to them? Let them be ashamed and troubled for ever and ever, and let them be confounded and perish.
Let them be ashamed and troubled and disgraced and lost, for ever and ever. And let them know that your name is Lord.
And so let both those and these know that you are called Lord, and that others are lords only as servants,
and so are still lords subject to your command. Let them learn that. And what else? That you alone are the Most High over all the earth.
That you alone are called the Most High over all the earth. Why then do those who are on the earth, and are themselves earth, raise themselves against you?
UNTO THE END, FOR THE WINEPRESSES, A PSALM FOR THE SONS OF KORAH. This psalm looks to Christ. It is sung about the winepresses, for the sons of the bald one.
The churches of God are winepresses. They are press-houses. In them are the Christians, who are trodden down in the pressures of many persecutions.

and from there they are strained into the storehouses of God. These are the sons of the bald one, the sons of the cross, the sons of the crucified one, who was hung up in the place of Calvary (the place of baldness).
HOW LOVELY ARE YOUR TABERNACLES, O Lord of hosts. How delightful your dwellings are, Lord of the hosts.
How toilsome it is to live here in the winepress-houses; how good it is to be with you, where there is no pressing.
My soul longs and faints. Thither it yearns; thither my soul wears itself out. Where to? Into the courts of the Lord. The pressed grape
flows from the winepress into wine, and into the vat, and into the storehouses of the Lord. My heart and my flesh have rejoiced in the living God.
My soul and my body rejoiced, from here toward there, in the living God. Hope has explained this 'exultation' to me.
For the sparrow has found itself a house. For the sparrow finds itself a house. My soul will yet find the house in heaven
where it may dwell from then on, just as the sparrow is always at home. And the turtledove a nest for itself, where it may lay its young.
And the turtledove finds itself a nest where it may lay its young. My body finds the place
to which it may bring its works. What place is that? Your altars, O Lord of hosts, my king and my God.
These are your altars, Lord of the hosts, my king and my God. Toward them my works look:
fasts, sacrifices, alms, and the rest. Blessed are those who dwell in your house. Blessed are those who dwell in your house. They have blessedness.
But what do they do? They will praise you for ever and ever. They praise you forever. They see you,
they praise you. They cannot grow weary of it, because their blessedness consists in this, that they are allowed to do it.
Blessed is the man whose help is from you. Blessed is he who has your help to come there. He has arranged ascents in his heart.
That help makes steps for him in his heart. In what region? In the valley of tears. Here in the vale of sorrow, in the winepresses.
Where do they lead? To the place which he has appointed. To the place which he has prepared for them, into the kingdom of heaven. For he will give a blessing,
he who gave the law. That is because the same one who earlier gave constraint will yet give blessedness. What happens after that?
They will go from strength to strength. They go from strengths to greater strengths. Here they had virtues for restraining the flesh. There
a new strength comes. Which is that? The God of gods will be seen in Zion. That is the power of contemplation. The virtue of contemplation.
The God of the Christians shows himself to them as he is. Where? In Zion, in the heavenly Jerusalem. O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer;
give ear, O God of Jacob. Lord God of all the hosts, hear my prayer; give ear to it, God of Jacob,
and make me from Jacob into Israel. When? When the God of gods appears in Zion. Behold, O God our protector.
Our protector, O God, look toward us. Where is the protection? Under the shadow of your wings. And look upon the face of your anointed.
And look upon the face of your anointed one. That is to say: let us see Christ incarnate, so that we may go from strengths to strength.
For one day in your courts is better than thousands. For one day in your courts is better than a thousand here.
Here day and night take turns, and in them people grow old. With you there is one day, in which no one grows old.
Is not one of yours there, then, better than many here? I have chosen to be cast down in the house of my God rather than to dwell in the tents of sinners.
I would rather be cast away in the house of God, in the Church, in the winepress,
so that I may still always be inside there, than be proud outside in the lodgings of sinners. Why?
For God loves mercy and truth. For God loves grace and truth: first he gives freely granted forgiveness to the penitent,
and after that the promised crown to the one who overcomes, as he did for Paul. The Lord will give grace and glory. God gives grace and glory.
Grace, as Paul said: "By the grace of God I am what I am." Glory, as he also said: "There remains for me the crown of righteousness."
He will not deprive of good things those who walk in innocence. He does not withhold good from the sinless. What is it that he gives them? Rest, eternity,
immortality, freedom from suffering. O Lord God of hosts, blessed is the man who hopes in you. Blessed is he who puts his trust in you, God of powers.
Unto the end, for the sons of Korah. This psalm leads us to that end, where we cannot go astray,
for in him is truth. It is sung for the sons of Korah, the sons of the bald one, whom we should not mock but should rather weep before.
He sings to us in the past tense what was then still in the future, for all future things are past to God. Lord, you have blessed your land.
You have blessed your earth, Christ, which you took on yourself by being born. As is shown there: You have turned back the captivity of Jacob.
You have turned away the exile of your people. Of this Paul says: "I see a law of my flesh fighting against the law of my mind
and leading me captive in the law of sin which is in my members." Where did the law of sin in the members come from?
From the first transgression. The outer man would never have become disobedient to his lord, the inner man,
if the inner man had not first become disobedient to his Lord and his Creator. When the law of the members prevails
and draws a person into sin, then he is a captive. Christ frees him from that captivity with his forgiveness, as the next verse says:
You have forgiven the iniquity of your people. You have forgiven the wrongdoing of your people. You have covered all their sins. You covered all
their sins; you did not want to keep them before your eyes. You have softened all your wrath. You have turned all your wrath to gentleness.
You have turned away from the wrath of your indignation, that is, you have turned yourself away from the wrath of your indignation. You have given up the anger of your wrath.
Convert us, O God our Savior. So do this, God our Savior: turn us back to you. And turn your wrath away from us.
And turn your anger away from us. You will not be angry with us forever, nor will you draw out your wrath from generation to generation.
You will not be angry with us forever, nor will you draw out your wrath from generation to generation.
The earlier generation, the one that was before Christ, was lost. The one that comes after is saved through baptism.
O God, you will turn and bring us to life. Lord, by turning us with your calling, you bring us to life.
When we flee from you, you turn us back to you and save us. And your people shall rejoice in you. And your people rejoices in you,
not in itself. Show us your mercy, O Lord, and grant us your salvation. Show us your grace, Lord,
and give us Christ, your Savior: to be seen not only in the flesh, but in his divinity,
according to the promise: "for we shall see him as he is." I will hear what the Lord God speaks in me.
I listen for myself to what the Lord God speaks in me. Let the noise of the world not disturb me, but let me be able to perceive
what the Holy Spirit says to me. For he will speak peace to his people, and to his saints, and to those who turn to him.
For he promises peace to his people, and to his saints, and to those who turn to him. When does
that come? When this bodily nature puts on incorruption and this mortal nature puts on immortality. Do not let it seem long to you, Christian. Here you have war;
here you must fight; there you shall rest. Yet his salvation is near to those who fear him, that glory may dwell in our land.
Yet his Savior does appear in the flesh among those who fear him: he will be born among the Jews,
so that glory may dwell in our land together with us, who were always his. Mercy and truth have met each other.
Truth and grace met each other. Gentiles and Jews came to one faith. For the Gentiles it is mercy;
for the Jews it is truth. Or: the truth of the Old Testament agrees with the mercy of the New Testament. Justice and peace have kissed.
Justice and peace kissed each other. They were always friends. Where there is justice, there is peace. That leads to peace:
that you do not do to another what you do not want for yourself. If you keep [?] to that, then you have made [?] peace. Truth has sprung from the earth,
and justice has looked down from heaven. Christ was born of Mary, and therefore justice looked upon us from heaven.
Through heavenly grace we were justified when Christ came here. Truth also comes from the earth
when a person makes a true confession, and heavenly justice follows it, for by that he is justified. So it happened to the publican,
who called himself a sinner. For the Lord will give sweetness, and our land will yield its fruit. Truly, God gives the sweetness of justice;
he makes us desire what is better. And our land will yield its fruit. And from that our fields bear their crop.
He visits our hearts; from that we begin to do good. Justice will walk before him, and will set his steps
on the way. Justice goes before. Which justice? Penance and confession.
By that he turns his steps onto the way that leads to our hearts. In this way one must prepare the way of the Lord.
A PRAYER OF DAVID. Christ is David. He is the head of the Church. Therefore this is her prayer, together with him.
INCLINE YOUR EAR, LORD, AND HEAR ME, FOR I AM NEEDY AND POOR. Incline your ear to me, Lord,
for I am needy and poor. I acknowledge how much I am in need of you.
Therefore I will trust that you hear me. Whoever relies on himself,
him you do not hear. Guard my soul, for I am holy. Protect my soul from scandals and from temptations, for I am holy.
Who can say that except Christ? His members say it too, because they are made holy by him.
Save your servant, my God, who hopes in you. Preserve your servant, God, who trusts in you. He is holy for this reason:
because he is humble and trusts in you. Have mercy on me, Lord, for I have cried to you all day. Have mercy on me, Lord,
for I cried to you all day long. At all times I cried to you, because at all times afflictions press upon me, and they never fail to come to me,
until the end of this world. One man, the one body of Christ, lasts until the end of the age. Some of his members are out of this distress,
those who cried before; some are in it now, those who cry now. And those who will cry then are still to come into it.
So the cry lasts all day, that is, for all time. At the end of time the cry comes to an end, and so do the afflictions. Gladden the soul of your servant,
for to you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul. Gladden the soul of your servant, because I lifted it up to you. Here
below there is bitterness; there on high there is joy. That is why I lifted it up there. You are the highest.
Whoever loves you lifts up his soul rightly and finds joy. For you, Lord, are sweet and mild.
For you, Lord, are both sweet, to take away bitterness, and gentle, to bear with sinners.
Sweet to the one who prays to you from the heart; gentle to the one who begins to pray and whose thoughts then lead him astray from it,
and yet you wait until he steadies his heart to make a pure prayer. What person would pay attention to someone
who began to talk with him, if that one meanwhile turned away and talked with someone else?
How hard it is for anyone's thoughts to stay steady in prayer, David showed when he said:
FOR I HAVE FOUND MY HEART, SO THAT I MIGHT PRAY TO YOU. He said that he found his heart, as if it were in the habit of fleeing from him.
And of great mercy. And very merciful. Not merely merciful, but very merciful. To whom?
To all who call upon you. To all who invite you to come to them. For those who cry to you for the sake of something else are not crying to you,
and they are not seeking you, but what they love. Even someone who asks for life for his son, and God does not hear him, and he then says:
"Surely I asked God for good things; why did he not hear me?" What does he know? What if it was not good for the son to live?
...so that he would not become worse? Was not the counsel of God better, then, than the counsel of man? So ask for what he grants you.
Ask for him himself. He hears that most gladly. Fix my prayer in your ears, O Lord, and attend to the voice of my supplication.
Let my prayer, my Lord, be fixed firmly in your ears, and listen to the voice of my pleading. These two things
God gladly grants to the one who holds his law firmly in his heart. In the day of my tribulation I cried to you, because you heard me. On the day of my distress I cried to you,
because you heard me. That is to say: you heard me because I cried to you. All our days are, for us, days of tribulation,
for as long as we are in the body we are pilgrims away from the Lord. Even if someone here could have eternal good things,
and yet should not see the face of the Lord, what would he then have gained, compared with what he had lost?
Who could take comfort in that? If there is anyone like that, he is no lover of God; he does not know about his pilgrimage.
Think on that, man, think on that, and let nothing be pleasing to you apart from the sight of him. There is none like you among the gods, O Lord.
There is none like you, Lord, among other gods, those called the gods of the gentiles, which have eyes and do not see,
ears and do not hear. And there is none according to your works. And none of them is like you in their works.
None of them works as you do. You made heaven and earth; what did they make? All the nations, whatever you have made, shall come
and shall worship before you, O Lord. All the peoples, however many you have made, come and pray before you.
This we now see fulfilled. And they shall glorify your name, for you are great and do wonders; you alone are God.
And they glorify you, because you alone are great and you alone do wonders. Just as you alone are God,
so too you alone are great and do wonders. The signs of the magicians are false and useless.
Those that have truth and usefulness in them belong to God alone. Lead me, O Lord, in your way, and I will walk in your truth. Lead
me in Christ, who is the way; then I will walk in your truth, which again is Christ. Those who are catholics walk in the way.
If God leads them and teaches them to walk carefully, then they walk in the truth, and they walk in him to him.
Let my heart rejoice so that it fears your name. Let my heart be so gladdened by hope that it still always fears your name,
and that I may be kept between your two [?]. I will confess to you, O Lord my God, with my whole heart, and I will glorify your name forever,
for your mercy is great toward me, and you have rescued my soul from the lower hell. I confess to you, Lord my God, with all my heart,
and I glorify your name forever, because your mercy is great toward me, in that you have rescued my soul
from the lower hell. If the upper hell is where the souls of the righteous rested before the coming of Christ,
then the lower one is where the torments of the wicked were, and still are. From that one, says the body of Christ, you have rescued me.
I gather Rahab and Babylon and all the Gentiles in there. Because of this she becomes glorious. "Behold, the foreigners and Tyre and the people of the Ethiopians, these were there."
See her glory. "Foreigners": such as Tyre, which lies near the Jews, and the Ethiopians, who are far from the Jews.
"These were there." "Were," because to God it is past; and yet they are still to come, because to us it is future. "'Mother Zion,' a man shall say."
A man calls the synagogue his mother. She does not recognize him as God. "And a man was born in her." And this cannot be denied:
he was born a man in her. "The Most High himself founded her." He himself, the Highest, founded her.
He founded his mother the synagogue before the foundation of the world. Who knows this? "The Lord has told it in the writings of the peoples and of the princes
of those who were in her." Christ himself said that it was written so, in the writings of the Jewish people,
and in the writings of the foremost men who were in the synagogue, such as Moses and the prophets. As it says:
"And beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he interpreted to them the scriptures concerning all the things that were about himself."
"As the dwelling of all who rejoice is in you." Like the dwelling of those who are glad, so is the dwelling of all of them there,
in the heavenly Jerusalem. There is the joy that is never followed by sorrow.
A SONG OF A PSALM FOR THE SONS OF KORAH. UNTO THE END, FOR AMALEK, THAT IS, FOR THE CHOIR, TO RESPOND. OF THE UNDERSTANDING OF HEMAN,
THAT IS, OF HIS BROTHER THE ISRAELITE. Now it is sung to the sons of the cross, for the sake of the choir,
so that it may be ready to answer. That is the understanding of his Israelite brother.
The Passion of the Lord is sung here. By this song the choir of martyrs is urged to respond. How? As John says:
"AS CHRIST LAID DOWN HIS LIFE FOR US, SO WE TOO OUGHT TO LAY DOWN OUR LIVES FOR THE BROTHERS."
That is what "to respond" means. They are Hemans; he saw fit to call them his brothers. They are Israelites in whom there is no guile.
"O LORD GOD OF MY SALVATION, BY DAY I HAVE CRIED, and by night, before you." Lord God of my salvation, in prosperity and in adversity I cried out to you.
These are words of Christ in the form of a servant. "Let my prayer come into your sight." Let my prayer come before you. "Incline your ear
to my prayer." Bend your ear to my plea. The two are one. "For my soul is filled with evils."
For my soul is filled with evils. Which evils? Not sins, but pain and sorrow. "And my life has drawn near to hell."
And my life has drawn near to hell. That is as he said: "MY SOUL IS SORROWFUL EVEN UNTO DEATH." "I am counted among those who go down into the pit."
The Jews count me together with the other sinners who go into the pit of hell. "I have become," that is, "I am counted,"
"as a man without help." I was thought of as a helpless man, even though my Father was with me,
who would have given me twelve legions of angels to help me, if I had wished it. "Free among the dead." Alone among the dead, master of himself.
For no other was there who had power to lay down his life and to take it up again. Like the wounded sleeping in the grave.
Therefore I was regarded like the other slain who sleep in the grave. Whom you remember no more.
Whom you do not yet remember, because their time to rise has not yet come. But my time is soon: on the third day.
Therefore I am not like the other slain and buried. But why are the dead called sleeping? Only because they shall awaken
in the resurrection. And they are cast out from your hand. Thus they themselves are what they accused me of being. They are thrust away from the help of your hand.
They are the helpless ones, not I, for they dug a pit and fell into it. They laid me in the lowest pit.
They set me in the lowest pit; that is, misery. They thought me to be one of the most wretched. In dark places
and in the shadow of death. Among the dark things, and among those who are in the shadow of death, such as those in whom impiety reigns.
Like these they regarded me. Your wrath was confirmed upon me. Your anger was fastened upon me.
You had set your wrath against me, so they thought, and that I should therefore suffer death, and even the death of the cross.
And all your suspensions, that is, your threats, you have brought upon me. And all the threats of the passion, according to the words of the prophets,
you laid upon me. Therefore they thought you were angry with me. You have put my acquaintances far from me. Even my acquaintances,
my disciples, you made to flee in my passion. They have made me an abomination to themselves. They loathed me:
not they, but the Jews, by mocking and bending the knee and saying: 'Vah! Hanged one [?], you who destroy the temple of God'
'and in three days rebuild it.' I was delivered up and did not go forth. I was given over by Judas.
Because of that I still did not show who I was; I did not reveal my divinity. My eyes grew weak because of want.
From that want my eyes became sick: my disciples, my brighter and more eminent members. They were disheartened
that I did not show my divinity. I cried to you, O Lord. Hanging on the cross I cried to you thus: 'Lay not this sin to their charge.'
All the day I stretched out my hands to you. At all times I stretched out my hands to you in good works. The Jews saw those works,
by which they ought to have amended themselves. That they would have done if they had not been dead. Therefore it says after this: Will you work wonders for the dead?
Do you work wonders before the dead? What does it help them? Are they not dead who, even through miracles, with obstinate heart will not become believers?
Or will physicians raise them up, and will they praise you? Or are there any physicians so good, even though they help the living, that they could bring the dead back to life?
and who would then thank you? Shall anyone declare in the grave, namely to those lying there, your mercy, and your truth in perdition?
Does anyone tell those lying in the grave and in perdition of your grace and your truth? Those who are not predestined to eternal life,
nor those who are not worthy that the Father should draw them to the Son, for they lie in the grave and in perdition.
What can one tell them? The unbelieving soul is in perdition, and its body is its grave.
Who can tell them anything good? Will your wonders be known in the darkness, and your justice in the land of forgetfulness?
Can your wonders be recognized in the darkness, which is what sinners are? Or your justice in the land of forgetfulness, which is what those are
who have forgotten God? And I have cried to you, Lord. And for that reason I too cried out to you, says Christ in the voice of his body.
Why does it say "and I"? Only because we too were once by nature children of wrath, and grace has separated us from the unbelievers.
And in the morning my prayer shall come before you. And in the morning, that is, once the darkness of unbelief has passed away,
even though the bright day has not yet come on which we shall see you face to face, my prayer nevertheless comes before you,
for now is the time of prayer; then will be the time of praise. Why, Lord, do you reject my prayer? Why, Lord, do you strike back
my prayer? Why do you put off the blessedness that we pray for? Do you turn your face away from me?
Why do you turn your face away from me, so that you do not grant my request? Do you do it for this reason,
that you may make us better by it? I am needy. I am poor, I, your Church, because as a pilgrim I suffer hunger and thirst for that
of which I shall yet obtain my fill in the homeland. And in labors from my youth. And in labors all the way from my youth.
I have suffered persecution ever since I began to grow. But having been exalted, I was humbled and troubled. When I, your people, had been raised up by prosperity,
I was at once brought low and troubled by adversity. Your wrath has passed over me. Your wrath passed over me.
Though it came, it did not last. But of the unbeliever it is written: The wrath of God abides on him.
And your terrors have troubled me. And your terrors troubled me, so that I was always in fear.
They surrounded me like water. They surrounded me like water, so many of them were there. All day long they surrounded me together.
At all times they surrounded me together, the terrors of your judgment. Not one of my limbs was outside them.
You have put friend and neighbor far from me, and my acquaintances, because of my misery. Friend and kinsman and acquaintances you put far from me. They fled from my misery,
so that they would not have to suffer it with me. Of them it is said: All forsook me; may it not be held against them.
The understanding of Ethan the Israelite. Ethan means "strong." Whatever Israelite wishes to be strong in the Lord, this psalm is his understanding. Now Ethan speaks.
I will sing of your mercies, Lord, forever. From generation to generation I will proclaim your truth with my mouth.
I sing of your mercies, Lord, forever. With them I tell of your truth, enduring in my mouth,
which you show in both generations, of the Jews and of the Gentiles. For you have said: Mercy shall be built up forever. For you said:
My mercy shall be built up forever. Such mercy makes me glad; it is the mercy I sing of, which is eternal.
Your truth shall be prepared in the heavens. In the holy preachers your truth will be prepared.
That also makes me sing. I have made a covenant with my chosen. You also said: I have appointed for my chosen ones a testament.
Which is that? None other than the New Testament, by which we are renewed by the Lord for the inheritance that is in heaven.
I have sworn to David my servant. You also said: I swore to my servant David. How was the oath made?
Thus I swore to him: I will prepare your seed forever. To eternity I prepare your seed,
that is, Christ and those who believe in him. And I will build up your throne from generation to generation. And I build your seat in all generations.
Here is the earthly generation; God sits in it, because he governs it. After this comes the heavenly one,
in which he sits again, because he reigns in it. Then they become heavens by carrying God. From this there follows at once:
The heavens shall confess your wonders, O Lord. The heavens tell your wonders, Lord. They do not tell of their own merit;
they praise you. And your truth in the church of the saints. And they tell your truth in the congregation of the
saints. When the heavens give dew, they wet the lands, which bear good fruit. For who among the clouds shall be equal to the Lord?
For they tell the truth to the church of the saints when they say: Who will be made equal to God among the clouds?
They are heavens because of the brightness of the truth; they are clouds because of the hidden things of the flesh. Who can see through clouds? And who knows what lies hidden in the flesh?
Was Christ not also a cloud? Was he not covered with flesh? Which of the clouds was like him? And who among the sons of God shall be like God?
And who among the sons of God is like God? What they are by grace, he is by nature. God, who is glorified in the council of the saints.
He is the God who is glorified in the council of the saints. Their counsel is to believe in him, whom they cannot be like.
In this way they glorify him. Great and terrible over all who are round about him. Great and terrible over all the sons of God who are around him,
because they are near him. Or they are 'around him' because he was born, died, was buried and rose again in Jerusalem,
and the nations are settled all around it. And there he thundered from his own cloud, and then he sent out other clouds to water the nations round about.
As he promised in the Passion: Hereafter you shall see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven. Lord God of hosts, who is like you?
Lord God of powers, who is like you? Though others may have power, they do not have it of themselves.
You are mighty, O Lord, and your truth is round about you. You, Lord, are mighty, and your truth is around you.
In yourself you are mighty; from you comes your truth in the others. You rule
the power of the sea. You are so mighty that you even rule the power of the sea. If the sea rose up against their truth,
that need not move them. Why? But you calm the motion of its waves. Because you still its waves.
You measured out the persecutions of the wicked. You humbled the proud one like one who is wounded. The devil himself you brought low, struck down as if by a wound.
That in which he gloried, you took from him. And with the arm of your strength you scattered your enemies.
And by your strength you scattered your enemies, the Jews and the persecutors. Yours are the heavens, and yours is the earth.
Yours are the heavens, from which the truth rains down; yours is the earth, which is watered from there. Or thus:
Yours are the heavens, in which the devil wished to rule; yours is the earth, on which the Jews wished to rage against you. The circle of the earth and its fullness you founded.
The circle of the earth and all that is in it you have founded; therefore you rule over it, and they can do nothing against you.
You created the north and the sea. The north and the sea you created. However much the devil may be in the north, as he said:
I WILL SET MY THRONE IN THE NORTH, and however much storm there may be on the sea, they can still do nothing against your will.
Tabor, that is, 'coming light,' and Hermon, that is, 'his anathema' (understood: the devil's), will rejoice in your name.
Tabor and Hermon are mountains of Syria. Those are also mountains whose light, that is, faith, coming from Christ, makes them renounce the devil.
They rightly rejoice, God, in your name. Your arm is with power. Your arm is mighty, both for fighting and for defending. Let be strength-
-ened your hand, and let your right hand be exalted. Let your hand grow strong to press down the proud, and let your right hand be exalted to glorify the humble.
Justice and judgment are the preparation of your throne. Righteousness and judgment are the preparation of your seat on the last day.
Therefore you will set some at the right hand and others at the left. But how is it now? Mercy and truth shall go before your face.
Now, in the meantime before that, mercy and truth go before your face. Mercy, because you will blot out sins;
truth, because you promised so. Blessed is the people that knows jubilation. Blessed is the people that knows that joy,
that can recognize how it should rejoice in these two. Lord, they shall walk in the light of your countenance.
Those who know this walk, Lord, in your light. You reveal it to them. And in your name they shall rejoice all the day.
And in your name they rejoice at all times. Those who do not rejoice in this way do not persevere in their joy.
And in your justice they shall be exalted. And in your righteousness they are exalted, not in their own righteousness.
The Jews wished to establish their own righteousness; therefore they were not subject to the righteousness of God. That brought them down.
For you are the glory of their strength, and in your good pleasure our horn shall be exalted. For you are the glory of their strength,
and in your well-beloved Christ our horn is exalted. From him we have the power to become sons of God. For our taking-up is the Lord's
and the Holy One's of Israel, our king. For our taking-up is the Lord's, and the Holy One's of Israel, our king. He took our nature upon himself
when he became incarnate. THEN YOU SPOKE IN A VISION TO YOUR SONS. Then you spoke in sight to your sons. You made your
the prophets looked upon in the Old Testament the things that they foretold about Christ. For this reason they are called 'seers' (videntes).
And you said. And so you spoke about him: I have laid help upon one who is mighty. Upon the mighty one I have set my help.
I made him mighty with my help. In the form of a servant he needed help. And I have exalted one chosen from my people.
And I made high the chosen one out of all my people. I have found David my servant. I found in him David, my servant.
With my holy oil I have anointed him. I anointed him with my holy ointment. I anointed him with the oil of gladness
above his companions. For my hand shall help him, and my arm shall strengthen him. My hand helps him;
my arm strengthens him. The enemy shall gain nothing against him. The enemy can do nothing against him, neither the Jew nor the devil.
If he suffers persecution, he does so gladly. And the son of iniquity shall not harm him. Nor does Judas the betrayer harm him,
nor does the false witness find any guilt in him. And I will cut down his enemies before his face. And I will cut down his enemies from his sight.
I make them believers one by one. And those who hate him I will put to flight. And I put to flight those who hate him.
I make them flee until they flee to him. And my truth and my mercy shall be with him.
And my mercy and my truth are in him. Let us too show mercy, so that we may have pity on the wretched;
let us love truth, so that we do not judge unjustly. By doing so we imitate him. And in my name his horn shall be exalted.
And in my name his power shall be exalted, as he himself says: ALL POWER IS GIVEN TO ME IN
HEAVEN AND ON EARTH. And I will set his hand in the sea. And I make him powerful in the sea; that is, he will rule over the nations.
And his right hand in the rivers. And I make his right hand powerful in the rivers. Rivers run into the sea;
greedy people hurry toward the bitterness of this world. Yet all of them become subject to him.
He shall call upon me: You are my Father, my God, and the upholder of my salvation. And I will make him the firstborn. He says to me: My Father,
my God, upholder of my salvation. And because I am so, I therefore honor him and set him up as firstborn,
high above the kings of the earth. Exalted before all kings, because all the kings of the earth worship him. Forever I will keep my mercy for him,
and my covenant shall be faithful to him. I will show him mercy forever, and my covenant is faithful to him,
because he is the most rightful heir of my kingdom; for him I have faithfully kept it. And I will establish his seed for ever and ever.
And I establish his seed for eternity. His seed are his co-heirs. And his throne as the days of heaven.
And I establish his throne like the days of heaven. The days of earth are unstable, because some pass away
and others come; but the days of heaven stand fast. But if his children forsake my law and do not walk in my judgments,
If they profane my justices and do not keep my commandments. But if his children, who are called sons of the bridegroom,
forsake my law, and do not walk in my judgments, and break my statutes, and do not keep my commandments,
I will visit their iniquities with the rod, and their sins with stripes. Then I will punish their wrongdoing with the rod, and their sins
with scourges. But my mercy I will not scatter away from him, nor will I do harm in my truth. But my mercy I will not remove from him,
nor will I harm him in my truth. The truth of my promise does not harm him,
because I promised him mercy in his children. Nor will I profane my covenant, and what proceeds from my lips I will not make void.
Nor will I profane my covenant, and what I speak, that I will not undo. Once I have sworn by my holy one.
Once I swore that I would make it good in my holy Son, when I gave him up to death for the sins of all.
If I lie to David, his seed shall remain forever. I will not become a liar to David; his seed endures forever.
His seed are the good, from whom the harvest grows, whose reapers are the angels. And his throne is like the sun in my sight.
And his throne will be like the sun in my sight. The righteous are his throne; on them he sits. They will shine in the future kingdom like the sun.
And like the full moon forever. And like an ever-full moon. In soul they will become perfect like the sun,
in flesh like the moon: not like this waning moon, but like the one that is always full. And a faithful witness in heaven.
And such a moon, which is forever a faithful witness against all those who deny the resurrection of the flesh.
But you have rejected and despised, and put off your anointed. Where has all that gone which you promised him?
Contrary to your promises you have thrust away, and dishonored, and put off your anointed one.
If you promised it to David, from whom our Christ came, you have broken it for him. He was thrust from the kingdom by his own son
and driven into flight, and in that flight he was dishonored by the son of Gemini. But our Christ you have only put off.
You have put him off, not taken him away. What about that other one? You have overturned the covenant of your servant. You have entirely set aside
and torn up your servant's covenant. Where is the old covenant of the Jews, under which David lived? Where do they now have the land of promise?
Where is their kingdom? Where is sacrifice, where is priesthood? You have profaned his sanctuary on earth. You have desecrated his temple on earth
and left it idle, for from now on no one may keep the sabbath and sacrifice cattle. You have destroyed all his walls.
You tore down all his fortifications, in which he was to have his strength. You have made his strongholds a terror.
The very strongholds from which courage should have come, you made into a cause of fear for them. All who pass along the way have plundered him.
All who travel along the way have torn him to pieces. By the Romans the first David was scattered among all the nations.
He has become a reproach to his neighbours. He has become a reproach to his neighbours, who lived around him. You have raised up the right hand of his enemies.
You have made all his enemies rejoice. You lifted high the right hand of his foes; you make his enemies rejoice over him.
You have turned away the help of his sword, and have not helped him in war. You turned away the help of his sword and did not help him in battle,
as you did before, when a few fighting used to lay many low. You have cut him off from cleansing. You separated him from purity,
which is the worst thing of all for him. In what does it lie? In faith. Of it is written: "Cleansing their hearts by faith."
That he does not have; he is faithless. What follows from that? Since he is not to be cleansed, he is to be cast away.
And you have dashed his throne to the ground. And you broke his throne on the earth. You made an end of the kingdom and of the throne.
You have shortened the days of his time. You shortened the days of his times. He lasted a shorter time than he expected. You have covered him with confusion.
You have filled him with shame, because he is a mockery to all people. How long, Lord, will you turn away? To the end? Will your anger burn like fire?
Since all this is so, how long, Lord, will you be turned away from them? Even to the end?
And how long will your anger burn like fire? Shall they not be converted at the end of the world? Then it may happen that you convert them.
Meanwhile your anger burns. Remember what my substance is. Remember what my being is, which is still to come in Christ,
so that your promises may be fulfilled to him, since I have been thrust away in the Jews. For you have not made all the sons of men in vain.
You never made all the sons of men in vain. Even though they all went in vanity, you did not create them in vain.
Still you wanted someone to come from them in whom there would be no vanity, and who would free others from vanity.
Remember this. What man is there who lives and will not see death? Will he deliver his soul from the hand of hell? What other man is there among them who lives in such a way
that he does not die again, and who frees his own soul from hell by himself? He also granted to others that they live and do not die again.
None of them freed his own soul from hell by himself. He alone could do that. The promises are his; may they hold for him [?]. Where are your ancient mercies,
Lord, as you swore to David in your truth? But now the martyrs speak: Where are your old mercies, Lord?
Where are they, according to which you swore to David in your truth that you would do good to him in his own?
Do we not have sorrow instead of good? Remember, Lord, the reproach of your servants, which I have held in my bosom, from many nations.
Remember, Lord, the reproach of your servants. It is held against us as a reproach that we are called Christians.
Remember the reproach of many peoples. All the many to whom I preached reproached me for your name.
I held that reproach in my bosom, that is, in my heart. Thanks be to God that the Christian name is no longer a reproach.
With which your enemies, Lord, have reproached. I bore the reproach that your enemies, the Jews and the pagans, cast on me.
What is the reproach? "Because they have reproached the change of your Christ." That they reproach us with the change of your anointed one,
which they did not recognize as being from earth to heaven, from temporal life to eternal life, from the Jews to the Gentiles; instead they thought it was destruction.
That led them astray. But Christ, rising from the dead, dies no more; death shall no longer have dominion over him. He would give that change to them as well, if they wished.
Of them it is written: "For there is no change for them, and they have not feared God." Blessed be the Lord forever.
May the Lord be praised forever. So be it, so be it. May it be so. Here ends the second sermon, delivered at the vigils of Saint Cyprian.
Here is the end of this psalm, which was preached at two matins of Saint Cyprian.
A PRAYER OF MOSES, THE SERVANT OF GOD. Although Moses did not write this psalm, yet
the title is there so that it may be all the more acceptable to us [?]. LORD, YOU HAVE BECOME OUR REFUGE from generation to generation.
Lord, you have become a refuge for us, in generation and in generation: in the old one and in the new one.
Before the mountains were made, or the earth and the world were formed, from age to age, that is, from eternity to eternity, you are God.
Before the mountains came to be, which are the angels, and before the earth came to be, which is human beings, and the world itself
in which both of them are, you exist before. From eternity to eternity you are. Do not turn man away into lowliness.
You do not turn man away down into lowliness; do not let him be desirous of what is low rather than of what is high.
And you said: Be converted, sons of men. And so you commanded; you said: Turn, you sons of men.
Help us toward what you commanded. For a thousand years before your eyes are like yesterday, which has passed.
This conversion is needed because before your eyes the ten hundred years that the people of old before the Flood nearly lived out
are as short as yesterday, which has passed. And like a watch in the night. And as short as a watch,
which according to the Romans is no more than three hours, that is, the fourth part of the night. If you wish to interpret mille according to custom as 'thousand' [dûsent],
then understand that this same word has been corrupted from another. The Romans say colloquially, for decies centum ('ten hundred'), 'dêscent';
in its place we say 'dûsent' [thousand]. Likewise they also say [?] 'eînhunt' 'unzent', 'ducent', 'tercent';
in their place we say 'one hundred', 'two hundred', 'three hundred'. Things that are counted as nothing, such will their years be. What you consider as nothing,
that is their years, even when they are most numerous. In the morning, that is, at first, may it pass like grass; in the morning may it flourish.
May their life at first pass like grass; may their life also blossom at first. And may it perish in the evening.
And after that may it be lost. May it fall: may it plunge into death. May it harden: may it grow stiff in the corpse.
And may it wither: and may it dry up in the ashes. For we have failed in your anger, and in your fury we have been troubled.
For we have lain prostrate in your anger, because of sickness, and in your fury we are grieved
for fear of death. That is: we lie in infirmity, and yet we tremble to end it. As was said to Peter:
ANOTHER SHALL GIRD YOU AND LEAD YOU WHERE YOU DO NOT WISH. Hence Christ himself said, in the person of the martyrs: MY SOUL IS SORROWFUL EVEN UNTO DEATH.
You have set our iniquities in your sight, our age in the light of your countenance. You set our iniquities in your sight,
and our world, which has now passed away, in the light of your face. At all times you took note of how we acted.
For all our days have failed. This shows in the fact that all our days, which we might have lived according to the age of our forefathers,
have vanished and have come down to few. And in your wrath we have failed. And in your anger we lost our long life.
Those before us who did evil, presuming on a longer life, deserved this. Our years shall be considered as a spider.
Our years are intent on corruptible works, as the spider is intent on its useless webs.
They are few, and those same ones come to nothing. The days of our years in them are seventy years. Our year-
days, which are like the spider, are in seventy years, because, like spiders, they look to the Old Testament,
where only temporal goods are promised. But if in the powerful, eighty years. But if they are in powers, then there are eighty of them,
because they look to the New Testament, in which eternal goods are promised, in which no power is lacking.
And what is more than these is their toil and sorrow. And those who go further and believe otherwise, as the heretics did, theirs is toil and pain.
Or it means: theirs is toil and pain, and all the more so because they are established in the powers of the New Testament,
because from this they are groaning, awaiting the adoption, the redemption of their body. For mildness has come upon us, and we shall be corrected. As also shows in this:
that the Lord's mildness comes to those powers, and by it we are rebuked. His correction looks to mildness,
for whom God loves he corrects, and he scourges every son whom he receives. And to certain great ones he gives a goad of the flesh, by which they are buffeted,
lest they be exalted by the greatness of their revelations. Who knows the power of your anger? Who can know the power of your wrath?
How far you can show it, who knows that? And for fear of you to number your wrath?
And who can count it, in the face of the fear of you? In the face of that terribleness of yours which is in it, no one can tell it.
Therefore the prosperity of fools is their destruction. No one recognizes this except he who creeps into the sanctuary
and there learns from their last things how far it leads to destruction. The law of God, that is God's sanctuary, which teach-
-es him this. Make your right hand known to us, and those learned in heart in wisdom. Make your right hand known,
and those inwardly taught in wisdom. Show us Christ, who is your right hand, and his elect, who are wise in this.
how insignificant the good is that is promised in the Old Testament, where there is the shadow of things to come, and that they therefore lightly give up their hope in such things.
And if Moses named earthly things to them, it was so that they might learn from Christ to understand heavenly things. And if it should also say:
"Make your right hand thus known, and those fettered in heart in wisdom," then it has the same meaning. Then Moses prays further
that Christ may thus become known to us, and his teachers, who are constrained in their hearts, so that they may draw us to spiritual understanding.
Turn, Lord, somewhat, and be entreated on behalf of your servants. Be turned somewhat, Lord, back here to us,
away from your anger, in which you are turned away, and be entreated for mercy on behalf of your servants.
Is this not the prayer of Moses in Exodus: BE APPEASED OVER THE WICKEDNESS OF YOUR PEOPLE? And if it says, "Turn, Lord, how long,"
or "until when," that again means "somewhat" or "to some extent," indefinitely, not as a question. Such is the prayer:
Spare somewhat, Lord, the martyrs, who are to endure many evils in the New Testament because they do not care for the things promised in the Old Testament.
Spare them somewhat, lest, overcome, they begin to flee from you. Yet let them not be without all distress, so that their crown does not escape them.
We have been filled in the morning with your mercy, and we have rejoiced and been delighted in all our days. Openly we are filled with your grace,
and for that we are gladdened, and delighted in all our days. That we shall openly see Christ in the flesh, that is our joy
all our days. We have been glad for the days in which you humbled us, the years in which we saw evils. We have also become glad because of the days
in which you made us humble, and because of the years in which we saw grievous things. Then they were grievous, now they are dear,
because we have been bettered by them. Look upon your servants, that is, the Jews, and upon your works. Look on your servants
and on your works. Those who are your servants are also your works. And direct their sons.
And direct their sons: if the forebears are scattered, let them nevertheless be converted at the end of the world. And let the splendour of the Lord our God be upon us.
And let the brightness of our God be over us. Let his face be shown to us. And direct the works of our hands over us.
And direct the work of our hands over us, so that we do not do it for worldly thanks, for then it is crooked.
And direct the work of our hands. And since all works look to the one work of charity, direct that one work.
Some books do not have the last verse. Of what does the name of Moses remind us here?
Only that his law and the whole Old Testament is written under a veil, and we therefore pray Christ to take away the veil.
David teaches us this prayer thus: UNVEIL MY EYES. "Uncover my eyes," he said. AND I WILL CONSIDER THE WONDERS OF YOUR LAW.
And then I will perceive wonders from your law. What wonders? Hidden mysteries, of which the Holy Spirit is the revealer.
PRAISE OF A SONG OF DAVID.
Here let us hear the same David the prophet sing to God a praise of song. He who dwells in the help of the Most High shall abide in the protection of the God of heaven.
He sits firmly in the help of the Highest who firmly trusts in it. He also dwells in the protection of the God of heaven.
Whoever trusts God, God also protects him. But whoever is proud and trusts in himself, he falls.
Just as those did who ate on the strength of the words that they would become as gods, and they lost immortality, and they found that
which God had threatened them with, not what the devil promised them. He will say to the Lord: You are my upholder and my refuge, my God.
He says to God: You are my receiver; you are my refuge. Who says that? He who dwells in the help of the Most High.
I will hope in him, for he will free me from the snare of the hunters and from the harsh word. He also says:
I hope in him, not in myself. For he frees me from the snare of the hunters and from the sharp word.
The devil and his angels are the hunters. They set snares in many enticements, that is, in many lures.
But the sharp word comes from people, when someone wants to live well among others who live badly,
and they hurry to lead him astray with mockery like this: "You are great, you are righteous, you are Elijah, you have come from heaven."
God frees from this the person to whom it means nothing and who is not ashamed of it. With his shoulders he will overshadow you, and under his wings you will hope.
With his shoulders he shades you, and under his wings you hope for protection. Just as birds'
young are under the wings, so they are also under the shoulders, for the wings come out of the shoulders.
This is said according to that likeness. His truth will surround you with a shield. His truth surrounds you with a shield.
It protects you on all sides. His truth is that he separates you, who hope, from those who do not hope. You will not be afraid of the terror of the night,
of the arrow flying by day. Therefore you do not fear night-terrors, that is, sins committed unknowingly,
nor the arrow shot by day, that is, sins committed knowingly. From the business that walks about in darkness.
From the busyness of those who walk in darkness, that is, when someone wants to lead you astray in secret. From ruin and the noonday demon.
From the fall and from the midday devil. That is the fiercest persecution, when the order was given like this: Whoever confesses himself a Christian,
let him be punished until he denies that he is a Christian. Because many people could not escape even that noonday demon, the next verse follows at once:
A thousand will fall at your side. So a thousand of those at your side fall, who gave all their goods to the poor,
and therefore expected to be judges alongside the apostles. And ten thousand at your right hand. And ten times as many again of those
who expected to be at your right hand and to hear there: "Come, you blessed of my Father." How does that happen?
Only through hidden pride, which God alone can know, and which taught them to rely on themselves, not on Christ. But it will not come near you.
But ruin does not come near you, nor the noonday demon. None of your members is brought down. Nevertheless with your eyes you shall con-
-sider, and you shall see the recompense of sinners. But even though this is so, though persecution is ruin for some,
and a crown for others, you will see with your eyes. What will you see with them? The reward of the sinners,
what it shall be. For if they are tormentors now, they are to be tormented forever. For you, Lord, are my hope.
Therefore I do not fall, because you, Lord, are my hope. Or thus: For you, Lord, are my hope.
You have made the Most High your refuge. Therefore you have set your refuge on high, because you are my hope.
From the earth you went to heaven, so that I, your body, your Church, might have hope of following after you.
No evils shall come to you. There no evils reach you. And the scourge shall not come near your tent.
Nor does any scourge come near your tent there, as it did here, while you were in the tent of flesh capable of suffering.
For he has given his angels charge concerning you, to guard you in all your ways. For your Father commanded his angels concerning you
that they should guard you in all your ways. That is why it is written: THERE APPEARED TO HIM AN ANGEL OF THE LORD, STRENGTHENING HIM,
because human weakness required it. In their hands they shall bear you. In their hands they carry you; they bring you to heaven,
not to help you but to serve you. Lest you ever strike your foot against a stone. So that you do not strike your foot against the stone.
You are the head; your feet are the evangelists, through whom you travel through this whole world. You do not want them to strike against the stone.
You do not want them to become guilty again under the law that was written on tablets of stone. Having gone to heaven,
you will send the Holy Spirit, who does not let them be guilty, liable under the law, and who unbinds them from fear and fills them instead with love.
Here one must take note, in the holy Gospel, of how the tempter twisted this meaning. You shall walk upon the asp and the basilisk,
and you shall trample the lion and the dragon. You walk over the asp: you overcome any demon at all; and over the basilisk: the devil himself, the king of demons;
and you tread on the lion that rages openly and the dragon that lies in wait in secret. The devil is a lion in persecutors and a dragon in heretics.
Because he has hoped in me, I will deliver him; I will protect him, because he has known my name. These words refer to him who dwells in the help of the Most High,
and to each of the faithful. Since he trusted in me, I deliver him, I shield him, because he knew my name,
the name of the God of heaven, of the Most High God. He called upon me, and I will hear him. He called upon me; I also hear him.
I am with him in tribulation. I am together with him in distress. I will rescue him. I deliver him out of it. And I will glorify him.
And I glorify him in heaven. With length of days I will fill him. I satisfy him with long days, there where the days are eternal
and all days are one day. And I will show him my salvation. And I show him Christ. In him he sees me.
A PSALM OF A SONG FOR THE SABBATH DAY. What does that mean? Simply this: this is the sabbath day's song. This is how one should sing on the sabbath.
Our sabbath is in the heart, for the sabbath is tranquillity of heart. A good conscience brings about that tranquillity.
Whoever is without it has neither tranquillity nor sabbath. Therefore he cannot SING in this way.
IT IS GOOD TO CONFESS TO THE LORD. One should confess to God; that is good. Confess your sins to him,
and blame them on yourself. Also acknowledge your good deeds to him, in such a way that you thank him for them.
And to sing psalms to your name, O Most High. And one should sing praise to your name, you Most High. That too is good.
The psaltery is a kind of instrument that is played with the hands. Move your hands and use them for good; that is called singing psalms to God.
To proclaim your mercy in the morning, and your truth through the night. And it is good to proclaim your mercy in prosperity,
and your truth in adversity; for in prosperity your mercy shines forth, and in adversity the truth of your justice shines forth.
By doing this, God is always praised. On the ten-stringed psaltery. It is good to sing to him on the ten-stringed psaltery,
that is, to keep the ten commandments of the law. With a song on the cithara. With a song sung on the cithara,
that is, with words together with works. For you have delighted me, Lord, in your making, and I will rejoice in the works of your hands.
All this is good for me because you have made me glad in your deed, and I rejoice in your handiwork.
My good deeds are yours, not mine. If I did evil, that would be mine; if I have done well, that is yours.
You gave me that joy. If this is true: HE WHO SPEAKS A LIE SPEAKS OF HIS OWN,
then this is equally true: HE WHO SPEAKS THE TRUTH SPEAKS FROM THE GIFT OF GOD. Every sin is called a lie, and all righ-
-teousness [is called] truth. How magnified are your works, O Lord! Your thoughts have become exceedingly deep. How great your works have been made, Lord!
Your thoughts have become very deep. No sea is as deep as God's thought, that the wicked flourish and the good toil.
In that depth many are shipwrecked who cannot understand this, and they consider God to be unjust. The senseless man does not know,
and the fool does not understand these things. The senseless man does not know it, and the foolish one does not grasp it. When sinners spring up like grass,
and all who work iniquity have appeared. He does not grasp that now is the time when sinners grow like grass,
and that another time is still to come at the judgment, when all those who now work injustice will be revealed. To what end?
That they may perish for ever and ever. That they may be lost from eternity to eternity. But you, O Lord, are the Most High forever.
But you, Most High Lord, endure forever, and from eternity you look down to see when the time of the wicked passes away
and the time of the righteous comes. For behold, your enemies shall perish, and all who work iniquity shall be scattered.
those whom he pleased, and who said of him: "For he is good." The Lord has clothed himself with strength. He put on strength
against those whom he displeased, who said: "No, but he leads the crowds astray." What is this strength? Nothing other than humility,
with which he endured them. Pride, its opposite, is weakness. And he has girded himself. And he was girded. He had before him,
when he hung on the cross, mockers who said to him: "Hail, King of the Jews." There he showed himself girded.
There he showed himself strong and ready to endure the wicked. For he has established the world, which shall not be moved.
By doing this he made the holy Church firm, which from now on stands steadfast and will not be moved. From now on it stands in faith.
It may be shaken; it will not be torn up. Your throne has been prepared since then. From then on, flesh is your seat. In the sixth age of the world
you came; since then you have sat in the hearts of the faithful. You are from everlasting. Before that, and before all time, you are. Forever and ever you are. The floods have lifted up, O Lord,
the floods have lifted up their voice. The rivers, Lord, the rivers raised up their voice. When the Holy Spirit came,
the apostles became very loud in their preaching. The floods have lifted up their waves, at the voices of many waters.
After them came other waters, which raised up their waves, meaning the boldness they had
from the roar of many waters. The more of them there were, the bolder they became. Wonderful are the surges of the sea.
From this the anger of worldly people became wonderful. From what? From the voices of many waters. How wonderful?
So wonderful that no one can count the host of martyrs who lay slain by that wrath. And what then? The Lord on high is wonderful.
The Lord was also wonderful in those very high and very powerful kings who did this.
Where does this appear? Your testimonies have become exceedingly credible. Your testimonies became very credible.
They became credible to the kings themselves, just as to the others. As it says: "In me you shall have peace."
"In the world you shall have distress. But take courage: I have overcome the world." What comes of this?
Holiness befits your house, O Lord, for length of days. Holiness befits your Church in eternity.
Its holiness appears in the other world. There it befits it, because there it will not be darkened.

A PSALM OF DAVID HIMSELF, FOR THE FOURTH DAY OF THE WEEK. A psalm to Christ for Wednesday. On that day the lights of heaven were made, which since then have shone on the good and the wicked. They stand fixed in the firmament
of heaven. So also stand those whose way of life is in heaven. And just as the lights do not care what is done on earth
and do not leave their courses because of it, so too those who are heavenly do not, because of earthly people,
fail to keep up [?] their way of life. Whatever is done to them or to others, they bear it with patience. Whoever loses that patience
falls from heaven. This psalm shows that. The Lord is the God of vengeance; the God of vengeance has acted freely.
God is the lord of vengeance, because he leaves nothing unavenged. The God of vengeance acted boldly when he came "among men."
As it says: "He was teaching them as one having authority, not as their scribes and Pharisees." Those whom he saw doing evil,
he rebuked boldly, because he is "the God of vengeances," and he wanted them to be spared "vengeance." "Be exalted, you who judge the earth."
Be exalted "in the resurrection," you who bring earthly men to judgment. Go boldly to heaven, you who were bold on earth.
"Render retribution to the proud." Repay the proud; forgive the humble. The proud who slew you were struck with terror
by the miracles of the apostles, and, having become humble, they said to them: "What shall we do, men and brothers?" Then they heard from Peter:
"Do penance, and let each one of you be baptized in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ."
Forgive them; forgive them the greatest debts. What is the debt? "They shed their own price."
What do you grant them in return "through forgiveness"? "Let them drink their own price." So your prayer has reached them, the prayer you made on the cross…
…"Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." "How long shall sinners, O Lord, how long shall sinners glory?"
The Holy Spirit himself speaks together with men and asks what they have to ask: How long, Lord, will sinners boast?
How long? "They will utter and speak iniquity; all who work injustice will speak." Sinners say and speak injustice.
All who do it speak it. They say: God does not know our injustice. Why do they say that, except that God bears with them
and lets them live? They hide from the police officer so that he will not catch them, but they do not hide from God,
because they do not think that he is present at their wrongdoing. They say: Since our wrongs displease judges,
the laws, emperors and prison officers, whom we flee, would we be any less able to escape him…
…if it displeased him, or if he knew of it beforehand? "Your people, O Lord, they have humbled, and your inheritance they have afflicted."
By speaking this way they humbled your people, who could not hear it without pain, and with it they troubled your inheritance,
that is, your faithful. "They slew the widow and the stranger, and they killed the orphans." They slew widows and strangers and orphans.
Of these it is written: "You shall not harm the pilgrim and the stranger." "And they said: The Lord will not see." And they said:
God does not see this. "Nor will the God of Jacob understand." Nor does the God of Jacob know it. "Understand, you foolish among the people,
and you fools, be wise at last." Take heed, you unwise among the people, and you fools, come to your senses at last.
"He who planted the ear, shall he not hear?" He who created the ear, does he not hear? "Or he who formed the eye, does he not…
…see?" Or he who made the eye, does he not see? Does he himself not have what he gave to others? "He who chastises the nations, shall he not rebuke?"
He who sent the prophets out beforehand "to chasten the nations," when he comes himself, shall he not then "rebuke"? What they did, shall he not do that?
Who teaches man knowledge? He makes another know; does he himself not know? The Lord knows the thoughts of men, that they are vain.
God knows the thoughts of men; he knows that they are vain. They do not know that his are right.
But he knows that theirs are vain. There are, however, some who know his thoughts; they are called friends of God.
Blessed is the man whom you instruct, O Lord, and teach out of your law. Blessed is the man whom you, Lord, teach,
and to whom you give teaching from your law. Which teaching? That you may calm him from the evil days. That you may make him gentle
and quiet him in the evil days, such as are those in which the wicked prosper. Until a pit is dug for the sinner. That he may restrain himself,
and that it may not weigh on him, until a pit is dug for the sinner, into which he falls and never stands up again.
What is the pit? It is his prosperity. It gives him pride, and through it he falls.
That comes from the hidden ordering of God. Whoever is taught this by him does not say to God: Why do the wicked reign
and the good are oppressed? For the Lord will not cast off his people. For God does not thrust his people away from him on that account.
What does he do, then? He exercises them; he does not cast them off. He improves them by means of the wicked, hardens them, makes them patient
and steadfast. And he will not forsake his inheritance. And he does not abandon his inheritance because of the others' wickedness. Those to whom he wishes to give the inheritance,
he scourges; the others he lets do what they want. Until justice is turned into judgment. Be righteous in the meantime,
and do not let God's ordering displease you until your justice is turned into judgment, until you sit together with him to judge,
just as the apostles too were first just and afterward become judges. And all who hold it are upright of heart.
Those who do this, who hold fast to justice, have a straight heart, not a crooked one.
Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? Or who will stand with me against the workers of iniquity? Who will come to help me against the malicious?
Or who will stand by me against those who act unjustly? They at once disparage my way of life
if they see me living in the Christian manner, with reproaches like this: Why do you not do what others do?
You alone are a Christian. Ecstasy has carried you off with Paul into the third heaven. Unless the Lord had helped me, almost,
that is, nearly, my soul would have dwelt in hell. If God did not help me, I could easily be led astray by such words
and my soul would go to hell. Among such people I would not be saved if God did not do it. If I said: My foot is moved,
your mercy, O Lord, helped me. If in humility I confessed my sins and said: My foot has slipped,
then your mercy, God, always helped me. According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, your consolations have gladdened my soul.
As many as the pains that were upon me, so many were the consolations that gladdened my soul.
Can the seat of iniquity be joined to you, you who frame pain in a precept? Does the seat of injustice cling to you at all?
Can any unjust person sit together with you, you who work pain in your commandment? That is to say:
you want pain to be commanded to us. Luctus means pain. You want that pain to be
commanded to us, because you say: BLESSED ARE THEY THAT MOURN. By commanding it, you work it. See for yourself, reader, how Augustine puts it:
YOU FORM, HE SAYS, PAIN IN A PRECEPT, that is, YOU MAKE A PRECEPT FOR US OUT OF PAIN, SO THAT PAIN ITSELF IS A PRECEPT FOR US.
Those are his words. The sense is: How can the wicked sit together with you, since you do not spare even the good man,
so that you would not will pain to be a precept for him? They will hunt after the soul of the just, and will condemn innocent blood.
They seize upon the life of the just, and they condemn sinless blood. Just so, the blood of Christ was innocent,
and yet it was condemned by the impious. How should they spare others, since they did not spare him?
Now the psalm comforts us again, thus: And the Lord has become my refuge. And so the Lord has become my refuge.
And my God the help of my hope. And my God is the help of my hope. He gives me eternal life
according to my hope, in exchange for this transitory one. And he will repay them their iniquity. He will also repay them their injustice.
And in their malice the Lord our God will destroy them. And in their evil will he will drive them out of his kingdom.
PRAISE OF A SONG, TO DAVID HIMSELF. To the true David, Christ, this psalm is both: both praise and song.
Laus (praise) shows devotion, canticum (song) shows cheerfulness. INVITATORY. COME, LET US REJOICE IN THE LORD. Come, people, come, you who are settled far away;
let us give up unrighteous joy, the kind that belongs to the world; practise the joy that belongs to God.
Let us shout for joy to God our Saviour. Let us jubilate to God our Saviour. Let us show joy with jubilation where
we cannot do it with words. Let us come before his face in confession. Let us go out ahead to meet his face in confession.
Because he is still to come to judge, let us therefore first give ourselves up to him by confessing our sins,
so that he will not then demand them of us in judgment. And let us jubilate to him in psalms. And let us jubilate to him in the psalms,
and show our spiritual joy in them. For God is a great Lord, and a great king above all gods.
For God is a mighty lord and a mighty king over all gods: over all those gods of whom it is said:
HE GAVE THEM POWER TO BECOME SONS OF GOD. They are gods because they are sons of God. They would not be that
if there were no grace. He is mighty over them because he made them mighty. For this reason we should jubilate to him.
For the Lord will not cast off his people. For God does not thrust away his people. Which people? The Jewish people.
Although they rejected him, as it says: "He came unto his own, and his own received him not," he still did not reject them, because the apostles
and other faithful came from among them. Therefore we should jubilate to him with every kind of voice, with songs of joy: with human voices,
organs, strings, pipes, cymbals, bells, horns, and the rest, in which "that which contains all things has knowledge of the voice."
That is called jubilating, that is, sounding without words. "For in his hand are the ends of the earth." This is also the reason:
because all the ends of the earth are in his hand. The Gentiles, who are seen as far as the end of the world, who are called the foreskin,
they too have come, together with the circumcision, and have joined themselves to the cornerstone, which makes both one.
"And the heights of the mountains are his." And his are the heights of the mountains. The earthly princes, who formerly
wanted to wipe out the Christian name by the laws they issued, are now Christians themselves. "For the sea is his, and he made it."
For the sea is his; he made it. What he made is necessarily his. He made the Gentiles, who listen to him;
they are what the sea signifies. "And his hands established the dry land." And his hands also made the dry earth firm. Because it is dry,
he therefore waters it. He knows well how much barren hearts need the rain of his teaching, with which he makes them firm.
"Come, let us worship and fall down before God; let us weep before the Lord who made us." Come, let us worship. And how should we worship?
Let us fall down before him and weep before the one who made us. It is right for this reason: "For he is the Lord God."
For he is our God. But what are we? "But we are his people and the sheep of his pasture." But we are his people
and the sheep of his pasture. "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts." If you hear his voice today,
then do not harden your hearts. "As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness." As the Jews did
in the wilderness, provoking me when they tempted me. "Where your fathers tempted me." There your fathers tempted me,
who are still not your fathers unless you imitate them. A man's father is the one he imitates. "They tested and saw my works."
They tested what I could do, and then they saw my works, which could have taught them this. "Forty years I was near to this generation."
For forty years I was near this generation. In what way? In the signs and wonders that I did before them,
by which they could have recognized me. "And I said." And then I said: "These always err in heart." They are always astray in their
hearts. If they were ever going to correct themselves, it would have happened in forty years. That is why I bore with them for so long:
so that I might show through them that there is a kind of people who never grow weary of their wickedness.
"And they have not known my ways," that is, the spiritual ones. And they did not recognize my ways, which are spiritual,
because "the carnal man does not perceive the things that are of the Spirit of God." "To whom I swore in my wrath: if they shall enter into my rest."
To whom I swore thus in my anger, and so threatened: they shall not come into my rest. That is: they shall not become blessed.
There all good is denied to them. This psalm begins in joy and ends in sorrow.
A SONG OF DAVID WHEN THE HOUSE WAS BEING BUILT AFTER THE CAPTIVITY. Thus David sang when the house was built after the exile.
Which house is this? Once a house was built after the exile, when Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, having returned from the Babylonian captivity,
rebuilt Solomon's house, which had been destroyed by the Chaldeans. Does this psalm speak of that? No.
It speaks of holy Church, which is the house of God: how it was built with the new song of faith, hope and charity
after the captivity of unbelief. SING TO THE LORD A NEW SONG. Sing to the Lord, all the earth. Sing to the Lord a new song.
Let all the earth sing it to him. Love is the new song, because it is the new commandment. All the earth is holy Church. It is the house of God,
and it is built with charity. In this building all the stones become one stone. How does that happen? In the unity of the Spirit, in the bond of peace. Sing
to the Lord. Sing to the Lord. Sing a new song; in this way you build a new house. Bless his name.
Praise his name. How? Announce well his salvation from day to day. Make his Savior, Christ, well known
from day to day, so that he may become ever better and better known. Announce his glory among the nations,
his wonders among all peoples. Make known his glory among the nations, and his wonders among all people.
In this way make him well known, and in this way build him a wide house. For the Lord is great and exceedingly to be praised,
terrible above all gods. For he is a mighty Lord, and greatly to be praised, and terrible above all gods.
What then are we to believe about them? For all the gods of the nations are demons. That is, all the gods of the heathen peoples
are devils. Those whom error invented, they are demons. But the Lord made the heavens. But the Lord made the heavens,
from which he cast them down; so mighty is he. Confession and beauty are in his sight. Confession and beauty are before him.
Let the confession of sins go first; then beauty follows at once. When you have washed yourself clean, you are beautiful before him.
Holiness and magnificence are in his sanctification. Holiness first, and great works afterwards, are in his sanctification.
His sanctification has this order: it brings you from holiness to magnificence. If you wish to be magnificent in signs and miracles first,
before you become holy, that cannot happen. Bring to the Lord, O families of the nations, bring to the Lord glory and honor.
You peoples, bring to the Lord glory and honor. Bring them to him, [?] not to yourselves, nor to other people.
Bring to the Lord glory for his name. Bring to him, in praise, glory for his name; say: NOT TO US, O LORD, NOT
TO US, BUT TO YOUR NAME GIVE GLORY. Take up sacrifices and enter into his courts. Take offerings that are fitting for him.
and go with them into his courts. Come with tears and with a contrite heart into his courts, which lead to his house.
Join yourselves to the apostles, to the preachers, so that they may bring you into holy Church, which is his house.
Worship the Lord in his holy court. When you come there, worship the Lord there in his holy court.
What is the court? That again is she, holy Church: a house for those who dwell in her, a court for those
who go to heaven through her. Let all the earth be moved before his face. Let all the earth be moved to repentance
by the sight of him. When he shows himself in the flesh and becomes known to them, then all will amend themselves.
Say among the nations: the Lord has reigned from the wood. Among all peoples say then: the Lord has reigned from the wood.
From the wood of the cross he began to reign, just as the devil had earlier reigned from the forbidden tree of paradise. For he has set the world right, which shall not be moved.
Thereby he has set the world right, which will not be put out of order again. Since the house has been built,
it stands from now on. He shall judge the peoples in equity. When the time for that comes, he will judge the people in justice. When is that?
At the second coming. Let the heavens rejoice and the earth exult. Let the raining heavens rejoice in his kingdom,
and the earth that has been rained on by them. Let the sea be moved and its fullness. But on the other hand, let the world rage against it,
and all of it as a whole, and from that let persecution come. The fields shall rejoice and all things that are in them. The gentle and the meek, who are God's fields,
and their followers rejoice at it. Then all the trees of the woods shall exult before the face of the Lord, because he comes. Then all the forest trees rejoice at his first
