coming, because they are used for the building of God's house. These are the pagans, cut from the wild olive
and grafted into the olive. For he comes to judge the earth. They also rejoice that he comes a second time to judge the people
who are earth, because there they will hear: "Come, you blessed of my Father." He shall judge the world in equity
and the peoples in his truth. He judges the world in justice: by this is meant the whole body of the good and the wicked.
And by "peoples in his truth" are meant those who are separated to the right and to the left.
A psalm of David himself, when his land was restored. A song to Christ himself, when his body rose again
and the unbelievers were invited to the faith. The Lord has reigned; let the earth exult. Christ, risen after death, reigned.
Let the continent rejoice at this. Let the many islands be glad. Let the lands broken up by waters rejoice at it too.
Land that holds together and lies outside the sea is called a continent. Land separated from it, in the sea
or in lakes, is called an island. Let the kingdom of Christ be a joy to both. Clouds and darkness are round about him.
Justice and judgment are the correction of his throne. Round about him: to some he is cloud and darkness, to others he is justice and judgment.
which are the correctives of his throne, for he gladly sits on those in whom he finds these two. Fire shall go before him.
and shall set his enemies on fire round about. Fire shall go before him before the Day of Judgment comes, and shall kindle his enemies
who are settled around him. For when the preachers begin to forbid the heathens their idols, they become inflamed. From
that, persecution arises. Persecution [?]. His lightnings shone over the whole world. His lightnings shone out over all the world.
These are the miracles of the preachers. The preachers are clouds; lightnings come from the clouds. The earth saw and was shaken. All the world saw the miracles
and was frightened by them. The mountains flowed like wax before the face of the Lord, before the face of the Lord of all the earth. Therefore the powerful and the proud melted like wax
at the sight of God, because they recognized his presence in the miracles. All the earth did the same, that is, all people.
They all gave up their hardness and became Christians. How did that come about? The heavens proclaimed his justice.
Because the preachers proclaimed God's justice to them. And all peoples saw his glory. And because all people saw the glory of God in the miracles,
Let all who worship graven images be put to shame. Since that is so, let all who worship carved images, that is, idols, be put to shame.
Who glory in their images. Those who boast of their likenesses, as if we did not know what we worship,
because we worship the invisible God, while they see their gods. Worship him, all his angels. Worship him, all his angels,
and if people want to worship you, then point them to him, for he is the God of all, whom both you and they ought to worship.
Zion heard and was glad. The early Church in Judea learned THAT THE GENTILES ALSO HAD RECEIVED THE WORD OF GOD,
and it rejoiced at the news. And the daughters of Judah rejoiced because of your judgments, O Lord. And the souls of the Jews who believed rejoiced
THAT GOD SHOWS NO PARTIALITY, BUT IN EVERY NATION WHOEVER FEARS HIM IS ACCEPTABLE TO HIM. For you
are the Lord most high over all the earth; you are exalted far above all gods. They rejoiced that you are the most high God, above all earthly beings,
far above all the saints. You who love the Lord, hate evil. Hate evil, all you who love God, and fear no one.
Why should you not? The Lord guards the souls of his saints. For he guards the souls of his saints. He will free them from the hand of sinners.
He frees them from the hand of the sinners, who can kill the body but not the soul. Light has risen for the just, and gladness for the upright of heart.
Light has risen for the just, not for the unjust. The light of faith, which is in the heart, is not shared with the unjust.
But the light of the sun is shared with them. And so there is gladness for the upright of heart. Isaiah denied this gladness to the wicked
when he said: THERE IS NO REJOICING FOR THE WICKED, SAYS THE LORD. Rejoice in the Lord, you just, and give praise to the remembrance of his holiness.
This gladness is in God; rejoice in him, you righteous, and give praise to his remembrance, which makes you holy.
Keep his words in remembrance, and give praise to that remembrance, that is, trust in it; that makes you holy.
THE LORD HAS REIGNED. After his resurrection Christ reigns, because then those were sent out who made his kingdom known to the people.
Let the peoples be angry. The people are angered at this, because their idols are to be destroyed. Or they are angry with themselves for their sins
and do penance. You who sit upon the cherubim, let the earth be moved. You who reach above all the fullness of knowledge, to you I say: LET THE EARTH BE MOVED.
Either to persecution, so that the martyrs may be crowned, or to penance, so that they themselves may be saved. What is the fullness of knowledge?
Of knowledge [the fullness] is charity. Have charity; then you reach to the cherubim. The Lord in Zion is great and exalted above all peoples.
Zion is the Church. Be in the Church; then God is great and exalted in you. Be also yourself Zion.
Be a contemplator of the divine light; then you will be illuminated, and from that illumination God becomes great and exalted in you in all virtues, above all the people
who were angry with him over their idols. Let them confess your great name. Let them acknowledge your great name.
Those who at first would not acknowledge him when he was small, because he had not yet come far, they will acknowledge him as great
when he becomes known everywhere. Why? Because it is terrible and holy. Because he is terrible and holy. Terrible
because he is the judge; holy because he is God. And the honor of the king loves judgment. And because the king's honor loves judgment,
therefore let everyone be just, because he loves judgment. You have prepared equity. You prepared right. Where?
Hear this. You have done judgment and justice in Jacob. In the holy Church you did judgment and right.
She did not take it from herself; you taught her both. Let everyone learn to do judgment. How?
By discerning between good and evil. But justice, how? That he turn away from evil and do good. Exalt the Lord our God.
Exalt the Lord our God; magnify him from whom we received justice, so that we may be justified.
And worship the footstool of his feet, for it is holy. And worship his footstool, because it is holy. The earth is the footstool of his feet.
He took earth from earth, flesh from the flesh of Mary. In that very flesh he walked here; that very flesh he gave us to eat; we must worship it
when we eat it, because it is a sacrament, and in a sacrament there is always a spiritual meaning. The footstool of his feet may also mean
the stability of his divinity. Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among those who call upon his name; they called upon the Lord, and he
heard them. Let us worship the footstool of his feet earnestly and gladly, so that he may hear us.
For Moses and Aaron, two of his priests, and Samuel, one of those who prayed to him, prayed to him, and he heard them.
Were there no more of them whom he heard? There was an infinite multitude of them, on whose behalf these three are named.
Was Moses a priest? He interceded for his people as priests do; therefore he is counted among them here.
He spoke to them in the pillar of cloud. He spoke to them out of the pillar of cloud. That was a figure.
for the cloud signifies the Holy Spirit. The pillar signifies the strength and beauty of the building. In the Holy Spirit he wished to strengthen the fabric of the Church.
He prefigured that for them. They kept his testimonies and the precepts which he gave them. Therefore he heard them.
that they kept his testimonies and his commandments, which he had entrusted to them. What were the testimonies?
Nothing but the precepts themselves, with which he made his will known to them. Or else the prefigurations of the things to come, which have now come to us.
O Lord our God, you heard them; O God, you were gracious to them. You, Lord, heard them; you were gracious to them,
wherever it was for their need. And taking vengeance on all their inventions. And you were an avenger in all their wishes
in which there was no need of theirs. As was shown in Paul, who prayed three times for something which God did not grant him. Why did he not grant it?
Because it was not for his need. What was he avenging? The self-exaltation that could have arisen from it.
But how was it with Moses, Aaron and Samuel? What did he have to avenge in them? That they were not without sin.
What was the vengeance? That they had daily toil from the wicked conduct of those among whom they lived. The better a man
is, the more heavily the evil deeds of others weigh on him. Exalt the Lord our God. Exalt the Lord our God,
both when he scourges and when he strikes. And worship at his holy mountain, for the Lord our God is holy.
And worship him, for he is holy, on his holy mountain, that is, the holy Church.
Whoever does not pray within it loses his prayer. But how is it a mountain? One reads that in Daniel.
There it says: A stone cut from the mountain without hands broke all the kingdoms of the earth and grew into a great mountain,
so that it filled the whole world. What is that mountain from which the stone was cut? The kingdom of the Jews, from which Christ came,
the stone which they reviled. How was it cut without hands? In that he was born without the work of men,
without marital union, born of a virgin, born without hands. How did it break all the kingdoms of the earth? Because the kingdoms of idols were broken,
the kingdoms of demons. What does 'grew' mean? That the body of the holy Church, whose head he himself is, by growing has spread to the ends of the earth.
A psalm in confession. What is this confession? It is both of praise and of penitence.
Shout for joy to the Lord, all the earth. Sing joyfully to God, all who dwell on the earth, for his blessing has come to you all.
Serve the Lord in gladness. Serve him in joy. He seeks willing and joyful service. Enter into his presence with exultation.
Go into your conscience with joy, which is in his sight, not in the sight of men.
Do not rejoice outwardly, but inwardly. Know that the Lord himself is
God. Know that the Lord is God. Who does not know that?
The Jews did not know it; therefore they slew him. For if they had known, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.
He made us, and not we ourselves. He made us, not we ourselves. From him we have being.
Therefore we must not despise him. But we are his people and the sheep of his pasture. We are his people,
and his pasture-sheep, because he is our shepherd. Which are the pastures? None other than the divine Scriptures, by which the soul is fed.
Enter his gates in confession. Go into his gates with confession. Humility, penance, baptism, charity,
and almsgiving are his gates, which lead to him with the confession of sins. His courts with hymns of confession.
Go also into his courts, which are in heaven, with praises of a different confession from that of penance. By confessing they go there;
by confessing they dwell there, because there is only the confession of joy there. Praise his name, for the Lord is sweet.
Praise his name, because he is a sweet Lord. His mercy is for ever. His grace is eternal,
because he gives the blessedness that he never afterwards takes away. And his truth is unto generation and generation.
And his truth is in all generations, both in the one that bears mortals and in the one that bears the eternal.
A Psalm of David himself. This song looks to Christ himself; this voice is his,
and, together with him, his Church's. Mercy and judgment I will sing to you, O Lord. Grace and judgment I sing to you, Lord.
Your works are in these two; therefore they are my song. Now is the time of mercy;
after this comes the time of judgment. Elsewhere these two are called justice and peace,
or mercy and truth, or justice and judgment. They show us how inseparably he is both merciful and just.
I will sing and understand in the undefiled way, when you come to me. I sing in the way that is not bent,
and from this I perceive when you come to me. I serve you with joy; that gives me perception of your coming.
I walked in the innocence of my heart. I walked in the harmlessness of my heart; by doing so I sang in the way that is not bent,
in which God meets man. He is not innocent who harms another, nor he who does not help another, nor yet he
who indulges himself too much. In the midst of my house. Where did this walking take place? In the midst of my house, in my heart.
I did not set an unjust thing before my eyes. I did not keep wrong before my eyes, because it was hateful to me;
therefore my eyes shunned it. I hated those who commit transgressions. I hated those who act wrongly — their work,
that is, I hated the unjust thing, not the people themselves. There are two names, man and transgressor: God made the man; the man made the transgressor.
I loved God's deed; I hated man's deed. A perverse heart did not cleave to me. Nothing perverse clung to me.
That is what an unrighteous heart says, such as belongs to the man who takes offence at God's will and so quarrels with him: GOD, WHAT HAVE I DONE TO YOU?
WHAT HAVE I COMMITTED? WHAT HAVE I DESERVED? I do not wish to be his companion, because with a perverse heart he considers himself just
and God unjust. The wicked one who turned away from me I did not know, that is, I did not approve. The heretic who turned to faithlessness I did not fol-
-low. Whoever secretly slandered his neighbour, him I persecuted. The man who backbit another I hunted down and persecuted,
because the persecution by which one hastens to make the man better is good. With the proud eye and the insatiable heart, with him I did not eat.
With the proud man, and with the one who out of envy cannot be sated by the woes of others, I did not eat. All the proud are envious,
and they are fed by the misfortunes of others, yet not satisfied. Their company is to be fled. My eyes are on the faithful of the earth,
that they may sit with me. My eyes are turned toward the faithful inhabitants of the earth. I desire their fellowship. For what purpose?
That they may sit with me to judge. As one of them said: DO YOU NOT KNOW THAT WE SHALL JUDGE ANGELS?
He who walked in the undefiled way ministered to me. Going in the unspotted way, he served me. Who is that?
None other than the faithful preacher of the gospel, who does not seek his own things but those of Jesus Christ. He who acts with pride shall not dwell in the midst of my house.
He who is proud does not dwell in my heart. I have one heart together with the humble; I have a heart that recoils from the proud.
He who speaks unjust things did not go straight in the sight of my eyes. Speaking wrong, he went astray before me.
Wherever he saw me, there he shied away; he fled from there. In the morning, that is, in the beginning, I killed all the sinners of the earth,
so that I might destroy from the city of the Lord all who work iniquity. In the beginning I slew all the sinners of the earth.
At the beginning of temptation I slew all the tempting demons, so that I might drive them out of my soul, which is the Lord's city
and his dwelling. Demons are rightly called sinners of the earth and workers of iniquity, because they cause
earthly people to sin and to act wickedly. But they are slain in their works by those who resist them right at the onset of temptation
and drive them away by cursing them. 'In the mornings' may also be understood as the day of judgment, as it says: JUDGE NOTHING BEFORE THE TIME,
UNTIL THE LORD COMES, WHO WILL BRING TO LIGHT THE HIDDEN THINGS OF DARKNESS AND WILL MAKE MANIFEST THE COUNSELS OF HEARTS. Now it is night;
now no one knows another. Then it will be seen who each one is; then it is morning; then all who work iniquity will be driven out of the city of the Lord.
THE PRAYER OF THE POOR MAN WHEN HE IS IN ANGUISH AND POURS OUT HIS PRAYER BEFORE THE LORD. This is a poor man's prayer when he is in distress
and then implores God about it. For this reason, in some places it applies to Christ, who for our sake became poor,
and to his bride, holy Church, which is one with him in one flesh and in one voice, and to each of his faithful who is in need.
LORD, HEAR MY PRAYER, AND LET MY CRY COME TO YOU. Lord Father, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to
[?] you. May my prayer be so loud that it comes to you. Ne avertas faciem tuam a me: Do not turn your face away from me.
Do not turn it away from those who are poor and are my members. In quacumque die tribulor, inclina ad me aurem tuam: On whatever day I am in distress, incline your ear to me.
Whenever I come into distress, incline your ear to me. I am in distress down below, but you are up above.
On whichever side there is need, help me on that side. In quacumque die invocavero te, velociter exaudi me: On whatever day I call upon you, hear me quickly. In this generation, in the second,
and in the third, and in whichever one I call upon you, hear me quickly, for I ask for what you gladly give.
What is that? Nothing other than the kingdom of heaven. Do as you promised when you said: "While you are still speaking, I will say:
'Here I am.'" Quia defecerunt sicut fumus dies mei: For my days have vanished like smoke. Therefore hear me soon, for my days have passed away like smoke.
Adam earned such days. Want and poverty lie upon me. Et ossa mea sicut in frixorio confrixa sunt: And my bones are fried as in a frying pan.
And my bones are roasted as if in a pan. They smolder for fear of the eternal fire.
These words belong to the penitent. But they may also be Christ's, in that he calls his strong ones bones, as the apostles are,
for in them he is burned, according to these words: "Who is made to stumble, and I do not burn?" Love causes the frying.
Percussum est sicut faenum et aruit cor meum: My heart is struck down like hay and has withered. My heart is struck, and so it dried up like hay. Hay dries from being cut.
I have become like hay because of sins that strike me down. Why is that? Quia oblitus sum manducare panem meum: Because I forgot to eat my bread.
Because I did not remember to eat my bread. God's commandment is the bread of the soul; against it I ate what was forbidden.
Therefore it has rightly befallen me. A voce gemitus mei adhaeserunt ossa mea carni meae: At the sound of my groaning my bones have cleaved to my flesh. At the sound of my sighing
my bones cleaved to my flesh. By sighing I obtained this from God: that we who are firm should cling to the infirm,
and we who are strong to the weak. They would not sigh over their infirmity, so I sighed for them.
As it says: "For we who are firm ought to bear the infirmity of the weak." Similis factus sum pellicano solitudinis: I have become like a pelican of the wilderness.
From sighing and from grief I am as lean as the pelican that flies in Egypt, in the wildernesses of the river Nile, of which the naturalists say
that it digests nothing of what it swallows, no more than the cormorant does here in these lakes.

Factus sum sicut nycticorax in parietinis, that is, in domicilio: I have become like the night raven among ruined walls, that is, in a dwelling. I have also become like the night raven in the ruined houses, where it is undisturbed,
because no human being is there. Instead of nycticorax, some understand bubo or noctua or onocrotalus,
that is, the eagle-owl or the owl or the bittern. Vigilavi et factus sum sicut passer singularis in tecto: I have kept watch and have become like a solitary sparrow on the roof.
I kept watch and have become like the sparrow that stays alone in the house, for other birds fly away;
the sparrow stays at home. These three birds stand for three ways of life of the saints. The pelican stands for hermits.
With the night raven: those who, living among other people, secretly at night say their prayers and give their alms as provision for their souls.
With the sparrow: those who like to be in the church, I mean in the oratory, and who stay behind there when the others have gone out.
Now let us also see how this fits Christ. He is the pelican in the wilderness, because he alone was born of the Virgin.
He is the night raven, because he suffered in the darkness of the Jews as if in the night. They were the ruined walls;
they were ruins, because they could not stand in the building. He loved them, and so he interceded for them like this: "Father, forgive them,
for they know not what they do." He was the watchful sparrow, that is, rising again, keeping watch after death, and flying into heaven.
There he is alone on the roof, interceding for us. "All day long my enemies reproached me, and those who praised me swore against me."
All day long my enemies reproached me, and those who praised me swore and joined together against me.
Praising him, they said: "Master, we know that you are truthful, and you teach the way of God in truth, and you do not regard the person of man."
Together with the praise, they had agreed to trip him up, like this: "Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar?" But why did they reproach me?
"Because I ate ashes like bread, and mixed my drink with weeping." Because I ate ashes like bread
and mixed my drink with weeping. How? By sharing fellowship with penitents, and by receiving tax collectors and sinners as if they were innocent.
They found that offensive. Or else the penitent says: I ate the bread dipped in the ashes, with tears.
"Because of your wrath and indignation." Because of the sight of your anger and your wrath, which came upon me from Adam.
"For having lifted me up, you have dashed me down." For after lifting me up through reason and free will, you at once struck me down and crushed me by the judgment of death.
You struck me down because I was proud of my high standing. "My days have declined like a shadow." After that my
days declined as a shadow declines. A shadow does not stand still, and neither do my days. If I had not turned away from you,
they could have been unchanging. "And I like the grass of the field." And so I withered like hay.
I am like hay that passes away. But what about you? "But you, Lord, endure forever." But you, Lord, endure forever.
You who are steadfast, keep me, who am unsteady. "And your remembrance from generation to generation." And your remembrance endures through all generations.
The promise of your coming shall always be remembered. "You will arise and have mercy on Zion." You will yet rise up and have mercy on Zion,
that is, on the Church. You come after a long delay; that becomes the remembrance. "For it is time to have mercy on her, for the time has come."
Because it is time, because the time has come, for you to have mercy on her. "For your servants have taken pleasure in her stones."
Because your servants, the apostles and prophets, held her stones dear: her children, whom they brought up through their preaching
and made firm. "And they will have pity on her dust." They have mercy even on her dust, even on the very sinners who killed Christ.
they turned to the faith: first three thousand, after that five thousand. So that they too become made solid into stones.
And the nations shall fear your name, O Lord, and all the kings of the earth your glory. Therefore, after that, all peoples too fear your name,
and all kings your glory, and the Church spreads itself over everything. Why is that? Because the Lord shall build up Zion.
For the Lord himself builds it. And he shall be seen in his glory. And when the time for that comes, he shall be seen in glory
who before was seen in weakness. He has regarded the prayer of the humble, and has not despised their petition. On the prayer of the humble
he looked, and he did not reject their entreaty. Since that is so, let all be humble in this building,
and let all pray. Let these things be written for another generation. Let these words, these prophecies, be written for another generation,
when the New Testament comes, so that they may be more useful to that generation than to the earlier one, and that it may be a memorial from generation to generation.
And the people that shall be created shall praise the Lord. And then the people that becomes a new creature in baptism praises God. For he has looked forth from his holy heaven;
the Lord has looked from heaven upon the earth. That will happen because the Lord looked down here; from heaven he looked to earth;
from on high he came to the humble. Why? That he might hear the groans of those in fetters. That he might hear the sighing of the oppressed.
The fear and discipline of God are the fetters whose prisoners he hears. And that he might set free the sons of the slain. And he also came
so that he might unbind the sons of the slain. Those who were slain by the devil's deceit — we are their sons.
He unbinds us because he gives us remission of sins. That the name of the Lord may be proclaimed in Zion, and his praise in Jerusalem.
That God's name may be made known by the apostles in the Church, and his praise in Jerusalem — that is again the Church.
When the peoples gather together into one, and the kingdoms, to serve the Lord. That peoples and kingdoms, coming together, serve God
and become his catholic Church. She answered him in the way of his strength. Then Jerusalem answered him
on the way of her strength, which is Christ. She responded to his calling with good works, with his help.
But the former Jerusalem answered him with evil works. Therefore she heard: BEHOLD, YOUR HOUSE SHALL BE LEFT TO YOU DE-
SERTED. Declare to me the fewness of my days. Make known to me, says the Church, the fewness of my days.
Let me hear: BEHOLD, I AM WITH YOU ALL DAYS, EVEN TO THE END OF THE WORLD.
Although that span is small compared with eternity, it still gladdens me that I do not pass away before then, and that the heretics are lying
who promise me otherwise. Do not call me back in the midst of my days. Do not turn me back at the half part of my days,
as they suppose. Do not let them be fewer than you have spoken. Your years are for ever and ever.
For ever and ever are your years. Compared with yours, mine are few. In the beginning, O Lord, you founded the earth.
and the heavens are the works of your hands. They will perish, but you remain. In the beginning you founded the earth,
and the heavens are your handiwork. Though they are so, they will pass away. You stand firm, and are what you are.
And all of them will grow old like a garment, and like a covering you will change them, and they will be changed. But you are the same, and your years will not fail.
And they will all grow old like clothing, and you will change them, and they will undergo the change. But you are always the same,
and your years do not pass away. In the Flood the heavens nearest the earth were destroyed, the ones in which the birds are. There are also higher heavens,
which are called the heavens of heavens. Whether these are to be destroyed by fire together with those,
or only those and not these, or what change is to happen to them, is a difficult dispute among the learned.
Or what is written here about the heavens can be understood of the saints and the righteous,
in whom God thunders with commandments, flashes with miracles, and rains upon the earth with the wisdom of tru-
-th, of whom it says: THE HEAVENS DECLARE THE GLORY OF GOD. Of them this is well understood: AND ALL WILL GROW OLD LIKE A GARMENT.
AND LIKE A COVERING YOU WILL CHANGE THEM, AND THEY WILL BE CHANGED. What are their bodies but the garments and coverings of the soul?
In these they will be changed, as the apostle says: AND THE DEAD WILL RISE INCORRUPT, AND WE SHALL BE CHANGED.
How shall we be changed? It is sown a natural body; it will rise a spiritual body. It is sown mortal; it will rise immortal. It is sown corruptible;
it will rise incorruptible. Their bodies too are heavens, because they carry God, according to the words of Paul:
GLORIFY AND BEAR GOD IN YOUR BODY. Such heavens grow old so that they may be renewed.
The children of your servants will dwell, that is, in your years. In your eternal years the children of the apostles dwell. And their seed will be directed forever.
And their offspring will be directed into eternity, where all things move in their proper order. The beginning of this psalm is words of groaning; the end is words of consolation.
BLESS THE LORD, O MY SOUL. My soul, give thanks to God. And all that is within me, bless his holy name.
And let all that is in me give thanks to his holy name. Let the reason that is in it, and all its thoughts, praise him. Bless the Lord, O my soul,
and do not forget all his rewards. Thank him, and do not forget any of his reward. You earned evil things; he gave you good things,
and still gives them, as is written further on: Who is merciful to all your iniquities, who heals all your diseases. Who to all your wrongs shows mer-
-cy, who heals all your sicknesses. Who redeems your life from destruction. Who redeems your life from perdition.
Who crowns you with compassion and mercy. Who crowns you with pity and with mercy. 'Corona' (crown) means an ornament of the head,
that is, the adornment of the head, as we see on kings. Who satisfies your desire with good things.
Who fulfills your desire with good, that is, who fills you with good. Your youth will be renewed like the eagle's.
Your youth will be renewed like the eagle's. It is said that in old age it happens to the eagle that its upper beak grows so far over the lower
that it cannot open it to eat. Then it knocks the beak against the rock
until it wears it down so far that it can eat again. And so it gains youthful strength, as it had at first.
So it also happens to anyone who hastens to wear away his sins on Christ, who is the rock, for he brings him back to innocence.
From that innocence he comes to the resurrection; there he is made young again. This saying refers to that: The Lord does acts of mercy
and gives judgment for all who suffer injury. The Lord is the one who shows mercy and gives justice to all who suffer wrong and who leave vengeance to him.
As he says: “Vengeance is mine; I will repay.” He made his ways known to Moses. He made his ways known to Moses,
that the law should be understood spiritually, and that through the giving of the law he wanted the people to recognize themselves, people who did not admit that they were sinners
or that they needed grace, until their transgression of the law showed it to them. He made that hidden counsel known to Moses.
His will to the children of Israel. Not to Moses alone, but to all true Israelites, in whom there is no guile, he made known his
will: that he wanted the five books of Moses to be like the five porches in which the sick lay,
so that they would be exposed, not so that they would be healed there. They were not healed in the porches. In the stirred water, that is, in the Jewish uproar
from which Christ's passion came, one was healed, that is, the unity of the Christian people. The Lord is merciful and compassionate, long-suffering and very merciful.
The Lord is gracious and shows mercy; he is long-suffering and very merciful. He will not be angry to the end,
nor will he be indignant forever. He is not angry to the end, nor does he rage forever. He has not dealt with us according to our sins,
nor has he repaid us according to our iniquities. He has not dealt with us according to our sins,
nor has he repaid us according to our wrongdoings. For as high as heaven is above the earth, so has he strengthened his mercy over those who fear him.
This is shown by the fact that, as high as heaven is above the earth, so has he made his mercy firm over those
who fear him. The height of heaven covers those who are beneath it, and he gives light, rain and wind for the sake of the fruits of the earth.
In the same way God tirelessly gives out mercy to those who stand in fear of him. As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our iniquities from us.
As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our wrongdoings from us. The setting flees from the rising.
So too, as his grace rises upon us, our sins fall away. As a father has mercy on his children, so the Lord has had mercy on those who fear him. As a father has mercy on his children,
so God has mercy on those who fear him. If he scourges them, they should love the scourges, because these come from their father's mercy.
Those whom he scourges he does not disinherit. For he himself knows how we were formed. He shows this fatherly
mercy because he knows what we are made of. He knows that it came from mud. He has remembered that we are dust.
He has not forgotten that we are dust. Those who could have been noble have become so lowly through sin. "Man, his days are like grass."
Man is like hay. His days are like hay. "As the flower of the field, so shall he flourish." Like the flower there in the field,
so he blooms and withers; so short-lived is he. "For the spirit shall pass away in him, and he shall not remain, and he shall no longer know his place."
For his spirit, which is in him, departs, and he does not remain here, nor does he ever return here again. If he is to be blessed after he has gone from here,
that comes through the grace of him who took on himself grass, to make gold out of it. "But the mercy of the Lord is from age to age, and for ever, upon those who fear him."
But God's grace is upon those who fear him, from the beginning of this world, and from then on into the world to come.
Here, where it says "from age" (a saeculo), many supposed, as Cassiodorus says, that grace was promised to Adam, because others came into being in the world (in saeculo);

he came into being from the beginning of the world (a saeculo). "And his righteousness is upon children's children, upon those who keep his covenant and are mindful of his commandments, to do them." And his righteousness
shows, that is, in our sons' sons; these are works and the rewards of works. And it shows in those who keep his covenant
and are mindful of his commandments so that they fulfil them. His covenant (testamentum) is his commandments.
They all consist in charity, and we must be mindful of them. "The Lord has prepared his throne in heaven, and his kingdom shall rule over all."
The Lord prepared his throne in heaven, at the right hand of the Father, and his kingdom rules over them all. "Bless
the Lord, all you his angels, mighty in strength, who do his word, hearkening to the voice of his words." Praise God, all his angels, mighty in power,
you who do his word to hear, that is, to fulfil the voice of his words. "Bless the Lord, all you his hosts,
his ministers who do his will." Praise the Lord, all his hosts, his servants,
you who fulfil his will. "Bless the Lord, all his works." Let all his works praise him. "In every place of his dominion,
bless the Lord, O my soul." In all the places where his power is, there praise God, my soul.
His power is everywhere; praise him everywhere, not only within the enclosures of the church but also outside its enclosures.
"BLESS THE LORD, O MY SOUL." My soul, praise the Lord for the beautiful things that this psalm shows.
"O Lord my God, you are magnified exceedingly." O Lord my God, you are greatly magnified. You have shown yourself great
to those who did not know your greatness before. "You have put on confession and beauty." You have clothed yourself in confession and adornment,
because your church put on these two. At first she was dark, before she began to confess her sins,
but by confessing she was made white. Her putting on is your putting on. "Clothed with light as with a garment." Covered with light
as with a garment. Her garment is your garment; that is the light of faith. "Stretching out the heaven like a skin."
Stretching out the heaven as a hide is stretched. After animals die, their hides are stretched.
The scriptures of the prophets were also, after their lifetime, stretched out and spread abroad to all nations. They were un-
heeded as long as they themselves were in the Old Testament. When the New came and they were no more, then their writings were brought forward, and then people began to recognize them.
And therefore they are heaven, because God is found in them. "Who coverest its upper parts with waters." You cover its upper parts with waters.
There are waters above heaven, as these are there; so you set the precepts of charity above all the precepts of the law. For charity too is poured forth in our hearts;
therefore it bears the name of water. "Who makest the cloud thy ascent." You set the cloud as steps for yourself
and as a reception, as it says: "And a cloud received him out of their sight." But mystically, the clouds are the preachers.
Through the preachers you bring the weak to the understanding of the Scriptures. "Who walkest upon the wings of the winds." You who outrun the swiftness of the winds,
because you send your word more speedily than the wind travels, although nothing is swifter. Or else: the winds are holy souls,
and their wings are the love of God and of neighbour. You step beyond that love, because your love toward them is greater than theirs toward you.
When they fly highest to perceive your love, they always see it higher still. Therefore,
when Paul said, "That you may be able to comprehend what is the breadth, the height, the length and the depth," he also said,
"To know also the surpassing knowledge of the charity of Christ." For just as one should know that the breadth is every good work, the height is the heart lifted up,
the length is perseverance in good work, and the depth is the sacrament of baptism and of the Eucharist, in which what it means lies buried, because one does not see it, so above all
things this is to be considered: how far the love of God has brought us, and how high it reaches.
"Who makest thy angels spirits." You make your spirits messengers when you send them out to Tobias, to Zechariah, to Mary.
But mystically: in your Church you make spiritual men be messengers of your word, and you send them to the carnal,
as if from heaven to earth. "And thy ministers a burning fire." And you make your servants be a burning fire.
For being fervent in spirit, they set their hearers on fire. "Who hast founded the earth upon its own stability." You have made the earth fast upon its steadiness.
You have established your Church on Christ; he is its stability. "It shall not be moved for ever and ever."
From now on it will not waver. If anyone wishes to understand the stability of the earth according to the letter, that is difficult.
For it also says, "Heaven and earth shall pass away." Therefore "it shall not be moved" does not fit it.
"The deep, like a garment, is its clothing." The great mass of waters is its covering, like a cloak. The water surrounds the earth.
So also the multitude of pagans surrounds the holy Church. "The waters shall stand above the mountains." And waters stand over the mountains, as happened in the Flood.
Even the most exalted, even the apostles themselves, were oppressed by the vastness of superstition and persecution. "At thy rebuke they shall flee."
After that it comes about that those same deeps flee from your rebuke. "And at the voice of thy thunder they shall be afraid."
And they fear because of the voice of your thunder, your threat, which is this: UNLESS YOU DO PENANCE,
YOU WILL ALL PERISH TOGETHER. The mountains rise up and the plains go down, to the place which you founded for them. So the preachers raise themselves up, and the peoples
let themselves down, as far as the place of your Church, which you made firm for them, because it will not be moved for ever and ever.
You have set them a boundary which they shall not pass over, nor shall they turn back to cover the earth. You set a boundary in the catholic faith, which they do not step beyond,
nor do they turn back again to cover the earth, that is, to renew their sins and to become unbelieving again.
You who send forth springs in the valleys. You who let the springs flow out in the valleys: you give the humble the knowledge of doctrine.
Between the mountains the waters will pass. In the midst of the mountains the waters flow away. The teaching of the apostles is common to all.
"The midst" means what is common. All the beasts of the forest will drink. From it all the nations drink. The wild asses will wait in their thirst.
The Jews wait in their thirst until Elijah and Enoch come. Above them the birds of the sky will dwell; from among the rocks they will give voice.
Above them sit the spiritual ones: the holy souls of the bishops take care of them. They speak out of stones:
what they have from the prophets and apostles, not from Plato, that is what they teach. Watering the mountains from his upper places.
But you water the apostles from heaven. Just as those others have it from the apostles, so the apostles in turn have it from you,
for you fill them with the Holy Spirit. The earth will be satisfied with the fruit of your works. With the increase of your works
the earth becomes satisfied. That is the earth that is satisfied with the teaching which you rain down from heaven.
Bringing forth hay for the cattle. Bearing hay for the cattle, as it says: YOU SHALL NOT MUZZLE THE MOUTH OF THE OX THAT TREADS OUT THE GRAIN.
And plants for the service of men. And plants for the service of men: giving provision to those who are ministers of the word of God,
whom he just now called cattle. That you may bring forth bread from the earth. That you, God the Father, thus reveal Christ out of the earth, out of earthen vessels,
in which the apostles held the treasure of doctrine. And wine gladdens the heart of man. And wine then gladdens the heart of man.
Spiritual drunkenness gives him love of heavenly things. Or the fill of the Lord's body and blood makes them glad.
That it may make the face cheerful with oil, that is, with brightness. That this fill may make his face cheerful with radiance,
so that some grace of God may shine openly in him: either of healings, or of tongues, or of prophecy, or of some other charism.
For it says: TO EACH ONE IS GIVEN THE MANIFESTATION OF THE SPIRIT FOR THE COMMON GOOD. And that bread may strengthen the heart of man. And bread,
that is, the soul's nourishment, may strengthen his heart. The trees of the field will be satisfied. With this grace, that is, with bread, wine and oil,
the common people of the nations become satisfied, that is, the ordinary ones. And the cedars of Lebanon. So the mighty also become satisfied, who stand above others,
as the cedars that grow on Lebanon stand above other trees. Are they all satisfied? No. Those which he planted.
They are only those that he planted. As the Saviour says: "Every plant which my Father has not planted shall be rooted up."
There the sparrows will make their nests. Under them small birds nest. They found monasteries on their own property,
so that the community of holy brothers may be there. The house of the coot is their leader. The fulica (coot) is a sea bird, or a pond bird,
and it nests on a rock, always far from the shore. The waves are dashed against it, just as the Jews were broken against Christ, who is the rock.
The Jews were broken. He is their leader; they are his soldiers. If the cedars grow angry and cause them troubles or scandals, and drive
them away from there, that is the shipwreck of the cedars, not of the sparrows, because the house of the coot is their leader.
Another edition says: "The house of the herodius is their leader." The herodius is the greatest of all birds; it overcomes the eagle
and eats it. It signifies the most powerful and mighty men, who sometimes also renounce the world and make their dwelling in heaven.
Their example also draws others there who are weaker, because they are pleased with their building [?]. "The high mountains for the harts." Let the high mountains
be the place for the harts. Let the spiritual hold fast to the more exalted precepts. But what about the humble and the penitent?
What shall their comfort be? "The rock is a refuge for the erinacii." Christ is the rock. Let him be a refuge for the erinacii, that is, for sinners.
The erinacius is an animal the size of the ericius, that is, the hedgehog, resembling a bear and a mouse; we call it the mountain mouse (marmot),
because it has its stronghold in holes in the Alps. "He made the moon for seasons." He made the Church in the time of this mortal life,
in which it wanes and waxes like the moon. But it will overcome this inconstancy when time passes away. "The sun knew its going down."
Christ, the sun of righteousness, recognized his death. What does that mean? He willed it, it pleased him, and he suffered it gladly.
"You have made darkness." Together with that death, you, God, made darkness. He did that to his disciples, because they then lost the hope
that they had in him. "And it became night." And then the night came, about which Christ said to Peter: "This night Satan has desired you,
that he might sift you like wheat." Did that not show itself when he denied him three times?
"In it all the beasts of the forest shall go about." In that night all the forest beasts go out to their pasture, all
the demons, so that they may lie in wait for Peter and the other faithful. "The young lions roaring to seize their prey." The whelps of lions go out roaring.
Why? Only so that they may snatch something. "And to seek their food from God." And so that they may get food from God,
without whose permission they cannot have any. "The sun rose, and they gathered together, and they will lie down in their dens." After that the sun rose:
Christ arose. Then those same forest beasts gathered together and withdrew into their holes, that is, into the hearts of the unbelievers.
For when Christ arose, they took flight, and then they made way for the faithful. "Man shall go out to his work
and to his labour until the evening." From then on, from the morning onward, every man goes to the work that the Church needs.
until evening. That is the end of the world. There work comes to an end. How great are your works, O Lord.
Lord Father, how great your works are. No others are like them. You have made all things in wisdom.
In Christ you created all things. The earth is filled with your possession. The earth is full of your possession. It is full of Christians.
They are your possession. This great sea, and spacious to the hands. This sea is great and wide-reaching. There are creeping things without number.
As is plain to see there, in it are creeping things beyond number. Small animals together with great.
In it are small beasts and great. There the ships will pass through. In the midst of them ships still sail.
What does this mean? Only that in this wide world there are many dangerous people, of higher rank and lower, both pagans and bad Christians,
from whom offences and persecutions arise. And yet the churches of God are granted to survive in their midst and to come safely
to the harbour of salvation, because Christ is their helmsman. This dragon, which you have formed to be mocked. In it is this dangerous dragon,
the ancient serpent, whom you have made to be mocked. Mocked by whom? By holy souls and by holy angels. How by holy souls?
Because they tread on his head, that is, they spurn the beginnings of his temptations. How by holy angels?
Simply by reproaching him that he came needlessly from glory to misery, and from an angel became a devil.
That is why the world is dangerous: because he is in it. All things wait upon you, that you may give them food in due season.
All of them wait for you, so that you may feed them when it is time: the creeping things, and the animals small and great,
and the dragon himself, and your possession, since you have filled the earth. What is the dragon's food? Earth. The lover of earth is his food.
That is why it says: "Set your minds on the things that are above, not on the things that are on the earth." Whoever thinks on things above is gold.
God does not give such a person to him to eat in place of earth. When you give to them, they will gather. When you give to them, they take.
Their own power does not give them food, but yours does. When you open your hand, all things will be filled with goodness.
When you have opened Christ, who is your hand, your possession is filled with all good. But when you turn away your face, they will be troubled.
But when you look away from them, they are troubled in the temptations they then suffer. Why? So that they may learn
that you watched over them when they were untroubled. You will take away their spirit and they will fail, and return to their dust.
You take away their spirit in this way: that is, their pride. And they renounce themselves and turn
back to the thought that they are dust. Send forth your spirit and they shall be created, and you will renew the face of the earth. Send forth your spirit and visit them,
since they have emptied themselves of what was their own. And from that they are created, they become a new creature, so that they know who they are.
And so you will renew the image of man. May the glory of the Lord endure forever. The glory belongs to the Lord forever, not to man.
The Lord shall rejoice in his works. The Lord rejoices in his own works, not in those of man, because those are evil.
Who looks upon the earth and makes it tremble. He who looks upon man and makes him tremble. Whomever he looks upon in this way,
upon him he rests. As he himself said: Upon whom does my spirit rest? Upon the humble and the quiet and the one who trembles at my words.
Who touches the mountains and they shall smoke. He who strikes proud men and pricks them to penance, and once struck in this way they smoke,
because then they lament their sins. I will sing to the Lord in my life; I will sing psalms to my God as long as I exist. I sing to the Lord as long as I live,
because here I have hope. I will also sing to him for as long as I am in eternity, where there is no other work except the praise of God.
Let my speech be pleasing to him; but I shall delight in the Lord. May my speech be pleasing to him; my delight is in him.
I make myself known to him, who knows; may he make himself known to me, who do not know. Let my confession be sweet to him; his grace is sweet to me.
That is mutual delight. Let sinners fail from the earth. Let sinners slip away from earthly desire. And the unrighteous, so that they may not be.
And let the unrighteous perish, so that they may not be, that is, may not be unrighteous. Then he sends forth his spirit for their renewal. Be-
-nedic anima mea dominum ("Bless the Lord, O my soul"). Praise the Lord, my soul. That was the beginning of the psalm; let it also be the ending.
Alleluia is Hebrew; in Latin it means "Praise the Lord." Give praise to the Lord. That is the same thing.
It says "Praise God," because here "confession" refers to praise. And call upon his name. And so, when it is time, come and call upon him.
Proclaim his works among the nations. Make known his works among the peoples. This is spoken to the apostles and to the evangelists.
Sing to him. Sing to him: that is, in words. And play psalms to him. And touch the strings for him:
that is, in deeds. Praise him in both of these. Tell all his wonders. Recount all his wonders.
Even if you are not able to, do not lack the will. Be praised in his holy name. Be praised in his name:
it is his power that makes you worthy of praise, not your own. Let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice.
Let the hearts of those who seek God be glad; let them be without bitter zeal. Seek the Lord and be strengthened. Seek God and be strengthened.
Draw near to him in such a way that you are first enlightened, so you can see what is to be done, and afterwards strengthened,
so that you do not grow weary in doing it. Seek his face always. Always seek his presence. You have found him by faith;
seek him by sight. When you see him face to face, even then seek him without end, because you will love him without end.
Remember the wonders that he did. Remember the wonders that he did in the parting of the Red Sea
and in turning back the Jordan. His portents. Remember the portents he showed in the plagues of Egypt. For portents
are things that never happened before. And the judgments of his mouth. And remember the judgments of his mouth, which he taught to Moses.
O seed of Abraham his servant, sons of Jacob his chosen one. You race of Abraham his servant, you sons of Jacob,
his chosen one, remember them. To you the Apostle said: "But if you are Christ's, then you are the seed of Abraham,
heirs according to the promise." He is the Lord our God; his judgments are in all the earth. He is the Lord our God;
his judgments are in all the earth. His Church is in all the world, and his judgments
and his decisions are there too. He has remembered his covenant forever, that is, for eternity. He remembered his covenant forever.
This does not mean the Old Testament, which was to be abolished by the New, but the covenant of faith, which was counted to Abraham as righteousness even before the Law.
The word which he commanded to a thousand generations. He remembered the word which he ordered to last through all generations. What is that?
The word of faith: that the righteous shall live by faith. Which he ordained to Abraham. That is what he promised to Abraham, who was justified by faith.
And his oath to Isaac. And he remembered the oath that he swore to Isaac concerning his offspring. And he established it,
that is, the word, for Jacob as a commandment and for Israel as an everlasting covenant. And he established that word of faith for Jacob as a firm commandment
and for Israel as an everlasting covenant. By these patriarchs we should understand Christians: they are Jacob, they are Israel, and they are the seed of Abraham.
Saying: thus he promised concerning it. "To you I will give the land of Canaan." To you I give the land of promise, to you, the faithful people. "As the measuring-cord of your inheritance."
As the measuring-cord of your inheritance: that you divide it with a cord, because of the covenant of faith that was kept. For faith, by which it is
tasted how sweet the Lord is, gives the kingdom of heaven; that is the land of promise. When they were few in number,
very few, and strangers in it, and they passed from nation to nation and from one kingdom to another people, he did not allow anyone to harm them.
When they were few, and indeed not many, and those same people were exiles there in the land of Canaan,
and they wandered from people to people, from kingdom to kingdom, he still let no one harm them.
And he rebuked kings for their sake. And he punished kings on their account, as he did to Abimelech, king of Gerar,
and to Pharaoh, king of Egypt. What did he say? "Do not touch my anointed ones." Do not touch my anointed ones.
Who anointed them? No one but the Holy Spirit. How then can it be true, as the Jews say, that he is not the Christ
who has not been anointed with royal ointment, and that therefore the Lord Jesus should not have that name? "And do no evil to my prophets."
And do not show malice toward my prophets. And he called a famine upon the land. Then he summoned hunger into the land.
He ordered a seven-year famine to come. And he broke every support of bread, that is, he used it up. And all the strength of bread
he destroyed. Because bread gives a man strength, the psalm said earlier: "And bread strengthens the heart of man."
He sent a man before them. He sent a man ahead of them. Whom? Joseph. God sent him ahead of his brothers.
How did he send him? He was sold as a slave. He was sold into slavery. But God wanted to make him a lord,
though they gave him away as a slave. They humbled his feet in fetters. They struck his feet into the stocks.
Potiphar ordered this done because of his wife's lie. Iron pierced his soul. Iron went through
his soul. He suffered great distress. This is like what is in the Gospel: "And a sword shall pierce through your own soul."
Until his word came. He was in that distress until his word came about the interpretation of dreams, in which his truthfulness was shown.
The word of the Lord set him on fire. God's speech kindled him; the Spirit of God spoke out of him. For he is fire,
and he kindles the tongues of those who prophesy. That is why he appeared in tongues of fire over the apostles. The king sent and set him free, the ruler of the peoples,
and let him go. Pharaoh, who had heard of him as a man who interpreted dreams, the king and ruler of the Egyptians,
sent servants to the prison and freed him. And he made him lord of his house and ruler of all his possessions.
And he set him up as lord of his house and as all-powerful ruler over his affairs. So that he might teach his princes as he taught himself.
So that he would teach his princes just as he taught himself. What would he teach them? Only the interpretation of dreams. And so that he would teach his elders wisdom.
And so that he would teach his chief men wisdom, that is, foresight of things to come. He wanted him to be next after himself in power
and ahead of him in mastery. And Israel entered Egypt, and Jacob was a sojourner in the land of Ham. Then his father traveled there
and became a settler there. Old settlers who belong to their own land are called indigenae (natives). Those who are foreign,
that is, who have come from elsewhere, are called alienigenae, advenae, accolae, incolae (foreigners, newcomers, sojourners, inhabitants). And he greatly increased his people
and made them strong over their enemies. Then God increased his people, for he multiplied them, and made them strong over their enemies.
He made them superior to their enemies, as was shown at the Red Sea, when these came out and
those others lay within it. He turned their heart so that they hated his people and dealt deceitfully with his servants. Before that, he turned their hearts toward this,
so that they hated his people and were quick to deceive his servants. How did he turn them toward this?
Only in that he let his servants begin to prosper, so much that those others begrudged them for it. God's favor stirred up their ill will
and hatred and persecution. He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, whom he chose. For this reason he sent his servant Moses there, and Aaron,
whom he chose for this. He placed in them the words of his signs and wonders in the land of Ham. He entrusted to the two of them the words
and the messages of his signs and of his wonders, which he meant to do in Egypt to protect his people.
Signs are things that show us something of the past or of the future. Prodigies are things we have never seen before,
and which are frightening for that reason. He sent darkness and made them dark. But he cast darkness on the Egyptians and darkened them.
He gave them hearts so darkened that they paid no heed to his command. "Because they embittered his words."
That is, they received them bitterly. This was plain from the way they received his words bitterly and loathed them.
"He turned their waters into blood and killed their fish." He turned their rivers into blood and killed their fish,
because they could not live without water. "Their land brought forth frogs, in the chambers of their kings." Their land cast out frogs,
even into the kings' bedchambers. "He spoke, and there came the dog-fly, and gnats in all their borders." Then he gave a command again,
and at once the dog-flies came, and gnats came into every region. "He made their rains
hail." He turned their rains into hail. "A burning fire in their land." He made burning lightning-fire in their land.
"And he struck their vines and their fig trees, and broke the trees of their borders." And the storm struck the vineyards and the fig trees,
and crushed every tree there in the land. "He spoke, and there came the locust and the caterpillar, of which there was no number." So he gave a command again,
and then the locust came, and its young, the chafer, came, and there was no end of them. "And it ate all the grass of their land
and ate all the fruit of their land." And it devoured the hay and all the produce of the earth. Who devoured it? Both the locust and the caterpillar.
"And he struck every firstborn in their land, the firstfruits of all their labor." Then he struck the firstborn there in the land; he struck the firstfruits,
that is, the earliest yield of all their labors. Their eldest children and the firstborn young of the cattle,
raised with toil, lay dead together. "And he led them out with silver and gold." He led them out laden with gold and silver.
He told them to borrow it. This was not because he commanded something unjust, but because his command cannot be unjust.
"And there was no weak one among their tribes." There was no sick person among them. God wanted them to be unhindered on their journey.
"Egypt was glad at their departure, because the fear of them lay upon them." Egypt rejoiced at their departure
after they had learned of Pharaoh's death, because fear of them lay upon them. They feared that the Israelites would come back
and wipe out the remnant. "He spread out a cloud to protect them." When they set out, he stretched the cloud over them by day
against the heat. "And fire to give them light through the night." And at night he gave fire to light their way. "They asked, and
the quail came." They asked for meat; then the quail came to them, and that is meat. "And with the bread of heaven,
that is, manna, he satisfied them." And he filled them with heavenly bread. That signified Christ, who came from heaven.
"He split the rock, and waters flowed." He split the rock, and water ran out of it. "Rivers ran in the dry places."
They crossed the Jordan on dry ground. "For he remembered his holy word, which he had given to Abraham his servant." He did all this
because he remembered the promise he had made to Abraham, his beloved. "And he led out his people with rejoicing."
and his chosen ones in gladness. And he led his people out in leaping joy. Again, this means the same thing:
and his chosen ones in joy. And he gave them the lands of the nations, and they took possession of the labours of the peoples. Then he gave them the lands of the peoples.
Again, this means the same thing: they took possession of the labours of other peoples. That they might keep his statutes and seek out his law.
That they might keep what is right and observe his law, because that is how the highest good is won, not by owning lands.
Alleluia is here too, because God's grace shone in his chosen ones, of whom the previous psalm spoke, and in the same way
it was not lacking in those who embittered him either, of whom we will now sing. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good.
Confess your sins to the Lord, and do not despair of his grace, because he is good. For his mercy endures forever.
For his mercy is in this world. In this world there is a place for repentance; after the end of the world comes the judgment.
Who shall tell of the mighty deeds of the Lord, and make all his praises heard? Who is there who could tell of God's mighty deeds, which cannot be put into words? And who
is so holy that he carries them all out once he has heard them? What are these praises? Nothing other than the works of his commandments,
which are rightly called his praises, because God, who works them in us, is to be praised in them. Blessed are those who keep judgment
and do justice at all times. Blessed are those who keep judgment and do what is right at all times. These are the people who judge others
and live rightly themselves. Remember us, Lord, in the good pleasure of your people. Remember us, Lord, in the favour you show your people.
Let us be among those you take pleasure in, for you do not take pleasure in everyone.
Visit us with your salvation. Visit us in Christ, your Saviour. When he comes and a new people comes into being,
then count us, the old people, among the new. To see the goodness of your chosen ones. To see the goodness of your chosen ones.
So that we, having become as good as they are, may see their joy together with them. To rejoice in the joy of your nation.
For us to rejoice in the joy of your people, the new one. That is, that you would let us old ones share in their joy.
We have sinned with our fathers. We have sinned together with our forefathers, because we were in their loins. Or it means:
As they did, so did we. We have acted unjustly, we have done wrong. We behaved unjustly; the wrong we did,
they also did. Our fathers in Egypt did not understand your wonders. Our fathers did not grasp the wonders
that you did in Egypt. They did not know that you wanted to lead them to eternal life. They thought about temporal things, not eternal ones.
They did not remember the abundance of your mercy. They did not remember your many mercies, since they later distrusted you and
said: 'Can God prepare a table in the desert?' They had no understanding of present things and no memory of past ones.
And they provoked him as they went up to the sea, the Red Sea. And they angered him when they went into the Red Sea.
and worshipped the graven image. Horeb means "skull" (calvaria). On that Calvary they worshipped an idol; on the other they slew Christ. And they changed their glory
into the likeness of a calf that eats hay. And their glory, which was in God, they exchanged for the image of the beast
that lives on hay. They forgot God who saved them, who did great things in Egypt, wonders in the land of Ham,
terrible things in the Red Sea. They forgot God who saved them, who did mighty works in Egypt, wonders in the land of Ham,
terrible things in the Red Sea. And he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen one stood in the breach before him,
And then he said that he would destroy them, if Moses his chosen one had not stood before him in the breach,
in the plague, to turn away his wrath, lest he destroy them. He stood so firmly that he turned away His wrath, so that He did not allow Himself
to destroy them as their guilt deserved. Jerome says it means "in the breach of his wrath," which we say
as "in the breach of his wrath." The intercession is this: "If you forgive them their sin, forgive; but if not, blot me out of your book."
He was sure that God's justice would not want to blot him out, so he stood and offered himself for the guilty.
So their destruction was left undone. And they counted the desirable land as nothing. And the delightful land, the land of promise,
that is, the kingdom of heaven, they counted as nothing. They did not believe his word. Nor did they trust his promise.
And they murmured in their tents. And so they whispered in their lodgings, speaking reproaches against God and Moses.
They did not heed the voice of the Lord. And they did not heed the voice of God, which forbade them to murmur. And he lifted up his hand over them
to cast them down in the wilderness, and to cast down their seed among the nations, and to scatter them among the lands. Then he raised his hand over them
to fell them there in the wilderness, so that those of them who were left would be brought low among the peoples, and to scatter them through the countries. And they were ini-
-tiated into Baal-Peor. Initiated [?]: that is, they were consecrated to Priapus. As the apostle says, having come into a reprobate mind,
they raged so far that God's justice was openly shown upon them. And they ate the sacrifices of the dead.
And they ate the offerings of dead men, such as Priapus was. It is as if God spared them in these words, though they did even worse than that.
And they provoked him with their inventions. And with their devisings they angered him. They devised various gods.
And ruin was multiplied among them. And so their fall became manifold; they all lay dead in the wilderness.
And Phinehas stood and appeased him, and the shaking ceased. And Phinehas stood against the wrongdoing; by this he appeased God,
and so at that time the affliction was stilled. Here "quassatio" (shaking) is what was called "confractio" (breach) earlier, that is, their destruction.
And it was counted to him as righteousness, from generation to generation for ever. And that was counted to him as righteousness
in all generations; so it will be for ever. And they provoked him at the water of contradiction, and Moses was troubled because of them.
who embittered his spirit. Then they angered him again at the place that is called the water of contradiction,
because there they spoke against God. And there Moses was troubled because of those who made his mind bitter.
And he made a distinction with his lips. That is, in his words he set apart the wonder of God that they then demanded from the earlier wonders.
He trusted the earlier ones; this one he did not trust. Therefore, before he struck the rock with the rod, he said in doubt:
"CAN WE BRING WATER OUT OF THIS ROCK?" Through that doubt he too became guilty, and the guilt did not let him come
into the land of promise. But those who did come there, what did they do? They did not destroy the nations that the Lord had told them about.
They did not wipe out the peoples whom God had commanded them to wipe out: the Canaanites, Amorites, Jebusites and others. And they were mingled among the nations and learned their works,
and served their graven images, and it became a stumbling block to them. They mixed with them and married their daughters,
and acted as they did, and served their idols. That turned out badly for them. Scandalum is a Greek word
and means offense, or the left-hand side, since this mingling led them to the left side. And they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons,
and they shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed to the graven images of Canaan.
And from there they went so far astray that they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons. That was sacrilege.
And they shed the innocent blood of the very children they sacrificed to idols. That was both homicide and parricide at once.
They learned that from the nations. And the land was slain with blood, and was defiled by their works, and they committed fornication in their own inventions.
Through such innocent blood the earth was slain: not the earth itself, but those who dwelt on it
were slain on it. And it was defiled by their works, and so they played the harlot,
that is, in this way they betrayed God in their inventions. Were these inventions really their own? No. They belonged to the nations.
For this reason other translators said: in their pursuits, or in their affections, or in their affectations, or in their pleasures, or in their observances.
And the Lord was angry with fury against his people, and he abhorred his inheritance. Then God was angered by all this, against his people, and
loathed his inheritance, which they were supposed to be. And he handed them over into the hands of the nations, and those who hated them ruled over them.
And so he gave them into the hands of other peoples, and their enemies ruled over them. These were the Moabites, Ammonites, Philistines and Syrians.
And their enemies afflicted them, and they were humbled under their hands. And those enemies of theirs oppressed them, and under their hands they were brought low.
Because they would not be redeemed by the gracious God, they had to serve ungracious lords again. Many times he set them free.
However all that may have been, he still set them free many times, as is written in the Book of Judges.
But they embittered him with their counsel, and they were humbled in their iniquities. But they started again and failed him in their counsel.
and so they were always brought low in their unrighteousness. They did not grow weary of righteousness, because they did not grow weary of unrighteousness.
And he saw when they were afflicted, and heard their prayer. Yet he saw them in their hardships, and heard their prayer
because of their distress. And he was mindful of his covenant. And he remembered his new covenant, which he promised to Abraham.
And he repented according to the multitude of his mercy. And he repented of his anger, with which he had avenged himself on them,
according to the multitude of his mercies. And he gave them over to mercies in the sight of all who had taken them captive. And he showed them mercy before all those
by whom they had been won in war, because he wanted Christ to come from them. Save us, O Lord our God,
and gather us from the nations. Save us, Lord our God, both the old and the new people, and gather us from all peoples
into one Christian people. That we may confess your holy name and glory in your praise. That we may confess your holy
name, and be glorified in your praise, not in our own. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from age to age,
and all the people shall say: So be it, so be it. Praised be the Lord God of Israel from world to world,
and to this praise all the people answer, gathered from the circumcision and the uncircumcision, thus: So be it, so be it.
Alleluia. What happened to the people of God, at times sinning, at times repenting, and how the Jews were rejected and the Gentiles called,
and how manifold the mercies of God are: this psalm tells of it. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Confess to God, for he is good. He would not have said "confess" to you if he were not good.
Confess to him, for his mercy is in this world; after that comes judgment. It can also mean:
his mercy is forever, because the Greek eis aiona means both "for an age" and "forever".
Now mercy is upon human beings for a time, so that they may live with the angels forever. Let them say, namely "alleluia", who are redeemed by the Lord,
whom he redeemed from the hand of the enemy, and gathered them from the regions. Let those sing alleluia, his praise, whom he redeemed with his blood
from the hand of the devil, and gathered from all districts. A province is the country; a region is a district.
There can be many regions in one province. He did not redeem them with perishable gold or with silver, but with his precious blood.
From the rising of the sun and from its setting, from the north and from the sea. Those whom he gathered from all parts of the world. They wandered in the wilderness, in a waterless place;
they did not find the way to a city to dwell in. They wandered, before he redeemed them, in the wilderness of this world; they wandered in
a land without water; they did not find the way to the city of dwelling, the heavenly city, the way that is Christ.
Plato promised them, Socrates promised them, Aristotle promised them, that they would show them the way.
None of them showed the right one. Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted within them. They wandered hungry and thirsty.
their soul fainted within them. They grew weak from want, because they did not have what they longed for.
They wanted to know the way of truth. That is what they longed for. In this the philosophers could not help them.
What then? They cried to the Lord when they were in trouble, and he delivered them from their distresses. They cried out to God
when they were in such need, and he took them out of that need. The compunction came to them from him.
And he led them onto the right way, so that they might go to a city of habitation. And he led them onto the right way, to Christ,
so that in him they might go to the city of eternal dwelling. Let them confess to the Lord his mercies, and his wonders to the children of men,
for he has satisfied the empty soul and filled the hungry soul with good things. Therefore confess his mercy to the Lord, you,
and confess his wonders, you, to the children of men: that he filled the empty and hungry soul with good things.
How is this meant: "confess mercy and wonders"? Only that he bids those to confess who have experienced them.
Those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, and bound in beggary and iron. For he filled the Gentiles, who once sat in darkness
and in the shadow of death, and were bound with sins; in beggary, because they were poor; in iron, that is, in the hardness of evils.
That was one temptation. For they provoked the words of God and scorned the counsel of the Most High; and their heart was humbled in labours; they were weakened,
and there was no one to help them. For they too, having come to the knowledge of the truth, spoke against God's word and his will,
not submitting to the righteousness of God and wishing to establish their own. And therefore their heart was humbled in the struggles
that they had undertaken in vain against the desires. Then they gave way under necessity, because there was no one to help them,
since God did not help them. But what then? They cried to the Lord when they were in trouble, and he freed them from their distresses.
And he led them out of darkness and the shadow of death and broke their bonds asunder. Then he took them a second time out of darkness and out of death
and out of bonds. Let them confess to the Lord his mercies, and his wonders to the children of men. For he has shattered the gates of bronze
and broken the bars of iron. Now let there again be confession of this: that he broke the bronze gates and the iron bars.
He took them up from the way of their iniquity; for because of their injustices they were humbled. And he took them away from the way of unrighteousness,
in that they wanted to be good without him; but they were first humbled because of those same unrighteous deeds.
That was the second temptation: the first was of ignorance, this one was of presumption. Their soul loathed all food,
and they drew near even to the gates of death. They loathed all food, because disgust for spiritual goods came upon them.
That also brought them to the gates of hell. But what then? They cried to the Lord when they were in trouble, and he freed them from their distresses.
He sent his word and healed them. For that too was an evil wound, and they were sick with that sickness.
Therefore he sent his own Son, Christ, and healed them and freed them from their perdition. Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mer-
-cies, and for his wonders to the children of men. And let them offer the sacrifice of praise, and proclaim his works with rejoicing.
For his mercies let there also be thanksgivings to him, as for the earlier ones. And from then on let them offer him the sacrifice of praise,
and let them proclaim his works in joy, not in sluggishness. That is the third temptation.
Those who go down to the sea in ships, doing their work on many waters, they have seen the works of the Lord and his wonders in the deep. Those who travel the sea in ships,
that is, the priests who govern this world in the various churches, busying themselves on many waters,
which are many peoples: they have seen God's works and his wonders in the deep.
What is deeper than the hearts of men? Storms of rebellion and discord often spring up from them, and God stills these storms wonderfully.
HE SPOKE, AND THE SPIRIT OF THE STORM STOOD. First God gave the command; because of that, the stormy wind rose up and kept blowing,
the wind that troubles the ship. And its waves were lifted up. And the wind's waves rose up. They go up to the heavens
and go down to the depths. They lift themselves up high, made bold, and fall just as deep, grieving. Their soul was wasting away in evils.
