so that the life-giving Spirit may help me in this, lest the letter kill. And what did I say? Have mercy on me according to your word.
Have mercy on me according to your promise, so that I may be a son of the promise in the seed of Abraham. I thought on my ways and turned my feet to your testimonies.
I thought about my ways, which displeased me, and turned them to your testimonies, so that they might be more righteous there.
TURN AWAY MY EYES SO THAT THEY DO NOT SEE VANITY. Turn my eyes away so that they do not see vanity,
and likewise the feet, so that they do not go astray. This is like: MY EYES ARE EVER TOWARD THE LORD,
FOR HE WILL PLUCK MY FEET OUT OF THE SNARE. I am ready and am not troubled, so that I may keep your commandments. I am ready to keep
your commandment, and I am untroubled, because no fear takes it from me. The cords of sinners have wrapped around me, and I have not forgotten your law.
As is shown there: the rope of the sinners wrapped around me, and still I did not forget your law. The sinners are both the carnal
and the spiritual enemies. They lengthen their wickedness like a rope, because they keep tying one piece to another, and with it they wrap up the just,
by threatening evils and promising temporal goods. That rope was escaped by the one who speaks here: At midnight I rose to confess to you
because of the judgments of your justice. In the most bitter persecution I rose to confess to you, that is, to praise you,
for the judgments of your justice, because they are just judgments, that you will the just to be wrapped in the cord of sinners.
Why? Only so that they may be improved by it. I am a partaker with all who fear you and keep your commandments.
Now Christ speaks to the Father together with his body: I am a sharer with all who fear you and keep your commandments.
Christ says this because if he had not become a partaker in our mortality, we would not have become partakers in his divinity.
The earth is full of the mercy of the Lord. Therefore the earth is full of the Lord's mercies. The grain of mustard seed died; from it came much fruit in all the earth.
Teach me your justifications. Teach me your righteous ordinances, for through those mercies I become justified.
You have dealt kindly with your servant, O Lord, according to your word. You showed goodness, Lord, to your servant.
You made me take delight in spiritual goods, according to your promise. That is a great gift of God, for he who does good without delight
does it servilely, not freely; that is, like the servant, not like the free man. And discipline,
that is, corrective tribulation, and knowledge teach me. Teach me goodness; although I have it by your gift, increase it in me,
and give along with it its discipline, and teach me to be patient in that, for it is never without hardship. As the apostle says:
All discipline for the present seems to be not a matter of joy but of sorrow. Some translators said 'instruction' instead of 'discipline'.
That is always the same thing, which always comes with scourges. Therefore he prays for patience, to bear the scourges with an even mind.
And teach me knowledge that builds up, for knowledge without charity does not build up but puffs up. For I have believed your commandments.
Why did he not say 'I obeyed'? One should obey commandments and believe promises. What does he mean by 'for I believed your commandments'?
Only that I believed they were not ministered by man. Even if they did come from a man who taught them to me outwardly,
could he then teach them inwardly, as you do? Before I was humbled, I sinned. I sinned in Adam before I was humbled.
In him creation was made subject to vanity, because it did not want to be subject to truth. Therefore I have kept your word.
Therefore I have kept your word ever since I felt that vanity in myself, so that I may never be humbled again.
I took care of this because I have incurred the death of the flesh, so that I might not also incur the death of the soul, but do as you have commanded. How?
So that, with pride cast down, obedience may be loved, and so misery may be destroyed, never to return. You are good; in your goodness teach me your justifications. You are good;
in your goodness teach me your righteous ordinances. He is in earnest about doing His justifications, since he wishes to learn them in His goodness.
Notice further how earnest he is about it. The iniquity of the proud has been multiplied over me. Over me the injustice of the proud has been multiplied,
who were not made any better by the fact that human nature was humbled after it sinned. But I will search out your commandments with my whole heart.
But I seek your commandments diligently. However much injustice reigns in the world, charity is not extinguished in me.
Their heart is curdled like milk. Their heart is curdled like milk; it is hardened and does not yield itself to good.
But I have meditated on your law. What did I do in response? I meditated on your law, by which the humble escape the humiliations of punishment.
It is good for me that you have humbled me, so that I may learn your justifications. Therefore it is good for me that you humbled me.
so that I, being so greatly compelled, may learn your justifications, and so that this may be the fruit of my humiliation. For he who does not heed the good,
that you humble him, and still does not mend his ways by it, things go worse for him. The law of your mouth is good to me
above thousands of gold and silver. Good to me is the law that comes from your mouth and is commanded by your mouth; it is better
than countless gold and silver. For my love (caritas) shall love the law of God more than greed (cupiditas) loves thousands of gold and silver.
YOUR HANDS, O LORD, HAVE MADE ME AND fashioned me; give me understanding, that I may learn your commandments. Your hands made me
and formed me; therefore give me understanding, so that I may learn your commandments. You gave me form; give me re-formation.
Since my nature was deformed by sinning, it has not been able to be whole in understanding. Therefore I am not fit to grasp the commandments of God unless I am renewed in the spirit of the mind.
Hands are named here to mean power, as also in the place where it says: AND HIS HANDS FOUNDED THE DRY LAND.
And again: THE HEAVENS ARE THE WORKS OF YOUR HANDS. And here Christ himself asks his Father for what he knows his body needs.
That need and that want he suffers in it, and he feels it, because its life is hidden with him in God.
Those who fear you shall see me and rejoice, because I have hoped beyond measure in your word. Those who fear you now shall see me at some time hereafter,
when the just shall shine like the sun; and then they will be glad. Who are they? None other than the people of holy Church, who now fear him.
They will then rejoice in their fear. This is because I hoped for more from your promise than I dared to ask.
As it says: GOD IS ABLE TO DO MORE THAN WE ASK OR UNDERSTAND. I have known, O Lord, that your judgments are equity,
and in your truth you have humbled me. I acknowledge, Lord, that your judgments are just, by which we have been cast into death,
and that in your truth you have humbled us. Let your mercy come to comfort me. After that let your grace come,
so that it may comfort me and I may be restored to life again. Let regeneration come to me; let faith, hope,
and love come to me, which here are the consolation of the wretched, not the joys of the blessed. According to your word to your servant.
According to your promise let it come to me, your servant. Let your mercies come to me, and I shall live. Let your mercies come to me, and then I shall live, and
live truly, so that I do not fear that I will die again. For your law is my meditation.
For your law is what I meditate on. My thought is in the faith that works through love; in that I do not fall short,
in that I live. Let the proud be confounded, because they have unjustly done wickedness against me; but I shall be exercised in your commandments. Let the proud be ashamed
that they acted unjustly against me; but I shall be exercised in your commandments, whatever they may do.
Let those who fear you turn to me, that is, toward me, and those who know your testimonies. These words cannot belong to anyone other than Christ.
"To me," says Christ, "let those be turned who fear you, Father, and who know your prophecies that were written about me."
This persona was also the speaker before. I am a companion of all who fear you. Let my heart be made spotless in your justifications, so that I am not put to shame.
"My heart," says the body of Christ again, "let it become unstained in your justifications, so that I am not put to shame." A similar verse comes before.
O that my ways may be directed to keep your justifications! Then I shall not be put to shame, when I look into all your commandments. My soul has fainted for your salvation.
My soul has fainted for your Savior. And in your word I have hoped beyond measure. And in your promise I have hoped beyond measure,
because more good shall come, together with Christ, whom you have promised us, than anyone can know. My eyes have failed for your word,
saying: When will you comfort me? My eyes have failed for your promise, saying to you: When will you comfort me?
The inward eyes long for him. Therefore they gaze toward him, and they sigh with longing, and ask for your
comfort. For I have become like a wineskin in the frost; I have not forgotten your justifications. For the desires of the flesh are frozen in me,
as a wineskin freezes in the hoarfrost. Therefore I was not unmindful of your justifications. Which are those? Only love, which came
when the heat of desire gave way. How many are the days of your servant? When will you execute judgment on those who persecute me? How many days does your servant have?
What does that mean? Only this: how long will your body, the holy Church, last? How long until you judge for me against my persecutors?
Since it is to last until the Judgment, when will that come? This is the question of the martyrs in the Apocalypse, and there it is answered:
"until the number of their brethren is fulfilled." This prophecy foretells that question. The wicked have told me tales, but not like your law.
The unjust told me idle tales, that is, exercises in pleasing speech, not like your law, in which truth pleases me, not words.
Such people have various professions. The writings of the Jews composed in this way are called deuterosis, in which there are thousands of fables,
apart from the canon of the divine Scriptures. The heretics have the same in their empty talk. Secular writings have such things too.
And what else is the story told of Marcolf matching himself against the proverbs of Solomon? In all of these there are beautiful words without truth.
All your commandments are truth; the wicked have persecuted me; help me. But all your commandments are true. Because I set them against the empty speeches of the wicked,
they persecuted me for it; but you, help me. They had almost made an end of me on earth. They had nearly destroyed me on earth,
when a great slaughter of martyrs had been made. But I have not forsaken your commandments. Therefore I did not give up your commandments, because it says:
"He who perseveres to the end shall be saved." According to your mercy give me life, and I shall keep the testimonies of your mouth.
Give me life according to your grace, and so I shall keep the testimonies of your mouth, that is, the commandments, which otherwise I cannot keep.
Do not let me deny life by loving life, nor lose life by denying life. For ever, O Lord, your word remains in heaven.
In heaven, O Lord, your word endures forever. The holy angels there are steadfast in their service.
Here I may grow weary of this changeableness and of earthly life, which is full of temptations. His truth is from generation to generation.
But on earth your truth endures among the generations that are not in heaven. Therefore there is change here, but not there.
You have founded the earth, and it abides. You are the foundation. You have established your Church, and so it endures without passing away.
By your ordinance [?] the day continues. By your ordering the day endures. For the faithful there is an eternal day in you.
In that day they shall walk honorably and rejoice in it. For all things serve you. For all things that belong to the day serve you,
but not those that belong to the night. Unless your law had been my meditation, I might then have perished in my humiliation.
If I had not heeded your law, which strengthens me in tribulation in this life, I might have been lost in my mortal humiliation.
Your law is charity, and it takes destruction away from me. I will never forget your justifications,
for by them you have given me life. I will never forget your justifications, for by them you gave me life.
Therefore I will not be lost in my humiliation. What is a man if you do not give him life? What can he do? He can kill himself, but not
give himself life. I am yours; save me, for I have sought out your justifications. I am yours. It has turned to grief for me that I wanted to be my own.
That is the first and greatest evil of disobedience. But now I am yours again; keep me safe, for I have sought your justifications,
and not my own will, so that I may be yours. Sinners have waited for me in order to destroy me; I have understood your testimonies.
Sinners waited for me so that they might destroy me. They wanted me to consent with them and deny you.
Then I would have been lost. I knew your testimonies to be such that whoever stands firm in them is saved.
I have seen an end to all perfection; your commandment is exceedingly broad. In all perfection I saw Christ as the end; in him all virtues are made perfect.
Among them, charity is a very broad commandment, for the law and the prophets are fulfilled in it. How have I loved your law?
How did I love your law? What kind of love did I have for it? It is my meditation all day long, so that it is in my thoughts at all times.
It never leaves my mind, for the flesh lusts against the spirit. Therefore I set the meditation of the law against the flesh all day long.
What is the law of God but the commands of God? His commands lead me to good works, so they are dear to me. You have made me wiser than my enemies through your commandment,
for it is mine forever. With your commandment you made me wiser than my enemies are,
for it is eternal to me. You have taught me that I am to be justified freely, through the grace of God.
Israel according to the flesh, which is my enemy, does not know this, for it is an enemy of the law of faith, and it boasts in the law of
works. Seeking to establish its own righteousness, it is not subject to the righteousness of God, and it imagines that it fulfills the law by its own strength.
Therefore he will be thrust out, as it is written: "The servant does not remain in the house forever; the son remains." There, however, I shall have the commandment of God forever,
that is, the love of God. "I have understood more than all my teachers, because your testimonies are my meditation." I understood more than my masters,
because your testimonies are my meditation. Who says that? Who can say it except Christ? He sat in the temple among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions,
and they were astonished at his understanding and his answers. He knew it so much better than they did that it made them astonished. Of this matter there is a prophecy here,
which sometimes speaks from the head, which is the Saviour, and sometimes from the body, which is the Church, and in this way makes them, as it were, one speaker.
As it says: "They shall be two in one flesh." That was because his Father's testimonies were his meditation, as he said:
"You sent to John, and he bore witness to me. But I do not receive testimony from man,
but I have a testimony greater than John's." Therefore it says next something that again means the same.
"I have understood more than the elders, because I have sought your commandments." I understood more than the old ones, because I sought your commandments,
not those of the elders. He calls "elders" those he called "teachers." He wished to make even the crowds more learned than those elders.
Therefore he said to them: "Hear and understand: it is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a man,
but what comes out of the mouth, this defiles a man." The elders did not know that, who so insistently
demanded washed hands. "I have kept my feet back from every evil way, so that I may keep your words." I drew my feet away from every evil way.
These words are not those of the head but of the body, whose wicked desires must be bridled, so firmly that it may dare to say: "I have not turned aside from your judgments,
because you have set a law for me." I did not turn away from your judgments; I always kept my mind on them, in keeping with what it says elsewhere:
"For I have feared your judgments." Why? Because you set a law for me. You have put it inside my heart,
with chaste fear, not servile fear. "How sweet are your words to my palate, sweeter than honey to my mouth." How sweet your words are to my throat;
to the mouth of my heart they are sweeter than honey. It is not fear of bodily harm that leads me to them, but delight in spiritual good.
"From your commandments I have gained understanding." Through your commandments I became understanding. By keeping your commandment, what I longed for came to me, as it is written:
"You have desired wisdom: keep the commandments, and God will give it to you." The humility of obedience leads to understanding,
and when understanding comes, obedience is not to be [?] (literally "looked up from"; probably "abandoned"). "Therefore I have hated every way of iniquity."
Therefore I hated all unrighteous ways, because I wanted understanding. "Your word is a lamp to my feet
and a light to my paths." The Word is Christ; the word is Christ's, the word that was spoken to the apostles and prophets.
It is about this word that it now says: Your word is a lamp to my feet. And again the same: It is a light to my paths.
I would not know where I should go if it did not guide me. "I have sworn and resolved to keep the judgments of your righteousness." I swore, and [?]
I resolved to keep the judgments of your righteousness. These are they: that no one does evil with impunity
nor good in vain. I have been humbled exceedingly, Lord, that is, very greatly. Therefore I am greatly humbled in great persecution.
Give me life according to your word. Quicken me according to your promise, for the word of your promise is also a lamp to the feet and a light to the paths.
Make the freewill offerings of my mouth well-pleasing, Lord, that is, let them please you. May the willing offerings of my mouth be dear to you, which love (caritas) brings forth,
not fear. And teach me your judgments. And teach me your judgments. Earlier he said: I HAVE NOT TURNED ASIDE FROM YOUR JUDGMENTS.
How then does he now say, "Teach me your judgments"? Is it not that he wants to learn them better? My soul is always in my hands.
My soul is always in my hands. It is in my hands because I always bring it to you to be given life. As it says elsewhere:
TO YOU I HAVE LIFTED UP MY SOUL. Sinners have laid snares for me, and I have not strayed from your commandments. Sinners set snares for me,
and yet I was not led astray by them into turning away from your commandments, because I had brought my soul to you
for you to give it life. I have acquired your testimonies as an inheritance forever. As an inheritance I sought your testimonies forever.
That I may always confess you and never deny you: that I wish to have as my inheritance. Grant me that.
By your granting they can be an inheritance for me forever. For they are the rejoicing of my heart. For they are the joy of my heart,
even though they are an affliction to my body. I have inclined my heart to perform your justifications forever, for the sake of the reward.
I have inclined my heart to do your righteous deeds forever, for the reward. Justifications are works of love (caritas). Who can do them forever? When the needs
of our neighbours come to an end, the works also come to an end; but the rewards do not come to an end. Therefore he declares that he does justifications forever.
Earlier he said, praying: INCLINE MY HEART TO YOUR TESTIMONIES, to show that it is a divine gift.
But here he says I HAVE INCLINED, to show his own will as well. I HAVE HATED THE WICKED, AND I HAVE LOVED YOUR LAW.
I hated the unrighteous, and I loved your law. As much as I loved your law, so much I hated their unrighteousness.
I hated them in so far as they are wicked, not in so far as they are human beings. I did not hate human nature, but vice.
You are my helper and my protector. You are my helper to do good, my protector to escape evil.
I have hoped exceedingly in your word. I have hoped beyond measure in your promise, like a son of the promise. Depart from me, you wicked ones,
and I will search out the commandments of my God. Get away from me, you ill-willed ones, and then I will search out my God's commandments. Let me consider
what is dear to God, so that I may be bound to what comes first, not, as you wish, to what comes last.
These words are directed against those who importunately demand our help in worldly business. Uphold me according to your word, and I shall live,
and do not put me to shame in my expectation. Receive me according to your promise, and so I shall live. Where? Surely in the future.
where there is life without death. And do not put me to shame in my waiting. Do not let what I wait for slip away from me.
Help me, and I shall be saved, and I will meditate on your justifications always. Help me, for I am sick, and so I shall be saved.
And because of that help I will always think on your justifications. You have spurned all who depart from your justices, because their thought is unjust.
You spurned all who separate themselves from your just commands, and rightly, for their thought is unjust.
How can someone be righteous who is unrighteous in thought? I have counted all the sinners of the earth as transgressors, that is, those who turn aside from the commandment.
I counted all sinners in the world as transgressors. Of what? Of God's law, either the law given in paradise,
or the natural law, or the law published in writing. How then does this agree with what the apostle says: "Where there is no law,
there is no transgression"? Only in that he says it of just one of these, the one that was handed down to the Jews in writing. Therefore I have loved your testimonies.
Therefore I loved your testimonies, which send me to your grace, so that through grace I may gain what I cannot gain through the law.
Pierce my flesh with your fear. Pierce my flesh through with your fear. Make me crucified with Christ on the cross,
and let the desires of the flesh be put to death in me by the grace of God, for the law cannot justify me, but only make me a transgressor.
Pierce my flesh through with chaste fear. Let the flesh be crucified with it, for fear of punishment does not make the flesh crucified.
Why? Because through it sins are forbidden rather than avoided. For I have feared your judgments. Those judgments of yours
that are in the law I feared. They were like tutors to me. From there lead me on to that fear
in which there is delight in justice, not fear of punishment. I have done judgment and justice; do not hand me over to those who slander me. I did judgment and justice.
Do not give me up to those who slander me. Who are they? Those who twist even good into evil. Do not let them
turn me to evil with their persecution, that is, do not let them force me, out of fear of suffering evil, to do evil. Justice directs judgment,
for it is not judgment unless it is right. Justice is a virtue of the mind; judgment is the working of that virtue. Receive your servant for good.
Receive me for good, for they want to lure me into evil. Do not let the proud slander me, that is, do not let them catch me by their slander.
Do not let the proud trap me, plotting behind my back because I worship Christ, for they say that Christians worship a dead man.
My eyes have failed, longing for your salvation. My eyes are worn out looking for your Savior. I long for him; I yearn for him.
And for the word of your justice. And for the word of your righteousness, which is learned in the Gospel, when he comes.
Deal with your servant according to your mercy. Deal with me, your servant, according to your grace, not according to my own deserving.
And teach me your justifications. And teach me your justifications, by which you make people righteous,
rather than their making themselves righteous. I am your servant. I am your servant. Things went badly for me because I wanted to be my own free man.
[?] not [?] your servant. Give me understanding, that I may know your testimonies, that is, your commandments. Give me understanding, that I may know your commandments.
Give me always to drink from the fountain of eternal light, so that I may know them, and by doing them may know them ever better and better.
It is time to act, Lord. It is time for the doing that you must do. Come and visit us, and do not delay. They have scattered your law.
They have scattered your law; that is why it is time. Who did that? The proud, who, wishing to establish their own righteousness,
were not subject to the righteousness of God. The law came in so that sin might abound; sin scattered the law. Therefore I have loved your commandments above gold and topaz.
Therefore I loved your commandments more than gold and topaz, because love can fulfil [them],
which fear could not. The grace of God gives love. Those who could not see the veiled face of Moses could not perceive grace.
They wanted to do your commandments for an earthly reward, yet they did not do them, because they loved other things. Neither servile fear nor love of earthly reward
could lead them to it. But I loved your commandments above gold and topaz, because no goods are equal to them
that do good to human beings. The topaz has two colours, one of gold, the other of the sky; and as beautiful as an eye [?]
so it shines in gold. Therefore I was directed to all your commandments. For that reason I became upright toward your commandments, because I loved them.
I have hated every wicked way. I hated all unrighteous ways. Why should I not, since I loved righteous ones? I shunned the ways
on which one can lose things more precious than gold and topaz. Wonderful are your testimonies; therefore my soul has searched them.
Wonderful are your precepts, that is, the precepts of the law; therefore my soul searched them.
That they are good, coming from the Good, is not what makes them wonderful. But that they were given to those
whom they cannot bring to life: that is to be marvelled at, that is astonishing. How do we know that the law cannot justify?
Because Paul says: "For if a law had been given that could give life, truly righteousness would come from the law." My soul searched this:
for what purpose it was given, since it could not give life. It did not do this in vain. How so? The unfolding of your words
gives light and gives understanding to the little ones. For the opening of your words enlightens the little ones and gives them understanding.
What is the unfolding of your words, if not the law? Why it was given to those whom it cannot justify, that the little ones understand,
that the humble understand, of whom I am one; therefore I wanted to search it. It was given for this purpose:
that it should make you, proud Jew, humble, and show you that your strength is not enough to fulfil it,
and that you should flee to grace and say plaintively [?]: "Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak." That is what you will have to do,
because through the law comes knowledge of sin, not justification. I opened my mouth and drew in breath, because I longed for your commandments.
Because I wanted your commandments, I opened my mouth and confessed that I, being weak, could not do strong things.
...a little one, great things. And thirsting, I drank in the good Spirit, who helped me to do what I could not do through the commandment, holy

and just and good. For it is not those who are led by their own spirit, but those who are led by the Spirit of God, who are the sons of God. This is not because they themselves do nothing, but so that they do not fail to do good:
they are moved by the Good so that they may act. "Look upon me and have mercy on me, according to the judgment of those who love your name." Look upon me
and have mercy on me according to the judgment of those who love your name. That means: according to the judgment that you made on those
who love your name. Why do they love? Only because you loved them first. As John says: "Let us love God,
because he first loved us." These are the words of one who has drunk sweetness and, having tasted the sweetness,
wants to drink more. "Direct my steps according to your word, and let no iniquity have dominion over me." Direct
my steps according to your commandment, and let no injustice rule over me. You commanded love: give me love.
Since you were willing to command it, be willing also to help me toward it. "Redeem me from the false accusations of men, and I will keep your commandments."
Free me from the slanders of men, and then I will keep your commandment. Calumnies are false accusations. Make me not fear them.
Then I will be kept safe in their midst through patience. Whoever fears them is easily turned to follow them. Do not let that happen to me.
"Make your face shine upon your servant." Let your face shine over your servant. Show me your presence by helping me.
"And teach me your statutes." And teach me your statutes. Teach them to me in such a way that I do them.
So it also says elsewhere: "Teach me to do your will." For whoever does not do them has not learned them.
So says the Truth: "Everyone who has heard from the Father and has learned comes to me." From this it is true that whoever does not do,
therefore does not come, because he has not learned. "My eyes have brought down streams of water, because they did not keep your law."
My eyes brought down outflowings of water, because they did not keep your commandments.
My eyes, which carelessly looked on misdeeds, weep for it. Their stream had to flow downward, to the humility of penitence,
because of the guilt of having gazed at the allurements of unlawful curiosity. So it happened to David on account of Uriah's wife.
In other books it reads: "My eyes have passed over [streams of water]," as if eyes could run more than springs of water.
This figure of speech is called hyperbole, that is, overstepping. "You are just, O Lord, and your judgment is right."
You are just, Lord, and your judgment is right. Therefore I wept much,
because every sinner must fear your justice, by which you condemn whoever is condemned, and there is no one who can rightly complain about his condemnation.
"You have commanded justice, your testimonies." You commanded what is right. What? Your testimonies. They are your justice, and you are just
in commanding justice. "And your truth exceedingly." And you commanded your truth strictly. What truth? Again, those same testimonies.
by which you wish to make yourself known; these one must keep all the more diligently, the more diligently they are commanded.
My zeal has made me waste away, because my enemies have forgotten your words. My zeal made me waste away,
because my enemies forgot your words. Because I loved them, I was grieved that they were not, together with me, fervent in the love of God.
That grief weighed on me so heavily that it made me waste away as if in sickness. Hence it is written elsewhere:
The zeal for your house has consumed me. Your word is exceedingly fiery, and your servant has loved it. Your word glows and kindles fiercely,
and your servant loved it. That is why I also wanted my enemies to love it, and for it to set them on fire. Cleopas felt this
when he said: "Was not our heart burning within us while he opened the Scriptures to us on the way?" I am young and despised;
I have not forgotten your statutes. I am younger than they are, and despised; yet I did not forget your statutes,
as they did. The people of the New Testament may say this, who were held in contempt by the people of the Old Testament. This may also be said in particular by
Joseph and David, who were held in contempt by their brothers and yet kept the statutes of God. Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness.
Your righteousness is eternal righteousness, not that of the Jews, for their righteousness, which they wanted to set above the righteousness of God, is made void.
And your law is truth. And your law is truth, as is evident from the fact that it bears witness to the righteousness of God. As it says:
"The righteousness of God has been made manifest, being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets." Trouble and anguish have found me; your commandments are my meditation.
What then has happened to me? Troubles and anxieties came upon me; yet your commandments were my thought.
Let them attack, let them help one another, let them persecute me; I only keep your commandments, and I even love them [my enemies] for the sake of your commandment.
Your testimonies are righteousness forever. Your testimonies, for which the martyrs died, are eternal righteousness, for they live forever by that righteousness.
Give me understanding, and I shall live. And give me understanding, and then I shall live. Make me understand how there is nothing
that persecuting enemies can take from me, and how I will then truly live if I lose temporal life
for the sake of confessing you. I have cried out with my whole heart; hear me, O Lord; I will seek your statutes.
I called with all my heart. This is what someone does who is intent on his prayer and in his earnestness does not let himself think of anything else.
Such prayer is constant for some, not for many. Whether it is ever so perfect for anyone is unknown. He who speaks here
claims such a prayer: Hear me, Lord, for my cry is in earnest. I seek your statutes, to carry them out faithfully,
not merely to know them. I cried out to you; save me, and I will keep your commandments. I cried out to you; save me,
and then I will keep your commandments. Give me the salvation of the soul; by that I will do what I know ought to be done.
I came early, at an untimely hour (that is, aoria in Greek), and cried out. I hurried at an untimely hour and cried out to you. At midnight.
before the morning time came, I rose up to pray. That time is called 'in-maturitas' (untimeliness), and it is one word, not two.
One of the translators said 'in immaturitate', that is, 'en aoria' in Greek, with two prepositions. That is the same sense.
For 'inmaturitas' means 'unripe', that is, an unseasonable time, which is also commonly called 'hora inportuna' (an inconvenient hour), as midnight is, and the dead of night (intempesta),
when it is not the time for working but for resting. This saying can be understood of every one of the faithful who often does this,
who rises so early. The untimely time can also mean the time before Christ came, when the prophets cried out and begged him to come,
as he had promised. That is why it says further on: 'In your word I have hoped exceedingly.' In your promise I trusted.
That is why I cried out. If I had not longed for your coming, I would not have cried so urgently. 'My eyes have gone before you to the morning.'
My eyes went ahead of the dawn, and they kept watch ahead of it toward you. What is this dawn?
Nothing other than when day began to break for those who sat in the shadow of death, and they began to see you in the flesh. Why did I do this?
'That I might meditate on your words.' So that I might keep your promises in mind, together with all those who announced them in the Law and the Prophets.
'Hear my voice according to your mercy, O Lord; according to your judgment give me life.' Lord, hear my voice according to your
mercy, so that you grant me forgiveness in the time of mercy. According to your judgment (I mean according to the judgment of those who love your name)
quicken me to life. 'Those who persecute me have drawn near to iniquity, but they have gone far from your law.'
My persecutors drew near to injustice. In what way? Only by tormenting my flesh, because to the soul, which bears the torment,
they come no nearer. But they went far away from your law. They were near to injustice and far from justice.
'Be near, O Lord.' Lord, be near to us. Let your nearness be within us, a nearness that never forsakes us.
'And all your ways are truth.' And all your ways are truth. In that truth of your justice
you will let us suffer afflictions, because we do not suffer them without guilt. 'From the beginning I have known of your testimonies,
for you have founded them forever.' At the beginning of this world I learned from your testimonies that you established them for eternity
and gave them a foundation in Christ. This was shown in Abel, with whom the city of God, the holy Church, began; it was shown in the patriarchs and prophets
and in the others in whom the holy Church then consisted, who had the testimonies of God founded in Christ. 'Initio' (at the beginning) is an adverb, as is 'katarchas' among the Greeks.
Others said 'ab initio' (from the beginning), so that it would be more understandable [?]. 'See my humility and deliver me, for I have not forgotten your law.'
See my humility and free me, because I did not forget your law, which says to us: 'Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled,
and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.' 'Judge my judgment and redeem me.' Examine my judgment. In other words: see my
humility; see how I have judged myself. 'And redeem me' [text: 'redi me' [?]]. In other words: 'and deliver me'. 'Because of your word give me life.' Because of your promise, quicken me.
Which ones? All except those [of whom it is said]: "He who believes in me shall not die in [?], but shall have eternal life." Salvation is far from sinners.
because they have not sought out your ordinances. Salvation is far from sinners. Why is that? Because they did not seek out your ordinances. I am not like them,
for I sought them out. Many are your mercies, O Lord; give me life according to your judgment. Many are your mercies, Lord.
Give me life according to your judgment, so that I do not go without that mercy. Many are they who persecute me and afflict me; I have not turned aside from your testimonies.
Many persecute me and afflict me, says holy Church in the person of the martyrs. For all that, I did not swerve from your testimonies.
Therefore the earth is purpled with the blood of the martyrs, heaven blooms with the crowns of the martyrs, the churches are adorned with the memorials of the martyrs,
the seasons are marked by the feast days of the martyrs, healings multiply through the merits of the martyrs. I saw the transgressors and I wasted away, because they did not keep your words.
I saw others turning away from it, who denied you in the persecution, and I wasted away from grief that they did not keep your words.
It weighed on me like the cutting off of my own limbs. Other translators say: "I saw those who did not keep the covenant." The covenant is:
"Whoever conquers will be crowned." Whoever does not keep it is a transgressor. See how I have loved your commandments. But see, I loved your commandments.
You commanded love; that I loved, and it made me steadfast in confessing you. Lord, give me life in your mercy. Lord, make me
live in your mercy. Persecutors kill me; you bring me to life. May your mercy give what I cannot earn.
See me, who loves you; keep me, who am in danger. Truth is the beginning of your words; all the judgments of your righteousness endure for ever.
Truth is the beginning of your words: they come from truth and they are true. They deceive no one,
neither the righteous man, to whom they promise life, nor the wicked man, to whom they promise punishment. These two are for ever the judgments of your righteousness.
Princes have persecuted me without cause. The body of Christ, holy Church, speaks here. What does it say? The lords of the world persecuted me though I was guiltless.
How did we Christians harm the earthly kingdoms? When Christ himself was asked whether one should pay tribute to Caesar, did he not say:
"Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's"? Did he not pay tribute to him himself,
with money taken from a fish's mouth? And what of his forerunner? Soldiers came to him and asked: "What shall we do?"
He did not say: "Unbuckle your belts, throw away your weapons, desert your king, so that you can serve God as soldiers." What did he say instead?
"Do violence to no one, accuse no one falsely, be content with your pay." And Paul, the companion of Christ,
what did he advise Christ's provincials, his own fellow soldiers? Did he not say: "Let every soul be subject to the higher powers"?
And again: "Render to all what is owed: tribute to whom tribute is due, custom to whom custom is due,
fear to whom fear is due, honour to whom honour is due." Did he not command that holy Church should pray for kings?
What wrong did Christians do against them that they should persecute them? Therefore holy Church rightly says: they persecuted [me] for nothing
[?] they [?] me. And my heart stood in awe of your words. So it was at your words, not at their words,
that my heart was afraid. They threatened: "I proscribe you, I kill you, I torture you with hooks, I burn you with fire, I hand you over to the beasts, I tear your limbs apart."
I feared none of that, because you said: "Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul,
but fear him who has the power to destroy both body and soul in Gehenna." I will rejoice over your words like one who finds much spoil.
I rejoice in your words like someone who finds a great deal of spoil, because my victory has given me a great deal of spoil,
in those who marveled at the patience of your soldiers, turned to you, and became believers. I hated and abhorred iniquity, but I loved your law.
I hated injustice and loathed it, but I loved your law. Although I feared your words, which are your law,
I still love them, and chaste fear does not get in the way of that love. In the same way children should fear and love their parents,
and a wife should fear and love her husband. Seven times a day I have praised you for the judgments of your righteousness.
Seven times a day I praised you because of the judgments of your righteousness. "Seven times" is to be understood as "always,"
because all time is counted in periods of seven days. As it says: "The righteous man will fall seven times and rise again,"
that is, he is humbled by every kind of tribulation and makes progress. Great peace belongs to those who love your law, and nothing makes them stumble, that is, nothing offends their mind.
Those who love your law have firm peace and do not stumble. Even if someone who loves the law does not understand it,
he still believes that it has hidden and holy meanings. So he honors it and blames himself for
his lack of understanding. But the Jews stumbled when they were told to understand the law spiritually, because they did not love spiritual things.
It can also be understood this way: neither prosperity nor adversity harms those who love God's law. I waited for your salvation, O Lord,
and loved your commandments. I waited for your Savior, Christ, O Lord, and loved your commandments, the love of God and of one's neighbor.
Anyone who does not love these commandments waits for him in vain. Those who love them are now waiting for him, so that when Christ, their life, appears,
they too may appear with him in glory. My soul has kept your testimonies and loved them greatly. My soul guarded your testimonies
and loved them greatly. The martyrs say this, because if they had not kept God's commandments, martyrdom without love would have done them no good.
I have kept your commandments and your testimonies, because all my ways are in your sight. I kept your commandments and your testimonies,
because all my ways are in your sight. Since you watch over them and look on them with merciful eyes,
I keep my uprightness in them. Let my prayer come near into your presence, O Lord;
give me understanding according to your word. Let my prayer, which is before you, come near to you, Lord, as it says:
"The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart." Give me understanding according to your promise. What promise is that?
"I will give you understanding and instruct you." Let my petition come into your sight; deliver me according to your word. May my prayer come before you.
Release me according to your promise. This says the same thing again. He prays well
who prays like this. By receiving understanding he is helped, because by trying to understand on his own he comes to harm.
My lips shall pour forth a hymn when you have taught me your justifications. My lips speak a song of praise when you teach me your righteous decrees.
God teaches those who are "taught of God," so that they keep God's righteous decrees not only by remembering them but by doing them.
My tongue shall proclaim your word, for all your commandments are equity. My tongue tells your speech
and teaches your commandments, because they are all just. Therefore I want to become a minister of the word, because there is equity in it.
But I know well that dangers will meet me from those who contradict and persecute me. What will become of me then?
Let your hand be there to save me. So let your help come to keep me, so that I am not lost in my soul. For I have chosen your commandments.
For I chose your commandments, so that with love for them I overcame fear. I have longed for your salvation, O Lord, and your law is my meditation.
I wanted Christ, your Savior; I longed for him. And your law is my meditation, because the law bears witness to Christ.
My soul shall live and shall praise you, and your judgments shall help me. In him my soul lives and praises you,
and your judgments help me, together with those who are to hear: "Come, you blessed of my Father." I have gone astray like a sheep that has perished.
I went astray like a lost sheep. Seek your servant, for I have not forgotten your commandments. Seek me, seek your servant,
for I did not forget your commandments. Those whom you sought, you found. Still seek those whom you are to find and save.
A Jew who was wise in his own way was asked why the Songs of Steps were given that name. He answered like this: When David wanted to build a temple to the Lord,
he leveled the temple mount and shaped it entirely to fit the temple he wanted to build. And he dug around it in such a way
that a small hill was left on top of the mount, and he wanted to build the temple on it. On the small hill he made fifteen steps,
going around it three times, set one below another [?], so that the workmen and all the people could go up and down easily.
And because he expected that he himself would complete the work, he at once composed joyful songs for that same work,
I mean for the fifteen steps, with the same number of psalms. And the first song shows at once
that he had envious people and opponents over that same work. That is why he said: "Lord, deliver my soul from wicked lips
and from a deceitful tongue," and so on. That is the end of the Jew's account. As far as the outer bark is concerned, I believe it should not be scorned.
But if we have tasted anything sweeter from the faithful, who pressed out the marrow, and want to bring it out into the open as far as we are able,
let no one call that wish pride, for it shows no envy, which is the handmaid of pride. The Songs of the Fifteen Steps.
Nor do they differ even in the number itself, as it seems to the Fathers. This same number is made up of twelve and three,
or of ten and five, or of nine and six, or of eight and seven,
or of twice seven and one, or of four and eleven, or of seven and eight, put together with a mystery known to many. And so it is, in these seven
ways, full of the adornments of the Holy Spirit. But how the whole Church, which along the ladder of virtues,
that is, of good deeds, climbs to heaven with her members, sounds in each song: that is delightful to perceive.
She says first of all that she dwells here below with those who dwell in Kedar, who hinder her so that she may not climb.
After that she says that she lifts up her eyes to the apostles, and wants to step on them, the twelve, as her step [?],
who are the foundation of the city into which she wants at last to climb fully, and then, having come in there, to sing with exultation: BEHOLD NOW, BLESS.
After that she steps onto the third step, in the voice of one sighing for the heavenly Jerusalem, whom the prophets and apostles then comfort so that she may attain it fully.
And she says with joyful exultation that they keep faith with her just as they promised her, that is, in these things that were said to me:
WE SHALL GO INTO THE HOUSE OF THE LORD. On the fourth step, which is the number of the perfect, the Church lifts up her eyes to God himself,
trusting tearfully, so that she will not take her eyes off him, even as he scourges her [?], until he sends her his grace.
On the fifth rung she takes the martyrs in hand, and steps so firmly that she also sets the other orders of the faithful,
with that strength, higher and higher, up to the tenth, which becomes her own special rung.
The sixth step is that of the confessors. The seventh is that of those who repented in time. Judas did not do that: FOR HE WAS ALREADY JUDGED.
The eighth is that of Saint Mary with the virgins and widows. The ninth is that of the married. The tenth is that of the Church, as we said,
that is, of all those who went before, together. On this step she gathers herself, in spite of her enemies, into the barn in her sheaves, the tares
and the grass on the housetops having been cast away. When the deep sinners then see this, who had very nearly lost the acceptable time,
they begin to fear for themselves, lest they become bundles for burning, and then they step up late,
that is, at the eleventh hour, onto the eleventh rung: OUT OF THE DEPTHS. And then they are redeemed with superabundant grace.
The twelfth step is that of the infants and the innocent; the Church need not gather them. Mother Grace nurses them in her arms.
On the thirteenth rung the perfected shepherds and flocks clothe themselves with the first robe,
in which they are to celebrate the wedding with the Bridegroom, as it says: ALL OF YOU WHO HAVE BEEN BAPTIZED IN CHRIST HAVE PUT ON CHRIST. On the fourteenth
they raise together, as brothers, a hymn and song of joy: BEHOLD HOW GOOD, and they step into the kingdom of heaven,
for there the Lord commanded the blessing. The song of the fifteenth step they sing seated on the height of the bridal throne.
Thus. "Behold now, bless [the Lord], you who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house," and, as it is in the Apocalypse: "Alleluia. Amen."
"Blessing and glory and wisdom." With this comfort the Church now at last speaks to those who still dwell in Kedar.
Since it may happen to you so graciously at your end, confidently in the nights lift up all your hands in the holy places and bless the Lord.
So the nights of this last song accord with the Kedar of the first. Alleluia. Praise the name of the Lord.
"You who stand," as also above. But also, what in the fifteen divisions of the musical monochord, that is, the four tetrachords,
this very power may signify — if anyone not unlearned has examined it, the power of the Holy Spirit, who, containing all things, has knowledge of the voice —
he will find wonderful ornaments. A SONG OF ASCENTS, THAT IS, OF STEPS. TO YOU, WHEN I WAS IN TROUBLE, I CRIED,
and you heard me. I cried to you, Lord, when I was in troubles, and you heard me.
Lord, deliver my soul from unjust lips and from a deceitful tongue. Lord, free me from unjust
and deceitful words. Such are the words of those who hasten to deceive me as though they were sparing me, and who hasten to turn me aside,
so that I do not climb up from vices to virtue. "Where do you want to go?" they say. "You want to go too far,
farther than you are able." What shall be given to you, and what shall be added to you against a deceitful tongue? Then I said to myself: What will be granted to you,
and what will be set against it for you? That is, what will you have to set against such deceitful words? Sharp arrows of the mighty one,
with desolating, that is, laying-waste, coals. Sharp arrows of the mighty one do that; these are the words of God. Set them against it,
with destroying coals, that is, with the examples of those who were cold but who then kindled themselves to destroy their errors.
By doing so you climb by steps, as they also did. Woe is me, why has my sojourning been prolonged? "Ah me," you then say,
"why has my exile become so long?" Because you at once begin to long to go hence as soon as you climb up to virtue,
and the wrongdoing of others begins to weigh on you; therefore this life at once seems to you an exile and full of sorrow.
I have dwelt with the tents, that is, with the inhabitants of Kedar. I sit with those who dwell in Kedar, where the dwelling of Ishmael is,
who is to be cast out of God's kingdom. As it says: "Cast out the bondwoman and her son,
for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the free woman." His tents are Kedar, that is, darkness; in them sit sinners,
among whom I dwell here. My soul has long been a sojourner. My soul is very much in exile here.
It is weary of the tents of Ishmael. With those who hated peace I was peaceable. I kept peace with those
who hate it. These are the ones among whom I sit in Kedar, whose wickedness I endure,
so that there may still be peace between us. When I spoke to them, they fought against me without cause. Needlessly they struggled against me when I greeted them.
because I did not seek my own profit when I greeted them, but the salvation of those who are in Christ.
And because they hate peace, they could not bear to hear any mention of Christ, who is our peace.
A Song of Degrees. I have lifted up my eyes to the mountains, from where help shall come to me. I looked up to the mountains.
that is, the apostles. From there help comes to me. By preaching the gospel they have shown us where the help is to come from.
My help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth. Help comes to me from God, who made heaven and earth. This is learned from them.
Do not let your foot be moved. Lord, do not let my foot slip through pride. Nor let him slumber who keeps Israel.
Nor let him slumber who guards you, Israel. Behold, he who keeps Israel will not slumber nor sleep. Nor does he.
He does not slumber, nor does he sleep, who guards Israel. Israel means "a man seeing God." Whoever believes in the incarnation of the Lord
is Israel, because he will come to behold the face of God. The Lord will keep you; the Lord is your covering
upon your right hand. God guards you. God is your covering and your shield over the power of your right hand,
that is, over the power of your blessedness, because you have the power to become a son of God and to be at his right hand. So he shields you,
so that you are not tempted more than you can bear. The sun shall not burn you by day, nor the moon by night. By day the sun does not harm you,
nor the moon by night. Prosperity and adversity do not harm you. The Lord keeps you from all evil; may the Lord keep your soul.
God guards you from all evil. May God guard your soul. Even if the body is slain,
may the soul be kept safe. May the Lord keep your coming in and your going out, from this time forth and for ever.
May God guard your going in when temptation begins to come upon you, so that he does not let you be too severely tested; and your going out,
so that you come out of it improved, like Job. From this time forth and for ever. May he guard you now and always.
The voice of one sighing for the Jerusalem above. I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: we shall go into the house of the Lord. I am glad of the things
that the prophets and apostles promised me. "We shall go," they said, "into God's house." That house is in heaven. Our feet were standing
in the courts of Jerusalem. Since those promises, our feet have stood in the courts of Jerusalem, because since then we have set our hope there.
Jerusalem, which is being built. That is the heavenly Jerusalem, which is being built like a city out of living and spiritual
stones. Whose participation is in the selfsame. Its participation, I mean hers: her participation is in the idipsum ("the selfsame").
She has a share in God; that is, her citizens have a share in him. He is always without change
and always one. That is why he is called idipsum ("the selfsame"), and that is why he is called est ("he is"). For there the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord.
My Lord's tribes, by which I mean those who believed in him, not those who crucified him, climbed up there into the city.
The testimony of Israel. Israel's testimony, that is, those in whom Israel is recognized, the ones who are without guile.
They go up there. To confess your name, O Lord. They go up there to confess your name
and to praise the Lord. For there the seats were set for judgment. For there the seats were set for judgment.
These are the righteous. They are God's seats; he rests on them. Seats over the house of David. They are seats,
that is, judges, over Christ's household, from which they received [it] and were brought forward when they came to it
with the message of the gospel. Ask for the things that make for the peace of Jerusalem. Ask, you seats, you who are both
seats and those who sit on the seats, about what leads to the peace of the city of Jerusalem. Those who gave away their goods
and showed mercy to Christ's poor are the ones who lead to the peace of Jerusalem. It will be judged in their favour that they go there.
And abundance for those who love her. And there is abundance there for those who love her. They lack nothing there.
Let there be peace in your strength. May peace come to you, Jerusalem, in your virtue, which you showed, that is, love and generosity.
And abundance in your towers. And let there be abundance in your towers. These are the ones who judge there, who find in God enough
of everything they desire. For the sake of my brothers and my neighbours I spoke peace about you. For the sake of my brothers and my
kinsmen I spoke peace about you. I sought their benefit, not my own. For the sake of the name of the Lord our God I have sought good for you.
For the sake of God's name I sought your good, not my own. I told them about it, that is, about the peace of your courts, so that I might guide them there.
A SONG OF ASCENTS. TO YOU I HAVE LIFTED UP MY EYES, you who dwell in the heavens. I lifted up my eyes, climbing up to you who dwell in heaven.
Does he dwell in heaven, then? Where did he dwell before heaven came to be, and before his saints, in whom he dwells?
He dwelt in himself and with himself, just as he still dwells in himself. Behold, as the eyes of servants are on the hands of their masters,
and as the eyes of a maidservant are on the hands of her mistress, so our eyes are on the Lord our God until he has mercy on us.
As the eyes of servants who are being flogged watch their masters' hands, and the eyes of a maidservant watch her mistress's hands,
[watching for] how soon [?] they mean to stop [?], so our eyes watch for God our Lord until he has mercy on us.
He has mercy on us when he takes away from us the scourge and the misery that we earned in Adam when we received corruption
and mortality. Whoever recognizes this and prays about it, he has mercy on them. Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us.
This is what we must say, because we suffer the scourge: Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us. For we are greatly filled with contempt.
For we are greatly filled with contempt from those who mock us for hoping for the blessedness
that we do not yet see. Our soul is filled to the utmost. Our soul has had its fill of it; it is full beyond measure.
…of the contempt. "Reproach to those who have plenty, and contempt to the proud." Reproach is with those who have plenty,
and contempt is with the proud. Plenty makes them proud; from this it comes that they mock the good.
THE VOICE OF THE MARTYRS. "IF THE LORD HAD NOT BEEN IN US, LET ISRAEL NOW SAY, if the Lord had not been in us,
when men rose up against us, perhaps they would have swallowed us alive." Now let Israel say: if God had not been in us,
when men attacked us, perhaps they would have swallowed us alive.
Those who knew that an idol is nothing, and yet were forced during persecution to sacrifice to it,
were swallowed alive. If they had believed that the idol was something, they would have been swallowed dead.
But no one could force the martyrs to do that, because God was in them. Those to whom this life was dearer than the eternal one,
and who therefore went knowingly to sacrifice so that they would not lose this life: God was not in them.
"When their fury was enraged against us, perhaps the water would have drowned us." When their rage was kindled against us,
perhaps the water would have drowned us (that is, the torrent of persecution) if God had not been in us, just as it drowned those
in whom God was not. "Our soul has passed through the torrent." Our soul waded through the torrent, which those others could not wade through.
"Perhaps (that is, do you think) our soul has passed through water without substance?" Do you believe that our soul has waded through water without substance?
That water is sins, which have no substance, only poverty, by which those people wanted to become rich and instead have become poor.
"Blessed be the Lord, who did not give us as prey to their teeth." Praised be God, who did not give us to their teeth as prey,
who did not let our persecutors hunt us down and catch us and lead us into sin.
"Our soul has been rescued like a sparrow from the hunters' snare." Our soul has been freed from the fowlers' snare,
like the sparrow that escapes from it. "The snare is broken, and we are delivered." The snare is crushed, and we have escaped.
"Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth." This is because our help was in the name of the one who made heaven and earth.
A SONG OF ASCENTS. "THOSE WHO TRUST IN THE LORD ARE LIKE MOUNT ZION; they will not be moved forever."
Those who put their trust in God can never be moved, like Mount Zion. "Who dwell in Jerusalem." These are those
who dwell in the heavenly Jerusalem. From then on no one disturbs them; they always stay firmly within it,
as Zion stands firmly in the earthly Jerusalem. "Mountains are round about it, and the Lord is round about his people."
The apostles surround it, and the Lord surrounds his people, because he gives them the unity of peace
through the apostles' message. "And this from now on and forever." From now onward and into eternity.
he fortifies the city. For he will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the righteous. For he does not leave the power of the sinners
over the portion of the righteous. Though he lets them rule over them for a time, he does not suffer it for long.
So that the righteous may not stretch out their hands to iniquity. For he does not want the righteous, because of that distress, to stretch out their hands to injustice
and become like the wicked. Do good, O Lord, to the good and to the upright of heart. Do well, Lord, to those who have good and upright
hearts, who do not follow after the wicked. But those turning aside into [?] (transuggellationes), the Lord will lead away with those who work injustice.
Those who turn to the likeness of the [?] (iruuurgton, perhaps 'the strangled'), and learn evil from the evil, God leads away with those who act unjustly.
They go after those whom they are like. And peace upon Israel. And upon Israel comes peace, that is, rest meets him.
A SONG OF DEGREES. WHEN THE LORD TURNED THE CAPTIVITY OF ZION, we became like those comforted. When God turned the exile of Zion,
then we became as if comforted. We were made exiles by our sins, and redeemed with Christ's blood,
and we are as if comforted, because, still weeping here, we hope to ascend there,
where we shall be fully comforted. That is in the resurrection of the righteous. Then our mouth was filled with joy, and our tongue with exultation.
Then our mouth and our tongue became full of joy and gladness. The heart has its own mouth and its own tongue;
it is of these that this is spoken. Then they shall say among the nations: The Lord has done great things with us; we have been made joyful.
Then they shall say among the peoples: The Lord has done mightily with us; we have been gladdened. Because he now says in the future tense, 'they shall say,'
therefore the past tenses too, 'turned' and 'was filled', which he spoke before, are to be understood as future.
In prophecies such speech is constant. Now is the time when we should say: THE LORD HAS DONE GREAT THINGS WITH US.
For we had done evil to ourselves; then the Son of God came and did the mightiest thing for us, in that he gave himself for us.
Turn, O Lord, our captivity, like torrents in the south. When this was prophesied in words of the past tense,
it was still to come; therefore he prays that it may come to pass, thus: Turn, Lord, our exile,
as the streams are turned in the south wind. The streams are frozen in winter; when the warm wind comes,
the ice melts, and then the streams run. So we were frozen in our sins until the wind of the Holy Spirit came
and melted our sins and made us run to the fatherland. Because this must take place with tears, he promises us comfort for them too,
saying thus: Those who sow in tears shall reap in joy. Those who sow with tears reap with joy. Those who here sow alms
and good works reap when they receive eternal life as their reward. Going, they went and wept, casting their seeds.
But coming, they shall come with exultation, carrying their sheaves. They go weeping while they sow, but they come joyful with their sheaves.
when they reap. If they weep here, they will be compensated for it when they receive the crown of life.
A SONG OF DEGREES. UNLESS THE LORD BUILDS THE HOUSE, those who build it have laboured in vain.
Unless our Lord builds the house, the labours of those who hurry to build it are lost.
All the preachers cannot make a person better unless God does it. He is the wise Solomon.
He builds the house, and success is his. Unless the Lord guards the city, the one who guards it keeps watch in vain.
Unless Christ guards the Church... It is vain for you to rise before the light. It is useless for you, before the day,
to get up, that is, to take things up ahead of Christ. Those who want to be exalted where he was humble do this.
Rise after you have sat down. Stand up once you have sat down. Be humble here, and then you can rise again in glory.
You who eat the bread of sorrow. I say this to you who eat bread in grief and mourn here in the valley of tears. When he gives sleep to his beloved,
behold the inheritance of the Lord. When he grants the end to his faithful ones, then the inheritance comes. After this life comes the reward.
Whoever longs for his own honour wants to stand up before he has sat down, and to have glory before he has humbled himself.
The reward of the Son. Then comes the reward of the Son. The fruit of the womb. Then comes the reward of the fruit of the holy womb.
It is his, and he gives it to them. He is the son of Mary, and he gives the resurrection of life as a reward. Like arrows in the hand of the mighty one,
so are the sons of those who have been shaken out. As arrows are in the hand of the mighty one, so are the sons of those who have been shaken out. The mighty one shoots far.
The words of the apostles have also travelled far, as it says: THEIR SOUND HAS GONE OUT INTO ALL THE EARTH, AND THEIR WORDS TO THE ENDS OF THE WORLD.
They are the children of the prophets, whose hidden writings have now been shaken out. Blessed is the man who has filled his desire from them.
God bless the one who turns to them to be filled. Blessed is the one who longs for their teaching. They will not be put to shame when they speak to their enemies in the gate.
They will not be ashamed when they speak to their enemies at the city gate. Christ is the city gate,
because he said: I AM THE DOOR. They stand in him until they overcome those who deny their message.
A SONG OF DEGREES. BLESSED ARE ALL WHO fear the Lord. Blessed are all who fear God. Who
walk in his ways. Blessed are those who walk in his ways and keep his commandments. You shall eat the labours of your fruits;
you are blessed, and it will go well with you. Because all the blessed are one in Christ, the prophet now speaks in the singular to those he had just addressed in the plural.
You eat the labours of your fruits. You have labours here, and they refresh you in hope.
You have fruits in the other world, and they lead you there to fullness. Therefore you are blessed now in hope,
and it will then go well with you in reality. Your wife is like a fruitful vine. Your Church, O Christ, is like the fruitful vineyard.
"On the sides of your house." In what is she fruitful? On the sides of your house. These are the ones who cling to you.
Those who are at a man's side cling to him. "Your children like new olive shoots around your table."
Your children surround your table like a newly planted olive grove. They are like the olive grove because they are peacemakers. "Blessed are the peacemakers,
for they shall be called children of God." They surround your table because they will possess your kingdom. "Behold, thus shall the man be blessed who fears the Lord."
The man who fears God receives such a blessing. "May the Lord bless you out of Zion." May God give you blessing from Zion, that is, from the watchtower.
The watchtower is in heaven, where we shall see God. You who fear God, desire such a blessing, so that you may see him.
"And may you see the good things of Jerusalem." And may you see the good things that belong to the city above. What are they?
What but the sight of God? That is the blessing from Zion. "All the days of your life." All the days of your life: that is the eternal day.
"And may you see your children's children," that is, the fruits of your works. And may you see the fruit of your works. "Peace upon Israel."
And peace upon every good man.
A SONG OF ASCENTS. "OFTEN HAVE THEY ATTACKED ME FROM MY YOUTH." The Church of God laments what she has suffered from the wicked.
Often, she says, they persecuted me, ever since I began to grow. "Yet they could not prevail against me."
They could never corrupt me, because they could not turn me over to their side. "Sinners built upon my back."
They built upon my back, that is, they loaded me with hardships. Because I would not be like them,
they persecuted me for it and were a burden to me. "They made their injustice long." They did their wrong far from me,
because I was not their accomplice. "The just Lord will cut the necks of sinners." The righteous Lord then hews their necks.
"Let all who hate Zion be put to shame and turned back." Let those who hate Christ's Church be put to shame and go backward.
"Let them be like grass on the housetops, which withers before it is pulled up." Let them fare badly, like the grass that grows on the roof,
which dries up before anyone takes it away. Before sinners die, they are already withered in God's sight.
"With which the reaper has not filled his hand, nor he who gathered the sheaves his bosom." With which the reaper did not fill his hand,
nor did he who gathered the sheaves fill his lap. The angels, who are the reapers, do not gather them into the Lord's barn, because they are tares,
and they are bound in bundles to be burned. "And those who passed by on the way did not say: The blessing of the Lord be upon you."
And the apostles and prophets passing by did not say to them, as the custom was in Judea:
"God's blessing be upon you." "We bless you in the name of the Lord." Nor did they say: "In God's name we bless
you." They gave their blessing to the good and the righteous, not to the wicked.
A Song of Steps. And the voice of the sinner. Out of the depths I have cried to you, O Lord. Lord, hear my voice.
Out of the depth of sins I called to you, Lord. Understand: not like the wicked man who, when he has come into the depth of sins, despises.
Lord, hear my voice. Let your ears be attentive to the voice of my pleading. Let your ears listen to my prayer.
If you will mark iniquities, O Lord, Lord, who shall endure it? If you will hold his wrong against every man, Lord,
Lord, who can bear it then? For with you there is forgiveness. I called to you, because in you there is atonement.
You atoned for us with your blood. Because of your law I have waited for you, O Lord. Because of your law I waited for you, Lord.
Which law? The one that says: "Bear one another's burdens, and so you will fulfil the law of Christ." Because I strove to be such [a person] [?],
I therefore waited for grace. I trusted in your promises. My soul has hoped in the Lord. From the morning watch until night.
From the dawn until night I hoped in my Lord. Before daybreak Christ rose,
guarded by soldiers. From early morning until my end I hope in him. For he rose, never to die again,
so that he has also promised that I shall rise. For with the Lord there is mercy, and with him there is plentiful redemption.
Therefore I hope in him, because with him there is mercy and full redemption.
And he will redeem Israel from all his iniquities. And he redeems Israel from all his wrongs.
A Song of Steps.
Lord, my heart is not exalted. Lord, my heart is not lifted up. I bring you this sacrifice, because it says:
"A sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit." Nor are my eyes lifted up on high. Nor are my eyes raised high.
I do not presume more of myself than I am able for. Nor have I walked in great things, nor in wonders above me. Nor did I go about in great things
and wonderful ones that people would tell of me. That is: I did not desire any fame, as Simon Magus did,
who wanted to receive the Holy Spirit in order to glorify himself with signs and wonders. If I was not humble-minded, but exalted my soul,
like one who is weaned from milk upon his mother, so be the reward to my soul. If I glorified myself and so was not humble,
then like the weaned child that is still in its mother's arms, so let my reward be. Let Israel hope in the Lord
from this time now and forever. Whoever wishes to see God, let him hope in him, from now on into eternity.
When he comes there, he has what he wanted in the thing itself, not in hope. That is: in reality, not in hope.
A Song of Steps. Remember, O Lord, David and all his meekness. Remember, Lord, David and all his gentleness.
David showed his gentleness toward Saul his enemy, when he could have killed him and yet did not kill him.
Christ is David, and in Christ the people of God. Christ showed his meekness when he prayed thus on the cross: Father, forgive them,
for they do not know what they do. He also taught the people of God to do the same, when he said: Pray for your enemies;
do good to those who hate [you]. How he swore to the Lord, he vowed a vow to the God of Jacob.
Remember him and help him to fulfil what he swore and vowed to God. What did he swear,
and what did the people of God vow? That he would be the temple of God. If I enter into the tabernacle of my house, if I go up onto the bed of my couch,
if I give sleep to my eyes and slumber to my eyelids and rest to my temples, until I find a place for the Lord, a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.
I do not go into the dwelling of my house; I do not climb into my bed; I do not allow sleep to my eyes, nor rest to my temples, before I find a place
and a dwelling for the God of Jacob. That is to say: I care for nothing of mine without him. I will not rejoice in any of my things
unless I may house him in my heart. Behold, we have heard of it (that is, the church) in Ephrata; we have found it in the fields of the forest.
The house of God, that is the church. Ephrata means 'mirror'. An image shines in a mirror. What is prophecy but an image of things to come?
We heard of it formerly in the mirror; we have found it in the forest-fields. The Gentiles, who had formerly grown wild as a forest through unbelief,
have become the church of God. We have entered into his tabernacles (that is, of the Lord God of Jacob). Now we have gone into his tent,
for we are in his church. We have worshipped in the place where his feet stood. We prayed
where his feet stood. In his church he has become settled. There he hears us. Arise, O Lord, into your rest,
you and the ark of your sanctification. Now arise, Lord, from death to rest, and together with you your church, which you
have sanctified. For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed. Do it for the sake of David your servant;
do not turn away from us the face of your anointed. This voice is addressed to the Father of Christ. The Lord has sworn truth to David, and he will not repent of it:
Of the fruit of your womb I will set upon your throne. For he swore to David something he will not regret, saying thus:
One born of you I will set on your throne. If your sons keep my covenant and these my testimonies which I shall teach them,
and their sons (that is, if they keep them), they shall sit for ever upon your throne. If your sons and the sons' sons keep
my covenant and my testimonies which I teach them, then they shall sit for ever on your throne. Those who do not fulfil this
are not children of David through faith. Yet on their account the oath does not become void. For the Lord has chosen Zion;
he has chosen it beforehand as a dwelling for himself. For the Lord chose his church; he chose it beforehand
as a dwelling for himself. This is my rest for ever and ever; here I will dwell, for I have chosen it beforehand.
Thus he promised: This is my rest for ever; here I dwell, for I chose it for myself beforehand. Its widow
[?]s of the Church. Blessing I will bless her widows, and I will satisfy her poor with bread. Her widows I bless; her needy I satisfy with bread.
He himself is the bread that he gives to widows and to the truly needy. Who are they? THE HUMBLE OF HEART.
I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her saints shall rejoice. Now the Father speaks: His priests I clothe with the Saviour,
as it says: AS MANY OF YOU AS HAVE BEEN BAPTIZED IN CHRIST HAVE PUT ON CHRIST. And his saints rejoice in that garment.
There I will raise up the horn of David. There I raise up the height of David; there I show the exaltation of CHRIST. I have prepared a lamp for my Christ.
For my anointed one I have a lamp all ready before him.
CHRIST showed that lamp in JOHN the Baptist, when he said: HE WAS A BURNING AND SHINING LAMP.
But upon him my sanctification shall flourish. On him my sanctification shines. Those whom I sanctify, I sanctify in him.
A SONG OF ASCENTS. BEHOLD HOW GOOD and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell in unity. See how good and how delightful it is
for brothers to dwell together. That is said of those who have one heart and one soul. Like ointment on the head,
