which ran down onto the beard, the beard of Aaron. They are like the ointment on Aaron's head that ran down from the head onto his beard.
CHRIST is a priest, as Aaron was, and the head of his Church. From him the Holy Spirit ran down into the apostles, who are his beard,
because they were manly in him and feared no suffering they had to endure for his sake. Which ran down onto the hem of his garment.
It also ran onto his garment. That is his Church; it is his garment, because he is in it. Like the dew of Hermon
which comes down on Mount Zion. Hermon means 'exalted light'. That is CHRIST. From him comes dew, that is, grace. Like the grace of God
that comes upon the sons of the Church, as the brothers who love one another are. For there the Lord commanded a blessing.
For where they are, there he commanded the blessing to be. And life for ever. And eternal life.
A SONG OF ASCENTS. BEHOLD NOW, BLESS THE LORD, ALL YOU SERVANTS OF THE LORD. You who stand in the house of the Lord,
in the courts of the house of our God. Now praise the Lord, all his servants, you who in his house
stand, in the courts of his house. The Church is the house; the breadth of charity is the court.
Praise him now in this toilsome world, so that you may praise him without toil in the world to come.
In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, and bless the Lord. By night, that is, in adversity, lift up your hands to holiness
and praise him, as Job did. May the Lord bless you out of Zion, he who made heaven and earth.
May God, who made heaven and earth, bless you, his people. HERE ENDS [THE SECTION] ON THE FIFTEEN PSALMS OF ASCENTS.
ALLELUIA. PRAISE THE NAME OF THE LORD. Praise the Lord's name. Praise the Lord, you servants. Praise your Lord, you servants.
For the Lord judges over his people which of them he shall illuminate or blind. As he said:
"For judgment I came into this world, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind."
And he will be called upon in his servants. And in his servants he will be called upon. For many, pricked with compunction, come of their own free will
and ask for baptism, and pray to him. The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the works of men's hands. They have a mouth and will not speak.
They have eyes and will not see. They have ears and will not hear, nor is there any breath in their mouth. God is the one who has always done all this
and still does it. But what are the idols of the nations? What are their gods? Gold and silver, the handiwork of men. They have a mouth
and do not speak; they have eyes and do not see; they have ears and do not hear; nor is there breath in their mouth.
Let those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them. May those who make them become like them, and all who put their trust in them.
These are the ones who do not have the eyes of faith or ears for hearing. House of Israel, bless the Lord.
You true Israelites, praise him. House of Aaron, bless the Lord. You leaders, praise him. House of Levi, bless the Lord.
You ministers, praise him. You who fear the Lord, bless the Lord. You who fear God, all of you say together like this: Blessed be the Lord out of Zion,
who dwells in Jerusalem. Praised be, from Zion, the one who dwells in Jerusalem. Those who await his coming and
look out for it, they praise him out of Zion, that is, out of watchfulness.
Alleluia. After the Songs of Ascents. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good. That is, praise the Lord by confessing him, for he is good. By confessing, praise God for this:
that he is good. For his mercy endures forever. For his grace is without end. Give thanks to the God of gods.
Confess him to be the God of the gods, such as those are of whom it is written: "I said, you are gods." Give thanks to the Lord of lords.
Confess him to be the Lord of the lords, who made all lords. Who alone does great wonders. Who alone does great wonders.
Who made the heavens in understanding, that is, in wisdom. Who made the heavens in his wisdom. Who established the earth above the waters.
Who made the earth firm beside the water. Where it is bare, there it is higher than the water. Who made the great lights.
Who made the great lights. The sun to rule the day. The sun to rule over the day. The moon and stars to rule the night.
The moon and the stars to rule over the night. These are the things he made by himself. The things that come after this
he made through angels and through men. Who struck Egypt with their firstborn. Who struck Egypt with its firstborn.
Who led Israel out from their midst. Who led Israel out from their midst. Just as he daily sets the good free from the wicked.
With a mighty hand and an uplifted arm. With a powerful hand and a high-raised arm. Who divided the Red Sea into parts.
Who divided the Red Sea. Just as he also divides baptism: for some unto life, for others unto death. And led Israel through its midst. And
...led Israel through there. Just as he now also leads his people through the bath of regeneration.
And he struck down Pharaoh and his host in the Red Sea. Whereby Pharaoh died there, and his might, that is, his army.
Just as baptism now takes away sins. Who led his people through the desert. He who led his people through the wilderness.
Just as he now leads us in this barren world and helps us to salvation. Who struck down great kings.
and slew mighty kings: Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan. He who slew the powerful and mighty kings,
such as Sihon was, and Og, by whom our vices are signified, which God slays. And he gave their land as an inheritance to Israel his servant.
And he gave their land to the lineage of Abraham. For what the devil possessed, he gave to Christ, who is the seed of Abraham. For in our humility God was mindful of us.
and redeemed us from our enemies. This he did because he remembered us in our humility, and redeemed us
with his Son's blood. Who gives food to all flesh, that is, to every race of men. He who gives food to all people.
What is that? That of which Christ said: "My flesh is true food." Give thanks to the God of heaven. Praise the God of heaven.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his mercy endures forever. Praise the Lord of lords, for his mercy is eternal.
A PSALM OF DAVID AND OF JEREMIAH. By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept, when we remembered Zion.
By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion. We wept in exile when we remembered our homeland. Zi-
-on is the homeland. God bless him who longs to go there and who therefore weeps in this Babylon.
What are the rivers of Babylon? Nothing other than the fleeting joys of this world, in which those do not wish to drown
who hope to win lasting joy in Zion. They wish to stay above them, so that they are never carried downstream by wading into them.
On the willows in the midst of it we hung up our instruments. On the willows that stand in its midst
we hung our instruments. There they hang and are silent, for the willows' barrenness has silenced them.
Greedy and insolent people, who are barren trees and turn to evil whatever good is told them:
on them we are to hang up the instruments of the Scriptures. For there those who led us captive asked us for
the words of songs. And those who carried us away said: Sing us a hymn from the songs of Zion. For there they asked us,
those who had driven us into exile, what the words of the songs say. "Sing to us," they said,
"your songs; sing to us in your fashion, as at home." The demons, who entice us into sins
and have thereby driven us into exile, say this to us through wicked people, their members. To them we answer:
How shall we sing the Lord's song in a strange land? How can we sing our Lord's song in a foreign land?
...which came from him? It is perilous for us to sing, and to provoke you to blasphemy. Against them we must set ourselves apart,
so that we are not like them, with these words: If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand be forgotten. If
I forget you, Jerusalem, then let my right hand forget me. If, for the sake of such people, I am willing to forget Jerusalem,
then let my right hand fail me. The right hand is eternal life, just as the left hand is the present life.
If I am willing to please people like these, then let me have the left hand instead of the right. For that is what happens to all those
who give up hope of Jerusalem and love temporal things more than eternal ones. Therefore these words are prophecies, not curses.
Let my tongue cleave to my jaws if I do not remember you. Let me become mute if I do not remember you, Jerusalem. If I do not set Jerusalem
at the beginning of my joy. And if I do not set Jerusalem first among my joys. The foremost joy is there,
where one may enjoy God himself. Therefore he speaks to God against all the enemies of the city: Remember, Lord, the sons of Edom,
that is, of Esau, in the day of Jerusalem. Remember in judgment, God, the children of the persecutor. Take your vengeance on the day of judgment on those
who are enemies of Christians, as Esau was to his brother. This too is prophecy, not a curse. Who say: Empty it, empty it, even
until we reach its foundation. Those who say of the Church what one says of a cistern:
'Draw it out down to the bottom.' Its bottom and its foundation is Christ, whom no one can take from it.
They wanted to do that when they slew the martyrs. Wretched daughter of Babylon, that is, the flesh, or carnal people,
blessed is he who will repay you the recompense that you paid out to us. Wretched daughter of Babylon, God bless the one who repays you with the same reward
that you paid to us. If the flesh or carnal people drive us toward vices, we who wanted to turn to vir-
tues, and they are against us, then we must stand against them by keeping vigil and fasting until we overcome them,
just as they wanted to overcome us. Blessed is he who will take your little ones and dash them against the rock. Blessed is he who takes your children
and dashes them against the stone. The children of Babylon are lusts. While they are still new, we must dash them to pieces on Christ before they grow older.
For David himself. I will confess to you, Lord, with my whole heart. I confess to you, Lord, says the Church, with all my heart.
I give you praise with a strong hand. For you have heard the words of my mouth. For you heard the words of my mouth. You heard me in the prayer of the prophets
and of the righteous, who prayed for your incarnation. In the sight of the angels I will sing psalms to you. Before the angels I sing to you; my song pleases them.
I will worship toward your holy temple. I pray toward your holy house, in which I know you. In your incarnation I know you.
Or else in your angels, before whom I sing. For your mercy and your truth. For your grace, by which you redeemed us,
and for your truth, by which you fulfilled what you promised. For you have magnified your holy name above everything.
For you have magnified your name above everything of yours that is renowned among angels and men.
On whatever day I call upon you, hear me swiftly. On whatever day I call upon you, on that day hear me speedily,
because I do not ask for temporal things, but for eternal ones. You will multiply strength in my soul. You will heap up many virtues in my soul. When I
am in need, then you strengthen me. Let all the kings of the earth confess you, Lord, for they have heard all the words of your mouth.
Let all the kings of the world confess you, Lord, and thank you, because they have learned all the words of your mouth,
which formerly only the Jews learned. And let them sing in the ways of the Lord, for great is the glory of the Lord.
And let them sing in the ways of my Lord that his glory is great. If they are humble,
then they sing in his ways. For the Lord is high, and he regards the lowly, and knows the lofty from afar. For God himself is high,
and he looks upon the lowly; the lofty he knows from afar. He takes heed of humility;
pride he despises. If I walk in the midst of tribulation, you will give me life, that is, you will gladden me. If I go in the midst of hardships,
that is, if I recognize that I am here in the vale of tears and in pilgrimage, then you will gladden me
after this life. And against the wrath of my enemies you have stretched out your hand, and your right hand has saved me.
Over the wrath of my enemies you stretched out your hand; you showed them that your wrath is more to be feared. And your right hand saved me;
that is, eternal life. Lord, you will repay on my behalf; Lord, your mercy endures forever; and do not despise the works of your hands.
You, Lord, repay my enemies on my behalf. Or: you pay the tribute for me; you give the stater.
Lord, your mercy is eternal, and you will not despise your work. Look upon your work, not upon mine.
ACCORDING TO AUGUSTINE. CHRIST SPEAKS TO THE FATHER ABOUT HIMSELF. Lord, you have tested me and known me. My Lord, you tested me
in the passion, and knew me, that is, you caused others to know me. You have known my sitting down and my rising up.
You knew my sitting down in death and my rising up after death. OR HE SPEAKS IN THE PERSON OF HIS BODY.
You knew my lowliness in penance when I was in exile, and my being raised up when I came
and obtained forgiveness. You have understood my thoughts from afar. You knew my thoughts from afar, when I began to loathe the worship of idols.
You have searched out my path and my boundary. My wretched path, on which I went away from you, and the end, which is mortality,
which I finally reached: that you searched out; it was not hidden from you. And you foresaw all my ways.
And you knew beforehand all my ways in which I went astray. You allowed me to walk them, so that, if I could go no further,
I would turn back to you. For there is no guile on my tongue. For now there is no deceit in my words.
Behold, Lord, you have known all things, the newest and the ancient. You know my latest things, when I became mortal, and the old things,
when I stood in sins. You formed me and laid your hand upon me. You created me, when I had sinned, for toils
in which I was not before, and you laid your hand upon me, for then you pressed me down.
Your knowledge has been made wonderful from me. Because of my guilt your knowledge has become wondrous and hard for me.
It has grown strong; I shall not be able to reach it. It is too strong for me; I cannot attain to it. But you can bring me near to it.
Where shall I go from your spirit? Where can I go before your spirit, of which the world is full? As it says: The Spirit of the Lord
will fill the whole world. And where shall I flee from your face? And where shall I flee from you? Where can I escape your wrath?
If I ascend into heaven, you are there. If I lift myself up high, there you press me back down.
If I descend into hell, you are present. If I hide myself so that I will not confess my sins, you make me confess them.
If I take my wings straight and dwell in the farthest parts of the sea, that is, of the world. If I take my wings, that is, the love of God and of neighbour,
to me in a straight course, and I dwell, that is, aim with hope at the end of this world,
which is the Day of Judgment, for there is the end of this sea of the world, in that way I escape your wrath.
For even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me. There, to that end, your hand brings me,
and your right hand holds me, so that I do not plunge into the sea before I fly across it. And I said:
Perhaps the darkness will trample me. And I said in fear: perhaps the darkness will trample me
and lead me astray. What is the darkness but this life? And the night is illumination in my delights. And therefore my night,
that is, my life, has become light in my delight, that is, Christ. He came into this night
to illuminate it. For the darkness will not be darkened by you. For by you, Christ, the darkness does not grow dark,
but by him who hides his sin and does not confess it. He doubles the darkness. And the night will be illuminated like the day.
And for the righteous man the night becomes just as light as the day; that is, adversity harms him no more than prosperity.
As its darkness, so also its light. For him prosperity and adversity go alike. For you have possessed my reins, Lord. For you
have possessed my loins; you do not allow me unchaste desires. You took me up from my mother's womb.
You have taken me out of my mother's womb. That is the perilous Babylon, whose children do not love the heavenly Jerusalem.
I will confess to you, Lord, for you have been made terribly wonderful. I confess to you, Lord, that you have become fearfully wondrous to us.
Your works are wonderful, God, and my soul will know it exceedingly. That is because your works are wonderful, God.
and now my soul knows them very well, though before I could not reach them. My bone is not hidden
from you, which you made in secret. My strength, which you gave me in secret, is not hidden from you. Of this Paul said:
AND NOT ONLY SO, BUT WE ALSO GLORY IN TRIBULATIONS. And my substance is in the lower parts of the earth, that is, in the flesh.
And my soul is in the depth of the body, though strength is given to it. LIKEWISE, SPOKEN IN THE PERSON OF THE HEAD: Your eyes saw my imperfect one.
His eyes saw my imperfect one, Peter. He promised what he could not carry out, yet God looked upon him,
as it says: AND THE LORD LOOKED UPON PETER. And in your book all shall be written. And in your book they will all be written,
the perfect and the imperfect. By day they will go astray. They go astray concerning Christ, because they think he is only a man,
and they abandon him in his passion. And none among them. And none of them holds fast to him completely, not even the one who said:
WITH YOU EVEN UNTO DEATH. But to me your friends, O God, are greatly honored. But your friends, once they have become so after my pas-
-sion, are greatly honored by me. Their principalities are greatly strengthened. Their apostleship is greatly strengthened. And I will number them,
and they will be multiplied above the sand. And I count them, and there are more of them than the sand of the sea. So many of them there will be after my passion,
of whom there were none before. I have risen, and I am still with you. I have risen after death, and I am still, Father, together with you.
I am not yet known to them, but only to you. If you slay sinners, O God, men of blood, depart from me. CONSTRUCTION:
If you slay sinners, O God, they will receive their cities in vanity. For you will say in thought: Men of blood,
depart from me. For you will say in thought, they will receive their cities in vanity. If you, God, slay, that is, blind, the sinners,
then they deceive their followers in vanity, because you say silently in the thoughts of the good:
Depart from me, you murderers. God teaches that the good should separate themselves from the wicked in their works
and yet live together with them [?]. Therefore the teaching of the slain, I mean of the blinded, is vanity. What is that teaching?
Only that they teach those like themselves, who are their cities, to hate the righteous. Why do they do that? Because to them their goodness
seems evil. Who are the men of blood? Only those who hate their brothers. Did I not hate those who hated you, O Lord,
and did I not pine away over your enemies? Why do they separate themselves from me, as if I were evil? Did I not hate those who hate you, Lord,
and did I not grieve over your enemies, because their wickedness pained me for your sake? I hated them with a perfect hatred. With perfect hatred
I hated them. That is, I hated them rightly, because I hated their wickedness, not them themselves.
They have become my enemies. They are my enemies because I hated their wickedness. Test me, O God, and know my heart.
Examine me, God, to see whether I have deserved that they should separate themselves from me, and know my heart.
because they do not want to know it. Search me and know my paths, and see whether there is a way of iniquity in me. Search me,
and know my paths, and see whether there is an unjust path in me. And lead me in the eternal way.
And direct me to the eternal way, CHRIST, in whom there is no injustice.
UNTO THE END, FOR DAVID HIMSELF. DELIVER ME, O LORD, FROM THE EVIL MAN, that is, the devil. Deliver me, Lord, says the Church,
from the evil man. That is the one of whom the holy Gospel says: AN ENEMY HAS DONE THIS.
From the unjust man deliver me. From the unjust man deliver me, so that I am not led into sin by him.
Who have devised injustices in their heart; all the day long they stirred up wars. Such are the unjust, who think unjust things in their hearts
and want to fight all day long, and bring in some schism or heresy, so as to stir up sedition. They have sharpened their tongues like serpents.
They have whetted their tongues like serpents. Their words are as dangerous as serpents. The venom of asps is under their lips.
Under their lips is hidden the deadliest venom. Keep me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner, that is, of the devil; from wicked men deliver me. Guard me,
Lord, from the devil's hands; deliver me from unjust men. Who have plotted to trip up my steps.
Who want to trip me up, who want to lead me astray from the right course. The proud have hidden snares for me.
The proud set snares for me. The heretics hurried to catch me with their wickedness. And they have stretched out cords as a snare for my feet.
And they stretched out cords as a snare for my feet; that is, they tied their cords so that my feet would be caught in them.
What are the cords but woven speech, made for leading people astray? Beside the way they have set a stumbling block, that is, an obstacle, for me.
Beside the way they laid something for me to stumble on. For they catch no others
except those who turn aside from the right path. I said to the Lord: You are my God. In those dangers I said to my Lord:
You are my God. But they cannot say this with confidence, because their pride separates them from God.
Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication. I also said: Hear, Lord, my prayer. O Lord, Lord, strength of my salvation.
You, Lord, I said, are the strength of my salvation; you give me the strength of that salvation. You have overshadowed my head in the day of battle.
In battle, that is, in temptation, you shaded my head so that I would not perish from the heat, as those perish
whose heat you do not cool. Do not hand me over, O Lord, from my desire, to the sinner. Because of desire, do not give me over, Lord, to the devil.
That desire is the heat which God's shade tempers, lest it hand us over, overcome, to the sinner.
They have plotted against me; do not forsake me, lest they be exalted, that is, lest they triumph over me. The wicked plotted against me;
do not forsake me, lest they become proud because of it. The head of their going-round; that is, their head is a going-round.
The devil is their head. He is a going-around; he never sets himself onto the way. "The labor of their lips,"
that is, the lie, "shall cover them." The labor of their mouth shields them. You shield me; their lie shields them.
With it they excuse themselves of their sins. That is harder to find than the truth.
"Coals of fire shall fall upon them." Glowing coals fall upon them, for they see those kindled
who were cold before. They see that these become earnest in good deeds. "You shall cast them down." There you cast them down.
That they begrudge those others, that is what fells them. "In miseries they shall not stand." Misery befalls them; before it they cannot stand.
But the righteous do stand, for one of the righteous said: "BUT WE GLORY ALSO IN TRIBULATIONS." "A man full of tongue shall not be directed upon the earth."
A man who talks too much never gains uprightness on earth, for it says: "IN MUCH SPEAKING YOU SHALL NOT ESCAPE SIN."
Whoever is a wagging tongue is often a liar; that is great unrighteousness. "Evils shall seize the unjust man unto destruction."
Evils seize the unrighteous man unto perdition. They can also seize the good, but not unto perdition.
"I know that the Lord will do justice for the needy." I know that God does justice for those who have nothing,
"and vengeance for the poor." And he takes vengeance on behalf of the poor. "But the just shall confess to your name."
But the righteous give credit to your name, not to themselves, for everything they are able to do. To you they owe for it
thanks. "The upright shall dwell with your countenance." The upright dwell together with your face,
as it says: "WHEN HE APPEARS, WE SHALL BE LIKE HIM, FOR WE SHALL SEE HIM AS HE IS."
UNTO THE END, FOR DAVID HIMSELF. "LORD, I HAVE CRIED TO YOU; HEAR ME." Lord, says the prophet, I cried to you; hear me.
"Attend to the voice of my supplication when I cry to you." Pay heed also to my prayer when I cry to you.
As you did in the past, so do in the future: hear me always. "Let my prayer be directed as incense in your sight."
Let my prayer rise up like smoke before you; let my prayer give off a sweet scent to you. "The lifting up of my hands, an evening sacrifice."
Let the lifting up of my hands be an evening offering to you. May you have regard for my good works at my end.
"Set a guard, O Lord, on my mouth, and a door enclosing my lips." Set a guard on my mouth, Lord,
and place a door around my lips. Teach me to be careful of my words. "Do not incline my heart to words of malice,
to make excuses in sins." Do not turn my heart to ill-willed words, to excusing sins.
Teach me pure confession, which frees from death. "With men who work iniquity, and with their chosen ones, I will not share."
With the unrighteous and with their chosen ones I have no fellowship. These are the ones who deny their own sins.
The righteous man shall correct me in mercy and rebuke me; but let not the oil of the sinner anoint my head. The righteous man rebukes me and reproves
me mercifully. Let not the oil of the sinner anoint my head. His oil, that is his praise
and his flattery, which a good man must always flee. For my prayer is still in the things that please them.
That is, of the sinners. For still [?] my prayer is in their liking. It will yet come to pass that it pleases them to say it.
FORGIVE US OUR DEBTS, AS WE ALSO FORGIVE OUR DEBTORS. Their judges, joined to the rock, have been swallowed up.
Their judges have been destroyed when set against Christ. The teaching of Plato and Aristotle is worth nothing when the gospel of Christ is set against it.
They shall hear my words, for they have prevailed. They hear my words, for these were mighty; those were powerless.
As the fatness of the earth has burst forth. From this the blood of the martyrs came like the fatness of the earth.
From it grew the holy crop, so that people everywhere became Christians. Our bones have been scattered beside hell, that is, the martyrs.
Our bones were scattered beside hell. Those who strengthened us were thrown as if into hell,
but they are glorious in heaven. For my eyes are toward you, O Lord, Lord. For my eyes look to you, Lord,
to your promises, not to their threats. In you I have hoped; do not take away my soul, that is, from your good things.
In you I hope; do not separate my soul from your good. Keep me from the snare that they have set for me
and from the stumbling blocks of those who work iniquity. Guard me from the snare that they have set for me, and from the stumbling block of the unrighteous.
Sinners shall fall into his net. Sinners are caught in his net. The net is the devil's; the snare is his. I am alone until I pass over.
That is, to the Father. I am alone, says Christ, until I die; after that I multiply my own.
OF DAVID HIMSELF. WITH MY VOICE I CRIED TO THE LORD. With my voice I made supplication to the Lord. With my voice I cried to the Lord;
with my voice I prayed to the Lord. My voice is the one that comes from the heart. Many cry out with their lips, not with their hearts.
God hears the heart; man hears the lips. I will pour out my prayer in his sight. Before him I pour out my prayer,
where only he sees it. No one else can see the heart, only he. I declare my trouble before him.
I tell my trouble before him. When do I do that? When my spirit fails within me. When my spirit grows faint.
Why should I do that? So that his Spirit may strengthen me. And you knew my paths. And you knew my paths.
You saw me walk rightly. On this way on which I walked they hid snares for me. They secretly set a snare for me,
says Christ, on the way on which I walked in innocence; even so they set up the gibbet of the cross for me. I looked to the right and saw,
and there was no one who would know me. So I looked around to see who was on my side, and there was no one who recognized my divinity.
Flight has failed me. I did not flee there, though others fled. And there is no one who seeks after my soul. That is, no one sought me out to help me.
I cried to you, Lord. Then I cried to you, Lord, like this: Father, into your hands I commend my spirit. I said: you are my hope.
I also said: you are my hope. My portion in the land of the living. My share of the inheritance in paradise, as was promised to the thief:
Today you shall be with me in paradise. Attend to my prayer, for I am brought very low. Hear my prayer, for I am greatly humbled
by death. Deliver me from those who persecute me. Release me from my persecutors, who do not spare me,
because they do not recognize me as God. As it says: For if they had known, they would never have crucified the Lord of majesty.
For they have grown too strong for me. For they have gained the upper hand over me and have thrust me into death. Bring my soul out of prison.
Bring me out of hell. So that I may confess your name. That is, so that my faithful may praise you. The righteous wait for me
until you reward me. My apostles wait until you give me my glory in the resurrection.
A prayer of David when his son pursued him. Lord, hear my prayer; take in my plea with your ears.
Lord, hear my prayer; attend to my plea. Hear me in your truth, in your righteousness. Hear me in your truth,
in your righteousness; hear me not in mine, for you gave me whatever righteousness I have. And do not enter into judgment with your servant,
for no one living will be justified in your sight. And do not deal with your servant by strict judgment,
but mercifully, for no living person is guiltless before you. As Job says: No one is clean
before you, not even an infant whose life on earth is one day long. For the enemy has persecuted my soul; he has brought my life low in the earth.
For the devil persecuted me and brought my life on earth into sins. These are the words of a penitent.
But if they are to be David's words about Absalom, or Christ's about Judas, then it says this: My enemy persecuted me
and brought me low; for the one was deposed from his kingdom, and the other was condemned on the cross. That is why Christ speaks right after this:
He has placed me in dark places, like those of the world who are dead. He thrust me into the darkness of the grave, like the dead of the world
who die justly, because they die for their guilt. And my spirit was in anguish within me; my heart was troubled within me.
And my soul was in anguish within me, and my heart was grieved within me. This follows the words: My soul is sorrowful even unto death.
I remembered the days of old. Now his body joins him in speaking: I remembered the days of old, when this world was made.
And I will meditate on the works of your hands. And I thought about your handiwork, which shines in heaven and on earth. From it I perceived this:
I stretched out my hands to you; I am like land without water before you. I stretched out my hands to you; as waterless earth is toward rain, so was I toward you.
Hear me quickly, Lord; my spirit has failed. Hear me quickly, for I can scarcely breathe.
As happens to those who become very weary and need refreshment. In my breath I am exhausted; in your refreshment, me.
Turn not your face away from me, and I shall be like those who go down into the pit. Do not turn your countenance from me, for then I
shall become like those who go down into the pit of hell. Make me hear your mercy in the morning. Let me hear your mercy in the morning.
When the day of judgment comes, then make me hear: COME, YOU BLESSED OF MY FATHER, RECEIVE THE KINGDOM. For in you I have hoped.
For I hope in you. Make known to me the way in which I should walk, for to you I have lifted up my soul. Make known to me the way
that is unknown to men, on which I should go. Make that known to me, for I have lifted up my soul to you, not down to this world.
Rescue me from my enemies, Lord; I have fled to you. Free me from my enemies; I have fled to you. Teach me to do your will,
for you are my God. Teach me to do your will, for you are my God, and I should will for you alone.
Your good spirit will lead me into the right land. May your good spirit lead me into the right land. The right land is the body,
as long as it is subject to the Holy Spirit. So too is the kingdom of the world to come. Therefore both are prayed for here.
For your name's sake, Lord, you will give me life in your equity. For your name's sake, since I have not earned it,
give me life in your justice. You will lead my soul out of tribulation. Lead my soul out of troubles. Let me end with forgiveness.
And in your mercy you will destroy my enemies. In your mercies you will destroy my enemies. And you will destroy all who afflict my soul,
for I am your servant. And you will destroy the devil, and all who torment me, for I am your servant.
DAVID AGAINST GOLIATH. BLESSED BE THE LORD MY GOD, WHO TEACHES
my hands for battle and my fingers for war. Praised be the Lord my God, who teaches my hands and my fingers to fight
against Goliath, who signifies the devil, and against the body, of which it is written: THE FLESH LUSTS AGAINST THE SOUL.
My mercy. You are my mercy, for you give it to me. And my refuge. And my refuge.
To him I flee; he is my fortress. My upholder and my deliverer, my protector. My receiver
and deliverer and protector. And in him I will hope, who subjects peoples under me. And in him I hope, who subjects people to me,
when after Saul I begin to rule my kingdom. Lord, what is man, that you have made yourself known to him? that is, the secret of the divinity. What is man,
that you make your secrets known to him? Or the son of man, that you take account of him? that is, that you esteem him so highly. Or the son of man,
that you take heed of him? Man has become like vanity; his days pass away like a shadow. Man is like vanity,
for his days pass away like a shadow. He was created more like truth; afterwards, through sins, he became like vanity.
Lord, bow your heavens and come down. Incline your heavens, Lord, and come down here; show yourself to us incarnate.
Touch the mountains and they will smoke. Touch the mountains, then they will smoke. Give compunction to proud hearts;
then they will do penance. Flash forth your lightnings and you will scatter them. Flash your lightning upon them, then you will scatter them.
Terrify them with your signs, then they will give up their conspiracy. Send forth your arrows and you will throw
them into confusion. Shoot your arrows at them, then you will afflict them. Send your apostles to them, then you will make them grieve for their sins.
Send forth your hand from on high. Send, Father, your Son from heaven. He is your hand, with which you created all things.
Rescue me and deliver me from many waters. Free me from many waters, from the many that come rushing in. From the hand of foreign sons.
Free me from the hands of foreign children, who are not children of the Church. Whose mouth has spoken vanity. I mean those
whose mouth always speaks vanity. Free me from those waters. And their right hand is a right hand of iniquity. And their right hand is
the right hand of injustice. That is because they hold on the right what they ought to hold on the left; I mean earthly goods.
They ought to hold eternal goods on the right. O God, I will sing a new song to you. When Christ comes, I will sing you a new song;
that is, that I may eat his body and drink his blood. On the psaltery of ten strings I will sing to you.
On the ten-stringed psaltery I sing to you, because the ten commandments of the law are yours, and so also is the tenfold Gospel.
They have both come from you. You who give salvation to kings. You give salvation to the righteous. You who delivered David your servant
from the malicious sword, deliver me. You who freed David your servant from Goliath's malicious sword, deliver me.
My Lord's sword is well-meaning, because it separates from evil; but the devil's sword is malicious,
because it separates from good. And rescue me from the hand of foreign sons, whose mouth has spoken vanity, and their right hand
is a right hand of iniquity. This verse says the same as it said before. Whose sons are like new plantings, firmly established from their youth.
Whose sons are new, like plantings, established from youth. They are as fair as newly planted vines,
because they have firmly established new heresies in place of the old teaching of the prophets and apostles. Their daughters are adorned, decorated all around like the likeness of a temple.
Their daughters go about decked out [?]; they go adorned in the manner of a church. They have the likeness of the adornment,
not the truth. Their storehouses are full, overflowing from this into that. Their cellars are full, changing the drink
from one to another. Their sheep are fruitful, abounding in their goings-out. Their sheep are fruitful, many in their goings-out.
Many go out of their folds. Their oxen are fat. Their cows are fat. There is no ruin of the wall.
Nor does their stone wall fall. Nor any passage. Nor can anyone pass through their house. They have privacy.
Nor any clamor in their streets. Nor is there shouting in their streets. No one wakes them. They have called the people blessed who have these things.
They called the people blessed who have such things. They did that because they held it as being on the right hand. I will say it more rightly.
Blessed is the people whose Lord is their God. That people is blessed which has God as its lord. If God is its lord, then it is blessed.
To David himself. I will exalt you, my God, the King, and I will bless your name forever, and forever and ever. To David himself,
that is, to Christ himself, the Church says: I exalt you, God, my king, and I praise your name in the world and forever after. Every day I will bless
you. Daily I praise you, not only in prosperity but also in adversity. And I will praise your name forever and ever.
And therefore I praise you here and in eternity. Whoever praises you worthily here will be granted
to praise you eternally. Great is the Lord and exceedingly to be praised, and of his greatness there is no end. Great is my Lord,
and very worthy of praise, and his greatness is without end. Without end also is my praise, for after this life I will praise you forever.
Generation and generation shall praise your works. Kindred and kindred praise your works: here in the world the sons of God, and in the other world the sons of the resurrection,
praise your name. And they shall declare your power. And they tell of your might. They credit to you what they themselves are able to do.
They shall speak of the magnificence of the glory of your holiness, and they shall tell of your wonders. They speak of the mighty work of your glorious holiness.
They recount your wonders. And they shall speak of the power of your terrible deeds. And they tell of the power of your fearsome things:
not only the kingdom of heaven, but also the eternal fire. And they shall tell of your greatness. And they recount your greatness,
that it is beyond measure. They shall pour forth the memory of the abundance of your sweetness. They belch forth the remembrance of the abundance of your sweetness. It is a sweet abundance
that you remember us. They eat it when they understand it; they belch it forth when they tell it and teach it.
Just as John feasted, lying upon the Lord's breast, and belched forth: "In the beginning was the Word."
And they shall exult in your justice. And they rejoice in your justice, not in their own justice. Just as they credit you with the fact that they exist,
so they also credit you with the fact that they are righteous. Otherwise they would give you the lesser part and themselves the greater.
The Lord is merciful and compassionate. The Lord is gracious, giving good freely, and forgiving, pardoning guilt. Patient and very merciful.
Patient in bearing with us, and very merciful in calling us to repentance. The Lord is sweet to all. A sweet Lord to all
who spiritually drink his gifts. And his mercies are over all his works. And his mercies are above all his works
that he does in us in secret; and yet his vengeance is over the devil's works. Let all your works confess to you, O Lord.
Let all your works confess to you, that is, let them praise you, Lord. They praise you because you are praised in them.
In them it is shown who you are. And let your saints bless you. And let your saints praise you: the holy angels, thrones, dominions.
…powers, principalities, and righteous men. They shall speak of the glory of your kingdom and tell of your power. They speak of the glory of your kingdom,
and they speak of your might, because you have given life to all living things, and to lifeless things the seed of their lasting.
That they may make known your power to the sons of men. That they make known your might to the children of men,
as Peter and John did when they made the man lame from his mother's womb able to walk. And the glory of the magnificence of your kingdom.
And the glory of the mighty work of your kingdom, which we do not yet see. For in the beauty of this world there dwell with us
beasts and worms and many loathsome things; but in that other world none will dwell with us except the angels alone. Your kingdom is a kingdom of all
ages. What kind of kingdom is it? When does it end? Your kingdom is an eternal kingdom; it lasts through all ages.
And your dominion is in every generation and generation. And your lordship lasts in every generation, the one that is now and the one yet to come.
The Lord is faithful in all his words. He is a faithful Lord in all his words, because he fulfilled what he promised.
HE DID NOT SPARE HIS OWN SON. That he promised. Eternal life he has yet to give. For that reason we have received the pledge of the Holy Spirit.
And holy in all his works. And he is holy in all his works. The Lord lifts up all who fall and raises up all who are crushed.
As is shown in this: he lifts up all who fall, and he raises up all who are crushed. The eyes of all hope in you,
and you give them their food in due season. They all wait on you, Lord, and you give them food at the fitting time.
You open your hand and fill every living creature with blessing. You open your hand and fill all living things with blessing.
From your hand comes all that they have. The Lord is just in all his ways and holy in all his works.
Our Lord is righteous in all his ways, that is, in all his creations, and he is holy in all his works.
The Lord is near to all who call upon him in truth. He is near to all who call on him in truth. Those do not do this
who ask him for wrongful things; therefore he is far from them. He will do the will of those who fear him, and he will hear their prayer and save them.
Those who fear him, he does their will; he hears them and saves them. The Lord keeps all who love him and will destroy all sinners.
He guards all who love him; all the sinful he destroys. My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord, and let all flesh bless his holy name forever
and for ever and ever. My mouth speaks the praise of my Lord, and let everyone praise his holy name forever and ever.
ALLELUIA. PRAISE THE LORD, O MY SOUL. My soul, praise God. Let every person's soul praise God,
since the prophet counsels his own soul to do so. I will praise the Lord in my life. I will praise him from now on, where my life is.
In eternal life, there I will praise him. I will sing to my God as long as I exist. I praise him here too, as long as I am here.
Put not your trust in princes, in the sons of men, in whom there is no salvation. Do not trust in the powerful.
Place no confidence in the children of men, on whom your salvation does not rest. It rests only in one Son of Man,
who is also the Son of God. His spirit shall go forth, and he shall return to his earth; in that day all their thoughts shall perish.
The man's soul departs, and then the body returns again to the earth from which it came. Then all their thoughts are gone.
Death takes them away entirely. Blessed is he whose helper is the God of Jacob. Blessed is he whose helper is the Lord God of Jacob,
who made that same Jacob into Israel. His hope is in the Lord his God, who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them.
Blessed is he whose hope is in the Lord his God, not in Saturn or Neptune, but in him who made heaven and earth and sea
and all that is in them. Who keeps truth forever, and executes judgment for those who suffer wrong.
Who always guards the truth, judging on behalf of those who suffer wrong, not of those who avenge themselves. He gives food to the hungry.
He gives food to the hungry. Those who hunger for righteousness, he satisfies. The Lord raises up the crushed. He raises up those who are brought low.
Those who fall so hard that they cannot rise up, he lifts up. The Lord looses the fettered. He frees those bound with fetters.
Heavy fetters are sins and this mortality; from both of these God frees us. The Lord enlightens the blind.
He makes the ignorant wise. The Lord loves the righteous. He loves the righteous. The Lord protects the stranger. He protects the newcomer.
That is the holy Church from among the Gentiles. He will take up the orphan and the widow. Orphans and widows he receives. And the way of sinners he will destroy.
And the broad way of sinners he casts out. He turns it away from himself; therefore it leads to hell.
The Lord shall reign forever, your God, O Zion, from generation to generation. Your God, O Zion, shall reign forever.
ALLELUIA. PRAISE THE LORD, FOR A PSALM IS GOOD. That is: praise the Lord, for it is good to praise the Lord.
Praise the Lord, because his praise is good. It is good that one praises him. Psalm-singing is good.
What is that, except that one sings on the psaltery? The psaltery sounds like a lyre or a harp
or an organ. And because what one sings on it sounds aloud, therefore 'psalm' means 'high song'.
He sings a high song who praises the Highest. He praises him who lives in a praiseworthy way. Let praise be joyful and seemly to our God.
Let praise be delightful and seemly to our God. He offers him seemly praise whose ways are seemly. He sings unseemly who
acts unseemly. As it says: PRAISE IS NOT SEEMLY IN THE MOUTH OF A SINNER. The Lord, building Jerusalem,
will gather the dispersed of Israel. Building the heavenly Jerusalem, he gathers the scattered people who are called 'those who see the Lord.'
The angels see him. Those who are to see him become like the angels. These he gathers in heaven.
...hardened from ice into stone. But when he converted them, he sent them out like pieces of bread.
For he revealed many gifts of the Holy Spirit in them. "Before the face of his cold, who will endure?" Who will stand before his frost?
Those whom he lets freeze, as he did to Pharaoh. What becomes of that? "He will send out his word and will melt them." The Father sends out his Word
and melts them. As it says: "Nor is there anyone who can hide himself from his heat." The Word of the Father thaws them.
"And his spirit will blow, and the waters will flow." And his Spirit blows upon them, and after that they flow to God,
because they have been melted by his warmth. "Who declares his word to Jacob, his justices and his judgments to Israel."
He who makes known his word, that is, his command, to Jacob, and his laws and his judgments to Israel.
Those who are his faithful, they are Jacob and Israel; to them he reveals how just he is in his judgments,
how no one is saved except by grace, because they all deserved death. "He has not done so for every nation, and he has not made his judgments known to them."
He did not make himself so familiar with every people, nor did he reveal his judgments to them as he did to Israel.
Psalm of Haggai and Zechariah. Alleluia. "Praise the Lord from the heavens." These two prophets rejoice
that praise comes to God from heaven and from earth. Therefore let us say together with them: Praise God, angels, from heaven. "Praise him in the heights."
Praise him on high. "Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts." Praise him all together, both angels and hosts. "Praise him, sun and
moon; praise him, stars and light." Praise him, sun and moon, stars and daylight. "Praise him, heavens of heavens,
and let the waters that are above the heavens praise the name of the Lord." Praise him, heavens of the heavens, that is, heavens above the heavens.
And let the waters that are above heaven, which hold up the firmament, praise his name. "For he spoke, and they were made;
he commanded, and they were created." For he bade them come into being; from that they came into being. He commanded their creation;
from that they were created. "He established them for ever and for ages of ages." He has established them for ever and in eternity.
Even if heaven and earth are changed, as it says of the world to come: "There will be a new heaven and a new earth,"
they still stand forever and endure forever. "He set a decree, and it will not pass away." He set them a law that does not pass away,
because it will not be resisted by them. "Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all depths." Give him praise from the earth,
flowing waters and all immeasurably deep waters. What are the flowing waters like, if not dragons? And what waters are as deep
as the sea that encircles the earth? "Fire, hail, snow, ice, and the stormy winds that do his word."
Fire and hail and snow and ice, and stormy winds, which carry out his command. "Mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and all cedars."
Mountains and hills, fruit-bearing trees, and all cedars. "Beasts and all cattle, serpents and feathered birds."
Wild beasts and all cattle, serpents and birds. Kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all judges of the earth,
young men and maidens, the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord, for his name alone is exalted. The kings of the land
and all the people of the world, and all judges, young men and maidens, old and young,
praise his name, for his name alone is exalted. His praise is above heaven and earth,
and he has exalted the horn of his people. His praise is above heaven and earth, because none of those who are in heaven or on earth can make themselves equal to him.
And he exalts the horn of his people when he sets them at his right hand and grants them the sight of him. A hymn to all his saints.
To all his saints a hymn is granted to sing. They sing this hymn in the heavenly Jerusalem, as it says: "A hymn befits you, O God, in Zion."
This hymn is common to them all; it is everlasting for them. To the people that draws near to him. It is granted to the people that draws near to him.
Alleluia. Sing to the Lord a new song. Sing to the Lord a new canticle. He sings it who hastens to put off the old man
and to put on the new; who loves heavenly things, not earthly; who lives in charity, not in discord; and who rejoices in the redemption which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
His praise is in the assembly of the saints. His praise is in the gathering of the saints. In heaven they gather together;
there they praise him. Those who also gather here in churches, they praise him. Let Israel rejoice in him who made him.
Let Israel rejoice in him who made him, not in treasure, nor in honors, nor in worldly fortune.
And let the sons of Zion exult in their king. And let Zion's sons rejoice in their king. The sons of Zion,
that is, Israel. Let them praise his name in chorus. Let them praise his name singing together. A chorus is the praise of singers, that is, a multitude singing together.
With timbrel and psaltery let them sing to him. Skin is stretched on the timbrel; strings are stretched on the psaltery.
With both of these, praise him. Let the hands be busy together with the mouth. That means: give alms, and do all good works.
That is the timbrel and the psaltery. For the Lord is well pleased with his people. For he is well pleased with his people.
That happens for him when he makes them like his angels. And he has exalted the meek unto salvation. And he exalts the meek unto salvation.
Many are proud, who exalt themselves unto death; but God exalts his meek unto salvation. The saints shall exult in glory;
they shall rejoice in their beds. The saints rejoice in glory. Where is that glory? In their chambers;
I mean in their hearts; there they rejoice. As Paul says: "For this is our glory, the testimony of our conscience."
The exultations of God are in their throats. God's joys are in their throats. They ascribe to God their glory,
in which they rejoice, and not to themselves. And two-edged swords are in their hands. And two-edged swords are in their hands.
That means the words of God, as it says: "The word of God is more piercing than any two-edged sword." For what do they use the swords?
